docs.title: resolve_mode_and_project(args)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_mode_and_project(args):

Description: Normalizes the active documentation mode and extracts a default project identifier if one was not explicitly supplied via CLI flags. Resolves backward compatibility for the legacy --advanced boolean switch against modern --mode options and strips trailing .git extensions or directory path prefixes.

Parameters:

  • args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI options containing mode, advanced, name, dir, and repo.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, str]: A 2-tuple of (mode, project_name) where mode is one of "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", or "sdk", and project_name is a sanitized string.

Example:

mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

def resolve_mode_and_project(args):
    """Resolve documentation mode (handling --advanced legacy flag) and derive project name.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: (mode, project_name)
    """
    if args.advanced:
        if args.mode != "tutorial":  # User explicitly set --mode AND --advanced
            emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE", mode=args.mode)
        mode = "advanced"
    else:
        mode = args.mode
    project_name = args.name
    if not project_name:
        if args.dir:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
        elif args.repo:
            project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
        else:
            project_name = "project"
    return mode, project_name

This function performs resolution precedence between the legacy --advanced switch and the newer multi-mode --mode flag, emitting an alert via emit() if both are supplied concurrently. If no explicit project name is provided via -n / --name, the function derives the identifier by taking the directory name of --dir or the final path segment of --repo, removing .git suffixes where present.

docs.title: build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name):

Description: Constructs the foundational dictionary serving as PocketFlow's shared memory store across all DAG nodes. Ingests normalized CLI arguments, calculated thinking schedules, exclusion pattern sets, and initializes empty result slots for downstream generation stages.

Parameters:

  • args (argparse.Namespace): The parsed command-line argument object.
  • github_token (str | None): GitHub Personal Access Token resolved from CLI or environment variables.
  • mode (str): Resolved documentation mode string.
  • thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Mapping of node identifier strings to their allocated thinking effort levels.
  • project_name (str): Derived or explicitly specified project name.

Returns:

  • dict[str, Any]: The initialized shared store dictionary containing configuration options, exclusion sets, and mutable output slots.

Example:

shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)

def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name):
    """Construct the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes.

    Returns:
        dict: The shared store with all CLI args, patterns, and empty output slots.
    """
    return {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": project_name,  # Resolved once in main so logs, --force-rebuild and output agree
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Cache flag (inverse of no-cache)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Max abstractions
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # LLM reasoning capabilities: global level (legacy) + per-node plan (utils/thinking.py)
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        "thinking_plan": thinking_plan,
        # Max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs populated by downstream nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }

The returned dictionary acts as the single source of truth across the entire lifecycle of the DAG execution. It combines user-specified exclusion rules with DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS imported from utils/exclude_patterns.py, sets up boolean switches for caching (use_cache = not args.no_cache), and primes list and dictionary containers (files, abstractions, relationships, chapters) that will be mutated by subsequent processing nodes.

docs.title: detect_llm_config(args)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def detect_llm_config(args):

Description: Dispatches provider detection and credential resolution to utils.llm_config. Retrieves the active provider type, model name, API endpoint URL, and context window size (using --max-tokens as an explicit override if provided, or fetching the dynamic default length from the model catalog).

Parameters:

  • args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments, specifically inspecting args.max_tokens.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, str, str, str, int]: A 5-tuple of (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length).

Example:

provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)

def detect_llm_config(args):
    """Detect LLM provider, model, endpoint, and context length from environment.

    Returns:
        tuple: (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length)
    """
    from utils.llm_config import get_model_context_length

    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key = resolve_llm_settings()
    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)
    return provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length

This helper wraps configuration lookup routines to keep inference details cleanly abstracted from main(). It performs late-importing of get_model_context_length from utils/llm_config.py to guard against premature module initialization and determine the effective maximum token window available for prompt packaging.

docs.title: resolve_thinking_plan(args)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_thinking_plan(args):

Description: Pure function that reconciles reasoning configurations across global CLI overrides, named thinking profiles, and per-node overrides into a comprehensive thinking schedule dictionary. Because it executes prior to localization catalogue initialization (init_output()), it avoids console side effects and defers argument validation messaging to _validate_thinking_args.

Parameters:

  • args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments containing advanced, mode, thinking_override, thinking_level, and thinking_profile.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, dict[str, str | None], list[str]]: A 3-tuple comprising:
    1. Resolved profile name string (e.g., "balanced", "global", "off").
    2. Dictionary mapping each pipeline node identifier to its resolved effort string or None.
    3. List of unrecognized or malformed per-node override strings.

Example:

thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)

def resolve_thinking_plan(args):
    """Build the per-node thinking plan from --thinking-override / --thinking-level / --thinking-profile.

    Pure (no emit): runs before init_output(). Validation messages come from _validate_thinking_args().

    Returns:
        tuple[str, dict, list[str]]: (resolved profile name, {node_key: level | None}, invalid override strings)
    """
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, invalid = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    profile = "global" if args.thinking_level else resolve_profile_name(args.thinking_profile, resolve_llm_settings()[0])
    return profile, build_thinking_plan(profile, mode, args.thinking_level, overrides), invalid

By leveraging functions imported from utils/thinking.py, this method establishes strict precedence: individual --thinking-override flags take priority over global --thinking-level values, which in turn supersede baseline --thinking-profile defaults. It determines whether a provider natively supports reasoning, generating a granular execution map passed to both UI emission and downstream generation nodes.

docs.title: display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan)
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan):

Description: Emits an exhaustive startup summary to standard output and log streams via utils.output.emit(). Displays provider details, endpoint paths, context ceilings, thinking allocations, batching rules, and target log paths.

Parameters:

  • args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments.
  • mode (str): Resolved operational mode (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk).
  • provider (str): Normalized LLM provider identifier.
  • model_name (str): Resolved model name string.
  • endpoint_url (str): HTTP URL of the target LLM API endpoint.
  • context_length (int): Maximum context tokens supported or clamped.
  • log_file (str): Filepath to the active logging destination.
  • thinking_profile (str): Name of the active reasoning profile.
  • thinking_plan (dict[str, str | None]): Mapping of node keys to thinking effort levels.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan)

def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan):
    """Emit all configuration values to the console."""
    emit("START_GENERATION", source=args.repo or args.dir, language=args.language.capitalize())
    emit("CFG_HEADER")
    emit("CFG_AI_PROVIDER", value=provider)
    emit("CFG_AI_ENDPOINT", value=endpoint_url)
    emit("CFG_AI_MODEL", value=model_name)
    emit("CFG_CONTEXT_LENGTH", value=f"{context_length:,}")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_LEVEL", value=args.thinking_level or "None")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_PROFILE", value=thinking_profile)
    if any(thinking_plan.values()):
        emit("CFG_THINKING_PLAN", value=describe_plan(thinking_plan, mode))
    emit("CFG_THINKING_SUPPORT", value=describe_thinking_support(provider, model_name))
    emit("CFG_TOKEN_RATIO", value=describe_token_ratio())
    emit("CFG_BATCH_SIZE", value=f"{args.batch}")
    _enabled = get("CFG_VALUE_ENABLED")
    _disabled = get("CFG_VALUE_DISABLED")
    emit("CFG_FORCE_BATCH", value=_enabled if args.force_batch else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_OUTPUT_MODE", value=mode)
    emit("CFG_MKDOCS", value=_enabled if args.mkdocs else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_INCREMENTAL", value=_enabled if args.incremental else _disabled)
    if args.incremental:
        emit("CFG_FORCE_REBUILD", value=_enabled if args.force_rebuild else _disabled)
    if mode == "api-reference":
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=get("CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX"))
    else:
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=str(args.max_abstractions))
    emit("CFG_LLM_CACHING", value=_disabled if args.no_cache else _enabled)
    if args.debug:
        emit("CFG_DEBUG_MODE")
    emit("CFG_LOG_FILE", value=log_file)
    print()  # Blank line after config block

This presentation function renders configuration data through catalog-backed string keys using utils/output.py. It formats large integer values with comma grouping, inspects provider capability diagnostics via describe_thinking_support(), displays the token ratio calibration state, and dynamically hides or displays mode-specific features such as incremental cache rebuild flags.

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def main():

Description: Primary application orchestrator. Coordinates the complete execution lifecycle across five distinct phases: argument parsing, validation/cleanup, preflight credential verification, pipeline graph execution, and final telemetry reporting.

Parameters:

None. Entry point invoked directly by Python's runtime environment.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • SystemExit: Raised with code 1 upon configuration errors, shell quoting syntax anomalies, invalid thinking parameters, or provider authentication failures.

Example:

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Phase 1: CLI Parsing and Pre-Initialization
docs.text:
parser, args = parse_arguments()
    # Resolved silently before init_output(): string translation itself uses the plan's translate_strings level.
    thinking_profile, thinking_plan, invalid_overrides = resolve_thinking_plan(args)
    # Translation of missing strings is an LLM call: deferred until arguments and credentials are checked.
    init_output(
        language=args.language,
        use_cache=not args.no_cache,
        thinking_level=thinking_plan["translate_strings"],
        debug=args.debug,
        auto_translate=False,
    )
    _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)
    _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)

The execution flow begins by parsing CLI flags and deriving the per-node thinking plan prior to initializing console logging. The localization catalog in init_output is initialized with dynamic string translation disabled (auto_translate=False) to ensure that preflight checks and argument parsing complete without invoking LLM inference endpoints prematurely. Immediate calls to _check_quoting_errors and _validate_thinking_args guard against corrupted command-line invocations.

docs.title: Phase 2: Argument Validation and Standalone Cleanup
docs.text:
# Handle standalone --cleanup (no --dir or --repo)
    if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
        _run_cleanup()
        return

    # Require --dir or --repo for generation
    if not args.dir and not args.repo:
        parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")

    # Fail fast (with setup instructions) before crawling if the configured provider cannot authenticate
    if not check_llm_auth():
        sys.exit(1)
    translate_missing_strings()
    notice_legacy_cache()

In this phase, main() checks if the invocation is a standalone maintenance operation (--cleanup). If not, it enforces that either a remote repository (--repo) or local directory (--dir) was provided. It then evaluates check_llm_auth() from utils/llm_config.py, failing fast with system exit code 1 if credentials or required SDK dependencies are missing. Once authenticated, any untranslated UI strings are synchronized via translate_missing_strings(), and legacy cache warnings are checked.

docs.title: Phase 3: Token Resolution and Cache Setup
docs.text:
# Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        if not github_token:
            emit("WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN")
    elif args.token:
        emit("WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO")

    mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
        emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
        args.incremental = False

    # --force-rebuild requires --incremental
    if args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        emit("ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        output_base = args.output or "output"
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            os.remove(manifest_path)
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED", path=manifest_path)
        else:
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_NO_MANIFEST", path=manifest_path)
        # The verified-facts cache (ExtractFacts) lives in facts.json: docs/api/ under --mkdocs, else next to the pages
        for facts_file in (facts_path(output_base, project_name, True), facts_path(output_base, project_name, False)):
            if os.path.exists(facts_file):
                os.remove(facts_file)
                emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED_FACTS", path=facts_file)

    # Warn about args ignored in api-reference mode
    if mode == "api-reference" and args.force_batch:
        emit("WARN_FORCE_BATCH_API_REF")
        args.force_batch = False

This phase handles GitHub token resolution from --token or the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, emitting warnings if unauthenticated rate limits will apply. It resolves project naming, verifies that --incremental caching is restricted solely to api-reference mode, and validates --force-rebuild dependencies. If rebuilding is enforced, it removes both the incremental tracking manifest (.doc_cache_manifest.json) and verified AST fact files (facts.json) discovered via utils/facts.py.

docs.title: Phase 4: Shared Store Assembly and Logging Configuration
docs.text:
shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode, thinking_plan, project_name)
    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
    log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
    display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file, thinking_profile, thinking_plan)

The fourth phase populates the shared store dictionary and detects LLM environment options. It initializes the file-backed logging engine via configure_logging(), provisioning an isolated log destination (logs/{project}_{mode}_{timestamp}.log) and flushing buffered early-boot console messages to disk. Finally, it displays the resolved configuration parameters to the user.

docs.title: Phase 5: DAG Execution, Cleanup, and Teardown
docs.text:
# Create and run the flow
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()
    try:
        tutorial_flow.run(shared)

        # Cleanup after run if requested
        if args.cleanup:
            _run_cleanup()
    finally:
        from utils.output import shutdown

        # Report spend even when the run fails — failed runs are often the expensive ones.
        try:
            _emit_usage_summary()
        except Exception as e:
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Usage summary failed: {e}", dest="LOG")
        shutdown()

The final phase constructs the PocketFlow DAG instance via create_tutorial_flow() and executes it against the shared state dictionary. Execution is guarded by a try...finally block to ensure that token usage metrics, multi-model billing ledgers, and cost summaries are calculated and printed even if the pipeline encounters fatal runtime exceptions. Post-run --cleanup requests are executed, and log buffers are flushed and closed by shutdown().

docs.title: _thinking_level_arg(value)
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _thinking_level_arg(value):

Description: Custom validator and type converter for the --thinking-level command-line argument. Converts empty strings or the keyword "default" to None, and asserts that any other input is a member of the canonical THINKING_LEVELS set.

Parameters:

  • value (str): The raw string argument passed to --thinking-level.

Returns:

  • str | None: The normalized thinking level string (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", "max"), or None if defaulting to native model behavior.

Raises:

  • argparse.ArgumentTypeError: If the supplied string is not a recognized thinking level.

Example:

parser.add_argument(
    "--thinking-level",
    default=None,
    type=_thinking_level_arg,
    # ...
)

def _thinking_level_arg(value):
    """argparse type for --thinking-level: a level from THINKING_LEVELS; '' or 'default' → None (model default)."""
    level = value.strip().lower()
    if level in ("", "default"):
        return None
    if level not in THINKING_LEVELS:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"invalid choice: {value!r} (choose from {', '.join(THINKING_LEVELS)}, default)")
    return level

This function performs input sanitization on command-line inputs by stripping whitespace and converting to lowercase. It maps neutral inputs ("" or "default") to Python None, signaling downstream LLM drivers to let the remote provider manage reasoning parameters natively. Any unrecognized string triggers an ArgumentTypeError, causing argparse to halt parsing with a clear error message.

docs.title: _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):

Description: Defensive shell syntax validator that inspects pattern values under --exclude and --include for swallowed CLI options. Detects scenarios where unescaped shell quotes cause subsequent flags (e.g., --language, --dir) to be merged into pattern strings, terminating the program before silent execution errors occur.

Parameters:

  • parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser instance used to extract registered option strings.
  • args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI argument values.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • SystemExit: Halts execution via sys.exit(1) if any pattern string contains a known CLI option flag.

Example:

_check_quoting_errors(parser, args)

def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):
    """Detect shell quoting errors where --exclude/--include values accidentally swallowed other CLI flags.

    When users misquote patterns (e.g., --exclude "autogen/* "SmartFO/*" --language Vietnamese),
    the shell merges subsequent flags into the pattern value. This silently causes ALL following
    arguments to be ignored. We detect this by checking if any pattern value contains a known
    CLI flag string, which no legitimate file/directory pattern would ever contain.

    Flags are extracted dynamically from the argparse parser — no hardcoded list to maintain.
    """
    # Extract all registered flags (both --long and -short) from the parser
    known_flags = set()
    for action in parser._actions:
        for opt in action.option_strings:
            known_flags.add(opt)

    for pattern_list, flag_name in [(args.exclude, "--exclude"), (args.include, "--include")]:
        if not pattern_list:
            continue
        for pattern in pattern_list:
            for known_flag in known_flags:
                if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
                    emit(
                        "ERROR_QUOTING",
                        flag=flag_name,
                        pattern=pattern[:120],
                        embedded=known_flag,
                    )
                    sys.exit(1)

This helper protects against a common shell quoting bug where a missing closing quote on glob arguments causes the shell interpreter to absorb adjacent command-line flags into the glob string. It dynamically inspects all registered option strings across parser._actions without requiring hardcoded flag registries. If an embedded flag pattern is found, it reports an ERROR_QUOTING diagnostic and exits immediately.

docs.title: _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides):

Description: Validates reasoning arguments after argument parsing and catalog initialization. Emits error messages and halts the process if invalid per-node override strings were detected, warns if overrides were assigned to nodes not executed in the active mode, and alerts if --thinking-level overrides an explicit --thinking-profile.

Parameters:

  • args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments.
  • invalid_overrides (list[str]): List of malformed NODE=LEVEL strings collected by resolve_thinking_plan.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • SystemExit: Halts execution via sys.exit(1) if invalid_overrides contains any elements.

Example:

_validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides)

def _validate_thinking_args(args, invalid_overrides):
    """Report malformed --thinking-override values (fatal), overrides for nodes the mode never runs,
    and --thinking-level/--thinking-profile conflicts."""
    if invalid_overrides:
        emit("ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE", value=", ".join(invalid_overrides), nodes=", ".join(NODE_KEYS), levels=", ".join(THINKING_LEVELS))
        sys.exit(1)
    mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode
    overrides, _ = parse_overrides(args.thinking_override)
    unused = [node for node in overrides if node not in MODE_NODES[mode]]
    if unused:
        emit("WARN_THINKING_OVERRIDE_UNUSED", nodes=", ".join(unused), mode=mode, active=", ".join(MODE_NODES[mode]))
    if args.thinking_level and args.thinking_profile != "auto":
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_OVERRIDES_PROFILE", level=args.thinking_level, profile=args.thinking_profile)

This validation step reconciles thinking parameters against node execution requirements defined in utils/thinking.py. It verifies that per-node override keys map to active steps within MODE_NODES[mode], emitting warnings for inactive nodes (such as specifying relationship analysis overrides during deterministic API reference generation). It also identifies conflicts between global thinking levels and profiles.

docs.title: _run_cleanup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _run_cleanup():

Description: Deletes persistent cache stores, temporary files, legacy cache manifests, tokenizer calibration files, and application log directories from disk.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
    _run_cleanup()
    return

def _run_cleanup():
    """Clean up cache files and log directory."""
    emit("CLEANUP_START")

    for cache_path in [cache_file, f"{cache_file}.tmp", LEGACY_CACHE_FILE, TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE, f"{TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE}.tmp"]:
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED", path=cache_path)
            except Exception as e:
                emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=cache_path, error=e)

    log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
            emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)

This cleanup utility operates on known cache artifacts—including the primary LLM cache (llm_cache_v2.json), atomic staging files (.tmp), legacy cache files, and the tokenizer calibration registry (llm_token_calibration.json). It also removes the logging directory configured via the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to logs/). File operations are wrapped in defensive try...except blocks to report deletion failures without aborting the cleanup run.

docs.title: _emit_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _emit_usage_summary():

Description: Gathers token metrics, prompt cache statistics, cost estimates, and operational event counts across all invoked LLM providers and pipeline steps, emitting a detailed execution summary.

Parameters:

None. Queries global state within utils.llm_common.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

finally:
    try:
        _emit_usage_summary()
    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Usage summary failed: {e}", dest="LOG")

def _emit_usage_summary():
    """Emit accumulated token usage and estimated cost per provider, then the per-step breakdown."""
    from utils.llm_common import get_step_summary, get_usage_summary
    from utils.token_utils import emit_step_usage, format_cost

    for name, usage in get_usage_summary().items():
        emit(
            "LLM_USAGE_SUMMARY",
            provider=name,
            models=", ".join(usage["models"]) or "-",
            calls=f"{usage['calls']:,}",
            input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
            output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
            thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
            cache_read=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
            cache_write=f"{usage['cache_write']:,}",
            cost=format_cost(usage),
            refusals=usage["refusals"],
            fallbacks=usage["fallbacks"],
            truncations=usage["truncations"],
        )
    steps = get_step_summary()
    if steps:
        emit("LLM_USAGE_STEPS_HEADER")
        for step, usage in steps.items():
            emit_step_usage("LLM_USAGE_STEP", step, usage)

This function formats inference metrics recorded during pipeline execution. It imports aggregators from utils/llm_common.py and utils/token_utils.py, summarizing total input, output, thinking, and prompt-cache read/write tokens per provider. It also reports operational anomalies—such as refusals, model fallbacks, and truncations—alongside a per-step breakdown of token consumption and cost.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive validation patterns to catch configuration problems and missing credentials before executing long-running workflows:

  • Custom CLI Type Validation: The _thinking_level_arg helper converts unrecognized --thinking-level strings into argparse.ArgumentTypeError, triggering standard CLI usage output and halting execution.
  • Shell Quoting Inspection: The _check_quoting_errors function dynamically checks parsed --include and --exclude patterns against registered option flags. If a flag is embedded within a pattern, it emits an ERROR_QUOTING diagnostic and exits with code 1.
  • Reasoning Plan Validation: _validate_thinking_args inspects the results of resolve_thinking_plan. If malformed override tokens are present, it emits an ERROR_THINKING_OVERRIDE listing valid node keys and thinking tiers, exiting with code 1.
  • Preflight Authentication Failure: Prior to file crawling, main() invokes check_llm_auth(). If the provider's API key is missing or the client SDK fails initialization, the program exits with code 1.
  • Flag Incompatibility Checks: Contradictory flag combinations—such as combining --force-rebuild without --incremental, or applying --incremental to modes other than api-reference—are caught and either normalized with warnings or terminated with errors.
  • Resilient Teardown: The core workflow is wrapped in a try...finally block inside main(). This guarantees that _emit_usage_summary() and output.shutdown() execute to flush logs and report token usage even when pipeline nodes raise unhandled exceptions.

  • utils/call_llm.py — Supplies cache file paths (cache_file, LEGACY_CACHE_FILE) and the legacy cache notification hook (notice_legacy_cache).
  • utils/exclude_patterns.py — Supplies DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS to configure file exclusion rules in the shared store.
  • utils/facts.py — Provides facts_path() to locate and clear facts.json during --force-rebuild operations.
  • utils/llm_common.py — Provides usage summary aggregators (get_usage_summary, get_step_summary) used to generate final telemetry reports.
  • utils/llm_config.py — Handles preflight authentication (check_llm_auth), settings resolution (resolve_llm_settings), thinking capability queries (describe_thinking_support), and context window lookup (get_model_context_length).
  • utils/output.py — Central output bus providing localized messaging (emit), raw output (emit_raw), string retrieval (get), logging lifecycle management (configure_logging, shutdown), and missing string translation (translate_missing_strings).
  • utils/thinking.py — Reasoning effort engine providing profile resolution (resolve_profile_name), plan construction (build_thinking_plan), override parsing (parse_overrides), plan description (describe_plan), and node constants (NODE_KEYS, MODE_NODES, THINKING_LEVELS, THINKING_PROFILES).
  • utils/token_utils.py — Provides token ratio diagnostics (describe_token_ratio), step usage emission (emit_step_usage), cost formatting (format_cost), and token calibration file references (TOKEN_CALIBRATION_FILE).

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The nodes.py module defines the concrete computational nodes and lifecycle methods executed within the pocketflow Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) for codebase documentation generation. Acting as the operational heart of the pipeline, it translates high-level documentation goals into staged state transformations across ingestion, architectural discovery, fact extraction, chapter synthesis, and publishing. The module accommodates diverse codebase scales and documentation targets, dynamically routing execution between single-prompt holistic analysis (IdentifyAbstractions), Map-Reduce batching (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions), and deterministic one-to-one module mapping (DeterministicFileMapper, ExtractFacts).

Execution relies on a shared memory dictionary (shared), where each node executes a three-phase lifecycle: prep extracts and formats necessary inputs from shared state, exec executes deterministic parsing or Large Language Model (LLM) inference, and post validates payloads and mutates shared state for downstream consumers. LLM-facing nodes integrate with token counting, budget reservation, thinking profile resolution, and multi-tier caching to guarantee deterministic boundaries. Resilience is enforced via the safe_exec decorator, structured exception handling, and dedicated batch fallback methods (exec_fallback) that maintain graph progression during partial downstream failures.

docs.title: safe_exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def safe_exec(func):

Description: A decorator that wraps a node's exec() implementation with standardized error trapping and diagnostic emission. When an unhandled exception occurs during node execution, safe_exec intercepts the error, emits a UI event (NODE_RETRY_ERROR), logs the complete stack traceback to the destination file logger, and re-raises the exception to let PocketFlow's retry engine manage retry policies.

Parameters:

  • func (Callable): The node exec() method to wrap.

Returns:

  • Callable: The decorated wrapper function.

Raises:

  • Exception: Re-raises any exception encountered during the invocation of func.

Example:

def safe_exec(func):
    """Decorator that wraps Node.exec() with standardized error handling.

    On exception: emits NODE_RETRY_ERROR, logs traceback, and re-raises.
    Eliminates the identical try/except pattern duplicated across all nodes.
    """

    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(self, *args, **kwargs):
        try:
            return func(self, *args, **kwargs)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("NODE_RETRY_ERROR", class_name=self.__class__.__name__, error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            raise

    return wrapper

The decorator intercepts failures originating from LLM network transport, YAML parsing, or invalid model structures across all decorated exec methods. By extracting the class name dynamically via self.__class__.__name__, telemetry events precisely identify the failing node. Logging the traceback directly to dest="LOG" preserves terminal cleanliness while providing comprehensive debugging context on disk.

docs.title: emit_step_subtotals()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def emit_step_subtotals(*steps: str) -> None:

Description: Inspects accumulated LLM resource accounting for specified execution steps and dispatches running subtotal telemetry. Batch nodes invoke this helper during their post() lifecycle to output running cost, token, and invocation totals immediately following batch processing phases.

Parameters:

  • *steps (str): Variable list of string step names (e.g., "extract_facts", "write_chapters") to inspect and report.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

def emit_step_subtotals(*steps: str) -> None:
    """Print the running usage subtotal of each step (batch nodes call this from post())."""
    summary = get_step_summary()
    for step in steps:
        if step in summary:
            emit_step_usage("LLM_STEP_SUBTOTAL", step, summary[step])

This helper connects intermediate batch execution cycles with the central ledger in utils.llm_common. It queries the ledger snapshot via get_step_summary(), matches each requested step identifier against recorded token metrics, and formats user-facing subtotal notifications via emit_step_usage. If an identified step has not recorded any calls, it is safely bypassed without warning.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class DeterministicFileMapper(Node):

Description: A deterministic mapping node used primarily in api-reference mode to map codebase files directly to documentation pages on a 1:1 basis. It requests an LLM file classification pass to filter out non-code assets and build manifests, then establishes an ordered module list sorted hierarchically by directory depth.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Extracts the candidate file listing from shared["files"], filters out whitespace-only files (such as bare __init__.py markers), constructs an index-annotated file listing, and builds a filtering prompt using build_code_file_filter_prompt.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary containing "files", "project_name", and execution flags.

Returns:

  • tuple: A 4-tuple containing (prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens).

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]

        # Empty/whitespace-only files (e.g. bare __init__.py) are left out: post() skips unlisted indices,
        # so they are never documented instead of flipping in and out with the LLM's answer.
        file_listing = "\n".join([f"{i} # {path}" for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data) if content.strip()])

        prompt = build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name, file_listing)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"DeterministicFileMapper prep | {len(files_data)} candidate files for filtering", dest="LOG")
        return prompt, shared.get("use_cache", True), resolve_thinking_level(shared, "filter_files"), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)

The method iterates through shared["files"] and excludes any entries where content.strip() is empty to prevent blank files from appearing inconsistently across LLM calls. It then formats the remaining entries into line-delimited index annotations ({i} # {path}) and constructs the prompt via build_code_file_filter_prompt. Finally, it returns the prompt alongside execution settings retrieved from shared.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Dispatches the classification prompt to the LLM under step "filter_files", parses the YAML response into code files and workspace manifests, and extracts numerical index arrays for both categories.

Parameters:

  • prep_res (tuple): The 4-tuple generated by prep().

Returns:

  • tuple: A 2-tuple (indices, manifest_indices) representing validated code files and package manifest files.

Raises:

  • Exception: Any network, token, or parsing exception raised during call_llm or parse_yaml_response.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens = prep_res
        emit("LLM_CALL_FILTER_FILES")
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="filter_files")
        parsed = parse_yaml_response(response)
        # {code: [...], manifests: [...]}; a bare list (older reply shape) is the code list
        code = parsed.get("code") if isinstance(parsed, dict) else parsed
        manifests = parsed.get("manifests") if isinstance(parsed, dict) else []
        indices = [idx for entry in (code if isinstance(code, list) else []) for idx in parse_file_indices(entry)]
        manifest_indices = [idx for entry in (manifests if isinstance(manifests, list) else []) for idx in parse_file_indices(entry)]
        return indices, manifest_indices

The execution flow delegates model invocation to call_llm with retry-aware caching policies (use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0). The returned YAML payload is evaluated using parse_yaml_response, normalizing both dictionary responses ({"code": [...], "manifests": [...]}) and legacy bare-list formats. Index ranges (e.g., "1-5") are resolved into discrete integer lists using parse_file_indices.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

Description: Validates extracted indices against physical file boundaries, populates shared["manifest_files"], generates 1:1 module descriptors in shared["abstractions"], and sorts shared["chapter_order"] by path depth (deepest subdirectories first, followed by alphabetical order).

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary.
  • prep_res (tuple): The tuple returned from prep().
  • exec_res (tuple): The (indices, manifest_indices) tuple returned from exec().

Returns:

  • str: Fixed action routing string "default".

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

        files = shared.get("files", [])
        code_indices, manifest_indices = exec_res
        valid_indices = set(code_indices)
        # Manifests are read by ExtractFacts (declared package names and path aliases), never documented as pages
        shared["manifest_files"] = sorted(
            {idx for idx in manifest_indices if 0 <= idx < len(files) and idx not in valid_indices and files[idx][1].strip()}
        )
        modules = []
        chapter_order = []

        for idx, (file_path, content) in enumerate(files):
            # Re-check emptiness: the LLM can return an index it was not shown (e.g. a contiguous range)
            if idx not in valid_indices or not content.strip():
                emit("SKIP_NON_CODE_FILE", path=file_path)
                continue

            clean_name = os.path.basename(file_path)
            # Forward slashes everywhere original_path is shown (nav dir labels, index) — the crawler keeps os.sep
            doc_path = file_path.replace(os.sep, "/")

            modules.append({"name": clean_name, "description": f"Internal API reference for `{doc_path}`", "files": [idx], "original_path": doc_path})
            chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

        shared["abstractions"] = modules
        # Sort chapter order by directory depth (deepest first, then alphabetical).
        # This ensures utility/leaf files are processed before orchestration files,
        # so their summaries are available as cross-chapter context.
        # Works universally across all languages (Python, C#, C++, Java, etc.).
        shared["chapter_order"] = sorted(
            chapter_order,
            key=lambda idx: (
                -modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep),
                modules[idx]["original_path"].lower(),
            ),
        )
        shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
        emit("DONE_DETERMINISTIC_MAPPER", count=len(modules))
        return "default"

The post-processing phase separates manifest assets from executable code, ensuring configuration manifests are marked for dependency and package-name inspection in ExtractFacts without producing standalone documentation chapters. Modules are constructed with uniform forward-slash doc paths (doc_path) regardless of host operating system path separators. Sorting chapter ordering by descending directory depth guarantees that leaf utilities are synthesized before high-level orchestrators, providing necessary summary context for cross-module linking.

docs.text:

Signature: class ExtractFacts(BatchNode):

Description: A batch processing node that extracts verified code facts (exported symbols, imports, configuration keys, and error behaviors) for each module. Facts are validated deterministically against the physical source code via utils.facts. Modules whose deterministic facts hash matches facts.json bypass LLM calls entirely.

docs.text:

Description: Defines the maximum number of iterative follow-up query rounds executed per module to extract facts from uncovered declaration-like or import-like source code lines.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Prepares individual batch items for every documented module and manifest file. Computes cryptographic fact hashes over the model signature, prompt template, file path, and source content to determine whether cached claims can be reused from facts.json.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary containing "files", "abstractions", and "manifest_files".

Returns:

  • list[dict]: List of extraction configuration dictionaries.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        template = load_prompt_template("extract_facts", mode="common")
        thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "extract_facts")
        provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
        signature = f"{provider}|{model_name}|{thinking_level or 'default'}|{hashlib.md5(template.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()}"
        self.facts_file = facts_path(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared["project_name"], shared.get("mkdocs", False))
        reuse = shared.get("incremental") or shared.get("use_cache", True)
        previous = load_facts(self.facts_file) if reuse else {}
        self.previous_manifests = load_facts(self.facts_file, section="manifests") if reuse else {}
        self.best = {}  # path → (found, claims) of the best attempt so far, kept when retries do worse
        # ... items compilation for modules and manifests ...
        return items

The method constructs a model-and-template signature using provider settings and MD5 digests. Under --incremental or standard cache configurations, existing facts are deserialized from disk using load_facts(). Each item dictionary receives precomputed facts_hash markers and cached claims when the hash matches previous runs, allowing unchanged files to skip extraction entirely.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, item):

Description: Executes claim extraction for a single batch item. If cached claims exist and no previous completeness follow-up failed, it returns cached records immediately. Otherwise, it queries the LLM, validates raw claims against physical source code lines using verify_file_claims, raises retry errors on low factual coverage, and triggers iterative completeness follow-ups.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): Item configuration dictionary returned by prep().

Returns:

  • dict: Verified extraction payload containing path, facts hash, claims dictionary, and follow-up metrics.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised when verified claims cover less than 50% of claimed facts (when total claims $\ge 4$) before the final retry attempt, signaling hallucinated or paraphrased quotes.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, item):
        if item.get("kind") == "manifest":
            return self._exec_manifest(item)
        if item["cached_claims"] is not None:
            emit("FACTS_CACHE_HIT", name=item["path"])
            followup = item["cached_followup"] if isinstance(item["cached_followup"], dict) else {"status": "none", "asked": []}
            if followup.get("status") != "failed":
                return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": item["cached_claims"], "followup": followup}
            claims, followup, calls = self._follow_up(item, item["cached_claims"], followup.get("asked") or [])
            return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": claims, "followup": followup, "followup_calls": calls}
        prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"], focus_note="")
        emit("LLM_CALL_EXTRACT_FACTS", name=item["path"])
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="extract_facts"
        )
        claims = parse_facts_response(response)
        checked = verify_file_claims(claims, item["content"])
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"FACTS | {item['path']} | claimed={checked['claimed']} | found={checked['found']}", dest="LOG")
        if self.cur_retry == 0:
            self.best.pop(item["path"], None)
        best = self.best.get(item["path"])
        if best is None or checked["found"] > best[0]:
            self.best[item["path"]] = best = (checked["found"], claims)
        # Mostly unfindable quotes mean the model paraphrased: retry uncached, then keep the best attempt's
        # verified part rather than losing the module
        if checked["claimed"] >= 4 and checked["found"] * 2 < checked["claimed"] and self.cur_retry < self.max_retries - 1:
            emit("FACTS_LOW_COVERAGE", name=item["path"], found=checked["found"], claimed=checked["claimed"])
            raise ValueError(f"only {checked['found']}/{checked['claimed']} claims found in the source")
        claims, followup, calls = self._follow_up(item, best[1])
        return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": claims, "followup": followup, "followup_calls": calls}

The method tracks the highest-coverage extraction attempt in self.best across retries. If the ratio of verifiable claims to total claims is low, it forces an uncached retry to correct model hallucinations. Once an acceptable extraction is obtained, it enters _follow_up() to gather claims on any declarations or imports that were missed during the primary pass.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.exec_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):

Description: Fallback handler invoked when all retries for an item are exhausted. Preserves the best partially verified extraction attempt achieved during earlier retries, stripping the facts_hash so subsequent runs re-attempt extraction while allowing the current workflow to proceed.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): The batch work item that failed execution.
  • exc (Exception): The exception that triggered the fallback.

Returns:

  • dict: Fallback fact payload preserving the best available claims or returning None.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):
        """The best earlier attempt if one parsed; else no facts for this module this run (no hash, so the
        next run retries it). The flow goes on either way."""
        emit("WARN_FACTS_FALLBACK", name=item["path"], error=exc)
        if item.get("kind") == "manifest":
            return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": None, "claims": None}
        best = self.best.get(item["path"])
        if best is not None:  # no follow-up ran: the next run asks it
            return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": best[1], "followup": {"status": "failed", "asked": []}}
        return {"path": item["path"], "facts_hash": None, "claims": None}

This method implements fault isolation, preventing a single malformed or paraphrased module from aborting the pipeline. If self.best contains a valid parsing pass from an earlier attempt, those claims are salvaged and tagged with "status": "failed" in the follow-up metadata. If no parsing attempt succeeded, claims evaluate to None, bypassing fact grounding for that file without terminating the run.

docs.title: ExtractFacts.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):

Description: Consolidates manifest and source extractions, performs cross-module symbol and dependency verification via ModuleTable and verify_dependencies, constructs the final facts.json ground truth document, and stores results in shared["module_facts"].

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary.
  • prep_res (list): Original list of prepared work items.
  • exec_res_list (list): List of completed execution payloads.

Returns:

  • str: Fixed routing action "default".

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
        manifest_results = [res for res in exec_res_list if res.get("kind") == "manifest"]
        exec_res_list = [res for res in exec_res_list if res.get("kind") != "manifest"]
        manifest_texts = {item["path"]: item["content"] for item in prep_res if item.get("kind") == "manifest"}
        manifests = {
            res["path"]: {
                **verify_manifest_claims(res["claims"], manifest_texts[res["path"]], res["path"]),
                "facts_hash": res["facts_hash"],
                "claims": res["claims"],
            }
            for res in manifest_results
            if res["claims"] is not None
        }
        contents = {item["path"]: item["content"] for item in prep_res if item.get("kind") != "manifest"}
        checked = {res["path"]: verify_file_claims(res["claims"], contents[res["path"]]) for res in exec_res_list if res["claims"] is not None}
        table = ModuleTable(list(contents), {path: result["symbols"] for path, result in checked.items()}, contents, manifests)
        resolved = verify_dependencies({path: result["dependencies"] for path, result in checked.items()}, contents, table)
        # ... modules dictionary assembly and dependency inversion ...
        save_facts(self.facts_file, build_facts_document(shared["project_name"], source_commit(shared.get("local_dir")), modules, manifests))
        shared["module_facts"] = modules
        # ... telemetry emission ...
        emit_step_subtotals("extract_facts")
        return "default"

The post-processing method splits manifest and module execution payloads, feeding verified symbols and declared package structures into ModuleTable. Import claims undergo resolution against the module table to establish cross-module depends_on links, which are then inverted to populate reciprocal used_by relationships. The resulting ground-truth graph is serialized atomically to disk via save_facts() and made accessible to chapter writers via shared["module_facts"].

docs.title: ContextRouter
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class ContextRouter(Node):

Description: The architectural routing node that inspects codebase size against LLM context boundaries. It calculates prompt template token consumption, directory layout overhead, and source file volumes, routing execution down "deterministic", "direct", or "batch" pipelines.

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Evaluates total file content tokens against calculated safety budgets. In api-reference mode, it short-circuits directly to "deterministic". Otherwise, it scans prompt templates to identify maximum prompt overhead, calculates batch-encoded file tokens, and returns routing decisions.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary containing "files", "mode", and token configurations.

Returns:

  • tuple: 7-tuple containing (route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, count_tokens_func, directory_tree).

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

        shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
        directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)

        if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
            # One chapter per file, one page call each: no routing budget is needed.
            emit("CAPACITY_API_REF_MODE")
            return ("deterministic", files_data, 0, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)

        # --- Calculate prompt overhead FIRST ---
        prompt_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts")
        max_template_tokens = 0
        for subdir in ["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"]:
            for template_name in ["map_abstractions.md", "identify_abstractions.md", "draft_chapters.md"]:
                template_path = os.path.join(prompt_dir, subdir, template_name)
                if os.path.exists(template_path):
                    with open(template_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                        t = count_tokens(f.read())
                    max_template_tokens = max(max_template_tokens, t)
        # ... token counting and capacity checks ...

The preparation phase establishes safe execution boundaries before LLM invocations occur. It computes the worst-case template size across all documentation modes and combines it with directory tree and chapter listing token footprints to determine total prompt overhead. Subtracting this overhead and thinking-effort reserves from max_tokens yields the effective_limit, which is compared against codebase size to select between "direct" and "batch" routing.

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Executes routing decisions. For "direct" or "deterministic" modes, it returns the route identifier directly. For "batch" mode, it partitions source files into cohesive, directory-isolated batches that respect both effective_limit and batch_size.

Parameters:

  • prep_res (tuple): 7-tuple returned by prep().

Returns:

  • str | list[list[tuple]]: Returns route string "direct" or "deterministic", or a nested list of file batches.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, _directory_tree = prep_res
        # ... debug telemetry ...
        if route == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if route == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"

        # Group by directory for coherence, with pre-computed tokens
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

        # Build token-aware batches (never mix directories)
        batches = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
                # Start new batch if adding this file would exceed effective limit or file count cap
                if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                    batches.append(current_batch)
                    current_batch = []
                    current_tokens = 0

                current_batch.append((i, path, content))
                current_tokens += tokens

            if current_batch:
                batches.append(current_batch)
        return batches

Batch generation preserves directory cohesion by ensuring files from different directories are never co-located within the same batch. As it iterates through lexicographically sorted directory groups, it tracks token accumulation using precomputed token maps (file_token_map). If appending a file would violate effective_limit or exceed batch_size, the active batch is finalized and a new batch is initiated.

docs.title: ContextRouter.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

Description: Persists the directory tree to shared["directory_tree"] across all execution paths, stores file batches in shared["file_batches"] when operating in batch mode, and returns the active action transition string.

Parameters:

Example:

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ContextRouter post | route={'batch' if isinstance(exec_res, list) else exec_res}", dest="LOG")
        # Store the directory tree built during prep() for EVERY route: draft_chapters and
        # group_modules prompts read shared["directory_tree"] on direct/deterministic routes too.
        shared["directory_tree"] = prep_res[-1]

            return "direct"
        if exec_res == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"
        shared["file_batches"] = exec_res
        return "batch"

The post-execution phase commits the generated directory tree to the shared store regardless of which route was selected, ensuring downstream chapter drafting templates can access project structure information. For batch workflows, exec_res is saved directly to shared["file_batches"], and the string literal "batch" is returned to trigger PocketFlow's conditional branch operator.

Signature: def exec(self, item):

Description: Constructs the batch mapping prompt, injects file contents and directory context, invokes the LLM, and parses YAML responses into partial abstraction dictionaries with validated file indices.

    def exec(self, item):
        batch_index = item["batch_index"]
        files = item["files"]
        emit("LLM_CALL_MAP_ABSTRACTIONS", batch_index=batch_index, file_count=len(files))

        context = ""
        for i, path, content in files:
            context += f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("map_abstractions", mode=item.get("mode", "tutorial"))
        # ... language formatting and prompt template injection ...
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="map_abstractions"

        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
        # ... validation of abstraction structures and indices ...
        return validated_abstractions

The method formats each file entry with its index and path (--- File Index {i}: {path} ---) to allow the LLM to reference files numerically. The raw LLM response is deserialized via parse_yaml_response(), after which the method iterates through returned items to parse integer file indices via parse_file_index(). Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Constructs the abstraction reduction prompt, queries the LLM to deduplicate and consolidate candidate concepts, and validates the returned YAML against schema boundaries and index constraints.

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        mapped_abstractions, project_name, language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, mode = prep_res

        context = ""
        for i, abs_obj in enumerate(mapped_abstractions):

        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
        # ... validation of abstraction fields and file indices ...
        return validated_abstractions

Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Dispatches crawling operations to crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files based on whether a remote repository URL is configured. Converts the returned file dictionary into an ordered list of (path, content) tuples.

Parameters:

  • prep_res (dict): Crawl configuration dictionary from prep().

Returns:

  • list[tuple[str, str]]: An ordered sequence of relative path and file content tuples.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised when the crawl produces zero matching files.

Example:

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        source = prep_res["repo_url"] or prep_res["local_dir"]
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE EXEC | node=FetchRepo | action=crawl_files | source={source}", dest="LOG")

        if prep_res["repo_url"]:
            emit("CRAWL_REPOSITORY", url=prep_res["repo_url"])
            result = crawl_github_files(
                repo_url=prep_res["repo_url"],
                token=prep_res["token"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )
        else:
            emit("CRAWL_DIRECTORY", path=prep_res["local_dir"])
            result = crawl_local_files(
                directory=prep_res["local_dir"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )

        # Convert dict to list of tuples: [(path, content), ...]
        files_list = list(result.get("files", {}).items())
        if len(files_list) == 0:
            raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")
        return files_list

The crawler traverses the target codebase and filters out binary assets, oversized files, and excluded directories. The resulting path-to-content map is converted into an indexed tuple list [(path, content), ...], establishing fixed integer indexes for every file across the rest of the pipeline. If pattern mismatches or empty directories result in zero files, execution fails fast with a ValueError.

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Concatenates repository source files into a context string bounded by input_token_budget, generates the structural directory tree, and resolves language localization directives.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary.

Returns:

  • tuple: 12-element configuration tuple containing the file context string, directory tree, total file count, and prompt configuration parameters.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]  # Get project name
        language = shared.get("language", "english")  # Get language
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)  # Get use_cache flag, default to True
        max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)  # Get max_abstraction_num, default to 10
        thinking_level = resolve_thinking_level(shared, "identify_abstractions")

        def create_llm_context(files_data):
            max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
            safety_limit = input_token_budget(max_tokens, thinking_level)
            context = ""
            current_tokens = 0
            for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
                entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
                entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)
                if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                    emit("WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED", index=i, path=path, limit=safety_limit)
                    break
                context += entry
                current_tokens += entry_tokens
            return context, current_tokens

        context, context_tokens = create_llm_context(files_data)
        directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)
        # ... return 12-element tuple ...

The method uses the nested helper create_llm_context to pack files sequentially until the token budget is reached. If the codebase exceeds this limit, remaining files are omitted and a WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED warning is emitted. It then builds a directory hierarchy with build_directory_tree and packages all parameters into a 12-element tuple for exec.

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Allocates file token budgets across abstractions using a two-pass algorithm. Pass 1 divides the available prompt budget equally among abstractions, prioritizing the largest files. Pass 2 pools unused tokens and reallocates them to abstractions with remaining unallocated files.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary containing "abstractions", "files", and token limits.

Returns:

  • tuple: 10-element configuration tuple containing the assembled file context, abstraction listing, total abstraction count, and LLM invocation parameters.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

        # Two-pass allocation:
        # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions that need more
        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        included_indices = set()
        abstr_results = []  # list of (included_files, remaining_files, unused_budget)

        for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
            budget = per_abstr_budget
            included_files = []
            remaining_files = []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= budget:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    budget -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions with remaining files
        total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
        if total_unused > 0:
            for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
                # ... reallocate unused tokens ...

The two-pass algorithm prevents large files in early abstractions from consuming the entire token budget. Pass 1 allocates an equal token share (total_budget // num_abstractions) to each abstraction. Pass 2 aggregates any remaining tokens from smaller abstractions and distributes them to abstractions that still have unallocated files, formatting budget-exhausted files as path-only references.

    def prep(self, shared):

        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)

docs.title: OrderChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Requests chapter sequencing from the LLM, parses the returned integer list, and confirms that the sequence contains a complete, non-duplicate permutation of all abstraction indices.

Parameters:

  • prep_res (tuple): 10-element tuple received from prep().

Returns:

  • list[int]: Complete ordered sequence of integer abstraction indices.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if the output is not a list, if indices are duplicated or out of bounds, or if the list length does not match the total number of abstractions.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        # ... unpack prep_res ...
        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("order_chapters", mode=mode)
        # ... call LLM ...
        ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)
        if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
            raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

        ordered_indices = []
        seen_indices = set()
        for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
            # ... parse integers, strip comments, validate bounds ...
            if idx in seen_indices:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
            ordered_indices.append(idx)
            seen_indices.add(idx)

        if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
            raise ValueError(f"Ordered list length ({len(ordered_indices)}) does not match abstractions ({num_abstractions})")
        return ordered_indices

The method validates the parsed sequence to ensure it forms a valid permutation over $[0, \text{num_abstractions}-1]$. It checks for out-of-bounds values, duplicate indices, and missing abstractions, raising a ValueError if any discrepancies are found to trigger a retry.
