  • exec_res (list): Validated list of ordered abstraction indices.

Returns:

  • None.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        shared["chapter_order"] = exec_res  # List of indices

This method commits the resolved index ordering to shared["chapter_order"]. WriteChapters iterates through this sequence to draft documentation chapters, while CombineTutorial uses it to structure site navigation.

docs.title: WriteChapters
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class WriteChapters(BatchNode):

Description: A batch processing node that synthesizes Markdown documentation chapters and accompanying technical summaries. Operates incrementally by verifying file contexts and generation signatures against .doc_cache_manifest.json.

docs.title: WriteChapters.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prep(self, shared):

Description: Generates target chapter filenames, formats the cross-chapter link catalog, attaches verified AST facts (for api-reference mode), computes cache invalidation signatures, and constructs batch work items for each sequenced chapter.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary containing "chapter_order", "abstractions", "files", and configuration flags.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: Complete list of batch execution payloads.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        chapter_order = shared["chapter_order"]
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        files_data = shared["files"]
        # ... generation signature calculation ...
        mode = shared.get("mode", "tutorial")
        provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
        template_digest = hashlib.md5(load_prompt_template("draft_chapters", mode=mode).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        generation_signature = f"{mode}|{language}|{provider}|{model_name}|{thinking_level or 'default'}|{template_digest}"

        self.chapters_written_so_far = []
        self.chapter_summaries = []
        # ... construct all_chapters and chapter_filenames ...
        # ... assemble items_to_process with verified facts and context maps ...
        return items_to_process

The method initializes execution state tracking (chapters_written_so_far, chapter_summaries) and generates a composite generation_signature. In api-reference mode, it maps verified AST facts to their respective modules using build_verified_facts_block(). Each item receives source code snippets for its assigned files via get_content_for_indices(), along with link references for preceding and succeeding chapters.

docs.title: WriteChapters.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, item):

Description: Generates documentation chapters and accompanying technical summaries. Checks incremental cache signatures, provides cross-chapter context via a rolling 50% context window of recent chapter summaries, dispatches generation and summarization prompts, and validates response headings.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): Batch configuration dictionary prepared by prep().

Returns:

  • dict: Chapter payload containing "content", "hash", "name", "cache_key", "filename", and "summary".

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if the generated chapter text is empty.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, item):
        # ... incremental cache check against .doc_cache_manifest.json ...
        # ... assemble rolling previous_chapters_summary up to 50% token budget ...
        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            # ... template variable bindings ...
            previous_chapters_summary=previous_chapters_summary or "This is the first chapter.",
            file_context_str=file_context_str or "No specific code snippets provided for this abstraction.",
            verified_facts=item.get("verified_facts", ""),
        )
        chapter_content = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level, step="write_chapters")
        if not chapter_content.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"Empty chapter response for '{abstraction_name.strip()}'")
        # ... validate and enforce ATX level-1 heading ...
        # ... call LLM for chapter_summary ...
        return {
            "content": chapter_content,
            "hash": current_hash,
            "name": abstraction_name,
            "cache_key": cache_key,
            "filename": filename,
            "summary": summary_entry,
        }

The execution flow begins by checking .doc_cache_manifest.json. If the combined hash of the generation signature, file context, and verified facts matches the manifest, it reads the existing chapter from disk and reuses or regenerates its summary. For cache misses, it builds a context string of recent chapter summaries (capped at 50% of the token context window, dropping older summaries first) and queries the LLM. After ensuring the chapter starts with a valid level-1 ATX heading (# Chapter {N}: {Name}), it calls the LLM with build_chapter_summary_prompt to generate a concise summary for downstream context.

docs.title: WriteChapters.exec_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):

Description: Fallback handler that preserves pipeline execution if a chapter fails generation after all retries are exhausted. Emits placeholder markdown and summary text while omitting the cache hash to ensure the chapter is regenerated on the next run.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): The batch work item that encountered terminal failure.
  • exc (Exception): The exception that triggered the fallback.

Returns:

  • dict: Fallback payload containing placeholder content and hash: None.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def exec_fallback(self, item, exc):
        """Keep the run alive when one chapter still fails after all retries.

        Returns a placeholder page with no manifest hash (regenerated on the next run) and a
        placeholder summary, so chapter_summaries stays aligned with the chapter list.
        """
        name = item["abstraction_details"]["name"]
        chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
        emit("WARN_CHAPTER_FALLBACK", chapter_num=chapter_num, name=name.strip(), error=exc)
        notice = get("UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE")
        summary = f"{get('UI_CHAPTER')} {chapter_num} — {name.strip()}:\n{notice}"
        self.chapter_summaries.append(summary)
        return {"content": f"# {name.strip()}\n\n{notice}\n", "hash": None, "name": name, "summary": summary}

The fallback method ensures that a failure in one chapter does not crash the entire documentation build. It appends a localized placeholder message (UI_CHAPTER_UNAVAILABLE) to self.chapter_summaries to keep summaries aligned with chapter indices, and returns placeholder markdown with hash: None to force a cache miss on future runs.

docs.title: WriteChapters.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):

Description: Commits generated chapter contents to shared["chapters"], builds the pending incremental manifest mapping, stores chapter summaries in shared["chapter_summaries"], and cleans up temporary instance state.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary.
  • prep_res (list): The list of batch work items from prep().
  • exec_res_list (list): List of chapter payload dictionaries returned by exec().

Returns:

  • None.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):

        # exec_res_list contains dicts with content and hashes
        shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

        # MD5 incremental manifest: rebuilt from this run's chapters only, so entries of removed modules
        # (and legacy name keys) drop out. Truncated or placeholder pages have no hash and are left out,
        # so they regenerate on the next run. CombineTutorial.post saves it once the pages are on disk.
        if shared.get("incremental"):
            shared["pending_manifest"] = {
                res.get("cache_key") or res["name"]: {"hash": res["hash"], "summary": res.get("summary", ""), "filename": res.get("filename")}
                for res in exec_res_list
                if res.get("hash") and res.get("name")
            }

        # Save summaries to shared store for CombineTutorial's LLM nav grouping
        shared["chapter_summaries"] = list(self.chapter_summaries)

        # Clean up the temporary instance variables
        del self.chapters_written_so_far
        del self.chapter_summaries
        emit("DONE_ALL_CHAPTERS", count=len(exec_res_list))
        emit_step_subtotals("write_chapters", "chapter_summary")

The post-processing method stores chapter contents in shared["chapters"] and builds the pending incremental cache manifest. Entries with missing hashes (such as truncated or fallback chapters) are excluded from the manifest so they are regenerated on subsequent runs. Finally, it copies chapter summaries to shared["chapter_summaries"] and deletes temporary instance variables to free memory.

Example:

    def prep(self, shared):
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        output_base_dir = shared.get("output_dir", "output")
        output_path = os.path.join(output_base_dir, project_name)

docs.title: CombineTutorial.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def exec(self, prep_res):

Description: Writes final documentation artifacts to disk. Creates target output directories and dispatches file serialization to write_mkdocs_output or write_standalone_output.

Parameters:

  • prep_res (dict): Publication configuration dictionary prepared by prep().

Returns:

  • str: The absolute path to the generated output directory.

Raises:

  • Exception: Any I/O error encountered while writing documentation files.

Example:

    @safe_exec
    def exec(self, prep_res):
        output_path = prep_res["output_path"]
        is_mkdocs = prep_res["is_mkdocs"]
        chapter_files = prep_res["chapter_files"]
        ui = prep_res["ui"]

        emit("COMBINE_WRITING_OUTPUT", path=output_path)
        os.makedirs(output_path, exist_ok=True)

        if is_mkdocs:
            write_mkdocs_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files)
        else:
            write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui)
        return output_path

The method creates the destination output directory on disk and branches based on is_mkdocs. In MkDocs mode, it delegates site generation to write_mkdocs_output(), which handles navigation grouping, static asset creation (mkdocs.yml), and static verification checks via chapter_check.py. In standalone mode, it calls write_standalone_output() to generate individual chapter files alongside aggregated index.md and full_content.md documents.

docs.title: CombineTutorial.post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):

Description: Records the final output directory in shared["final_output_dir"] and atomically commits the pending incremental manifest (.doc_cache_manifest.json) using temporary file renaming.

Parameters:

  • shared (dict): Central shared pipeline dictionary.
  • prep_res (dict): Configuration dictionary from prep().
  • exec_res (str): Output path returned by exec().

Returns:

  • None.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        shared["final_output_dir"] = exec_res  # Store the output path

        # Save the incremental manifest only now that the pages it describes are on disk: saved earlier,
        # an interrupted run left new hashes next to old pages, which later runs served as cache hits.
        manifest = shared.get("pending_manifest")
        if shared.get("incremental") and manifest is not None:
            manifest_path = os.path.join(exec_res, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            tmp_path = f"{manifest_path}.tmp"
            with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)
            os.replace(tmp_path, manifest_path)

        emit("GEN_COMPLETE", path=exec_res)

Saving the incremental manifest is deferred until post() to guarantee that hashes are written only after all documentation files are safely written to disk. Writing to .doc_cache_manifest.json.tmp before performing an atomic os.replace prevents manifest corruption if execution is interrupted, ensuring subsequent runs do not serve outdated cache hits.

docs.title: ExtractFacts._exec_manifest()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _exec_manifest(self, item):

Description: Extracts package metadata, declarations, and path alias mappings from workspace configuration manifests (such as package.json, Cargo.toml, or go.mod).

Parameters:

  • item (dict): Batch item dictionary for a manifest file.

Returns:

  • dict: Manifest claims payload containing kind: "manifest", path, facts_hash, and extracted claims.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if the manifest response contains unparseable YAML items and retries remain.

Example:

    def _exec_manifest(self, item):
        """Declared package names and path aliases of one manifest (prompts/common/extract_manifest.md). A reply
        with items that do not parse is retried uncached; on the last attempt its readable items are kept
        without a facts hash, so the next run asks again."""
        if item["cached_claims"] is not None:
            emit("FACTS_CACHE_HIT", name=item["path"])
            return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": item["facts_hash"], "claims": item["cached_claims"]}
        prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"])
        emit("LLM_CALL_EXTRACT_MANIFEST", name=item["path"])
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
        response = call_llm(
            prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"], step="extract_facts"
        )
        claims = parse_facts_response(response, MANIFEST_KEYS)
        if claims["unparsed"] and self.cur_retry < self.max_retries - 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{claims['unparsed']} manifest items are not valid YAML")
        facts_hash = None if claims["unparsed"] else item["facts_hash"]
        return {"kind": "manifest", "path": item["path"], "facts_hash": facts_hash, "claims": claims}

This helper parses workspace manifests to help resolve external dependencies and path aliases during cross-module analysis. If the LLM generates invalid YAML for some manifest entries, it raises a ValueError to trigger an uncached retry. On the final retry attempt, any successfully parsed items are preserved while setting facts_hash to None, ensuring the manifest is re-evaluated on subsequent runs.

docs.title: ExtractFacts._follow_up()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _follow_up(self, item, claims, asked=()):

Description: Executes targeted follow-up query rounds for source code lines identified as declaration-like or import-like that were missed during the primary extraction pass.

Parameters:

  • item (dict): The active module work item.
  • claims (dict): Claims accumulated so far for the module.
  • asked (tuple | list, optional): Line numbers queried in previous follow-up rounds. Defaults to ().

Returns:

  • tuple: A 3-tuple (claims, followup_metadata, calls_count) where followup_metadata tracks status ("none", "done", or "failed") and the list of queried line numbers.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

    def _follow_up(self, item, claims, asked=()):
        asked, calls, lines = list(asked), 0, split_lines(item["content"])
        for _round in range(self.FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS):
            hints = completeness_hints(item["content"], verify_file_claims(claims, item["content"]), claims)
            already = set(asked)
            pending = [number for number in hints["uncovered"] if number not in already]
            if not pending:
                break
            note = build_facts_focus_note([(number, lines[number - 1]) for number in pending])
            prompt = item["template"].format(project_name=item["project_name"], file_path=item["path"], source=item["content"], focus_note=note)
            emit("FACTS_FOLLOWUP", name=item["path"], count=len(pending))
            log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"])
            answer = None
            for attempt in range(2):
                calls += 1
                try:
                    response = call_llm(
                        prompt,
                        use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0 and attempt == 0),
                        thinking_level=item["thinking_level"],
                        step="extract_facts",
                    )
                    answer = parse_facts_response(response)
                    break
                except Exception as e:
                    emit_raw("WARNING", f"FACTS FOLLOW-UP FAILED | {item['path']} | attempt {attempt + 1} | {e}", dest="LOG")
            if answer is None:
                return claims, {"status": "failed", "asked": asked}, calls
            claims = merge_claims(claims, answer)
            asked += pending[:FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT]
        return claims, {"status": "done" if asked else "none", "asked": asked}, calls

The method runs up to FOLLOWUP_ROUNDS (3) iterations, querying completeness_hints on each round to detect uncovered declaration or import lines. Unexamined lines are formatted into a focused prompt note using build_facts_focus_note (capped at FACTS_FOCUS_LIMIT per request). Each follow-up response is merged into the existing claims via merge_claims(). If a follow-up query fails, the existing claims are retained and the status is marked as "failed" to prompt a re-check on the next incremental run.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements the following error handling and recovery patterns:

  1. Central Execution Shield (safe_exec): All public exec() methods are wrapped with @safe_exec. When an exception occurs, the decorator logs the class name, error message, and full stack traceback to the destination log file (dest="LOG") and emits a NODE_RETRY_ERROR telemetry event before re-raising. This ensures failures are recorded consistently while allowing PocketFlow's retry engine to manage backoff.

  2. Low Factual Coverage Detection: In ExtractFacts.exec(), extractions are verified against the source code via verify_file_claims. If a model returns 4 or more claims but fewer than 50% can be verified against the physical source lines (checked["found"] * 2 < checked["claimed"]), the method emits FACTS_LOW_COVERAGE and raises a ValueError. This triggers an uncached retry to correct paraphrased or hallucinated quotes.

  3. Batch Fault Isolation (exec_fallback): Both ExtractFacts and WriteChapters implement exec_fallback(). When an individual batch item exhausts all retry attempts:

  4. ExtractFacts checks self.best and returns the highest-coverage attempt parsed during earlier retries, or falls back to an empty record with facts_hash: None.

  5. WriteChapters emits WARN_CHAPTER_FALLBACK, appends a placeholder summary to self.chapter_summaries to maintain index alignment, and returns a placeholder chapter with hash: None.

  6. Atomic File Serialization: Incremental cache manifests (.doc_cache_manifest.json) and verified facts documents (facts.json) are serialized using atomic writes. Content is written to a .tmp sibling file before executing os.replace, ensuring abrupt terminations do not leave corrupted JSON files on disk.

  7. Defensive Schema and Index Validation: Every node that parses LLM responses validates the output against expected types and ranges. parse_yaml_response is coupled with type checks (isinstance(..., list), isinstance(..., dict)). File index references are parsed using regular expressions and bounds-checked against [0, len(files)). Out-of-bounds indices are discarded with descriptive warnings (WARN_INVALID_RELATIONSHIP, WARN_PARSE_INDEX), preventing IndexError exceptions during downstream lookups.

docs.title: call_llm.py
docs.text: Source: utils/call_llm.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/call_llm.py module serves as the primary LLM interaction layer and caching facade for the Codebase Knowledge Builder pipeline. It exposes a unified entry point, call_llm(), that routes prompt requests to configured LLM providers—including Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, and generic OpenAI-compatible APIs (such as local Ollama instances). The module handles provider configuration resolution, model sampling constraints, thinking/reasoning effort adjustments, token usage accounting, and cached response persistence.

To optimize operational cost and turnaround time during iterative documentation generation, utils/call_llm.py implements an in-memory singleton cache backed by an atomic file-persisted JSON store (llm_cache_v2.json). Cache keys are calculated using SHA-256 hashes scoping the prompt against the active provider, model name, and thinking level. Responses flagged as truncated or empty are strictly excluded from the cache to prevent persistent serialization of broken generation states.

The module also integrates tightly with pipeline tracking systems. It records pre-call token estimates, intercepts and records provider refusals to short-circuit redundant retries, snapshots ledger usage deltas before and after network operations, and surfaces real-time usage metrics and cost calculations through the unified utils.output console emission system.

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def load_cache():

Description: Loads the disk-based JSON cache into the global singleton _cache. If _cache is already populated in memory, it is returned immediately. If the cache file does not exist, an empty dictionary is initialized. Any decode or file access errors trigger a warning log and reset _cache to an empty dictionary to prevent pipeline crashes.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • dict: In-memory dictionary containing cached SHA-256 hash keys mapped to cached response strings.

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; handles FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, and OSError internally.

Example:

cache = load_cache()
if key in cache:
    cached_response = cache[key]
    emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
    record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens, cache_hit=True)

The function checks the singleton _cache reference, deserializes the JSON cache file from disk on first call, emits a diagnostic message indicating how many items were loaded, and handles missing or corrupt files by falling back to an empty dictionary.

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def save_cache(cache):

Description: Updates the in-memory singleton _cache and commits the dictionary to disk. To prevent cache file corruption if the process is terminated mid-write, the data is dumped into a temporary file (llm_cache_v2.json.tmp) and then atomically moved into place using os.replace.

Parameters:

  • cache (dict): The dictionary of hash keys mapped to response strings to persist.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; catches OSError and TypeError and emits a warning message.

Example:

if use_cache and response_text and not getattr(response_text, "truncated", False):
    cache = load_cache()
    cache[key] = response_text
    save_cache(cache)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

The function assigns the updated cache dictionary back to the global _cache variable, writes the serialized JSON output to a temporary staging file, and performs an atomic rename via os.replace to safeguard existing cache entries against unexpected pipeline termination.

docs.title: notice_legacy_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def notice_legacy_cache() -> None:

Description: Inspects the working directory for the existence of LEGACY_CACHE_FILE (llm_cache.json). If present, it calculates the file size in megabytes and notifies the user via an emitted event, advising that the file is obsolete and consuming unnecessary disk space.

Parameters:

  • None.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; catches OSError if the file cannot be accessed or measured.

Example:

if not check_llm_auth():
    sys.exit(1)
notice_legacy_cache()

test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

The function reads the file size of LEGACY_CACHE_FILE using os.path.getsize(). If successful, it calculates the size in megabytes and triggers the CACHE_LEGACY_FOUND emission event to inform the user of potential disk reclamation.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None, step: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Main entry point for submitting prompt requests across the pipeline. It resolves active provider settings, computes cache keys, verifies prior refusal state, routes calls to provider implementations, calculates usage deltas, and saves valid responses to disk.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The full text prompt to send to the language model.
  • use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to check and write to the local response cache. Defaults to True.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort or budget (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.
  • step (str | None, optional): Node identifier used for usage ledger categorization and reporting. Defaults to None (mapped internally to "other").

Returns:

  • str: The text response returned by the language model. May be an instance of TruncatedResponse if the model terminated due to length constraints.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: If the LLM provider explicitly rejects the request.
  • ValueError: If required environment variables are absent.
  • RuntimeError: If provider APIs return malformed responses.
  • Exception: On network timeouts, connection drops, or HTTP communication errors.

docs.title: Phase 1: Configuration and Cache Lookup
docs.text:
step = step or "other"
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"{'=' * 80}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}", dest="LOG")

    # Check cache if enabled
    key = _cache_key(prompt, provider, model, thinking_level)
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if key in cache:
            cached_response = cache[key]
            emit("CACHE_HIT", chars=f"{len(cached_response):,}")
            record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens, cache_hit=True)
            emit("LLM_CALL_CACHED", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}", dest="LOG")
            emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit", dest="LOG")
            return cached_response
        emit("CACHE_MISS")

The function resolves the provider configuration using resolve_llm_settings(), calculates the prompt token count, and writes trace diagnostics to the debug log. If use_cache is enabled, it generates a hash key via _cache_key() and verifies whether a cached response exists. On a cache hit, it updates token estimates, emits cache hit notifications, logs the response, and returns the cached string immediately without invoking any external API.

docs.title: Phase 2: Refusal Checking
docs.text:
# A request the provider already declined this run is declined again: do not re-send it on
    # node retries (rate limits, billed partial output). The node retry still sees the error.
    refusal_key = request_key(provider, model, thinking_level, prompt)
    refused = previous_refusal(refusal_key)
    if refused is not None:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "LLM CALL END | result=refused_before (not re-sent)", dest="LOG")
        raise refused

Before dispatching an outbound network request, the function generates a request identifier via request_key() and checks if this specific prompt and model configuration previously experienced a non-retryable refusal during this run. If a prior refusal exists in the memory store, it skips making duplicate network calls and immediately raises the stored LLMRefusalError.

docs.title: Phase 3: Provider Execution and Usage Accounting
docs.text:
# Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...", dest="LOG")

    # Usage of this call = ledger delta for the provider: it includes every billed request the call
    # made (Anthropic truncation retry, resend after fallbacks were disabled), even when it raises.
    before = usage_snapshot(provider)
    returned = False
    try:
        with usage_step(step):
            if provider == "GEMINI":
                response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            elif provider == "ANTHROPIC":
                response_text = _call_llm_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            elif provider == "OPENROUTER":
                response_text = _call_llm_openrouter(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
                response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
        returned = True
    except LLMRefusalError as e:
        if not e.retryable:
            remember_refusal(refusal_key, e)
        raise
    finally:
        call_usage = usage_delta(before, usage_snapshot(provider))
        measured = call_usage["calls"] - call_usage["unmeasured_calls"]
        if measured:
            record_estimate(step, prompt_tokens * measured)
            _emit_call_usage(step, prompt_tokens, call_usage, measured)
        elif returned:  # answered, but the provider reported no usage
            emit("LLM_CALL_USAGE_MISSING", step=step, estimate=f"{prompt_tokens:,}")

Execution snapshots the current provider token usage via usage_snapshot() and routes the call to the appropriate internal provider function inside a usage_step(step) context manager. If a non-retryable LLMRefusalError occurs, it registers the error via remember_refusal() before re-raising. In the finally block, the function computes the differential ledger delta using usage_delta(), records prompt estimates, and emits per-call token usage and cost metrics.

docs.title: Phase 4: Cache Write and Finalization
docs.text:
elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}", dest="LOG")

    # Update cache if enabled. Empty and truncated responses (llm_common.TruncatedResponse)
    # are never cached — they would be replayed on every later run.
    if use_cache and response_text and not getattr(response_text, "truncated", False):
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[key] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", "CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache", dest="LOG")

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s", dest="LOG")
    return response_text

After completion of the API call, the elapsed time and response size are logged. If caching is enabled, the response text is non-empty, and the object is not marked as truncated (truncated=False), the new result is persisted to disk via save_cache(). Finally, the raw response string (or TruncatedResponse wrapper) is returned to the caller.

docs.title: _cache
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _cache = None

Description: Module-level cache singleton holding the in-memory representation of llm_cache_v2.json. Initialized to None and populated on the first invocation of load_cache().

docs.title: _cache_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:

Description: Generates an isolated SHA-256 digest string based on the provider, model name, normalized thinking level, and prompt string. This ensures responses cached under one model or reasoning setting are never returned for a different configuration.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The raw prompt input.
  • provider (str): Active provider identifier (e.g., "ANTHROPIC").
  • model (str): Configured model identifier (e.g., "claude-sonnet-5").
  • thinking_level (str | None): Reasoning effort string or None.

Returns:

  • str: Hexadecimal digest string representing the SHA-256 hash.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

def _cache_key(prompt: str, provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The helper formats a scoping string containing the provider, model, and lowercase thinking level (defaulting to "default"), joins it with the prompt separated by a newline, encodes the concatenated string to UTF-8 bytes, and computes the hex digest via hashlib.sha256().

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes calls against generic OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints (such as local Ollama deployments or custom inference servers). It reads endpoint URLs and API keys from environment variables, adjusts reasoning parameters, makes synchronous HTTP requests via requests.post, and parses output choices and token usage.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The prompt string to submit.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: Extracted response text, wrapped in TruncatedResponse if finish_reason == "length".

Raises:

  • ValueError: If LLM_PROVIDER, model, or base URL environment variables are unset, or if invalid JSON is returned.
  • RuntimeError: If the returned JSON response lacks the required 'choices' field.
  • Exception: On network connection failures, request timeouts, or HTTP status error codes.

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment Validation and Setup
docs.text:
# Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    # Read the provider-specific variables
    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")  # API key is optional, default to empty string

    # Validate required variables
    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    # Append the endpoint to the base URL
    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"

The function fetches the active provider name using get_llm_provider(). It constructs dynamic environment variable keys based on that provider name (e.g., OLLAMA_MODEL, OLLAMA_BASE_URL), ensures mandatory configuration values are present in the environment, and normalizes the target endpoint to end in /v1/chat/completions.

docs.title: Phase 2: Payload and Thinking Effort Assembly
docs.text:
# Configure headers and payload based on provider
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    }
    if api_key:  # Only add Authorization header if API key is provided
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        # Ollama reasoning models accept low/medium/high; xhigh/max clamp to high.
        # Some Ollama SDKs / API versions look for `think`, others look for standard `reasoning_effort`
        effort = _clamp_level(thinking_level.lower(), ["low", "medium", "high"]) or "medium"
        payload["think"] = effort
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = effort
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    if rejects_sampling_params(model):
        # Claude Opus 4.7+ / Opus 5.x / Sonnet 5 / Fable reject sampling parameters (400).
        payload.pop("temperature", None)

The HTTP headers and base payload are constructed with a default temperature of 0.7. If the provider is "OLLAMA" and a thinking_level is provided, the value is clamped to "low", "medium", or "high", and applied to both think and reasoning_effort payload fields while setting temperature to 1.0. Models that reject sampling parameters (checked via rejects_sampling_params()) have their temperature field stripped to prevent 400 Bad Request responses.

docs.title: Phase 3: HTTP Dispatch and Response Validation
docs.text:
try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        response.raise_for_status()  # HTTP status first: an HTML 502 page must not look like a JSON bug
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            from utils.output import emit

            emit(
                "WARN_INVALID_JSON",
                status_code=response.status_code,
                preview=response.text[:200].strip(),
            )
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None

        # Defensive check: API may return 200 with error/rate-limit payload missing 'choices'
        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            from utils.output import emit

            emit("WARN_API_NO_CHOICES", detail=str(error_detail))
            raise RuntimeError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

The request is sent using requests.post with a connection timeout of 10 seconds and read timeout of 300 seconds. Status codes are checked immediately using raise_for_status(). The response body is decoded into JSON, raising an explicit ValueError if parsing fails. A defensive check verifies that the returned JSON contains a non-empty choices list; if missing, an error is logged and a RuntimeError is raised.

docs.title: Phase 4: Token Usage Accounting and Output Parsing
docs.text:
usage = response_json.get("usage") or {}
        from utils.llm_common import record_usage
        from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw, observe_prompt_tokens

        prompt_tokens = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
        record_usage(
            provider,
            model,
            input_tokens=prompt_tokens,
            output_tokens=usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0,
            thinking_tokens=(usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0,
            cache_read=(usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens") or 0,
            cost=None,
            measured=bool(usage),
        )
        if usage:
            observe_prompt_tokens(provider, model, count_tokens_raw(prompt), prompt_tokens)
        choice = response_json["choices"][0]
        text = (choice.get("message") or {}).get("content") or ""
        if choice.get("finish_reason") == "length":
            from utils.llm_common import TruncatedResponse

            return TruncatedResponse(text)
        return text
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except Exception:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

Token metrics from the usage block are recorded via record_usage() and benchmarked via observe_prompt_tokens(). The message content is extracted from the first choice object. If the API indicates completion stopped due to max tokens (finish_reason == "length"), the text is returned as a TruncatedResponse object. The function includes structured exception handlers for HTTP, connection, timeout, and request errors, wrapping them in descriptive Exception instances.

def _call_llm_anthropic(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

docs.title: _emit_call_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:

Description: Emits a formatted single-line log detailing token utilization and financial cost for a completed LLM call. Calculates percentage deviation between the estimated input tokens and actual measured billed tokens, and reports input, output, thinking, cached tokens, and total cost.

Parameters:

  • step (str): Name of the executing workflow node.
  • estimate (int): Pre-computed token count estimate.
  • usage (dict): Usage ledger dictionary containing token metrics.
  • measured (int): Count of underlying API requests that reported measured usage.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

def _emit_call_usage(step: str, estimate: int, usage: dict, measured: int) -> None:
    """One console line per LLM call: billed input vs the estimate, output (thinking), cached, cost.
    `measured` = requests with provider-reported usage (the deviation is per measured request)."""
    from utils.output import emit, get
    from utils.token_utils import format_cost

    per_request = usage["input"] / measured
    deviation = f"{(per_request - estimate) / estimate:+.0%}" if estimate else get("CFG_VALUE_UNKNOWN")
    emit(
        "LLM_CALL_USAGE",
        step=step,
        input=f"{usage['input']:,}",
        estimate=f"{estimate:,}",
        deviation=deviation,
        requests=get("LLM_CALL_REQUESTS", count=measured) if measured > 1 else "",
        output=f"{usage['output']:,}",
        thinking=f"{usage['thinking']:,}",
        cached=f"{usage['cache_read']:,}",
        cost=format_cost(usage),
    )

The helper calculates average per-request input token usage by dividing total input tokens by the number of measured requests. It calculates deviation against the initial estimate, formats numeric quantities with comma separators, and triggers the LLM_CALL_USAGE event via emit().

docs.title: Response Cache Dictionary
docs.text:
The structure returned by load_cache() and stored in llm_cache_v2.json.

Field Type Description <sha256_hash> str SHA-256 hash computed across provider, model, thinking level, and prompt, mapping directly to the response string.

Example structure: 

{
  "a3b8f1c849e0...": "Chapter 1: Architecture Overview\n\nThis system consists of..."
}

docs.title: Usage Ledger Dictionary
docs.text:
The dictionary shape passed to _emit_call_usage() and returned by usage_delta().

Field Type Description input int Total billed prompt/input tokens consumed. output int Total billed completion/output tokens consumed. thinking int Tokens generated during model internal reasoning. cache_read int Prompt tokens served from provider-side prompt cache. calls int Total number of HTTP requests issued during this execution block. unmeasured_calls int Number of requests where the provider did not return usage metrics.

docs.title: Generic OpenAI Payload Schema
docs.text:
The dictionary structure built inside _call_llm_provider() and serialized as JSON to /v1/chat/completions.

Field Type Description model str Model identifier string (e.g., "deepseek-r1:14b"). messages list[dict[str, str]] List of chat message objects (e.g., [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]). temperature float Sampling temperature; omitted if rejects_sampling_params() is True. think str Clamped thinking effort level for Ollama models (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). reasoning_effort str Standard OpenAI reasoning effort parameter mirroring think.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/call_llm.py standardizes provider error handling into predictable behavior:

  • Missing Configuration: If LLM_PROVIDER, <provider>_MODEL, or <provider>_BASE_URL are not defined when calling generic providers, a ValueError is raised immediately before issuing network requests.
  • Missing Dependencies: When Anthropic or Gemini providers are invoked without their corresponding SDKs installed (anthropic, google-genai), the module traps ImportError and raises an ImportError with an explicit installation message (pip install -r requirements.txt).
  • Provider Refusals: If an LLM explicitly refuses a prompt (represented by LLMRefusalError), the module catches the error, checks if it is marked as non-retryable, registers it in the refusal cache via remember_refusal(), and re-raises it. Future attempts to dispatch the identical prompt within the same session raise the cached error immediately.
  • Malformed API Responses: In _call_llm_provider(), invalid JSON payloads trigger WARN_INVALID_JSON and raise a ValueError. Responses missing the 'choices' array trigger WARN_API_NO_CHOICES and raise a RuntimeError.
  • Network & HTTP Failures: Network exceptions (requests.exceptions.HTTPError, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout) are caught, enriched with any diagnostic error messages returned by the remote API, and wrapped in descriptive Exception instances.
  • Cache Fault Tolerance: Failures encountered while loading or saving cache files (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, OSError, TypeError) log warnings through emit("WARN_CACHE_LOAD_FAIL") or emit("WARN_CACHE_SAVE_FAIL") rather than aborting execution. Truncated or empty responses are ignored during cache writes.

docs.title: chapter_check.py
docs.text: Source: utils/chapter_check.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/chapter_check.py module is a deterministic, offline static-analysis and verification engine designed to audit generated documentation chapters. Operating entirely without LLM inference, it acts as an automated quality gate that inspects generated Markdown pages against structural, syntactical, factual, and renderer-specific rules before publication. Pages are never mutated; instead, the module performs non-destructive read passes and outputs diagnostic telemetry along with an aggregated JSON report (chapter_check.json).

The verification pipeline operates across three primary layers: 1. Syntactical and Structural Auditing: It parses Markdown text conforming to CommonMark rules to isolate prose, headings, and code fences. It checks for broken relative links (resolving URL escapes, cross-page targets, and anchors), detects malformed or unclosed code blocks, and performs syntax analysis on Mermaid diagram blocks to catch fatal layout errors (unsupported diagram types, invalid code operators like >>, unbalanced quotes, and unescaped brackets in node labels). 2. Renderer Discrepancy Detection: Documentation generators (specifically Python-Markdown under MkDocs) apply stricter parsing rules than standard GitHub CommonMark. Lists without preceding blank lines, improperly indented sublists, tables missing blank line buffers, and code blocks with invalid fence delimiters can render as broken inline text. By injecting non-rendering Unicode private-use markers ( / ) and feeding the rendered HTML through a streaming HTMLParser (_MarkContexts), the module verifies whether structural elements rendered into expected tags (<li>, <th>, <pre>) or degraded into plain text. 3. Deterministic Factual Validation: For API-reference chapters possessing verified code facts (extracted via utils.facts), the module verifies that documented symbols exist in the source, validates declared signatures token-by-token (distinguishing benign embellishments from fatal parameter mismatches), flags fabricated CamelCase type names that appear nowhere in the scanned repository, and ensures the "See Also" section includes verified module dependencies while excluding unrelated files.

docs.title: parse_page()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def parse_page(markdown: str) -> dict:

Description: Parses raw Markdown text according to CommonMark block conventions, isolating fenced code blocks (delimited by matching sequences of three or more backticks or tildes) from prose lines and headings. Line numbers are normalized to 1-based indices. If a fenced block is left open at the end of the file, it is classified as unclosed; its contents are restored to prose, and its opening line is recorded in the unclosed list.

Parameters:

  • markdown (str): The raw Markdown source of the documentation page.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing parsed block entities:
    • "prose": List of (line_number, text) tuples.
    • "blocks": List of code block dicts ({"lang": str, "start": int, "end": int, "text": str}).
    • "headings": List of (line_number, level, text) tuples.
    • "unclosed": List of integer line numbers representing unclosed fences.

Example:

parsed = parse_page(markdown)

The parsing algorithm tracks opening fence character types (` or ~), indentation depth, and length, ensuring that inline code containing triple backticks (e.g. ```mermaid```) within prose is not misinterpreted as a block opener. It scans lines sequentially, tracking heading levels from #{1,6} tokens while ignoring code contents.

docs.title: resolve_link()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_link(page: str, target: str) -> str | None:

Description: Resolves a relative Markdown link target against the current page path, converting it into a normalized site-relative path. It ignores external URI schemes (e.g., https:, mailto:), root-relative paths starting with /, and local page anchor fragments starting with #. Query parameters and anchor hashes are stripped, and URL percent-encoded entities (such as %20) are decoded using urllib.parse.unquote.

Parameters:

  • page (str): The site-relative file path of the page containing the link (e.g., docs/api/core.md).
  • target (str): The raw link target string extracted from Markdown link syntax or an HTML anchor tag.

Returns:

  • str | None: The resolved, normalized POSIX relative path, or None if the target is external, root-relative, or an anchor.

Example:

resolved = resolve_link(page, target)
if resolved is not None and not exists(resolved):
    problems.append({"line": number, "target": target})

The function utilizes posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(page), path) followed by posixpath.normpath to handle relative path navigations such as ../ and ./. Empty target paths evaluate to None.

docs.title: broken_links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def broken_links(page: str, parsed: dict, exists) -> list[dict]:

Description: Audits all links, reference definitions, and inline image targets across the page's prose lines to identify references that point to non-existent local files. Targets are resolved via resolve_link() and tested against a caller-supplied predicate.

Parameters:

  • page (str): The path of the current page relative to the site directory.
  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure returned by parse_page().
  • exists (Callable[[str], bool]): A callable predicate returning True if a site-relative path exists.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of dictionaries for each unresolved link, each containing:
    • "line" (int): 1-based line number of the link.
    • "target" (str): The raw link target string.

Example:

report = {
    "page": page,
    "module": module,
    "broken_links": broken_links(page, parsed, exists),
    "diagram_problems": diagram_problems(parsed),
    "unclosed_fences": [{"line": line} for line in parsed["unclosed"]],
}

The check ignores code blocks and inline code spans by delegating extraction to _links(). Only local relative targets that fail the exists predicate are reported, avoiding false positives on external web links or anchor-only cross-references.

docs.title: mermaid_problems()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def mermaid_problems(source: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Inspects raw Mermaid diagram source code for syntactic flaws that cause Mermaid rendering engines to fail. Frontmatter sections enclosed in --- and comment lines starting with %% are skipped. The validator verifies that the first non-comment line specifies a supported diagram type (e.g., flowchart, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram). For flowchart and graph diagrams, it validates quotation mark balance, detects non-Mermaid arrow operators (such as code assignment operator >>), flags unescaped parentheses inside unquoted square bracket node labels, and checks delimiter balance ([], (), {}).

Parameters:

  • source (str): The text content of a Mermaid fenced code block.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of findings, each containing:
    • "line" (int): 1-based relative line number within the diagram block.
    • "problem" (str): Problem type identifier ("type", "arrow", "quotes", "brackets", or "label").

Example:

problems = mermaid_problems(block["text"])

def mermaid_problems(source: str) -> list[dict]:
    lines = source.split("\n")
    body = [(number, line) for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1) if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("%%")]
    if body and body[0][1].strip() == "---":  # frontmatter (title / config) before the diagram type
        closing = next((i for i, (_n, line) in enumerate(body[1:], start=1) if line.strip() == "---"), None)
        body = body[closing + 1 :] if closing is not None else []
    if not body:
        return []
    first = body[0][1].strip().split()[0].rstrip(":")
    if first not in _MERMAID_TYPES:
        return [{"line": body[0][0], "problem": "type"}]
    if not first.startswith(("flowchart", "graph")):
        return []
    # ...

The validator accommodates multi-line Markdown strings delimited by " and `, skipping bracket and quote parity checks on blocks containing markdown strings to prevent false positives.

docs.title: diagram_problems()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def diagram_problems(parsed: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Locates all fenced code blocks tagged with the mermaid language identifier within a parsed page, invokes mermaid_problems() on each, and maps diagram-relative line numbers back to absolute page line coordinates.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure returned by parse_page().

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of issue records, each containing:
    • "diagram" (int): 1-based index of the Mermaid diagram on the page.
    • "line" (int): 1-based absolute line number within the documentation page.
    • "problem" (str): The specific syntactic problem classification.

Example:

def diagram_problems(parsed: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """``mermaid_problems`` of every ```mermaid block, with the block's number and page line."""
    diagrams = [block for block in parsed["blocks"] if block["lang"] == "mermaid"]
    return [
        {"diagram": number, "line": block["start"] + problem["line"], "problem": problem["problem"]}
        for number, block in enumerate(diagrams, start=1)
        for problem in mermaid_problems(block["text"])
    ]

This function maps relative block coordinates to global page line numbers using block["start"] + problem["line"].

docs.title: markup_problems()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def markup_problems(markdown: str, parsed: dict, render) -> dict:

Description: Identifies subtle formatting flaws where Python-Markdown (or MkDocs' pipeline) renders Markdown content differently than CommonMark specifications. Common discrepancies include loose lists rendered as inline text, flattened nested lists lacking 4-space indentation, accidental list merging, split lists, unrendered tables lacking surrounding blank lines, and swallowed text caused by mismatched code fence closures.

docs.title: Phase 1: Marker Injection
docs.text:
lines = markdown.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("", "").replace("", "").split("\n")
    marks = _intended_marks(lines, parsed["blocks"])
    tagged = list(lines)
    for number, (index, kind, expect) in enumerate(marks):
        mark, line = _MARK.format(number), tagged[index]
        cut = expect["cut"] if kind == "table" else _HARD_BREAK_RE.search(line).start()  # before a hard break's spaces / "\"
        tagged[index] = line[:cut] + mark + line[cut:] if cut >= 0 else line + mark
    contexts = _MarkContexts()

The function normalizes line breaks and sanitizes the source of existing Unicode private-use markers. It invokes _intended_marks() to determine expected CommonMark block types (item, content, table, code, after), formats invisible markers ({i}), and splices them into the lines immediately before trailing hard breaks or table header pipes.

docs.title: Phase 2: HTML Parsing and Context Registration
docs.text:
contexts.feed(render("\n".join(tagged)))
    contexts.close()
    found = contexts.found
    owners = {}  # rendered code block -> [(mark, opener)] of the fenced blocks whose first code line it shows
    for number, (_index, kind, expect) in enumerate(marks):
        if kind == "code" and found.get(number) and found[number]["code"]:
            owners.setdefault(found[number]["code"], []).append((number, expect["opener"]))
    problems = {kind: [] for kind in _MARKUP_KINDS}
    blamed = set()  # fenced blocks already reported

The tagged Markdown string is passed to the renderer callable (render), and the resulting HTML is ingested by a _MarkContexts HTML parser. The parser maps each marker index to its rendered DOM environment (tag names, list depth, item counter, table header presence, or enclosing <pre> block).

docs.title: Phase 3: Structural Discrepancy Detection
docs.text:
for number, (index, kind, expect) in enumerate(marks):
        where = found.get(number)
        if where is None:  # the mark vanished (raw HTML, a comment): nothing to compare
            continue
        if kind != "code" and where["code"]:
            opened = [opener for mark, opener in owners.get(where["code"], []) if mark < number]
            if opened:
                blame(opened[-1])
            run = None
            continue
        # ...

The function correlates intended marker semantics against actual rendered HTML contexts. If an intended list item was not enclosed in an <li> tag or still retains visible list marker characters in its text, it is classified as lists_as_text. Discrepancies in indentation depth are flagged as lists_flattened, unexpected list element transitions as lists_merged, and separated continuation content as lists_split. Consecutive list issues of the same type are aggregated into runs.

Parameters:

  • markdown (str): The raw Markdown text of the page.
  • parsed (dict): The parsed structure returned by parse_page().
  • render (Callable[[str], str]): A compiler function transforming Markdown into HTML (e.g., utils.mkdocs.site_renderer).

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary mapping error categories (_MARKUP_KINDS) to lists of finding dicts:
    • "lists_as_text": list[dict] containing "line" and "items".
    • "lists_flattened": list[dict] containing "line" and "items".
    • "lists_merged": list[dict] containing "line" and "items".
    • "lists_split": list[dict] containing "line".
    • "tables_as_text": list[dict] containing "line".
    • "code_blocks_not_rendered": list[dict] containing "line" and "opener".

Example:

if render:
    report |= markup_problems(markdown, parsed, render)

docs.title: missing_symbols()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def missing_symbols(parsed: dict, symbols: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:

Description: Cross-references verified symbols extracted from the codebase against the documentation page's prose and code blocks (excluding Mermaid diagrams). A symbol is considered missing if its leaf name (the segment following the final period, stripped of leading $) does not appear as an independent word token or verbatim identifier in the page text.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure returned by parse_page().
  • symbols (list[dict]): A collection of verified symbol dictionaries extracted from utils/facts.py.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: Dictionaries representing verified symbols omitted from the page, containing "name", "kind", "parent", and "line".

Example:

def missing_symbols(parsed: dict, symbols: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Verified symbols whose name the page never writes (prose or code), matched like facts.py matches
    names: word tokens, and verbatim for names with punctuation (``valid?``, ``operator==``)."""
    text = _page_text(parsed)
    words = set(re.findall(r"\w+", text)) | {word.lstrip("$") for word in re.findall(r"\$\w+", text)}
    words |= set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*", text))  # an identifier glued to CJK prose: 调用run_flow函数
    missing = []
    for symbol in symbols:
        name = str(symbol.get("name", "")).split(".")[-1].lstrip("$")
        if name and not (name in words or _names_in(text, name)):
            missing.append({k: symbol.get(k) for k in ("name", "kind", "parent", "line")})
    return missing

The function extracts all word tokens, including identifiers adjacent to CJK characters. It evaluates punctuation-heavy symbol names (such as Ruby predicates or C++ operator overloads) using _names_in from utils.facts.

docs.title: signature_issues()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def signature_issues(parsed: dict, source: str, symbols: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:

Description: Compares declared function, method, and constructor signatures in the documentation against verified source declarations. Signatures are identified via labelled code patterns (e.g., **Signature**: \...``) or code blocks directly following bold label lines. If a signature does not match the source text verbatim, it is parsed into tokens and compared against verified candidates: * Embellished: The parameter names, sequence, and modifiers match the source, but additional type annotations or return types were added. * Mismatch: Parameters were added, removed, reordered, or renamed, or default values/variadic indicators were altered.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure returned by parse_page().
  • source (str): The complete source code of the underlying source module.
  • symbols (list[dict]): The verified symbol definitions for the module.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]: A tuple containing (mismatches, embellished).

Example:

mismatches, embellished = signature_issues(parsed, source, symbols)

def signature_issues(parsed: dict, source: str, symbols: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    flat_source = _collapse(source)
    by_name = {}
    for symbol in symbols:
        by_name.setdefault(str(symbol.get("name", "")).split(".")[-1], []).append(_head(str(symbol.get("signature", ""))))
    mismatches, embellished = [], []
    for number, text in _signatures(parsed):
        if _collapse(text).rstrip(":{; ") in flat_source:
            continue
        name = _declared_name(text)
        candidates = by_name.get(name[0]) if name else None
        if not candidates:
            continue
        verdicts = [_compare(_head(text), candidate) for candidate in candidates]
        if "same" in verdicts:
            continue
        if "embellished" in verdicts:
            embellished.append({"line": number, "signature": text})
        else:
            mismatches.append({"line": number, "signature": text, "source": _collapse(candidates[0])[:200]})
    return mismatches, embellished

The function strips decorators, annotations, and comments before comparing parameter token subsequences via _compare(). Verbatim matches bypass token analysis entirely.

docs.title: unknown_type_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def unknown_type_names(parsed: dict, known_words: set) -> list[dict]:

Description: Scans inline code spans within Markdown headings for PascalCase / CamelCase identifiers (e.g., ###FactClaim``) that do not appear in any crawled file in the repository. This detects instances where documentation authors invent formal class or type names for unstructured data shapes (such as raw dictionaries or tuples).

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure returned by parse_page().
  • known_words (set): The set of all word tokens extracted from all crawled source files.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: A list of findings containing "line" and "name".

Example:

def unknown_type_names(parsed: dict, known_words: set) -> list[dict]:
    """Type-like names written as code in headings (``### `FactClaim` ``, ``### Stream result (`StreamResult`)``)
    that occur in no crawled file: the writer named a dict or tuple shape as if it were a declared type. Names
    starting with an acronym count (``LLMConfigTuple``); brand names in heading prose do not."""
    if not known_words:
        return []
    found = []
    for number, _level, text in parsed["headings"]:
        spans = " ".join(match.group(2) for match in _CODE_SPAN_RE.finditer(text))
        names = sorted(set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*", spans)))  # ASCII: a name glued to CJK text still counts
        found.extend({"line": number, "name": word} for word in names if _TYPE_NAME_RE.match(word) and word not in known_words)
    return found

The regular expression _TYPE_NAME_RE targets type-like names (beginning with uppercase letters, containing mixed capitalization or uppercase acronym prefixes) while ignoring normal prose outside inline code spans.

docs.title: see_also_issues()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def see_also_issues(page: str, parsed: dict, module: str, module_by_page: dict, facts: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:

Description: Evaluates cross-references in the page's "See Also" section against verified import dependencies extracted by utils.facts. Links to modules lacking an import relationship in either direction (depends_on or used_by) are flagged as unrelated. Documented dependencies missing from the section are flagged as missing.

Parameters:

  • page (str): The site-relative path of the current documentation page.
  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure returned by parse_page().
  • module (str): The repository-relative path of the source module documented by this page.
  • module_by_page (dict): Mapping of site-relative page paths to their corresponding source module paths.
  • facts (dict): The verified facts dictionary for the module.

Returns:

  • tuple[list, list]: A tuple of (unrelated, missing) lists:
    • unrelated: Records of {"line": int, "module": str} for extraneous links.
    • missing: Records of {"module": str} for omitted dependencies.

Example:

unrelated, missing = see_also_issues(page, parsed, module, module_by_page or {}, facts)

def see_also_issues(page: str, parsed: dict, module: str, module_by_page: dict, facts: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:
    depends = {edge["module"] for edge in facts.get("depends_on", [])} & set(module_by_page.values())  # only documented ones can be linked
    related = depends | set(facts.get("used_by", []))
    linked = {}
    pages = set(module_by_page)
    section = _see_also_section(parsed, pages, page)
    for number, target in _links(section):
        resolved = resolve_link(page, target)
        target_module = module_by_page.get(resolved) if resolved else None
        if target_module and target_module != module:
            linked.setdefault(target_module, number)
    unrelated = [{"line": number, "module": target} for target, number in sorted(linked.items(), key=lambda item: item[1]) if target not in related]
    missing = [{"module": target} for target in sorted(depends - set(linked))]
    return unrelated, missing

The check ignores the deterministic "Used by" line by searching for USED_BY_MARKER within _see_also_section().

docs.title: check_chapter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_chapter( page: str, markdown: str, exists, module: str = "", facts: dict | None = None, source: str = "", known_words=None, module_by_page=None, render=None, ) -> dict:

Description: Executes all validation routines on a single documentation chapter. The check runs unconditionally for syntax and broken links, and conditionally for MkDocs rendering fidelity and factual alignment (when verified facts and source contexts are supplied).

Parameters:

  • page (str): Site-relative path of the chapter file.
  • markdown (str): The raw text of the chapter.
  • exists (Callable[[str], bool]): Path existence validation callable.
  • module (str, optional): Repository path of the documented source file.
  • facts (dict | None, optional): Verified facts dictionary extracted for the module.
  • source (str, optional): Raw source code of the module.
  • known_words (set, optional): Repository-wide identifier token set.
  • module_by_page (dict, optional): Map of documentation paths to source file paths.
  • render (Callable[[str], str] | None, optional): Renderer function for markup verification.

Returns:

  • dict: Aggregated chapter verification report mapping issue types to finding lists.

Example:

report = check_chapter(
    cf["filename"], cf["content"], exists, module, module_facts.get(module), sources.get(module, ""), known_words, module_by_page, render
)
reports.append(report)

    parsed = parse_page(markdown)
    report = {
        "page": page,
        "module": module,
        "broken_links": broken_links(page, parsed, exists),
        "diagram_problems": diagram_problems(parsed),
        "unclosed_fences": [{"line": line} for line in parsed["unclosed"]],
    }
    if render:
        report |= markup_problems(markdown, parsed, render)
    if facts and facts.get("claims") is not None:
        symbols = facts.get("symbols", [])
        mismatches, embellished = signature_issues(parsed, source, symbols)
        unrelated, missing = see_also_issues(page, parsed, module, module_by_page or {}, facts)
        report |= {
            "missing_symbols": missing_symbols(parsed, symbols),
            "signature_mismatches": mismatches,
            "signatures_embellished": embellished,
            "unknown_type_names": unknown_type_names(parsed, known_words or set()),
            "see_also_unrelated": unrelated,
            "see_also_missing_dependencies": missing,
        }
    return report

docs.title: run_chapter_check()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def run_chapter_check(output_path: str, site_dir: str, chapter_files: list, prep_res: dict, standalone: bool = False, render=None) -> dict:

Description: High-level orchestrator that iterates over all generated chapters, executes check_chapter() on each, logs warnings and telemetry via utils.output.emit(), writes the final chapter_check.json report, and returns the aggregate report object.

docs.title: Phase 1: Setup and Target Resolution
docs.text:
module_facts = prep_res.get("module_facts") or {}
    sources = prep_res.get("sources") or {}
    known_words = prep_res.get("known_words") or set()
    pages = {cf["filename"] for cf in chapter_files}
    module_by_page = {cf["filename"]: cf.get("original_path") for cf in chapter_files if cf.get("original_path")}
    generated = {"index.md", "full_content.md", "facts.json"}

    def exists(path):
        if path in pages or path in generated:
            return True
        if standalone and path.endswith(".md"):
            return False
        return os.path.exists(os.path.join(site_dir, *path.split("/")))

Sets up fact dictionaries, token sets, and page maps from prep_res. Defines the local exists() predicate, ensuring that links to newly generated files (index.md, facts.json, etc.) or in-memory chapter pages resolve correctly, while preventing stale markdown files from validating in standalone mode.

docs.title: Phase 2: Per-Chapter Auditing Loop
docs.text:
reports = []
    for cf in chapter_files:
        module = cf.get("original_path") or ""
        report = check_chapter(
            cf["filename"], cf["content"], exists, module, module_facts.get(module), sources.get(module, ""), known_words, module_by_page, render
        )
        reports.append(report)
        for problem in report["broken_links"]:
            emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_BROKEN_LINK", page=cf["filename"], line=problem["line"], target=problem["target"])
        grouped = {}
        for problem in report["diagram_problems"]:
            grouped.setdefault((problem["diagram"], problem["problem"]), []).append(str(problem["line"]))
        for (diagram, problem), lines in grouped.items():  # one warning per diagram and kind, its lines listed
            emit(_DIAGRAM_KEYS[problem], page=cf["filename"], line=", ".join(lines), diagram=diagram)
        for kind in _MARKUP_KINDS:  # one warning per page and kind, its lines listed
            if report.get(kind):
                emit(_MARKUP_KEYS[kind], page=cf["filename"], count=len(report[kind]), lines=_line_list(report[kind]))
        for kind in _FACT_KINDS:
            for item in report.get(kind, []):
                emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_DETAIL", page=cf["filename"], kind=kind, detail=json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False))

Iterates over chapter_files, running check_chapter() on each file. It processes broken links, groups diagram syntax failures by diagram number and kind, aggregates markup errors, and emits structured diagnostic events for fact mismatches.

docs.title: Phase 3: Diagnostic Aggregation and Telemetry
docs.text:
totals = {kind: sum(len(report.get(kind, [])) for report in reports) for kind in _COUNTED}
    totals["diagrams_failing"] = sum(len({problem["diagram"] for problem in report["diagram_problems"]}) for report in reports)
    document = {"pages": len(reports), "totals": totals, "reports": reports}
    report_path = os.path.join(output_path, REPORT_FILENAME)
    with open(report_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(document, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    emit(
        "CHAPTER_CHECK_DONE",
        pages=len(reports),
        path=report_path,
        broken_links=totals["broken_links"],
        diagram_problems=totals["diagrams_failing"],
        unclosed_fences=totals["unclosed_fences"],
    )
    if render:
        emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_MARKUP", **{kind: totals[kind] for kind in _MARKUP_KINDS})
    if any("missing_symbols" in report for report in reports):  # pages with verified facts
        emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_FACTS", **{kind: totals[kind] for kind in _FACT_KINDS})
    return document

Computes grand totals across all counted problem categories, writes the JSON document to disk at report_path, and emits telemetry summaries for overall completion, markup discrepancies, and factual issues.

Parameters:

  • output_path (str): Target directory for chapter_check.json.
  • site_dir (str): Root documentation directory used to resolve links.
  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter dicts containing "filename", "content", and optional "original_path".
  • prep_res (dict): Context dictionary containing module_facts, sources, and known_words.
  • standalone (bool, optional): Whether output is standalone Markdown (skips markup rendering checks). Defaults to False.
  • render (Callable[[str], str] | None, optional): Renderer function for MkDocs compilation checks.

Returns:

  • dict: Complete report document containing "pages", "totals", and individual "reports".

Example:

report_doc = run_chapter_check(output_path, site_dir, chapter_files, prep_res, standalone=False, render=renderer)

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def source_context(files_data: list) -> tuple[dict, set]:

Description: Constructs a normalized source dictionary and extracts repository-wide token sets from raw crawled files. File paths are standardized with POSIX forward slashes, and every alphanumeric word token is extracted into a flat vocabulary set.

Parameters:

  • files_data (list): List of (file_path, file_content) tuples obtained during repository crawling.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, set]: A tuple (sources, known_words) where sources maps POSIX file paths to contents and known_words is a set of all extracted word strings.

Example:

def source_context(files_data: list) -> tuple[dict, set]:
    """``(sources, known_words)`` for ``run_chapter_check``: every crawled file's text by forward-slash path,
    and the identifier tokens of all of them (a type name the page uses must occur somewhere in the code)."""
    sources = {path.replace(os.sep, "/"): content for path, content in files_data}
    known_words = {word for content in sources.values() for word in re.findall(r"\w+", content)}
    return sources, known_words

This helper prepares the factual validation environment, allowing unknown_type_names() to determine whether a documented type name appears anywhere in the target repository.

docs.title: _links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _links(prose: list) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:

Description: Scans prose lines to extract link targets, image destinations, and reference definitions outside inline code spans and HTML comments.

Parameters:

  • prose (list): List of (line_number, text) tuples.

Returns:

  • list[tuple[int, str]]: Unique (line_number, target) tuples in order of appearance.

Example:

def _links(prose: list) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
    found = []
    for number, line in prose:
        text = _HTML_COMMENT_RE.sub("", _CODE_SPAN_RE.sub(lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), line))
        for pattern in (_LINK_RE, _IMAGE_RE, _HTML_HREF_RE):
            found.extend((number, match.group(1)) for match in pattern.finditer(text))
        reference = _REFERENCE_RE.match(text)
        if reference:
            found.append((number, reference.group(1)))
    targets = [(number, target[1:-1] if target.startswith("<") else target) for number, target in found]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(targets))

This helper blanks out inline code spans with equivalent spaces to preserve line offsets, removes HTML comments, and processes angle brackets around targets.

Signature: def _cells(row: str) -> int:

Description: Calculates the number of cells in a Markdown table row by splitting on unescaped pipe characters.

Parameters:

Returns:

Example:

def _cells(row: str) -> int:
    row = row.strip().removeprefix("|")
