docs.title: _cell_cut()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _cell_cut(line: str, start: int) -> int:

Description: Determines the character offset before the first unescaped cell-delimiting pipe in a table header row to safely inject tracking markers.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Raw table line.
  • start (int): Indentation offset.

Returns:

  • int: Character index of the cut position, or -1 if no pipe exists.

Example:

def _cell_cut(line: str, start: int) -> int:
    body = line[start:]
    offset = start + len(body) - len(body.lstrip()) + (1 if body.lstrip().startswith("|") else 0)
    match = _CELL_PIPE_RE.search(line, offset)
    return match.start() if match else -1

docs.title: _html_block_end()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _html_block_end(lines: list[str], index: int, content: str, previous: str) -> int | None:

Description: Calculates the closing line index for CommonMark raw HTML blocks starting at a given line.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): Complete lines of the document.
  • index (int): Current 0-based line index.
  • content (str): Expanded content of the current line.
  • previous (str): Content classification of the preceding line ("text", "blank", etc.).

Returns:

  • int | None: 0-based line index where the HTML block ends, or None if the line does not start an HTML block.

Example:

def _html_block_end(lines: list[str], index: int, content: str, previous: str) -> int | None:
    for start, end in _HTML_RAW_BLOCKS:
        if start.match(content):
            if end.search(content):
                return index + 1
            return next((line + 1 for line in range(index + 1, len(lines)) if end.search(lines[line])), len(lines))
    if _HTML_BLOCK_RE.match(content) or (previous != "text" and _HTML_TAG_LINE_RE.match(content)):
        return next((line for line in range(index + 1, len(lines)) if not lines[line].strip()), len(lines))
    return None

docs.title: _intended_marks()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _intended_marks(lines: list[str], blocks: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[int, str, dict]]:

Description: Analyzes page lines under CommonMark parsing rules to identify where structural tracking markers must be injected. Tracks nesting depth, open list item stacks, blockquotes, code block fences, tables, and continuation paragraphs.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of all lines in the document.
  • blocks (list[dict]): Fenced code blocks identified by parse_page().

Returns:

  • list[tuple[int, str, dict]]: Tuples of (line_index, kind, expectations).

Example:

marks = _intended_marks(lines, parsed["blocks"])

def _intended_marks(lines: list[str], blocks: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[int, str, dict]]:
    fences = {block["start"] - 1: block for block in blocks}
    marks, stack = [], []  # stack: (content column, numbered) of the open list items, outermost first
    previous, after, depth = "blank", None, 0
    index = 0
    while index < len(lines):
        quote = _QUOTE_RE.match(lines[index])
        prefix = quote.group(0) if quote else ""
        if prefix.count(">") != depth:  # a quote starts or ends: its content is read on its own
            depth, stack, previous = prefix.count(">"), [], "blank"
        expanded = lines[index][len(prefix) :].expandtabs(4)
        indent = len(expanded) - len(expanded.lstrip(" "))
        # ...
        index, previous = index + 1, "text"
    return marks

The function manages an internal stack of open list items, tracking indentation levels to distinguish sublists, continuation paragraphs, and indented code blocks.

Description: Constructs a snapshot dictionary of the current HTML parser context for an encountered tracking marker.

    def _context(self, code: int | None = None, marker: bool = False) -> dict:
        tags = [tag for tag, _classes in self.stack]
        lists = [tag for tag in tags if tag in ("ul", "ol")]
        return {
            "li": "li" in tags,
            "depth": len(lists) - 1,
            "number": self.items[-1] if self.items else 0,
            "list": lists[-1] if lists else None,
            "th": "th" in tags,
            "code": code,
            "marker": marker,

docs.title: _MarkContexts.handle_starttag()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public (on private class _MarkContexts)

Signature: def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):

Description: Pushes tags and class attributes onto the stack, updates list item counts, resets text accumulation for block-level elements, and initializes code block capture when encountering <pre> or Mermaid container tags.

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag == "br":
            self.text += "\n"
        if tag in _VOID_TAGS:
            return
        if tag in _BLOCK_TAGS:
            self.text = ""
        classes = (dict(attrs).get("class") or "").split()
        self.stack.append((tag, classes))
        if tag in ("ul", "ol"):
            self.items.append(0)
        elif tag == "li" and self.items:
            self.items[-1] += 1
        if self.code is None and (tag == "pre" or "mermaid-raw" in classes):
            self.blocks += 1
            self.code = (len(self.stack), self._context(self.blocks), [])

Description: Pops matching tags from the stack. When closing a code block, it flushes accumulated code text and maps any enclosed tracking markers to that block's context.

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        depth = next((depth for depth in range(len(self.stack) - 1, -1, -1) if self.stack[depth][0] == tag), None)
        if depth is None:
            return
        if tag in _BLOCK_TAGS:
            self.text = ""
        if self.code and depth < self.code[0]:
            for match in _MARK_RE.finditer("".join(self.code[2])):
                self.found[int(match.group(1))] = self.code[1]
            self.code = None
        for closed, _classes in self.stack[depth:]:
            if closed in ("ul", "ol") and self.items:
                self.items.pop()
        del self.stack[depth:]

Signature: def handle_data(self, data):

Description: Appends character data to the current block or code buffer. Searches text chunks for embedded tracking markers (_MARK_RE) and records their active context snapshots into self.found.

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if self.code:
            self.code[2].append(data)
            return
        for match in _MARK_RE.finditer(data):
            line = (self.text + data[: match.start()]).rsplit("\n", 1)[-1]
            self.found[int(match.group(1))] = self._context(marker=bool(_VISIBLE_MARKER_RE.match(line)))
        self.text += data

Signature: def _is_subsequence(wanted: list[str], have: list[str]) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether the token sequence wanted appears as an ordered subsequence within have.

Parameters:

  • wanted (list[str]): Expected token sequence.
  • have (list[str]): Actual token sequence found.

Returns:

  • bool: True if wanted is an ordered subsequence of have.

Example:

def _is_subsequence(wanted: list[str], have: list[str]) -> bool:
    position = 0
    for word in have:
        if position < len(wanted) and word == wanted[position]:
            position += 1
    return position == len(wanted)

docs.title: _head()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _head(text: str) -> str:

Description: Extracts the declaration head from a code snippet up to the line where parameter parentheses balance and close, stripping decorators and trailing body code.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Raw declaration code.

Returns:

  • str: Truncated declaration head string.

Example:

def _head(text: str) -> str:
    text = _strip_decorators(text)
    name = _declared_name(text)
    start = name[1] if name else text.find("(")
    if start < 0:
        return text.split("\n", 1)[0]
    depth = 0
    for position in range(start, len(text)):
        char = text[position]
        if char in "([":
            depth += 1
        elif char in ")]":
            depth -= 1
            if depth <= 0:
                end = text.find("\n", position)
                return text if end < 0 else text[:end]
    return text

docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _declared_name(text: str) -> tuple[str, int] | None:

Description: Identifies the primary function or method name and the character offset of its opening parenthesis. Handles JS/TS arrow functions, Go receiver syntax, and generic parameters.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Declaration text.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, int] | None: (name, open_paren_offset) or None.

Example:

def _declared_name(text: str) -> tuple[str, int] | None:
    arrow = _ARROW_RE.match(text)
    if arrow:
        return arrow.group(1), text.find("(", arrow.end(1))
    receiver = re.match(r"^\s*func\s*\([^)]*\)", text)
    found = _NAME_BEFORE_PAREN_RE.search(text, receiver.end() if receiver else 0)
    return (found.group(1), found.end() - 1) if found else None

Signature: def _signatures(parsed: dict) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:

Description: Extracts explicit declaration signatures from a parsed page, searching both inline labelled code spans (**Signature**: \...``) and fenced code blocks following bold label lines.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): The parsed page structure returned by parse_page().

Returns:

  • list[tuple[int, str]]: Tuples of (line_number, signature_text).

Example:

def _signatures(parsed: dict) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
    found = []
    prose = dict(parsed["prose"])
    for number, line in parsed["prose"]:
        found.extend((number, match.group(2).strip()) for match in _LABELLED_CODE_RE.finditer(line) if _declaration_shaped(match.group(2)))
    for block in parsed["blocks"]:
        label = prose.get(block["start"] - 1, "").strip()
        if block["lang"] == "mermaid" or not (_BLOCK_LABEL_RE.match(label) and re.search(r"[:\uff1a]", label)):
            continue
        head = _head(block["text"])
        if _declaration_shaped(head):
            found.append((block["start"] + 1, head.strip()))
    return found

docs.title: _compare()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _compare(page_head: str, source_head: str) -> str:

Description: Compares a documented signature head against a source signature head, classifying the comparison as "same", "embellished", or "mismatch".

Parameters:

  • page_head (str): Documented signature head.
  • source_head (str): Ground-truth source signature head.

Returns:

  • str: Comparison verdict ("same", "embellished", or "mismatch").

Example:

def _compare(page_head: str, source_head: str) -> str:
    have, wanted = _PARAM_TOKEN_RE.findall(page_head), _PARAM_TOKEN_RE.findall(source_head)
    if have == wanted:
        return "same"
    page, source = _params(page_head), _params(source_head)
    if page is None or source is None:
        return "embellished" if _is_subsequence(wanted, have) else "mismatch"
    (page_params, _page_closed), (source_params, source_closed) = page, source
    if not source_closed:
        source_params = source_params[:-1]
        if len(page_params) < len(source_params):
            return "mismatch"
        page_params = page_params[: len(source_params)]
    elif len(page_params) != len(source_params):
        return "mismatch"
    if not all(_is_subsequence(want, got) for want, got in zip(source_params, page_params, strict=True)):
        return "mismatch"
    return "embellished" if not source_closed or _is_subsequence(wanted, have) else "mismatch"

docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _see_also_section(parsed: dict, pages: set, page: str) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:

Description: Locates the prose lines belonging to the "See Also" section of an API reference page by scanning top-level ## sections in reverse, excluding automatically generated "Used by" lines.

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict): Parsed page structure.
  • pages (set): Set of known chapter page paths.
  • page (str): Current page path.

Returns:

  • list[tuple[int, str]]: Line tuples (line_number, line_text) of the section.

Example:

def _see_also_section(parsed: dict, pages: set, page: str) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
    starts = [number for number, level, _text in parsed["headings"] if level == 2]
    if not starts:
        return []
    sections = [
        [(number, line) for number, line in parsed["prose"] if start < number < end and USED_BY_MARKER not in line]
        for start, end in zip(starts, [*starts[1:], float("inf")], strict=True)
    ]
    for section in reversed(sections):
        if any(resolve_link(page, target) in pages for _number, target in _links(section)):
            return section
    return sections[-1]

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements a non-terminating, fault-tolerant inspection strategy. Rather than raising exceptions and halting documentation builds, all validation routines catch malformed states and append descriptive records to findings lists:

  • Unclosed Code Fences: When parse_page() encounters an opening backtick or tilde fence that is never closed, it records the opener's line number in unclosed and restores all subsequent lines to prose. This prevents downstream prose and link checkers from silently dropping remainder text.
  • Resilient Link Parsing: Malformed URI escapes in resolve_link() are safely decoded via urllib.parse.unquote. Unresolvable external URIs, protocol schemes, and anchor fragments return None and are skipped without error.
  • HTML Parser Safety: _MarkContexts inherits from Python's standard html.parser.HTMLParser with convert_charrefs=True. Unknown tags and mismatched closing tags are tolerated without raising parse exceptions.
  • Missing Facts Handling: When facts dictionaries are absent or their extraction failed (facts.get("claims") is None), check_chapter() skips factual checks without throwing errors, returning only syntax and link reports.
  • Mermaid Syntax Tolerance: mermaid_problems() ignores empty lines, frontmatter metadata, and comments. Diagram parsing errors are captured as structured issue records rather than propagating runtime failures.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The crawl_github_files.py module provides automated file extraction and directory ingestion capabilities for remote GitHub repositories. It supports two primary ingest workflows: shallow cloning via Git SSH protocol for repository URLs using SSH syntax, and targeted tree traversal over the GitHub REST API (v3) for HTTP/HTTPS repository URLs. The crawler enables surgical repository extraction by allowing callers to target specific commits, branches, and subdirectories while filtering files through inclusion glob patterns, exclusion patterns, file-size ceilings, and repository-level .gitignore rules.

When operating in REST API mode, the module parses the provided GitHub URL, extracts repository identifiers (owner, repo), resolves branch names or Git tree object identifiers (SHAs), and fetches contents iteratively. For directory resources, it inspects directory names and relative paths against exclusion criteria before recursing. For file resources, it evaluates size metadata against max_file_size, selectively uses direct download URLs (download_url) or base64 API payloads, and decodes textual file contents while discarding non-text binary assets. When configured for SSH execution, it clones the repository into a temporary workspace, parses the local .gitignore rules with pathspec, walks the file system, and gathers text content before cleaning up temporary disk allocations.

Diagnostic telemetry and localized console notifications are integrated throughout the traversal lifecycle via utils.output. Ingest operations track processed files, excluded paths, size violations, and non-text decode rejections, generating a consolidated execution summary upon task completion.

docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: 

def crawl_github_files(
    repo_url,
    token=None,
    max_file_size: int = DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE,
    use_relative_paths: bool = False,
    include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None,
    exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None,
)

Description: Crawls files from a designated path in a GitHub repository at a specific branch or commit hash. It determines whether to perform a temporary local clone via Git SSH or to query the GitHub REST API based on the format of repo_url. Traversal filters file entries using include_patterns, exclude_patterns, .gitignore specifications, and max_file_size, decoding all text contents into an in-memory dictionary.

The execution workflow is structured into six sequential phases:

  1. Input Normalization and Pattern Sanitization: Converts string-based inclusion and exclusion patterns into standard sets and determines protocol routing.
  2. SSH Repository Cloning and Local Tree Traversal: Clones SSH repositories to a temporary directory, parses the local .gitignore, and traverses files on disk.
  3. GitHub URL Parsing and Target Ref Resolution: Decomposes HTTPS URLs into repository components and verifies branch names or tree commit SHAs.
  4. Remote .gitignore Retrieval and Rule Parsing: Retrieves the remote .gitignore through the GitHub API and compiles gitwildmatch rules using pathspec.
  5. Recursive REST Directory Traversal and File Fetching: Walks the repository hierarchy remotely, applies directory exclusion filters, validates file sizes, and extracts content.
  6. Summary Telemetry and Return Assembly: Compiles traversal metrics into console events and packages the file contents and crawl metadata into a return dictionary.

docs.title: Phase 1: Input Normalization and Pattern Sanitization
docs.text:
# Convert single pattern to set
    if include_patterns and isinstance(include_patterns, str):
        include_patterns = {include_patterns}
    if exclude_patterns and isinstance(exclude_patterns, str):
        exclude_patterns = {exclude_patterns}

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

    # Detect SSH URL (git@ or .git suffix)
    is_ssh_url = repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git")

Phase 1 normalizes caller arguments to ensure include_patterns and exclude_patterns are represented as sets, enabling uniform membership and iteration logic regardless of whether strings or sets were provided. It establishes the nested filter helper should_include_file, which sequentially applies positive glob matching against file names, negative pattern evaluation against .gitignore specifications, and explicit exclusion patterns against the relative file path. Finally, it checks the syntax of repo_url to select between the SSH execution path and the REST API execution path.

docs.title: Phase 2: SSH Repository Cloning and Local Tree Traversal
docs.text:
if is_ssh_url:
        # Clone repo via SSH to temp dir
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
            emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
            try:
                repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
            except Exception as e:
                emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
                return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

            # Walk directory
            files = {}

            # --- Counters ---
            count_processed = 0
            count_excluded = 0
            count_size_limit = 0
            count_non_text = 0
            skipped_size_list = []
            skipped_non_text_list = []
            entry_num = 0

            # --- Load .gitignore ---
            gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
            gitignore_spec = None
            if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
                try:
                    with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                        gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
                    emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path="repository")
                except Exception:
                    pass

            for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
                # Filter directories
                excluded_dirs = set()
                for d in sorted(dirs):
                    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
                    reason = None
                    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                        reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
                    elif exclude_patterns:
                        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                            dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                                reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                                break

                    if reason:
                        excluded_dirs.add(d)
                        entry_num += 1
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

                for d in dirs.copy():
                    if d in excluded_dirs:
                        dirs.remove(d)

                # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
                dirs.sort()

                for filename in sorted(filenames):
                    abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
                    rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
                    entry_num += 1

                    # Check include/exclude patterns
                    if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                        continue

                    # Check file size
                    try:
                        file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
                    except OSError:
                        continue

                    if file_size > max_file_size:
                        count_size_limit += 1
                        skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = file_size / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    # Read content
                    try:
                        with open(abs_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                            content = f.read()
                        files[rel_path] = content
                        count_processed += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except Exception as e:
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, error=e)
            // ... (summary and return logic follows)

Phase 2 executes when an SSH URL is detected. It provisions an isolated temporary directory via tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() and clones the repository using GitPython's git.Repo.clone_from(). If an exception occurs during cloning, it emits an error event and immediately returns an error structure. When the clone succeeds, it locates and loads .gitignore rules using pathspec, walks the file tree using os.walk(), and dynamically prunes ignored or excluded directories from dirs in-place. For individual files, it verifies pattern inclusion, validates size thresholds against max_file_size, and reads text content using utf-8-sig encoding, capturing UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError exceptions to categorize non-text binary assets.

    parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)

        raise ValueError(f"Invalid GitHub URL: {repo_url}")

    # Extract the basic components
    owner = path_parts[0]
    repo = path_parts[1]

    # Setup for GitHub API
    headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"}
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"token {token}"

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        # ... queries /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches ...
        pass

    def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str):
        # ... queries /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree} ...
        pass

    # Check if URL contains a specific branch/commit
    if len(path_parts) > 3 and path_parts[2] == "tree":

        def join_parts(i):
            return "/".join(path_parts[i:])

        branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)
        branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)

        # Fetching branches was not successful
        if len(branches) == 0:
            return None

        # Check branch name
        relevant_path = join_parts(3)

        # Find a match with relevant path and get the branch name
        filter_gen = (name for name in branch_names if relevant_path.startswith(name))
        ref = next(filter_gen, None)

        # If match is not found, check for is it a tree
        if ref is None:
            tree = path_parts[3]
            ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None

        # If it is neither a tree nor a branch name
        if ref is None:
            emit_raw("ERROR", "The given path does not match with any branch and any tree in the repository.\nPlease verify the path is exists.")
            return None

        # Combine all parts after the ref as the path
        part_index = 5 if "/" in ref else 4
        specific_path = join_parts(part_index) if part_index < len(path_parts) else ""
    else:
        # Don't put the ref param in query
        # and let Github decide default branch
        ref = None
        specific_path = ""

Phase 3 handles HTTPS URLs by parsing the URL path with urllib.parse.urlparse. It ensures at least two path components exist (owner and repo), raising a ValueError if the URL is malformed. If the URL contains /tree/, it determines whether the subsequent path segment matches an active branch name via fetch_branches() or a valid Git tree object SHA via check_tree(). Once the Git reference (ref) is identified, any trailing path segments are assembled into specific_path, defining the subdirectory within the repository where crawling should begin.

Phase 6 compiles traversal metrics from either the REST execution counters or the SSH loop variables. It emits localized summary logs to the user console via emit(), listing total examined items, successfully processed files, and itemized lists of files skipped due to size restrictions or non-text content. It constructs and returns the finalized dictionary containing the in-memory files mapping and traversal metadata in the stats key.

Parameters:

  • repo_url (str): Full URL of the GitHub repository, optionally containing branch, commit, and subdirectory paths (e.g., 'https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/e45a15766746d95f8cfaaa705b0371267bec812e/python/packages/autogen-core/src/autogen_core' or an SSH URL like 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git').
  • token (str | None): GitHub personal access token used for API authentication. Required for private repositories and recommended for public repositories to avoid rate limits. If omitted, defaults to None.
  • max_file_size (int): Maximum file size in bytes to download. Files exceeding this limit are skipped. Defaults to DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE (1,048,576 bytes).
  • use_relative_paths (bool): When True, keys in the returned files dictionary are relative to the subdirectory path specified in the URL rather than repository root. Defaults to False.
  • include_patterns (str | set[str] | None): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns designating files to include (e.g., "*.py" or {"*.md", "*.txt"}). If None, all files are eligible.
  • exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns designating files or directories to exclude. If None, no exclusions are applied.

Returns:

  • dict | None: A dictionary containing extracted file contents under "files" and operational statistics under "stats", or None if branch/tree resolution failed.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if repo_url is an invalid HTTP GitHub URL with fewer than two path segments (owner and repository).
  • Exception: Raised if GitHub API rate limits (HTTP 403 or 429) are encountered when no authentication token is provided.

result = crawl_github_files(
    repo_url,
    token=github_token,
    max_file_size=1 * 1024 * 1024,
    use_relative_paths=True,
    include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"},
)

stats = result["stats"]

docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested inside crawl_github_files)

Signature: 

def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool

Description: Evaluates whether a candidate file should be ingested or skipped based on glob inclusion patterns, .gitignore path specifications, and exclusion patterns. Inclusion patterns check only the file's basename, whereas .gitignore specifications and exclusion patterns evaluate the repository-relative file path.

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The function executes three filtering stages. First, if include_patterns is populated, it tests the basename file_name against each glob with fnmatch.fnmatch. If the file matches (or if no include patterns exist), it consults gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path) if a compiled gitignore rule set was provided. Finally, if the file passes gitignore inspection, it evaluates exclude_patterns against file_path. If any exclude pattern matches, the file is rejected.

Parameters:

  • file_path (str): Relative path of the candidate file within the repository.
  • file_name (str): Basename of the file (e.g., main.py).
  • gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec | None): Compiled PathSpec matcher representing repository .gitignore rules, or None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the file passes all inclusion criteria, is not ignored by gitignore, and does not match any exclusion pattern; otherwise False.

Example:

# Call site inside crawl_github_files (REST path processing):
if not should_include_file(rel_path, item["name"], gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
    continue

docs.title: fetch_branches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested inside crawl_github_files)

Signature: 

def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str)

Description: Dispatches an HTTP GET request to the GitHub REST API to list all branches in the specified repository. Used to determine whether a URL path segment refers to a valid branch name.

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get branches of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.",
                )
            else:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository.",
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()

The function queries https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches. If the GitHub API returns HTTP 403 or 429 and no token was configured, it raises an exception indicating rate limit exhaustion. On HTTP 404, it emits a contextual diagnostic message advising the user on private repository token configuration and returns an empty list. For all other non-200 responses, it emits an error string and returns an empty list; otherwise, it parses and returns the JSON payload containing branch metadata objects.

Parameters:

  • owner (str): Repository owner (organization or user account).
  • repo (str): Repository name.

Returns:

  • list: A list of branch descriptor dictionaries returned by GitHub, or an empty list if retrieval failed.

Raises:

  • Exception: Raised if an API rate limit error (HTTP 403 or 429) occurs without a GitHub token.

Example:

# Call site inside crawl_github_files URL branch resolution:
branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)
branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)

    def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str):

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}"

docs.title: fetch_contents()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested inside crawl_github_files)

Signature: 

def fetch_contents(path)

Description: Recursively retrieves files and directory listings from the GitHub REST API at the specified directory path. Downloads file contents, applies exclusion and gitignore rules, validates file size thresholds, decodes textual payloads, and recurses into child directories.

    def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.",
                )
            elif not path and ref == "main":
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found. Check if the default branch is not 'main'\n"
                    "Try adding branch name to the request i.e. python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo/tree/master",
                )
            else:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    f"Error 404: Path '{path}' not found in repository or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    f"Please verify the token has access to this repository and the path exists.",
                )
            return None

        if response.status_code != 200:
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching {path}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return None

        contents = response.json()

        # Handle both single file and directory responses
        if not isinstance(contents, list):
            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]

            # Calculate relative path if requested
            if use_relative_paths and specific_path:
                # Make sure the path is relative to the specified subdirectory
                if item_path.startswith(specific_path):
                    rel_path = item_path[len(specific_path) :].lstrip("/")
                else:
                    rel_path = item_path
            else:
                rel_path = item_path

            if item["type"] == "file":
                api_counters["entry"] += 1
                entry_num = api_counters["entry"]

                # Check if file should be included based on patterns
                if not should_include_file(rel_path, item["name"], gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    continue

                # Check file size if available
                file_size = item.get("size", 0)
                if file_size > max_file_size:
                    api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                    api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                    size_kb = file_size / 1024
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                    continue

                # For files, get raw content
                if item.get("download_url"):
                    file_url = item["download_url"]
                    file_response = requests.get(file_url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

                    # Final size check in case content-length header is available but differs from metadata
                    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get("content-length", 0))
                    if content_length > max_file_size:
                        api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                        api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = content_length / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    if file_response.status_code == 200:
                        files[rel_path] = file_response.text
                        api_counters["processed"] += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    else:
                        api_counters["non_text"] += 1
                        api_skipped_non_text.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_HTTP_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, status=file_response.status_code)
                else:
                    # Alternative method if download_url is not available
                    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
                    if content_response.status_code == 200:
                        content_data = content_response.json()
                        if content_data.get("encoding") == "base64" and "content" in content_data:
                            # Check size of base64 content before decoding
                            if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size calculation
                                estimated_size = int(len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75)
                                api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                                api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                                size_kb = estimated_size / 1024
                                emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                                continue

                            file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode("utf-8")
                            files[rel_path] = file_content
                            api_counters["processed"] += 1
                            emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                        else:
                            api_counters["non_text"] += 1
                            api_skipped_non_text.append(rel_path)
                            emit("CRAWL_FILE_UNEXPECTED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    else:
                        api_counters["non_text"] += 1
                        api_skipped_non_text.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_HTTP_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, status=content_response.status_code)

            elif item["type"] == "dir":
                # Check if directory should be excluded before recursing
                dir_excluded = False
                dir_reason = None

                if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(rel_path):
                    dir_excluded = True
                    dir_reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")

                if not dir_excluded and exclude_patterns:
                    dir_name = item["name"]  # basename of the directory
                    for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                        dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                        if (
                            fnmatch.fnmatch(item_path, dir_pattern)
                            or fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, dir_pattern)
                            or fnmatch.fnmatch(dir_name, dir_pattern)
                        ):
                            dir_excluded = True
                            dir_reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                            break

                if dir_excluded:
                    api_counters["entry"] += 1
                    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=api_counters["entry"], path=rel_path, reason=dir_reason)
                    continue

                # Only recurse if directory is not excluded
                fetch_contents(item_path)

        return None

The function contacts the GitHub API endpoint /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}. It automatically backs off and sleeps if secondary rate limits or standard limits are hit with a valid token, retrying upon expiration. For each entry in the received directory listing, it computes relative paths according to use_relative_paths. For file nodes, it validates patterns and size constraints, preferring direct raw CDN downloads via download_url, but falling back to base64 decoding of the API payload when download_url is absent. For directory nodes, it checks both gitignore rules and directory-level exclusion globs (stripping trailing /*) before triggering recursive calls to fetch_contents().

Parameters:

  • path (str): Repository-relative subdirectory or file path to query from the GitHub contents API.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates the enclosing scope's files dictionary and api_counters in-place.

Raises:

  • Exception: Raised if an unauthenticated API request encounters an HTTP 403 or 429 rate limit error.

Example:

# Initial invocation inside crawl_github_files:
fetch_contents(specific_path)

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements distinct error-handling strategies depending on whether operations occur over local disk abstractions or remote HTTP network transports:

  • URL Validation: If repo_url is an HTTP URL that fails to yield at least an owner and repository component when split by path delimiters (len(path_parts) < 2), a ValueError is raised immediately.
  • Rate Limit Handling:
    • Unauthenticated Calls: When requests to GitHub REST endpoints return HTTP status 403 or 429 indicating rate limits, an Exception is raised notifying the user that a token must be provided via --token or the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.
    • Authenticated Calls: When rate limits occur with a configured token, fetch_contents() inspects the X-RateLimit-Reset HTTP header, calculates the wait delta until quota replenishment (reset_time - time.time() + 1), logs a warning via emit_raw(), sleeps via time.sleep(), and retries the request recursively.
  • Missing Repositories and Authentication (HTTP 404): When GitHub returns HTTP 404 during branch lookups, tree checks, or content fetching, the module distinguishes between unauthenticated runs (suggesting the repository may be private and requiring a token) and authenticated runs (indicating missing permissions or incorrect branch names like main vs master).
  • SSH Clone Failure: Errors during git.Repo.clone_from() are caught via a generic Exception handler, logged via emit_raw("ERROR", ...), and returned as an error dictionary ({"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}) rather than terminating the process.
  • Encoding and Binary Fallbacks: During both SSH local disk reads and REST API payload decoding, character decoding failures (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) are trapped. The problematic files are categorized as non-text assets, appended to skipped lists, and omitted from the returned files dictionary.
  • Gitignore Ingestion Resilience: Remote and local .gitignore ingestion is wrapped in try...except Exception: pass blocks, ensuring that malformed gitignore files or network errors do not prevent repository crawling.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The crawl_local_files.py module provides deterministic scanning, pattern-based filtering, and text ingestion for local directory hierarchies within the documentation generation pipeline. Serving as the local filesystem counterpart to remote repository scrapers, it normalizes source code trees into an in-memory mapping of relative file paths to string contents. This file abstraction layer enables subsequent static analysis and language model processing stages to evaluate codebases residing on the local filesystem or mounted inside containerized environments without coupling to external version control hosting APIs.

The extraction pipeline is driven by an inline, single-pass directory traversal powered by Python's standard os.walk. To optimize traversal performance on large software repositories, the module incorporates early pruning of excluded subtrees by mutating directory lists in-place before child directories are entered. In addition to glob-based inclusion and exclusion pattern sets evaluated via fnmatch, the module provides comprehensive .gitignore parsing using pathspec.PathSpec configured with the gitwildmatch dialect. It discovers and layers .gitignore definitions hierarchically, parsing root-level rules as well as nested configurations encountered deeper in the filesystem hierarchy. Paths are checked against the relevant directory scope, normalizing directory boundaries and filesystem path separators to maintain consistent matching across operating systems.

The module incorporates defensive text-decoding mechanisms and unified telemetry reporting. Files are read using the utf-8-sig encoding to handle UTF-8 data transparently while stripping optional byte-order marks. Non-text assets, binary files, and corrupted payloads that raise UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError are trapped gracefully, logged to the emission framework, and categorized into summary metrics rather than terminating execution. Throughout execution, progress and filtration events are dispatched through utils.output, ensuring synchronized user interface logging and internationalized reason formatting.

docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def crawl_local_files( directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None, max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True, ):

Description: Recursively scans a local directory hierarchy, dynamically loads and evaluates .gitignore specifications alongside caller-specified glob filters, prunes excluded directories, and ingests all matching text files into a dictionary mapping file paths to their string contents. Execution is broken into distinct phases covering directory validation, hierarchical gitignore loading, in-place subtree pruning, multi-criteria file evaluation, fault-tolerant text reading, and consolidated metrics emission.

docs.title: Phase 1: Directory Validation and Gitignore Initialization
docs.text:
if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")

    files_dict = {}

    # --- Counters ---
    entry_num = 0
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_limit = []
    skipped_non_text = []

    # --- Gitignore specs: {abs_dir_path: pathspec} ---
    gitignore_specs = {}
    root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
    if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
        spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
        if spec:
            gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
            emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

    # Translated reason strings (looked up once)
    reason_excluded = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
    reason_gitignore = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")

The function verifies that the targeted filesystem directory exists via os.path.isdir, raising an immediate ValueError if the path does not resolve to an active directory. It then initializes execution counters, tracking the count of processed, excluded, oversized, and non-text files, along with diagnostic arrays for skipped entries. The root directory is inspected for an immediate .gitignore file; if found, it is compiled into a pathspec.PathSpec object and stored in gitignore_specs keyed by the directory's absolute path. Localized audit reason strings (CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED and CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE) are cached from utils.output.get to eliminate repeated lookup overhead throughout traversal loops.

docs.title: Phase 2: Directory Walk and Nested Gitignore Discovery
docs.text:
# --- Single-pass: walk, filter, and process inline ---
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
        abs_root = os.path.abspath(root)

        # Check for nested .gitignore in current directory (skip root, already loaded)
        if abs_root != os.path.abspath(directory):
            nested_gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
            if os.path.exists(nested_gi):
                spec = _load_gitignore(nested_gi)
                if spec:
                    gitignore_specs[abs_root] = spec

The traversal initiates a single-pass filesystem walk using os.walk(directory). As each subdirectory (root) is visited, its absolute path is resolved. To support multi-tiered Git ignore behaviors common in monorepos or nested submodules, the iterator checks for the presence of a nested .gitignore file within any non-root directory. When detected, the nested rules are parsed via _load_gitignore and appended to gitignore_specs keyed by the absolute path of that specific subdirectory, scoping those patterns to all descendent files and subdirectories.

docs.title: Phase 3: Directory-Level Exclusion and Pruning
docs.text:
# --- Directory filtering ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            abs_d = os.path.join(abs_root, d)
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(abs_d, directory)

            reason = None
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
                reason = reason_gitignore
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = reason_excluded
                        break

            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)

        # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
        dirs.sort()

Directory filtering prunes subtrees before os.walk recurses into them. The subdirectories in dirs are sorted and evaluated against both the accumulated .gitignore specifications (using directory-aware matching with is_dir=True) and caller-defined exclude_patterns. Pattern evaluation strips /* suffixes using removesuffix to test directory path fragments against glob definitions using fnmatch.fnmatch. Excluded directories are added to excluded_dirs, logged via emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED"), and mutated out of the dirs list in place. The remaining surviving subdirectories are sorted in place to guarantee deterministic, reproducible crawling order across different platforms and file systems.

docs.title: Phase 4: File-Level Filtering
docs.text:
# --- File processing (inline, sorted) ---
        for filename in sorted(files):
            filepath = os.path.join(root, filename)
            abs_filepath = os.path.abspath(filepath)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(filepath, directory) if use_relative_paths else filepath
            entry_num += 1

            # Check gitignore (all levels)
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_filepath):
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check exclude patterns
            excluded = False
            if exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        excluded = True
                        break
            if excluded:
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check include patterns
            if include_patterns:
                matched = False
                for pattern in include_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    count_excluded += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                    continue

            # Check size limit
            if max_file_size and os.path.getsize(filepath) > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_limit.append(relpath)
                size_kb = os.path.getsize(filepath) / 1024
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=relpath, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                continue

For each file in the current directory, the method computes absolute and relative paths according to use_relative_paths. The file is passed through a sequence of filtration gates: first against the loaded gitignore_specs using _matches_any_gitignore, then against caller-specified exclude_patterns, followed by positive verification against include_patterns (if provided). If the file fails any gate, telemetry is dispatched (CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE, CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED, or CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED) and the loop advances to the next entry. Finally, if max_file_size is defined and os.path.getsize exceeds this byte threshold, the file is bypassed, appended to skipped_size_limit, and logged with CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT.

docs.title: Phase 5: File Ingestion and Text Decoding
docs.text:
# Try to read as text
            try:
                with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files_dict[relpath] = content
                count_processed += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=relpath, error=e)

Files that pass all filter gates are ingested into memory using open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig"). The UTF-8-SIG encoding standardizes parsing by stripping optional UTF-8 byte order mark (BOM) prefixes while reading standard UTF-8 strings cleanly. If decoding fails due to binary payloads or encoding corruption (UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError), the file is categorized as non-text, recorded in skipped_non_text, and signaled via CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT. Any unforeseen operating system or filesystem I/O exceptions are caught by the generic Exception clause, which logs CRAWL_FILE_ERROR with the error payload without aborting the rest of the crawling loop. Successfully ingested files are placed into files_dict keyed by relpath, and count_processed is incremented.

docs.title: Phase 6: Telemetry and Summary Reporting
docs.text:
# --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_HEADER")
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_TOTAL", count=total_fetched)
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_PROCESSED", count=count_processed)
    if count_excluded > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED", count=count_excluded)
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_SIZE_LIMIT", count=count_size_limit)
        for f in skipped_size_limit:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)
    if count_non_text > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_NON_TEXT", count=count_non_text)
        for f in skipped_non_text:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)

    return {"files": files_dict}

Once os.walk finishes traversing all accessible directories, the method aggregates cumulative metrics reflecting total entries scanned, files processed, exclusions, size limit skips, and unreadable binary files. A structured summary sequence is transmitted to emit(), logging each skipped filename under skipped_size_limit and skipped_non_text for complete visibility. Finally, the function packages the accumulated in-memory dictionary into a standardized container structure ({"files": files_dict}) and returns it to the caller.

Parameters:

  • directory (str): Path to the target local filesystem directory to crawl.
  • include_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob file patterns to explicitly include (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}). Defaults to None.
  • exclude_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob patterns to exclude from traversal (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.pyc"}). Defaults to None.
  • max_file_size (int | None): Maximum allowable file size in bytes. Files exceeding this threshold are skipped. Defaults to None.
  • use_relative_paths (bool): Whether dictionary keys should be relative to directory (True) or preserve absolute paths (False). Defaults to True.

Returns:

  • dict[str, dict[str, str]]: A dictionary with a single "files" key mapping file paths to their string contents.

Raises:

  • ValueError: If directory does not exist or is not a valid filesystem directory.

Example:

    files_data = crawl_local_files(
        "..",
        exclude_patterns={
            "*.pyc",
            "__pycache__/*",
            ".venv/*",
            ".git/*",
            "docs/*",
            "output/*",
        },
    )

docs.title: _load_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path):

Description: Reads a specified .gitignore file from disk and parses its pattern rules into a compiled pathspec.PathSpec object using the gitwildmatch pattern syntax.

def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path):
    """Load a .gitignore file and return a PathSpec, or None on failure."""
    try:
        with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
            return pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Failed to load .gitignore at {gitignore_path}: {e}", dest="LOG")
        return None

The helper attempts to read the target .gitignore file using utf-8-sig encoding, ensuring that leading byte order marks do not corrupt pattern definitions. The extracted lines are passed to pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines configured with the "gitwildmatch" pattern dialect, accurately mirroring native Git pattern semantics. If the file cannot be opened or parsed due to permission restrictions, missing files, or syntax errors, the exception is caught, a warning is dispatched via emit_raw, and the function returns None rather than halting the crawler.

Parameters:

  • gitignore_path (str): Filesystem path to the .gitignore file to load.

Returns:

  • pathspec.PathSpec | None: A compiled PathSpec object if parsing succeeds; otherwise, None.

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised; all runtime errors are trapped internally and logged.

Example:

    root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
    if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
        spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
        if spec:
            gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
            emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

docs.title: _matches_any_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False):

Description: Evaluates whether a given absolute path matches any rule in an active collection of compiled PathSpec instances, scoping evaluations relative to each .gitignore file's parent directory.

def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False):
    """Check if a path matches ANY loaded .gitignore spec.

    Each spec is checked with the path relative to its own .gitignore directory.
    For directories, a trailing '/' is appended for proper gitignore matching.

    Args:
        gitignore_specs: dict of {abs_dir_path: pathspec.PathSpec}
        abs_path: absolute path of the file or directory to check
        is_dir: True if checking a directory
    Returns:
        True if the path matches any gitignore rule
    """
    for gi_dir, spec in gitignore_specs.items():
        rel = os.path.relpath(abs_path, gi_dir)
        # Skip if the path is not under this gitignore's scope
        if rel.startswith(".."):
            continue
        match_path = rel.replace("\\", "/")
        if is_dir:
            match_path = match_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
        if spec.match_file(match_path):
            return True
    return False

The helper iterates through gitignore_specs, which maps absolute directory paths to their respective pathspec.PathSpec instances. For each specification, it computes the relative path from the .gitignore directory (gi_dir) to the target abs_path. If the relative path starts with .., the target file or directory resides outside that .gitignore file's subtree scope and the check is skipped. Windows path separators (\) are converted to standard POSIX slashes (/), and if is_dir is True, a trailing slash (/) is enforced so that directory-only gitignore rules (such as build/) match correctly. If spec.match_file(match_path) resolves to True, the function returns True immediately. If no specifications match after checking all scoped specs, it returns False.

Parameters:

  • gitignore_specs (dict[str, pathspec.PathSpec]): Mapping of absolute directory paths to their corresponding compiled PathSpec rule sets.
  • abs_path (str): Absolute filesystem path of the candidate file or directory to check.
  • is_dir (bool): Flag indicating whether abs_path represents a directory (True) or a file (False). Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • bool: True if abs_path matches any active, in-scope .gitignore rule; False otherwise.

Raises:

  • No exceptions are raised.

Example:

            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
                reason = reason_gitignore

Internal tracking dictionary stored in gitignore_specs within crawl_local_files() to support scoped, hierarchical Git pattern matching.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• ValueError: Raised at the entry point of crawl_local_files() if directory does not point to an existing filesystem directory (if not os.path.isdir(directory)).
  • UnicodeDecodeError / ValueError Trapping: During file ingestion in crawl_local_files(), attempts to decode files via utf-8-sig may fail if the target is a binary file (e.g., compiled shared libraries, images, bytecode). These exceptions are intercepted in a multi-exception except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError): clause, preventing pipeline crashes, incrementing count_non_text, recording the file in skipped_non_text, and emitting CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT.
  • Filesystem I/O Error Interception: Any unanticipated operating system or permission failures encountered while reading files in crawl_local_files() are caught by except Exception as e:. The crawler logs CRAWL_FILE_ERROR with the associated exception object, categorizes the entry as non-text, and proceeds with subsequent files.
  • .gitignore Parsing Fault Tolerance: In _load_gitignore(), file read or parsing exceptions are trapped inside a broad try...except Exception as e: block. Rather than failing the crawl when an unreadable or malformed .gitignore file is encountered, the helper logs a warning via emit_raw to dest="LOG" and returns None, allowing crawling to continue without that specific specification active.

docs.title: exclude_patterns.py
docs.text: Source: utils/exclude_patterns.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/exclude_patterns.py module defines the baseline filtering configuration used across the repository scanning infrastructure of the Codebase Knowledge Builder pipeline. When analyzing large repositories to construct documentation, processing every discovered file leads to severe token bloat, runtime latency, binary decoding failures, and potential security hazards. This module provides a single constant set, DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, which establishes standard file and directory exclusion rules for both local filesystem scans and remote GitHub repository crawls.

The patterns in this module are evaluated using standard Unix shell-style glob matching (fnmatch). They are categorized into two primary structural forms: directory-level rules ending with /*, and file-level matchers targeting specific file extensions or exact filenames. During traversal, directory patterns instruct filesystem walkers to prune entire directory branches before recursing into them, eliminating unnecessary I/O overhead. File-level patterns filter out individual files during iteration, ensuring that non-source assets such as compiled binaries, ephemeral editor swap files, and serialized database dumps are stripped prior to downstream parsing.

In addition to traditional build outputs and multimedia assets, DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS places heavy emphasis on credential security and AI agent isolation. It includes blanket patterns covering cryptographic keys, certificates, SSH key pairs, and environment variable files across arbitrary directory depths, preventing secrets from being transmitted to external Large Language Model (LLM) APIs or recorded in persistent response caches. Furthermore, it comprehensively catalogs configuration and session artifacts from modern AI coding assistants and agentic IDEs, guaranteeing that developer-agent scratchpads and rulesets do not pollute the analyzed codebase knowledge base.

docs.title: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS = {

Description: A module-level constant set containing Unix shell-style glob expressions (fnmatch format) that specify paths, extensions, and directory hierarchies to exclude during repository crawling. Directory rules terminate with /* to signal branch pruning, while file rules match file extensions or exact file basenames.

Parameters:

  • None (module-level constant).

Returns:

  • set[str]: A set of string glob patterns matching ignored files and directories.

Raises:

  • None.

Example:

"""Default file/directory exclusion patterns for the codebase crawler.

These patterns are applied during os.walk() to skip irrelevant files and directories.
Pattern format uses fnmatch glob syntax. Directory patterns end with /*.
"""

DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS = {
    # 1. Media, Data, and Static Assets
    "assets/*",
    "data/*",
    "images/*",
    # ...
}

The sections below document each logical functional domain within DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.

docs.title: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS Pattern Specification
docs.text:
The module exports a single data structure, DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, formatted as a native Python set of string literals. The table below outlines each pattern grouping, its target matching category, and its system objective.

Pattern Group Syntactic Form Matching Domain Pipeline Objective Media and Static Assets assets/*, data/*, *.png, *.pdf, *.zip Binary assets, documents, media Prevents binary decode exceptions and eliminates unneeded token payload costs. Build and Transpilation Outputs dist/*, build/*, target/*, .next/* Generated code and framework bundles Avoids duplicate symbol extraction from compiled or bundled distributions. Environments and Dependencies venv/*, node_modules/*, vendor/* External third-party packages Restricts documentation scope strictly to first-party source code. Security Credentials and Keys */.env, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa* Cryptographic identities and secrets Prevents inadvertent transmission of credentials to LLM endpoints and disk caches. Dependency Lockfiles package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock Serialized dependency state Suppresses massive, redundant dependency graphs from context prompts. Language and Runtime Artifacts __pycache__/*, *.class, *.o, *.so Bytecode, object files, native libraries Ensures crawlers only process human-readable source files. Version Control and OS Artifacts .git/*, .svn/*, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db VCS internals and OS desktop indices Avoids recursing into VCS object databases and ignores platform-specific filesystem noise. IDE Workspaces .vscode/*, .idea/*, *.iml, .project Developer editor configurations Eliminates user-specific IDE settings from analyzed codebase data. AI Agent and Assistant Tooling .cursor/*, .windsurf/*, .clinerules, .copilot/* AI assistant prompts and scratchpads Prevents developer-agent conversation histories and rule sets from biasing documentation.

docs.title: Pattern Syntax and Matching Semantics
docs.text:
The string entries in DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS conform to standard fnmatch wildcard semantics:

  • Directory Subtree Pruning (<dir>/*): Patterns ending with /* denote entire directory subtrees. When a candidate directory matches this pattern, crawling engines truncate recursion into that folder immediately.
  • Universal File Extensions (*.<ext>): Standard glob extensions match candidate filenames across any folder level without regard to directory nesting.
  • Arbitrary Depth Wildcards (*/<pattern>): Patterns prefixed with */ match files or directories located within any subfolder, enabling deep matching for sensitive files such as */.env or */id_rsa.
  • Exact Filenames (<filename>): Specific target names without wildcards match root or basename occurrences directly (e.g., .DS_Store, package-lock.json).

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/facts.py implements a language-agnostic verification engine that validates LLM-extracted claims against actual repository source code. Documentation generation pipelines frequently ingest large language model (LLM) assertions regarding symbols, import dependencies, configuration keys, and error roles. Rather than relying on heavyweight, language-specific abstract syntax tree (AST) parsers that fail on polyglot repositories or non-standard syntax, this module adopts a deterministic textual and lexical verification strategy. A claimed fact is accepted only when its accompanying verbatim source quote can be located within the physical file—either as a single-line collapsed match, a multiline squashed string span, or an in-order identifier token sequence.

The module operates across two distinct execution phases: per-file verification and cross-module resolution. In the per-file phase, verify_file_claims consumes raw claims, instantiates a SourceIndex to locate quotes, calculates 1-based line intervals, determines error roles (raised, caught, or mentioned), and rejects hallucinations with explanatory diagnostic strings. In the cross-module phase, ModuleTable aggregates symbols across all documented files alongside workspace manifest definitions (package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, etc.). It cross-references relative imports, aliased module paths, directory index conventions, and namespace declarations to resolve claimed dependency targets to real physical file paths.

Verified facts are compiled into an immutable JSON document structure conforming to schema version 1 (facts.json). Downstream consumers—including documentation chapter generators and static quality gates like chapter_check.py—use this document to verify code citations, detect missing architectural dependencies, and prevent hallucinated symbols from appearing in published developer guides.

docs.title: split_lines()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def split_lines(content: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Splits source file text into discrete lines strictly across CR (\r), LF (\n), and CRLF (\r\n) boundaries. Trailing empty lines resulting from a final newline delimiter are stripped to align 1-based line indexing with standard text editors and GitHub diff counters.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw text content of a source file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of lines preserving leading and trailing internal whitespace.

Example:

def split_lines(content: str) -> list[str]:
    """Lines as editors and GitHub number them (only CR, LF, CRLF break a line)."""
    lines = _LINE_BREAK_RE.split(content)
    return lines[:-1] if lines and lines[-1] == "" else lines

The function relies on the precompiled regular expression _LINE_BREAK_RE = re.compile(r"\r\n|\r|\n"). Unlike Python's standard str.splitlines(), which splits on additional Unicode boundaries such as form feed (\f), vertical tab (\v), next line (\x85), line separator (\u2028), and paragraph separator (\u2029), split_lines restricts line termination to byte sequences recognized by source control and editors.

docs.title: SourceIndex
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class SourceIndex:

Description: In-memory text normalization and index structure for a single source file. Pre-computes normalized representations (Unicode NFC), whitespace-collapsed lines, squashed text, and word token occurrence maps to perform rapid, multi-strategy quote location.

docs.title: SourceIndex.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def __init__(self, content: str):

Description: Initializes the index by calculating cumulative line offset arrays, squashed string mappings, and an inverted index of token occurrences across lines.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Raw file text.

Example:

    def __init__(self, content: str):
        self.lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
        self.collapsed = [_collapse(line) for line in self.lines]
        # Collapsed lines joined by "\n" (never inside a collapsed line or quote, so no match spans two lines)
        self.collapsed_text = "\n".join(self.collapsed) + "\n"
        self.collapsed_offsets = list(accumulate((len(line) + 1 for line in self.collapsed), initial=0))
        squashed = [_squash(line) for line in self.lines]
        # All lines without whitespace, back to back, with each line's start offset: one str.find per quote
        self.squashed_text = "".join(squashed)
        self.offsets = list(accumulate((len(line) for line in squashed), initial=0))
        self.words = [_words(line) for line in self.lines]
        self.word_sets = [set(words) for words in self.words]
        self.word_lines = defaultdict(list)  # word → lines it occurs on, for the token fallback
        for number, words in enumerate(self.word_sets):
            for word in words:
                self.word_lines[word].append(number)
        self._chains = None  # block_chain(), built on first use

The constructor converts text to Unicode NFC format so that precomposed characters emitted by LLMs match decomposed filesystem bytes. It precomputes two parallel search vectors: collapsed_text (internal whitespace collapsed to single spaces with newline separators) and squashed_text (all whitespace removed). Line offsets are maintained using itertools.accumulate, allowing string offset matches found via str.find to be mapped to 0-based line indices via binary search (bisect_right).

docs.title: SourceIndex.block_chain()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def block_chain(self, line: int) -> tuple:

Description: Returns the enclosing code blocks for a specified line number, ordered from innermost to outermost enclosing scope.

Parameters:

  • line (int): 0-based target line index.

Returns:

  • tuple: Tuple of enclosing block descriptors (indent, text, kind, named).

Example:

    def block_chain(self, line: int) -> tuple:
        """The blocks *line* sits in, innermost first: ``(indent, text, kind, named)`` per enclosing line
        (``_block_chains``)."""
        if self._chains is None:
            self._chains = _block_chains(self.lines)
        return self._chains[line]

Block chains are lazily evaluated on the first invocation and cached in self._chains. The underlying helper _block_chains analyzes indentation levels and block keywords across stripped code lines, ensuring that child functions and class methods resolve their surrounding structural context.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def text(self, first: int, last: int) -> str:

Description: Retrieves the raw source text spanning inclusive 0-based line boundaries first through last.

Parameters:

Returns:

Example:

    def text(self, first: int, last: int) -> str:
