The method slices the pre-split original lines array without string mutation, returning the original formatting and indentation for the requested span.

docs.title: SourceIndex.locate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def locate(self, quote, start: int = 0, end: int | None = None) -> list[tuple[int, int, str]]:

Description: Locates occurrences of an extracted code quote within an optional line range start to end. The search progressively executes three match strategies: exact single-line match, joined multiline squashed match, and in-order rare token fallback.

docs.title: Phase 1: Exact Collapsed Match
docs.text:
end = len(self.lines) if end is None else min(end, len(self.lines))
        collapsed = _collapse(quote)
        if not collapsed or start >= end:
            return []
        exact = []
        pos = self.collapsed_text.find(collapsed, self.collapsed_offsets[start])
        while 0 <= pos < self.collapsed_offsets[end]:
            line = bisect_right(self.collapsed_offsets, pos) - 1
            exact.append((line, line, "exact"))
            pos = self.collapsed_text.find(collapsed, self.collapsed_offsets[line + 1])  # next line: one hit per line
        if exact:
            return exact

The exact search collapses consecutive whitespace inside the search quote and searches self.collapsed_text. Because each collapsed line in the search corpus is separated by \n and _collapse strips all line breaks, an exact match is guaranteed to reside entirely on a single line. The line number is located by binary searching self.collapsed_offsets.

docs.title: Phase 2: Multiline Squashed Match
docs.text:
window = max(_WINDOW, len(split_lines(str(quote))) + 1)
        squashed = _squash(quote)
        joined = []
        pos = self.squashed_text.find(squashed, self.offsets[start])
        while 0 <= pos < self.offsets[end]:
            first = bisect_right(self.offsets, pos) - 1
            last = bisect_right(self.offsets, pos + len(squashed) - 1) - 1
            if last - first < window and last < end:
                joined.append((first, last, "joined"))
            pos = self.squashed_text.find(squashed, pos + 1)
        if joined:
            return list(dict.fromkeys(joined))

If single-line collapsed matching yields no hits, the engine strips all whitespace from both the quote and the file text. This accommodates quotes spanning line wraps, chained function calls, or multiline parameter lists. Matches are accepted only if the span between first and last line does not exceed window (derived from _WINDOW = 8 or the quote's natural line count).

docs.title: Phase 3: Rare Token Fallback Search
docs.text:
words = _words(quote)
        if len(words) < _MIN_TOKEN_QUOTE or any(word not in self.word_lines for word in words):
            return []
        # Only windows around the quote's rarest word can hold all of its words
        rarest = min((self.word_lines[word] for word in words), key=len)
        starts = sorted({i for line in rarest for i in range(max(start, line - window + 1), min(line + 1, end))})
        found = []
        for i in starts:
            if words[0] not in self.word_sets[i]:
                continue
            last = self._words_in_order(words, i, min(i + window, end))
            if last is not None:
                found.append((i, last, "tokens"))
        return found

When squashed matching fails, the method attempts to match identifier tokens in order. This handles cases where an LLM quotes a statement along with a distant keyword (such as prepending import to an item inside a Go parenthesized import block). The rarest token in the quote is identified to constrain candidate window starting positions before executing _words_in_order.

Parameters:

  • quote (Any): The code string or expression to locate.
  • start (int, optional): 0-based lower bound line index. Defaults to 0.
  • end (int | None, optional): 0-based upper bound line index. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • list[tuple[int, int, str]]: Tuples of (first_line, last_line, match_kind) where match_kind is "exact", "joined", or "tokens".

docs.title: SourceIndex.excerpt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def excerpt(self, first: int, last: int, quote) -> tuple[str, bool]:

Description: Extracts a normalized snippet of source code bounded by _EXCERPT (300 characters) surrounding the matched quote within lines first through last.

Parameters:

  • first (int): Starting 0-based line index.
  • last (int): Ending 0-based line index.
  • quote (Any): The target search quote.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool]: A 2-tuple containing the extracted snippet string and a boolean flag indicating whether the text was truncated.

Example:

    def excerpt(self, first: int, last: int, quote) -> tuple[str, bool]:
        """The matched source text, at most ``_EXCERPT`` characters around the quote: ``(text, truncated)``. A
        quote longer than the window keeps its start (a long signature keeps its keyword and name)."""
        text = self.text(first, last).strip()
        if len(text) <= _EXCERPT:
            return text, False
        flat, wanted = _collapse(text), _collapse(quote)
        pos = max(flat.find(wanted), 0)
        start = max(0, min(pos - max(0, (_EXCERPT - len(wanted)) // 2), len(flat) - _EXCERPT))
        return flat[start : start + _EXCERPT], True

The method prevents minified or unusually dense code blocks from bloating stored verification records. If the extracted block exceeds 300 characters, it centers a 300-character window around the matched quote, preserving immediate context while marking truncated = True.

docs.title: verify_file_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verify_file_claims(claims: dict, content: str) -> dict:

Description: Audits LLM-extracted claims for a single source file against its actual text. Verifies symbols, dependencies, configuration items, and error handling constructs, resolving exact 1-based source lines and rejecting ungrounded claims.

docs.title: Phase 1: Initialization and Unparsed Claims Handling
docs.text:
index = SourceIndex(content)
    result = {key: [] for key in CLAIM_KEYS}
    rejected = []
    claimed = 0
    unparsed = claims.get("unparsed", 0) if isinstance(claims, dict) and isinstance(claims.get("unparsed"), int) else 0
    if unparsed:
        claimed += unparsed
        rejected.extend({"kind": "unparsed", "reason": "reply item that is not valid YAML"} for _ in range(unparsed))

    symbols = _claim_list(claims, "symbols")
    claimed += len(symbols)
    kept, symbol_rejects = _verify_symbols(symbols, index)
    result["symbols"] = kept
    rejected += symbol_rejects

The function initializes a SourceIndex and sets up tracking accumulators. Any items flagged as unparsed YAML during upstream LLM parsing are counted toward total claims and registered directly in the rejected list. Claimed symbols are delegated to _verify_symbols for scope-aware resolution.

docs.title: Phase 2: Dependency Claim Location
docs.text:
for item in _claim_list(claims, "dependencies"):
        claimed += 1
        target, evidence = _as_text(item.get("target")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
        matches = index.locate(evidence) if target else []
        if not matches:
            rejected.append({"kind": "dependency", "target": target, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "evidence not in source"})
            continue
        first, last, how = matches[0]
        text, truncated = index.excerpt(first, last, evidence)
        entry = {"target": target, "line": first + 1, **_end(first, last), "evidence": text, "match": how}
        result["dependencies"].append({**entry, "truncated": True} if truncated else entry)

Dependencies are located based on their evidence string. If the evidence cannot be grounded in the source text, the dependency claim is rejected. Accepted claims record 1-based start and end lines alongside the match type.

docs.title: Phase 3: Configuration and Error Verification
docs.text:
for key in ("config", "errors"):
        for item in _claim_list(claims, key):
            claimed += 1
            name, evidence = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
            # A quote that opens a multi-line call (`parser.add_argument(`) also covers the call's lines when the
            # name is not on its own lines (`extended`)
            matches = []
            for first, last, how in index.locate(evidence) if name else []:
                if _names_in(index.text(first, last), name):
                    matches.append((first, last, how, False))
                    continue
                end = _call_span(index, first, last)
                if end > last and _names_in(index.text(first, end), name):
                    matches.append((first, end, how, True))
            if not matches:
                rejected.append({"kind": key, "name": name, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "name/evidence not in source"})
                continue
            # Of several places: the name used in code, then written as a whole string, then only mentioned in
            # prose; the quote's own lines before extended spans; for errors, raising before handling
            roles = {m: _error_role(index, m[0], m[1], name) for m in matches} if key == "errors" else {}
            matches.sort(key=lambda m: (_ROLE_RANK.get(roles.get(m), 0), _name_rank(index.text(m[0], m[1]), name), m[3]))
            first, last, how, extended = matches[0]
            text, truncated = index.excerpt(first, last, evidence)
            if extended and not _names_in(text, name):  # a long call: center the stored text on the name
                text, truncated = index.excerpt(first, last, name)
            entry = {"name": name, "line": first + 1, **_end(first, last), "evidence": text, "match": how}
            if key == "config":
                entry["kind"] = _as_text(item.get("kind")).strip() or "config"
            else:
                entry["role"] = roles[matches[0]]
            result[key].append({**entry, "truncated": True} if truncated else entry)

Configuration items and errors undergo call-span expansion via _call_span if the item name appears within an unclosed bracket expression (such as add_argument(...)). Candidate matches are ranked by code occurrence priority, string literal priority, and error handling role (raising takes precedence over handling, which takes precedence over mention).

docs.title: Phase 4: Span Deduplication and Summary
docs.text:
# One fact quoted twice (a whole signature and its first line, an import and its block) is kept once; a
    # config key or error found both on a call's line and inside its extended span keeps the narrower place
    for key, fields in (("symbols", ("parent", "name")), ("dependencies", ("target",)), ("config", ("name",)), ("errors", ("name",))):
        seen, unique = set(), []
        for entry in result[key]:
            marker = (*(entry.get(field) for field in fields), entry["line"])
            if marker not in seen:
                seen.add(marker)
                unique.append(entry)
        if key in ("config", "errors"):
            narrow_first = sorted(unique, key=lambda e: e.get("end_line", e["line"]) - e["line"])
            kept_spans = []
            for entry in narrow_first:
                low, high = entry["line"], entry.get("end_line", entry["line"])
                if not any(other["name"] == entry["name"] and low <= other["line"] <= high for other in kept_spans):
                    kept_spans.append(entry)
            unique = [entry for entry in unique if any(entry is other for other in kept_spans)]
        claimed -= len(result[key]) - len(unique)
        result[key] = unique
    result["rejected"] = rejected
    result["claimed"] = claimed
    result["found"] = claimed - len(rejected)
    return result

The final phase removes duplicate claims where multiple quotes overlap the same identity fields and line coordinates. For configuration keys and errors, if both an extended call span and an exact inner line are captured, the narrower span is preserved.

Parameters:

  • claims (dict): Raw claims dictionary extracted by the LLM.
  • content (str): File source text.

Returns:

  • dict: Verified results dictionary containing symbols, dependencies, config, errors, rejected, claimed, and found.

docs.title: code_view()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def code_view(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:

Description: Strips block comments, inline comments, and multiline docstrings while preserving line counts and line indices. Replaces non-code tokens with blank spaces or empty strings so that language-agnostic heuristics are not confused by prose or commented-out declarations.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of original source lines.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of lines where comments and block strings are blanked out.

Example:

def code_view(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    last = {}  # closer → (line, column) of its last occurrence
    for closer in set(_BLOCK_CLOSERS.values()):
        for number in range(len(lines) - 1, -1, -1):
            column = _rfind_closer(lines[number], closer)
            if column >= 0:
                last[closer] = (number, column)
                break
    view, closing = [], None
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        out, position = "", 0
        if closing:
            end = _find_closer(line, closing, 0)
            if end < 0:
                view.append("")
                continue
            position, closing = end + len(closing), None
        elif line.lstrip().startswith(("#", "//")):
            view.append(line)
            continue
        # ... token scanning loop replaces comments and docstrings with whitespace ...
        view.append(out.rstrip())
    return view

The function handles Python triple quotes (""", '''), C-style block comments (/* ... */), and single-line comment markers (#, //, --). Lines beginning with preprocessor directives such as #include are preserved. Block strings are replaced with empty string literals ("") so variable assignments retain valid syntax.

docs.title: declaration_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def declaration_like(line: str) -> bool:

Description: Heuristic evaluation determining whether a source line represents an exportable symbol declaration (function, class, struct, interface, constant, or macro) across multiple programming languages.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Single line of code to analyze.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the line matches structural declaration patterns.

Example:

def declaration_like(line: str) -> bool:
    """Whether a source line looks like a declaration a reader would look up (language-agnostic hint)."""
    stripped = line.strip()
    if not stripped:
        return False
    if stripped.startswith("#"):
        return stripped.startswith(("#define ", "#macro "))
    if not (stripped[0].isalpha() or stripped[0] in "_@$"):  # comments, closers, strings, operators
        return False
    unindented = line[:1] not in (" ", "\t")
    constant = _CONSTANT_RE.match(stripped)
    if constant and not re.search(r"(?:^|\s)[a-z]+\s+[a-z]+[^()\[\]{}]*\.$", constant.group(1)):  # not prose: `X=off disables it.`
        return True
    if _SQL_CREATE_RE.match(stripped) or _EXPORTED_FUNCTION_RE.match(stripped):
        return True
    if unindented and (_C_FUNCTION_RE.match(stripped) or _SIGNATURE_RE.match(stripped)):
        return True
    # ... checks modifiers, declaration keywords, and function call patterns ...

The function inspects leading tokens using _lead to strip annotations and access modifiers (public, export, async, static). It verifies whether the subsequent keyword is an element of _DECLARATION_WORDS or matches regular expressions for C/C++ function definitions, SQL CREATE statements, Node.js module.exports, or capitalized constant assignments.

docs.title: import_statement_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def import_statement_like(line: str) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a line of code constitutes an import statement across languages (e.g., Python import/from, JavaScript import/require, Rust use, C/C++ #include, Go import, Shell . path).

Parameters:

  • line (str): Source line to evaluate.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the line imports external or internal dependencies.

Example:

def import_statement_like(line: str) -> bool:
    stripped = _ANNOTATIONS_RE.sub("", line.strip())  # @testable import X
    if stripped.startswith(("//", "/*", "*", "--")):  # comments, a Lua / SQL `--` line too
        return False
    if stripped.startswith("#"):  # only a preprocessor include (`#include "x.h"`, `# include <y>`, `#import`)
        if not re.match(r"#\s*(?:include|import)\s*[<\"]", stripped):  # not a commented-out `# import os`
            return False
        stripped = "#" + stripped[1:].lstrip()
    if stripped.startswith(("'", '"', "`")):
        return False
    strings = [m.span() for m in _STRING_RE.finditer(stripped)]
    if any(not any(low <= call.start() < high for low, high in strings) for call in _IMPORT_CALL_RE.finditer(stripped)):
        return True  # require('x') / import('x') in code, not in a message such as "call require('x') first"
    # ... evaluates leading keywords and relative import semantics ...

The heuristic defensively filters out comments, prose sentences, and inline assignments. It confirms that call-based imports like require('x') occur within code rather than inside string literals, and rejects statements where an import keyword is followed by arithmetic operators or invalid punctuation.

docs.title: import_block_lines()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def import_block_lines(lines: list[str]) -> set[int]:

Description: Identifies 0-based line indices residing within multi-line import blocks, specifically targeting Go parenthesized import ( ... ) blocks.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of source lines.

Returns:

  • set[int]: Set of line numbers that contain import entries inside a block.

Example:

def import_block_lines(lines: list[str]) -> set[int]:
    """0-based lines inside an ``import ( ... )`` block (Go): bare quoted paths with no keyword of their own."""
    found, inside = set(), False
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if re.match(r"^import\s*\($", stripped):
            inside = True
        elif inside and stripped == ")":
            inside = False
        elif inside and _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.match(line):
            found.add(number)
    return found

The function tracks block entry and exit across lines, applying _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE to capture bare quoted import specifiers.

docs.title: enclosing_blocks()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def enclosing_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[str | None]:

Description: Computes the structural enclosing block category ("function", "container", or None) for each line based on indentation shifts, ignoring intermediate control flow statements.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of source lines.

Returns:

  • list[str | None]: Per-line list of enclosing block types.

Example:

def enclosing_blocks(lines: list[str]) -> list[str | None]:
    kinds, stack = [], []  # stack of (indent, kind)
    for line in lines:
        kind = _block_kind(line) if line.strip() else None
        if kind is None:
            kinds.append(None)
            continue
        indent = _indent(line)
        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        kinds.append(next((k for _i, k in reversed(stack) if k != "control"), None))
        stack.append((indent, kind))
    return kinds

Using an indentation stack, this helper associates nested lines with their surrounding scope. Control statements (if, for, while) are bypassed so that local functions inside methods or helper classes inside modules resolve directly to their functional or structural containers.

docs.title: completeness_hints()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def completeness_hints(content: str, checked: dict, claims: dict | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Compares source lines against verified claims to identify uncovered imports and declarations, generating diagnostic hints for follow-up LLM prompting.

Parameters:

  • content (str): File source text.
  • checked (dict): Output dictionary from verify_file_claims.
  • claims (dict | None, optional): Original unverified claims dictionary.

Returns:

  • dict: Diagnostic dictionary containing 1-based line arrays: import_lines, declaration_lines, and uncovered.

Example:

def completeness_hints(content: str, checked: dict, claims: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    lines = split_lines(_nfc(content))
    view = code_view(lines)
    imports = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if import_statement_like(line)} | import_block_lines(view)
    enclosing = enclosing_blocks(view)
    declarations = {n for n, line in enumerate(view) if n not in imports and enclosing[n] != "function" and declaration_like(line)}

    import_numbers, import_texts = set(), set()
    for entry in checked.get("dependencies", []):
        span = range(entry["line"] - 1, entry.get("end_line", entry["line"]))
        import_numbers.update(span)
        import_texts.update(_collapse(lines[n]) for n in span if n < len(lines))
    import_texts.update(_collapse(_as_text(item.get("evidence"))) for item in _claim_list(claims or {}, "dependencies"))
    symbol_numbers = set()
    for entry in checked.get("symbols", []):
        symbol_numbers.update(range(entry["line"] - 1, entry.get("end_line", entry["line"])))
        symbol_numbers.update(n - 1 for n in entry.get("ambiguous_lines", []))
    uncovered = {n for n in imports if n not in import_numbers and _collapse(lines[n]) not in import_texts}
    uncovered |= {n for n in declarations if n not in symbol_numbers}
    return {
        "import_lines": sorted(n + 1 for n in imports),
        "declaration_lines": sorted(n + 1 for n in declarations),
        "uncovered": sorted(n + 1 for n in uncovered),
    }

The function identifies potential declaration and import lines using heuristic scanning and excludes those already encompassed by verified symbols or dependencies. Declarations within local function bodies are omitted. The resulting uncovered line list indicates potential missed facts.

docs.title: unexplained_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def unexplained_names(content: str, source_path: str, depends_on: list[dict], table) -> list[dict]:

Description: Identifies external symbols used in a file that are uniquely defined by another module in the project, but have no associated verified dependency edge. Useful for implicit-package languages like Go, Java, or C#.

Parameters:

  • content (str): File source text.
  • source_path (str): Path of the file being audited.
  • depends_on (list[dict]): Verified dependencies for the file.
  • table (ModuleTable): Cross-module lookup table.

Returns:

  • list[dict]: Dictionaries of {"name": str, "module": str} representing unlinked symbol references.

Example:

def unexplained_names(content: str, source_path: str, depends_on: list[dict], table) -> list[dict]:
    # ... extracts code while preserving string interpolations ...
    code = "\n".join(code_of(line) for line in code_view(split_lines(_nfc(content))))
    bound = set()
    for pattern in (_KEYWORD_BINDS_RE, _LINE_BINDS_RE, _KWARG_BINDS_RE):
        for match in pattern.finditer(code):
            bound.update(name.strip() for name in match.group(1).split(","))
    used = set(_FIRST_NAME_RE.findall(code)) | set(_SHELL_VAR_RE.findall(code))
    # ... calculates dotted subchains and checks table.symbol_owner ...
    linked = {edge["module"] for edge in depends_on}
    own = table.all_symbols.get(source_path, set())
    found = []
    for name, module in sorted(table.symbol_owner.items()):
        hit = (name in dotted or name.split(".")[-1] in used) if "." in name else name in used
        if module != source_path and module not in linked and name not in own and name not in bound and hit:
            found.append({"name": name, "module": module})
    return found

The function extracts all candidate identifier references from executable code, filtering out locally declared variables, parameters, and destructured bindings. It then searches table.symbol_owner for names owned exclusively by a single other file. If the current module does not import that file, an entry is added to the return list.

docs.title: merge_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def merge_claims(first: dict, second: dict) -> dict:

Description: Computes the union of two claim sets (e.g., initial extraction and completeness follow-up), dropping duplicates that share identical identity fields.

Parameters:

  • first (dict): Initial claims dictionary.
  • second (dict): Subsequent claims dictionary.

Returns:

  • dict: Merged claims dictionary with summed unparsed tallies.

Example:

def merge_claims(first: dict, second: dict) -> dict:
    """Union of two replies' claims (first pass + follow-up), duplicates dropped (same identity fields, first
    kept); ``unparsed`` added up."""
    merged = {}
    for key in CLAIM_KEYS:
        seen, items = set(), []
        for item in [*_claim_list(first or {}, key), *_claim_list(second or {}, key)]:
            marker = tuple(_collapse(_as_text(item.get(field))) for field in _IDENTITY_FIELDS[key])
            if marker not in seen:
                seen.add(marker)
                items.append(item)
        merged[key] = items
    merged["unparsed"] = (first or {}).get("unparsed", 0) + (second or {}).get("unparsed", 0)
    return merged

Identity deduplication markers are governed by _IDENTITY_FIELDS: symbols checks (parent, name, signature), dependencies checks (target, evidence), and config/errors check (name, evidence).

docs.title: normalize_name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize_name(text: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes package, crate, and module names for canonical cross-language comparison by converting Unicode to NFC, stripping whitespace, case-folding, and replacing hyphens with underscores.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Identifier or package name string.

Returns:

  • str: Normalized canonical string.

Example:

def normalize_name(text: str) -> str:
    """Case-folded, ``-`` as ``_``: package, crate and distribution names compare equal across spellings
    (``shop-core`` in Cargo.toml, ``shop_core`` in ``use shop_core::store``)."""
    return _nfc(text).strip().casefold().replace("-", "_")

This normalization handles package naming discrepancies across ecosystems, such as Rust crates or npm packages defined with hyphens (shop-core) but imported using underscores (shop_core).

docs.title: verify_manifest_claims()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verify_manifest_claims(claims: dict, content: str, manifest_path: str) -> dict:

Description: Validates claims extracted from configuration and build manifests (package.json, Cargo.toml, etc.) regarding package names provided and path aliases configured.

Parameters:

  • claims (dict): Manifest claims dictionary containing provides and aliases.
  • content (str): Manifest file text.
  • manifest_path (str): Project-relative path to the manifest.

Returns:

  • dict: Verified results dictionary containing provides, aliases, rejected, claimed, and found.

Example:

def verify_manifest_claims(claims: dict, content: str, manifest_path: str) -> dict:
    index = SourceIndex(content)
    flat = _collapse(content)
    result = {"provides": [], "aliases": [], "rejected": []}
    # ... checks unparsed items and loops over provides ...
    for item in _claim_list(claims, "provides"):
        claimed += 1
        name, evidence = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("evidence"))
        matches = [m for m in (index.locate(evidence) if name else []) if _collapse(name) in _collapse(index.text(m[0], m[1]))]
        if not matches or not _declares_name(_collapse(index.text(matches[0][0], matches[0][1])), name):
            result["rejected"].append({"kind": "provides", "name": name, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "..."})
            continue
        # ... checks entry points and registers valid provides ...

The function verifies that claimed package names are declared using declaration keys (such as name, package, or module) via _declares_name, rather than merely appearing as dependency references. Declared aliases are validated to ensure both the alias key and target path appear in the source text.

docs.title: manifest_rules()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def manifest_rules(manifests: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:

Description: Converts verified manifest claim dictionaries into structured package definitions and path alias rules for ModuleTable.

Parameters:

  • manifests (dict): Dictionary mapping manifest paths to verified claims.

Returns:

  • tuple[list, list]: A 2-tuple (packages, aliases) sorted for prefix matching.

Example:

def manifest_rules(manifests: dict) -> tuple[list, list]:
    packages, aliases = [], []
    for path, verified in (manifests or {}).items():
        directory = posixpath.dirname(path)
        for provided in verified.get("provides", []):
            if "*" in provided["name"]:
                continue
            entry = provided.get("entry")
            entry_path = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(directory, entry)) if entry else None
            packages.append({"segments": _name_segments(provided["name"]), "name": provided["name"], "dir": directory, "entry": entry_path})
        for alias in verified.get("aliases", []):
            key = alias["alias"]
            if key.startswith(("./", "../")) or not key.split("*", 1)[0]:
                continue
            mode = "star" if "*" in key else "prefix" if key.endswith("/") else "exact"
            template = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(directory, alias.get("base") or ".", alias["target"]))
            aliases.append({"prefix": key.split("*", 1)[0], "template": "" if template == "." else template, "mode": mode, "dir": directory})
    packages.sort(key=lambda package: -len(package["segments"]))
    return packages, aliases

Packages are extracted with normalized path segments, root directories, and optional entrypoints. Aliases are classified into star (wildcard mapping), prefix (directory mapping), or exact match modes.

docs.title: ModuleTable
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class ModuleTable:

Description: Cross-module symbol, path, and package directory resolver. Maintains the global index of documented file paths, directory memberships, symbol ownership, manifest rules, and namespace bindings.

docs.title: ModuleTable.__init__()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def __init__(self, paths: list[str], symbols_by_path: dict, contents: dict | None = None, manifests: dict | None = None):

Description: Builds inverted indices mapping filenames, directories, and unique symbols to their defining source files.

Parameters:

  • paths (list[str]): List of all documented project file paths.
  • symbols_by_path (dict): Dictionary mapping paths to verified symbol lists.
  • contents (dict | None, optional): Mapping of paths to raw source content. Defaults to None.
  • manifests (dict | None, optional): Mapping of manifest paths to verified claims. Defaults to None.

Example:

    def __init__(self, paths: list[str], symbols_by_path: dict, contents: dict | None = None, manifests: dict | None = None):
        self.paths = list(paths)
        self.contents = contents or {}
        self.packages, self.aliases = manifest_rules(manifests)
        self.segments = {path: _segments(path) for path in self.paths}
        self.extensions = {os.path.splitext(path)[1] for path in self.paths if os.path.splitext(path)[1]}
        self.by_dir = defaultdict(list)
        for path in self.paths:
            self.by_dir[posixpath.dirname(path)].append(path)
        owners = defaultdict(set)
        self.top_symbols, self.all_symbols = {}, {}
        for path, symbols in symbols_by_path.items():
            self.all_symbols[path] = {symbol["name"] for symbol in symbols}
            self.top_symbols[path] = {symbol["name"] for symbol in symbols if symbol.get("kind") not in _OWNER_EXCLUDED_KINDS}
            for name in self.top_symbols[path]:
                if len(name) >= 3:
                    owners[name].add(path)
        self.symbol_owner = {name: next(iter(paths)) for name, paths in owners.items() if len(paths) == 1}
        self.owned = defaultdict(set)
        for name, path in self.symbol_owner.items():
            self.owned[path].add(name)

The constructor computes symbol_owner for all top-level symbols (excluding generic method names like get or run via _OWNER_EXCLUDED_KINDS) that are defined in exactly one module. If a symbol name is defined in multiple modules, it is excluded from single-owner resolution to prevent false dependency linkages.

docs.title: ModuleTable.normalize()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize(self, target: str) -> tuple[list[str], str]:

Description: Normalizes an import target string into path segments and an optional recognized extension.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Raw import target string (e.g., "crate::store::Repo", "@/components/Button.tsx", "./util").

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str]: A 2-tuple (segments, extension).

Example:

    def normalize(self, target: str) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
        text = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,")
        for prefix in ("@/", "~/", "$/"):
            text = text.removeprefix(prefix)
        ext = os.path.splitext(text)[1]
        if ext in self.extensions:
            text = text[: -len(ext)]
        else:
            ext = ""
        text = text.replace("::", "/").replace("\\", "/").replace(".", "/")
        parts = [part.strip() for part in text.split("/")]
        return [part for part in parts if part and part not in ("*", "crate", "super", "self") and _SEGMENT_RE.match(part)], ext

The method strips string delimiters and framework alias prefixes (@/, ~/, $/), translates namespace separators (::, \, .) into forward slashes, and filters out language-specific qualifiers (*, crate, super, self).

docs.title: ModuleTable.resolve_manifest()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_manifest(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set, prefer_local: bool = False) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves an import target using workspace manifest rules (package names and path aliases).

Parameters:

  • target (str): Import specifier.
  • source_path (str): Path of the importing source file.
  • source_words (set): Set of token words present in the importing file.
  • prefer_local (bool, optional): Whether to prefer local relative files before manifest rules. Defaults to False.

Returns:

Example:

    def resolve_manifest(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set, prefer_local: bool = False) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
        text = re.sub(r"^[A-Za-z][\w+.-]*:(?![/:\\])", "", target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,"))
        if not text or text.startswith(("./", "../", ".\\", "..\\")) or re.match(r"^\.+\w", text):
            return None
        # ... checks alias scopes, package prefixes, and resolves package roots ...

The method evaluates path aliases scoped to manifest directories, supporting wildcard replacement templates. For package references, it resolves package roots, directory index files, or specific exported submodules.

docs.title: ModuleTable.resolve()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str]:

Description: Primary cross-module target resolver. Resolves relative paths, suffix matches, directory packages, and unique symbol owners.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Target string written in the import statement.
  • source_path (str): File path of the importing module.
  • source_words (set): Word tokens appearing in the importing file.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str]: 2-tuple (resolved_paths, match_mechanism) where mechanism is "path", "package", "symbol", "external", or "ambiguous".

Example:

    def resolve(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
        relative = self._resolve_relative(target, source_path, source_words)
        if relative is not None:
            return relative
        parts, ext = self.normalize(target)
        for size in range(len(parts), 0, -1):
            tail = parts[-size:]
            hits = self._suffix_hits(tail, ext, source_path)
            if len(hits) == 1:
                return (hits, "path") if self._corroborated(target, parts, size, hits[0], source_path, source_words) else ([], "external")
            if hits:
                return [], "ambiguous"
            # ... checks directory index files and package directories ...
        if parts and parts[-1] in self.symbol_owner and self.symbol_owner[parts[-1]] != source_path:
            return [self.symbol_owner[parts[-1]]], "symbol"
        return [], "external"

Resolution follows a strict fallback order: 1. Relative path evaluation (./, ../, leading dots). 2. Suffix matching against project file paths with corroboration. 3. Directory-level package resolution. 4. Single-owner symbol resolution using the terminal segment. 5. External classification if no internal candidates match.

docs.title: ModuleTable.used_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def used_names(self, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> set:

Description: Finds top-level symbols defined by path that appear in source_words and are not defined by source_path.

Parameters:

  • path (str): Candidate target module path.
  • source_path (str): Current source module path.
  • source_words (set): Set of token words from the current module.

Returns:

  • set: Set of symbol names from path used by source_path.

Example:

    def used_names(self, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> set:
        """Owning names (``top_symbols``) of *path* that the source uses and does not define itself; a dotted
        name (``MyApp.Accounts.User``) counts when its last part is used."""
        names = self.top_symbols.get(path, set()) - self.all_symbols.get(source_path, set())
        return {name for name in names if name in source_words or name.split(".")[-1] in source_words}

This method confirms dependency linkages for wildcard or implicit package imports by verifying that the importing module actually references symbols defined in the candidate file.

docs.title: ModuleTable.namespace_members()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def namespace_members(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Identifies modules that declare a given namespace and export symbols utilized by the importing source module.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Namespace target (e.g., "Acme.Accounting").
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Token words from the importing source.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of module paths satisfying the namespace import.

Example:

    def namespace_members(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
        name = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,").removesuffix(".*").removesuffix("::*")
        if len(re.split(r"::|[./\\]", name)) < 2:
            return []
        return [
            path
            for path in self.paths
            if path != source_path
            and declares_namespace(self.contents.get(path, ""), name)
            and self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words) & self.owned[path]
        ]

This method supports languages like C# (using Acme.Accounting;) where a namespace does not map directly to a directory path. It filters candidates by checking both namespace declarations and symbol usage.

docs.title: evidence_names_module()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def evidence_names_module(evidence: str, target_path: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, how: str, relative_style: bool = False, per_line: bool = False) -> bool:

Description: Enforces the evidence rule: verifies whether the quoted source line explicitly names the resolved module via file stem, unique symbol, directory reference, or namespace.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Quoted evidence line.
  • target_path (str): Resolved target module path.
  • source_path (str): Importing file path.
  • table (ModuleTable): Cross-module lookup table.
  • how (str): Resolution mechanism ("path", "package", "symbol", etc.).
  • relative_style (bool, optional): Whether relative import style applies. Defaults to False.
  • per_line (bool, optional): Whether to evaluate token matches line-by-line. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the evidence validates the resolved dependency.

Example:

def evidence_names_module(
    evidence: str, target_path: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, how: str, relative_style: bool = False, per_line: bool = False
) -> bool:
    words = set(_words(evidence))
    checked = re.sub(r"[\"'`][\w-]+[\"'`]", " ", evidence) if relative_style else evidence
    name = target_path.split("/")[-2] if how == "package" and "/" in target_path else _stem(target_path)
    extension = "" if how == "package" else os.path.splitext(target_path)[1]
    # ... validates stem in path context, symbol ownership, or namespace declarations ...

The evidence rule prevents tenuous dependency linkages. A resolved dependency is accepted only if the evidence line contains the target module's filename stem, a symbol uniquely defined by the target, or a valid directory/namespace path.

docs.title: declares_namespace()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def declares_namespace(content: str, dotted: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a source file explicitly contains a package or namespace declaration matching dotted.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Source file text.
  • dotted (str): Dotted namespace string (e.g., "com.acme.billing").

Returns:

  • bool: True if a matching declaration line is found.

Example:

def declares_namespace(content: str, dotted: str) -> bool:
    """Whether *content* has a namespace/package/module declaration line naming *dotted*
    (``namespace Acme.Accounting``, ``package com.acme.billing;``, ``namespace App\\Repo;``)."""
    for line in split_lines(content):
        words = _words(line)
        if words and words[0] in _NAMESPACE_WORDS and dotted in line:
            return True
    return False

The function checks lines starting with keywords in _NAMESPACE_WORDS (namespace, package, module, defmodule, library, unit).

docs.title: scan_import_candidates()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def scan_import_candidates(content: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool = False) -> set[str]:

Description: Scans source text for import statements that reference known documented project modules, used for recall diagnostics to identify missed dependencies.

Parameters:

  • content (str): Source text.
  • source_path (str): Current source path.
  • table (ModuleTable): Cross-module lookup table.
  • relative_style (bool, optional): Whether relative import style applies. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • set[str]: Set of candidate target file paths.

Example:

def scan_import_candidates(content: str, source_path: str, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool = False) -> set[str]:
    found = set()
    lines = code_view(split_lines(_nfc(content)))
    block = import_block_lines(lines)
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        if not (import_statement_like(line) or number in block):
            continue
        if relative_style:
            line = re.sub(r"[\"'`][\w-]+[\"'`]", " ", line)
        words = set(_words(line))
        for path in table.paths:
            if path == source_path:
                continue
            stem = _stem(path)
            if stem in words and _names_path(line, stem, os.path.splitext(path)[1], table.extensions):
                found.add(path)
    return found

The function evaluates import lines against project module stems using _names_path, generating a baseline set of candidate dependencies without requiring LLM extraction.

docs.title: relative_import_extensions()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def relative_import_extensions(located: dict) -> set:

Description: Identifies file extensions in the repository that use relative import paths (./, ../).

Parameters:

  • located (dict): Mapping of file paths to lists of located dependency claim dictionaries.

Returns:

  • set: Set of file extensions (e.g., {".ts", ".js"}) that utilize relative imports.

Example:

def relative_import_extensions(located: dict) -> set:
    """File extensions whose files import this project by relative path (``./x``, ``../x``) somewhere.

    Files of such a language write packages as bare names (``import config from 'config'``), so there
    a bare name is external, not a same-named local module, even in a file with no relative import.
    """
    return {os.path.splitext(path)[1] for path, claims in located.items() if any(_is_relative(claim["target"]) for claim in claims)}

This detection enables ecosystem-specific import interpretation: in languages where relative imports use ./, bare identifiers (such as import config from 'config') are treated as external packages rather than local files.

docs.title: target_written()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def target_written(target: str, evidence: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies that a claimed dependency target string is explicitly written within the quoted evidence line, rather than being an LLM paraphrase or hallucination.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Target string from the claim.
  • evidence (str): Quoted evidence line.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the target is found verbatim or as a valid path expression.

Example:

def target_written(target: str, evidence: str) -> bool:
    text = _collapse(target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,"))
    if not text:
        return False
    if re.search("[\"'`]", text) and text in _collapse(evidence):  # the whole expression copied: __DIR__ . '/src/Db.php'
        return True
    first = (_words(text) or [""])[0]
    quoted = [q for q in re.findall(r"(?=[\"'`<]([^\"'`<>\s]+)[\"'`>])", evidence) if re.search(r"[/.]", q) or (first and first in _words(q))]
    if quoted:  # whole, or the end of a path built at run time: "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/log.sh", __DIR__ . '/src/Db.php'
        bare = _bare_path(text)
        if any(_bare_path(q) == bare or q.endswith("/" + bare) for q in quoted):
            return True
        # the static part of a path built from a template: require(`./plugins/${name}`) → ./plugins
        if any(_bare_path(q).startswith(bare + "/") and re.search(r"[$#%]\{|\{\w", _bare_path(q)[len(bare) :]) for q in quoted):
            return True
    code = _without_bindings(re.sub(r"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|`[^`]*`", " ", evidence))
    if quoted and not _words(code):
        return False
    wanted, have = _words(text), _words(code)
    position = 0
    for word in have:
        if position < len(wanted) and word == wanted[position]:
            position += 1
    return bool(wanted) and position == len(wanted) and not quoted

The function handles string literals, dynamically concatenated paths (such as __DIR__ . '/src/Db.php'), and template strings (require(\./plugins/${name}`)). For languages without quoted import paths (like Python or Java), it verifies that target words appear in sequence outside local import aliases (as billing`).

docs.title: judge_dependency()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def judge_dependency(claim: dict, source_path: str, source_words: set, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool, shadowed: frozenset = frozenset()) -> tuple[str, list]:

Description: Evaluates a single located dependency claim against manifest rules and ModuleTable indices, returning an acceptance verdict and resolved targets.

Parameters:

  • claim (dict): Located dependency claim dictionary.
  • source_path (str): Importing source file path.
  • source_words (set): Token words from the source file.
  • table (ModuleTable): Cross-module lookup table.
  • relative_style (bool): Whether the source file uses relative import style.
  • shadowed (frozenset, optional): Set of package names shadowed by external imports. Defaults to frozenset().

Returns:

  • tuple[str, list]: A 2-tuple (verdict, details) where verdict is "depends_on", "external", or "rejected".

Example:

def judge_dependency(
    claim: dict, source_path: str, source_words: set, table: ModuleTable, relative_style: bool, shadowed: frozenset = frozenset()
) -> tuple[str, list]:
    target, evidence = claim["target"], claim["evidence"]
    if _BARE_NAME_RE.match(target) and normalize_name(target) in shadowed:
        return "external", []
    written = target_written(target, evidence)
    per_line = claim.get("match") == "tokens"
    manifest = table.resolve_manifest(target, source_path, source_words, prefer_local=not relative_style)
    if manifest is not None:  # declared names win over the relative-import convention: `import 'utils'` may be a workspace package
        targets, _prefix = manifest
        if not targets:
            return "external", []
        if written and _imports_target(evidence, target):
            return "depends_on", [(module, "manifest") for module in targets]
        return "rejected", [(module, "evidence does not import the declared package or alias") for module in targets]
    # ... executes table.resolve, checks namespaces, and validates evidence_names_module ...

The judgment process evaluates targets in order: checking shadowed external names, resolving manifest aliases and packages, checking language relative-import rules, running ModuleTable.resolve(), and finally enforcing the evidence rule via evidence_names_module.

docs.title: shadowed_names()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def shadowed_names(claims: list[dict], verdicts: list[tuple]) -> frozenset:

Description: Identifies bare package names imported from external libraries that could shadow internal modules with the same name.

Parameters:

  • claims (list[dict]): List of dependency claims for a file.
  • verdicts (list[tuple]): List of preliminary (verdict, details) tuples from judge_dependency.

Returns:

  • frozenset: Set of shadowed bare package names.

Example:

def shadowed_names(claims: list[dict], verdicts: list[tuple]) -> frozenset:
    """Bare names that are the last segment of an external import and of no internal import of the same
    source (``store`` of ``example.com/other/store``): a bare ``store.X`` there means that external package."""

    def last(claim):
        segments = _name_segments(claim["target"])
        return segments[-1] if len(segments) > 1 else None

    external = {last(claim) for claim, (verdict, _) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True) if verdict == "external"} - {None}
    internal = {last(claim) for claim, (verdict, _) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True) if verdict == "depends_on"} - {None}
    return frozenset(external - internal)

If a file imports an external library such as example.com/other/store, a subsequent reference like store.New() refers to the external package rather than an internal store.go module. This function detects these collisions so judge_dependency can adjust its verdicts accordingly.

docs.title: verify_dependencies()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verify_dependencies(located: dict, contents: dict, table: ModuleTable) -> dict:

Description: Cross-module orchestrator that evaluates located dependencies across all project modules, returning verified internal edges, external packages, rejections, and missed imports.

Parameters:

  • located (dict): Mapping of paths to lists of located dependency claims.
  • contents (dict): Mapping of paths to file source contents.
  • table (ModuleTable): Cross-module lookup table.

Returns:

  • dict: Results mapping each path to a dictionary with depends_on, external, rejected, and missed entries.

Example:

def verify_dependencies(located: dict, contents: dict, table: ModuleTable) -> dict:
    results = {}
    relative_extensions = relative_import_extensions(located)
    for path, claims in located.items():
        words = set(_words(contents.get(path, "")))
        depends_on, external, rejected, seen = [], [], [], set()
        relative_style = os.path.splitext(path)[1] in relative_extensions
        verdicts = [judge_dependency(claim, path, words, table, relative_style) for claim in claims]
        shadowed = shadowed_names(claims, verdicts)
        if shadowed:
            verdicts = [judge_dependency(claim, path, words, table, relative_style, shadowed) for claim in claims]
        for claim, (verdict, detail) in zip(claims, verdicts, strict=True):
            # ... categorizes depends_on, external, and rejected ...
        missed = sorted(scan_import_candidates(contents.get(path, ""), path, table, relative_style) - seen)
        results[path] = {"depends_on": depends_on, "external": external, "rejected": rejected, "missed": missed}
    return results

The function runs a two-pass evaluation per file: an initial pass to detect external package targets, followed by a second pass that accounts for shadowed symbols. It also runs scan_import_candidates to identify any valid internal import statements that the LLM failed to claim.

docs.title: facts_hash()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def facts_hash(signature: str, path: str, content: str) -> str:

Description: Computes a deterministic MD5 digest over an extraction signature, file path, and source content to invalidate cached facts when files change.

Parameters:

  • signature (str): Extraction version or model prompt signature.
  • path (str): Project-relative file path.
  • content (str): Source code string.

Returns:

  • str: Hexadecimal MD5 hash digest.

Example:

def facts_hash(signature: str, path: str, content: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.md5(f"{signature}|{path}|{content}".encode()).hexdigest()

The resulting digest serves as a cache key in pipeline orchestrators to avoid re-extracting facts from unmodified source files.

docs.title: source_commit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def source_commit(local_dir) -> str | None:

Description: Resolves the Git HEAD commit SHA for the analyzed repository by executing git rev-parse HEAD.

Parameters:

  • local_dir (str | os.PathLike): Filesystem path to the local git clone directory.

Returns:

  • str | None: 40-character commit hash, or None if git execution fails or the directory is invalid.

Example:

def source_commit(local_dir) -> str | None:
    """HEAD commit of the crawled checkout (not of this tool's working directory), or None."""
    if not local_dir or not os.path.isdir(local_dir):
        return None
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", local_dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, check=False)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    return (out.stdout.strip() or None) if out.returncode == 0 else None

The function executes git -C <local_dir> rev-parse HEAD with a 10-second timeout. Any OSError or SubprocessError is trapped to allow execution on non-git directory trees.

docs.title: build_facts_document()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_facts_document(project_name: str, commit, modules: dict, manifests: dict | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Constructs the root dictionary conforming to facts document schema version 1.

Parameters:

  • project_name (str): Target project name.
  • commit (str | None): Source repository commit hash.
  • modules (dict): Mapping of module paths to verified facts dictionaries.
  • manifests (dict | None, optional): Mapping of manifest paths to verified claims. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • dict: Document dictionary matching the facts.json schema.

Example:

def build_facts_document(project_name: str, commit, modules: dict, manifests: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """The published document: every listed fact is backed by a source line; lists may be incomplete.
    ``manifests``: the names and aliases the project's code is imported by, per manifest file."""
    return {
        "schema": FACTS_SCHEMA,
        "project": project_name,
        "commit": commit,
        "note": (
            "Every symbol, dependency, config key and error below was found in the source at the given line. "
            "Presence is verified, completeness is not: 'coverage' compares verified to claimed facts per module."
        ),
        "modules": modules,
        "manifests": manifests or {},
    }

The resulting document contains the schema version, project metadata, commit hash, verified module data, and manifest alias mappings.

docs.title: load_facts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def load_facts(path: str, section: str = "modules") -> dict:

Description: Loads a specific section ("modules" or "manifests") from an existing facts.json file on disk.

Parameters:

  • path (str): Filesystem path to the facts.json file.
  • section (str, optional): Top-level document key to extract. Defaults to "modules".

Returns:

  • dict: The extracted section dictionary, or {} if the file is missing, corrupt, or has an incompatible schema version.

Example:

def load_facts(path: str, section: str = "modules") -> dict:
    """``{path: entry}`` of a section (``modules`` or ``manifests``) of an earlier facts.json, or ``{}``."""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            document = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}
    entries = document.get(section) if isinstance(document, dict) else None
    return entries if isinstance(entries, dict) and document.get("schema") == FACTS_SCHEMA else {}

The function handles missing files, unreadable JSON, and schema version mismatches by returning an empty dictionary rather than raising exceptions.

docs.title: save_facts()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def save_facts(path: str, document: dict) -> None:

Description: Serializes and writes a facts document to disk using an atomic temporary-file replacement pattern.

Parameters:

  • path (str): Target destination path.
  • document (dict): Facts document dictionary to serialize.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def save_facts(path: str, document: dict) -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    tmp_path = f"{path}.tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(document, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    os.replace(tmp_path, path)

The function creates parent directories as needed, writes formatted JSON to a temporary file (.tmp), and performs an atomic filesystem swap using os.replace. This prevents corruption if the process is terminated mid-write.

docs.title: facts_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def facts_path(output_dir: str, project_name: str, is_mkdocs: bool) -> str:

Description: Computes the canonical output path for facts.json based on the output directory, project name, and MkDocs site generation mode.

Parameters:

  • output_dir (str): Root documentation output directory.
  • project_name (str): Project identifier.
  • is_mkdocs (bool): Whether documentation is being generated for MkDocs.

Returns:

  • str: Filesystem path to the destination facts.json.

Example:

def facts_path(output_dir: str, project_name: str, is_mkdocs: bool) -> str:
    """docs/api/facts.json under --mkdocs (published with the site and kept by CI's docs cache), else next to the pages."""
    base = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name)
    return os.path.join(base, "docs", "api", FACTS_FILENAME) if is_mkdocs else os.path.join(base, FACTS_FILENAME)

In MkDocs mode (is_mkdocs=True), the file is placed under docs/api/facts.json so it is published alongside generated static site assets. Otherwise, it is placed in the root project output directory.

Signature: def _nfc(text) -> str:

Description: Normalizes input text into Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC). Ensures consistency between decomposed filesystem paths and precomposed strings from LLMs.

Visibility: Private

Signature: def _words(text: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Extracts word tokens from NFC-normalized text using _WORD_RE.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Input string.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of extracted word tokens.
def _words(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return _WORD_RE.findall(_nfc(text))

docs.title: SourceIndex._words_in_order()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _words_in_order(self, words: list[str], first: int, end: int) -> int | None:

Description: Checks whether a target sequence of words appears in order across lines first through end, returning the 0-based index of the line containing the final word.

Parameters:

  • words (list[str]): Ordered list of word tokens.
  • first (int): Starting line index.
  • end (int): Ending line index.

Returns:

  • int | None: Line index where the sequence completes, or None if the sequence was not found.
    def _words_in_order(self, words: list[str], first: int, end: int) -> int | None:
        position = 0
        for line in range(first, end):
            for word in self.words[line]:
                if word == words[position]:
                    position += 1
                    if position == len(words):
                        return line
        return None

docs.title: _has_words()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _has_words(text: str, name: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether the word tokens of name appear in order within text.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Corpus text to search.
  • name (str): Target identifier or name string.

Returns:

  • bool: True if all words in name appear in order.
def _has_words(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    """Whether the identifier tokens of *name* occur in *text* in order (``--max-size`` → max, size)."""
    wanted, have = _words(name), _words(text)
    if not wanted:
        return False
    position = 0
    for word in have:
        if word == wanted[position]:
            position += 1
            if position == len(wanted):
                return True
    return False

docs.title: _names_in()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _names_in(text: str, name: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether name appears in text. For alphanumeric identifiers, checks word tokens in order; for operator names or punctuation (such as == or []), verifies squashed exact matches.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Corpus text.
  • name (str): Symbol or operator name.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the name is found in the text.
def _names_in(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
    if re.fullmatch(r"\w+", _nfc(name)):
        return _has_words(text, name)
    return _squash(name) in _squash(text) and (not _words(name) or _has_words(text, name))

docs.title: _as_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _as_text(value) -> str:

Description: Safely converts scalar values to strings. Returns empty strings for None and boolean values to avoid stringifying "True" or "False".

Parameters:

  • value (Any): Value to convert.

Returns:

  • str: Converted string representation.
def _as_text(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None:
        return ""
    return value if isinstance(value, str) else str(value) if isinstance(value, (int, float)) else ""

Description: Extracts a list of dictionary claims from an input dictionary, ignoring non-dictionary entries.

docs.title: _verify_symbols()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _verify_symbols(symbols: list[dict], index: SourceIndex) -> tuple[list, list]:

Description: Resolves symbol locations and scopes within a file. Places top-level symbols first, then resolves child members within their parent's line span or enclosing block chain.

Parameters:

  • symbols (list[dict]): Extracted symbol claim dictionaries.
  • index (SourceIndex): Source index of the file.

Returns:

  • tuple[list, list]: A 2-tuple (kept_symbols, rejected_symbols).
def _verify_symbols(symbols: list[dict], index: SourceIndex) -> tuple[list, list]:
    kept, rejected, placed = [], [], {}
    pending, unscoped = sorted(symbols, key=lambda item: bool(_as_text(item.get("parent")).strip())), False
    while pending:
        pending_names = {_as_text(item.get("name")).strip() for item in pending}
        waiting = []
        for item in pending:
            name, parent = _as_text(item.get("name")).strip(), _as_text(item.get("parent")).strip()
            if not unscoped and parent and parent != name and parent not in placed and parent in pending_names:
                waiting.append(item)
                continue
            signature = _as_text(item.get("signature"))
            # ... locates signature within parent span or file-wide using _parent_verdict ...

Top-level symbols are resolved first to establish boundary anchors for child symbols. When locating members (methods, fields), searches are constrained between the parent symbol's declaration line and the next top-level declaration. If disambiguation fails, candidates are verified using _parent_verdict and _in_parent.

docs.text:

Description: Returns {"end_line": last + 1} (1-based) if a match spans multiple lines, or an empty dictionary if it occupies a single line.

Parameters:

  • last (int): Ending line index (0-based).

Returns:

def _end(first: int, last: int) -> dict:
    return {"end_line": last + 1} if last > first else {}

docs.title: _enclosing()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _enclosing(containers: list[tuple[int, str]], line: int) -> str | None:

Description: Identifies the nearest container symbol declared prior to line.

Parameters:

  • containers (list[tuple[int, str]]): List of (line_number, container_name) tuples.
  • line (int): Current line index.

Returns:

  • str | None: Name of the nearest preceding container, or None.
def _enclosing(containers: list[tuple[int, str]], line: int) -> str | None:
    names = [name for start, name in containers if start < line]
    return names[-1] if names else None

docs.title: _parent_verdict()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _parent_verdict(index: SourceIndex, match: tuple, parent: str) -> bool | None:

Description: Determines whether the enclosing code blocks for a match belong to the claimed parent. Returns True if confirmed, False if confirmed to belong to a different container, or None if undetermined.

Parameters:

  • index (SourceIndex): File source index.
  • match (tuple): Match tuple (first_line, last_line, kind).
  • parent (str): Expected parent symbol name.

Returns:

  • bool | None: Scope validation verdict.
def _parent_verdict(index: SourceIndex, match: tuple, parent: str) -> bool | None:
    if parent in _words(index.text(match[0], match[1])):
        return True
    if not _indent(index.lines[match[0]], 8):
        return None
    for indent, text, kind, named in index.block_chain(match[0]):
        if _names_in(text, parent):
            return True
        if named:
            return False
        if not indent:
            return True if kind == "container" else False if kind == "function" else None
    return None

The function checks receiver parameters (e.g., Go func (c *Cache) Put), C++ class qualifiers (Class::), and enclosing container definitions (class Foo:, Rust impl Foo). It traverses outer blocks while ignoring intermediate control statements and anonymous structures.

docs.title: _in_parent()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _in_parent(index: SourceIndex, match: tuple, parent: str, containers: list) -> bool:

Description: Resolves whether a file-wide symbol match belongs to parent, checking _parent_verdict first and falling back to _enclosing.

Parameters:

  • index (SourceIndex): File source index.
  • match (tuple): Match location tuple.
  • parent (str): Target parent name.
  • containers (list): List of preceding container declarations.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the match is within the parent container.
def _in_parent(index: SourceIndex, match: tuple, parent: str, containers: list) -> bool:
    verdict = _parent_verdict(index, match, parent)
    return verdict if verdict is not None else _enclosing(containers, match[0]) in (None, parent)

docs.title: _call_span()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _call_span(index: SourceIndex, first: int, last: int) -> int:

Description: Scans up to _CALL_SPAN_LINES forward from a match to locate the line where open parentheses or brackets balance out.

Parameters:

  • index (SourceIndex): File source index.
  • first (int): Starting line of match.
  • last (int): Initial ending line of match.

Returns:

  • int: Updated ending line index covering the balanced call span.
def _call_span(index: SourceIndex, first: int, last: int) -> int:
    depth = 0
    for number in range(first, min(len(index.lines), last + 1 + _CALL_SPAN_LINES)):
        code = _STRING_RE.sub('""', index.lines[number])
        depth += code.count("(") + code.count("[") - code.count(")") - code.count("]")
        if number >= last and depth <= 0:
            return number
    return last

docs.title: _name_rank()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _name_rank(text: str, name: str) -> int:

Description: Ranks how name appears in text: 0 for unquoted code, 1 for exact string literals, and 2 for partial substring matches inside larger strings.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Matched code text.
  • name (str): Target identifier name.

Returns:

  • int: Priority rank (0, 1, or 2).
def _name_rank(text: str, name: str) -> int:
    if _names_in(_STRING_RE.sub('""', text), name):
        return 0
    return 1 if any(m.group()[1:-1] == _nfc(name) for m in _STRING_RE.finditer(_nfc(text))) else 2

docs.title: _error_role()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _error_role(index: SourceIndex, first: int, last: int, name: str) -> str:

Description: Determines how an error is used on the line that names it, returning "raised", "caught", or "mentioned".

Parameters:

  • index (SourceIndex): File source index.
  • first (int): Starting line of match.
  • last (int): Ending line of match.
  • name (str): Error class or symbol name.

Returns:

  • str: Role classification string.
def _error_role(index: SourceIndex, first: int, last: int, name: str) -> str:
    pattern = re.compile(r"(?<![\w$])" + re.escape(_nfc(name)) + r"(?![\w$])")
    for number in range(first, last + 1):
        code = _STRING_RE.sub('""', _nfc(index.lines[number]))
        found = pattern.search(code)
        if not found:
            continue
        head = code[: found.start()]
        handler = max((m.end() for m in _HANDLER_RE.finditer(head)), default=-1)
        if re.search(r"(?<![\w.$])on\s+$", head):
            handler = len(head)
        raiser = max((m.end() for m in _RAISE_RE.finditer(head)), default=-1)
        return "caught" if handler > raiser else "raised" if raiser >= 0 else "mentioned"
    return "mentioned"

The function searches lines in the match span for the error name, blanks out string literals, and inspects preceding code tokens. If a handler keyword appears after the last raising keyword, the role is "caught". If a raising keyword appears, it is "raised". Otherwise, it defaults to "mentioned".

docs.title: _find_closer()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _find_closer(line: str, closer: str, start: int) -> int:

Description: Locates the position of a block comment or string closer starting from index start, avoiding false positive comment closers inside directory globs (e.g., build/*/).

Parameters:

  • line (str): Source line.
  • closer (str): Closing token string (e.g., "*/").
  • start (int): Search offset.

Returns:

  • int: Position index, or -1 if not found.
def _find_closer(line: str, closer: str, start: int) -> int:
    position = line.find(closer, start)
    while closer == "*/" and position > 0 and line[position - 1] == "/":
        position = line.find(closer, position + 1)
    return position

docs.title: _rfind_closer()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _rfind_closer(line: str, closer: str) -> int:

Description: Scans backward from the end of line to find the last occurrence of a block closer, ignoring directory globs.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Source line.
  • closer (str): Closing token string.

Returns:

  • int: Column index, or -1 if not found.
def _rfind_closer(line: str, closer: str) -> int:
    position = line.rfind(closer)
    while closer == "*/" and position > 0 and line[position - 1] == "/":
        position = line.rfind(closer, 0, position)
    return position

docs.title: _lead()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _lead(stripped: str) -> tuple[list[str], str | None, str, str]:

Description: Parses leading tokens from a code line, separating modifiers from the initial keyword, separator, and remaining text.

Parameters:

  • stripped (str): Stripped line text.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str | None, str, str]: 4-tuple (modifiers, word, separator, rest).
def _lead(stripped: str) -> tuple[list[str], str | None, str, str]:
    text, modifiers = _ANNOTATIONS_RE.sub("", stripped.lstrip("$")), []
    while True:
        text = re.sub(r"^(\w+)\(\w+\)\s+", r"\1 ", text)  # private(set) var → private var
        lead = _WORD_AT_RE.match(text)
        if not lead:
            return modifiers, None, "", text
        word, separator = lead.group(1), lead.group(2)
        rest = text[lead.end() :]
        is_modifier = word in _DECLARATION_MODIFIERS or (word == "case" and re.match(r"(?:class|object)\b", rest))
        if is_modifier and separator and not separator.strip():
            modifiers.append(word)
            text = rest
            continue
        return modifiers, word, separator, rest

docs.title: _indent()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _indent(line: str, tab: int = 4) -> int:

Description: Calculates the indentation column width of a line, expanding tab characters to a fixed column width.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Source line text.
  • tab (int, optional): Tab expansion column size. Defaults to 4.

Returns:

  • int: Indentation column count.
def _indent(line: str, tab: int = 4) -> int:
    expanded = line.expandtabs(tab)
    return len(expanded) - len(expanded.lstrip())

docs.title: _block_kind()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _block_kind(line: str) -> str | None:

Description: Identifies what kind of structural scope a line opens for subsequent indented lines ("function", "container", "control", "other", or None).

Parameters:

  • line (str): Source line text.

Returns:

  • str | None: Block category string, or None if no block is opened.
def _block_kind(line: str) -> str | None:
    stripped = line.strip()
    if not re.search(r"\w", stripped) or stripped[0] in ")]}" or re.fullmatch(r"end\b\W*", stripped):
        return None
    _modifiers, word, separator, rest = _lead(stripped)
    if word in _FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return "function"
    if word in _CONTAINER_WORDS:
        return "container"
    if word in _BLOCK_CONTROL_WORDS:
        return "control"
    if _CLOSURE_RE.search(stripped) or (word and _METHOD_RE.match(f"{word}{separator}{rest}") and re.search(r"[)\]{:]\s*$", stripped)):
        return "function"  # a callback (describe('x', () => {), a method head (public void run() {, int main(void))
    return "other"

docs.title: _nameless()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _nameless(text: str) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a container declaration line is anonymous (e.g., companion object {, class << self, typedef struct {).

Parameters:

  • text (str): Declaration line text.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the container declaration specifies no name.
def _nameless(text: str) -> bool:
    rest = _ANNOTATIONS_RE.sub("", text.strip())
    while True:
        rest = re.sub(r"^<[^<>]*>\s*", "", rest)
        word = re.match(r"([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*", rest)
        if word and (word.group(1) in _CONTAINER_WORDS or word.group(1) in _DECLARATION_MODIFIERS):
            rest = rest[word.end() :]
            continue
        return not re.match(r"[A-Za-z_$]", rest)

docs.title: _block_chains()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _block_chains(lines: list[str]) -> list[tuple]:

Description: Analyzes indented blocks across lines in a single pass, returning an inheritance chain of enclosing blocks for each line.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): List of source lines.

Returns:

  • list[tuple]: Per-line list of tuples containing (indent, text, kind, named).
def _block_chains(lines: list[str]) -> list[tuple]:
    chains, stack = [], []
    for text in code_view(lines):
        indent = _indent(text, 8)
        chains.append(tuple(entry for entry in reversed(stack) if entry[0] < indent))
        if not re.search(r"\w", text) or _COMMENT_START_RE.match(text):
            continue
        kind = _block_kind(text)
        label = _LABEL_RE.fullmatch(text)
        if kind is None or (label and kind != "container" and (label.group(1) or label.group(2)) not in _BLOCK_CONTROL_WORDS):
            continue
        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        stack.append((indent, text, kind, kind == "container" and not _nameless(text)))
    return chains

docs.title: _declares_name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _declares_name(line: str, name: str, keys: set | None = None) -> bool:

Description: Verifies whether a manifest line declares name as an output package rather than referencing it as a dependency.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Manifest line text.
  • name (str): Candidate package name.
  • keys (set | None, optional): Allowed declaration keys. Defaults to _NAME_KEYS.

Returns:

  • bool: True if name is preceded by a valid declaration key outside nested brackets.
def _declares_name(line: str, name: str, keys: set | None = None) -> bool:
    before = line.split(_collapse(name), 1)[0]
    words = _words(before)[-3:]
    key_at = max((before.rfind(word) for word in words if word.casefold() in (keys or _NAME_KEYS)), default=-1)
    return key_at >= 0 and not re.search(r"[{(]", before[:key_at])
