docs.title: ModuleTable._suffix_hits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _suffix_hits(self, tail: list[str], ext: str, source_path: str) -> list[str]:

Description: Searches known module paths for entries whose terminal segments match tail, checking exact case first and falling back to case-insensitive matching.

Parameters:

  • tail (list[str]): Ordered path segments to match.
  • ext (str): File extension constraint.
  • source_path (str): Path of importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List of matching module paths.
    def _suffix_hits(self, tail: list[str], ext: str, source_path: str) -> list[str]:
        for fold in (str, str.casefold):
            wanted = [fold(part) for part in tail]
            hits = [
                path
                for path in self.paths
                if path != source_path and (not ext or path.endswith(ext)) and [fold(part) for part in self.segments[path][-len(tail) :]] == wanted
            ]
            if len(hits) > 1:
                near = [path for path in hits if posixpath.dirname(path) == posixpath.dirname(source_path)]
                if len(near) == 1:
                    return near
            if hits:
                return hits
        return []

docs.title: ModuleTable._index_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _index_file(self, directory: str) -> str | None:

Description: Finds the standard package index or entrypoint file in a directory based on _INDEX_STEMS order of preference (mod, index, __init__, init, main, lib).

Parameters:

  • directory (str): Directory path to search.

Returns:

  • str | None: Path to the directory entrypoint file, or None.
    def _index_file(self, directory: str) -> str | None:
        members = {_stem(path): path for path in self.by_dir.get(directory, [])}
        return next((members[stem] for stem in _INDEX_STEMS if stem in members), None)

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_relative()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_relative(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves relative path targets (./, ../, super::, leading dots) against the importing file's directory.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Target string.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Words present in the importing source.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str] | None: (paths, mechanism) or None if target is not relative.
    def _resolve_relative(self, target: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
        text = target.strip().strip("\"'`<>()[];,").replace("\\", "/")
        parent = re.match(r"^super(?:::(.*))?$", text)
        if parent:  # `super` names the parent module: the directory's index file, or one level up from an index file
            # ... resolves Rust super module paths ...
        dots = re.match(r"^(\.+)(\w[\w.]*)$", text)
        if dots:
            text = "../" * (len(dots.group(1)) - 1) + "./" + dots.group(2).replace(".", "/")
        if not text.startswith(("./", "../")):
            return None
        base = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(source_path), text))
        resolved = self._resolve_rooted(base, source_path, source_words)
        if resolved is not None:
            return resolved
        if dots:
            return [], "external"
        return None

docs.title: ModuleTable._resolve_rooted()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_rooted(self, base: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:

Description: Resolves a project-root-relative path against known module files and package directories.

Parameters:

  • base (str): Normalized root-relative base path.
  • source_path (str): Importing module path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing module.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], str] | None: Matched module path list and resolution kind, or None.
    def _resolve_rooted(self, base: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
        base = "" if base in (".", "") else base
        stem_match = [path for path in self.paths if path != source_path and (os.path.splitext(path)[0] == base or path == base)]
        if not stem_match:  # every extension dropped
            stem_match = [
                path
                for path in self.paths
                if path != source_path and posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(path), posixpath.basename(path).split(".")[0]) == base
            ]
        if len(stem_match) == 1:
            return stem_match, "path"
        if not stem_match and base in self.by_dir:  # a directory: its index file and the files whose names the source uses
            index_file = self._index_file(base)
            used = [
                path for path in self.by_dir[base] if path != source_path and (path == index_file or self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
            ]
            if used:
                return used, "package"  # the evidence names the directory, not a file in it
        return None

docs.title: ModuleTable._matches_whole()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _matches_whole(self, target: str, source_path: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies whether all segments of target match the end of an existing file or directory path (e.g., Maven com.acme.billing.Invoice matching .../com/acme/billing/Invoice.java).

Parameters:

  • target (str): Import target string.
  • source_path (str): Current source path.

Returns:

  • bool: True if every segment matches an existing path suffix.
    def _matches_whole(self, target: str, source_path: str) -> bool:
        parts, _ = self.normalize(target)
        return bool(parts) and (
            any(path != source_path and self.segments[path][-len(parts) :] == parts for path in self.paths)
            or any(d.split("/")[-len(parts) :] == parts for d in self.by_dir if d)
        )

Visibility: Private

Signature: def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:

Description: Resolves entrypoint files for a package directory, checking manifest entry, standard index files, and package-named files (e.g., lib/shop.rb).

Parameters:

  • package (dict): Package descriptor dictionary.
  • under (list[str]): Modules residing under the package directory.
  • source_path (str): Importing file path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing file.

Returns:

  • list[str]: List containing entrypoint module path(s).
    def _package_root(self, package: dict, under: list[str], source_path: str, source_words: set) -> list[str]:
        directory, entry, last = package["dir"], package["entry"], package["segments"][-1] if package["segments"] else ""
        if entry:
            hits = [path for path in under if path == entry or os.path.splitext(path)[0] == os.path.splitext(entry)[0]]
            if hits:
                return hits[:1]
        for sub in ("", "src", "lib", last, f"src/{last}"):
            index_file = self._index_file(posixpath.join(directory, sub).rstrip("/") if sub else directory)
            if index_file and index_file in under:
                return [index_file]
        # ... checks files named after the package stem and falls back to used_names ...

docs.title: ModuleTable._corroborated()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:

Description: Verifies that a suffix match is corroborated by aliases, namespace declarations, or used symbol names when leading segments of a qualified target are dropped.

Parameters:

  • target (str): Original target string.
  • parts (list[str]): Full normalized segments.
  • size (int): Suffix length that matched.
  • path (str): Matched module path candidate.
  • source_path (str): Importing source path.
  • source_words (set): Tokens in importing source.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the match is corroborated.
    def _corroborated(self, target: str, parts: list[str], size: int, path: str, source_path: str, source_words: set) -> bool:
        if size < len(parts):
            dropped = parts[: len(parts) - size]
            alias = not re.match(r"\w", dropped[0]) and not (self.packages or self.aliases)  # manifests declare the real aliases
            return alias or declares_namespace(self.contents.get(path, ""), dropped[-1]) or bool(self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
        if len(parts) == 1 and not _is_relative(target):
            directory, source_dir = posixpath.dirname(path), posixpath.dirname(source_path)
            ancestor = not directory or source_dir == directory or source_dir.startswith(directory + "/")
            return ancestor or bool(self.used_names(path, source_path, source_words))
        return True

docs.title: _names_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether name appears in evidence as part of a path or qualified module reference rather than an unadorned identifier.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence line text.
  • name (str): Candidate module stem name.
  • extension (str): Expected file extension.
  • extensions (set): Set of all project extensions.

Returns:

  • bool: True if name is qualified by path delimiters, quotes, or file extensions.
def _names_path(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:
    for match in re.finditer(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}(?!\w)", evidence):
        before = evidence[match.start() - 1] if match.start() else ""
        after = evidence[match.end() :]
        written = re.match(r"\.\w+", after)
        if written and written.group() in extensions and written.group() != extension:
            continue
        if before in _QUALIFIERS or (extension and after.startswith(extension)) or (after and after[0] in _CLOSERS):
            return True
    return False

docs.title: _plain_occurrence()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether name appears in evidence as a distinct token rather than referring to a sibling file with a different extension (e.g., socket in socket.h does not match socket.cpp).

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Line text.
  • name (str): Filename stem.
  • extension (str): Target file extension.
  • extensions (set): All project extensions.

Returns:

  • bool: True if a valid plain occurrence exists.
def _plain_occurrence(evidence: str, name: str, extension: str, extensions: set) -> bool:
    for match in re.finditer(rf"(?<!\w){re.escape(name)}(?!\w)", evidence):
        written = re.match(r"\.\w+", evidence[match.end() :])
        if not (written and written.group() in extensions and written.group() != extension):
            return True
    return False

docs.title: _names_directory()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether evidence references directory by its terminal segments as a path or dotted namespace.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence line text.
  • directory (str): Target directory path.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the directory is referenced.
def _names_directory(evidence: str, directory: str) -> bool:
    tail = [re.escape(part) for part in directory.split("/")[-2:]]
    return re.search(r"(?<!\w)" + r"(?:\.|/|\\|::)".join(tail) + r"(?!\w)", evidence) is not None

docs.title: _import_like()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether an evidence line begins with an import-related keyword after stripping modifiers.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Line text.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the line starts with an import keyword.
def _import_like(evidence: str) -> bool:
    words = _words(evidence.lstrip().lstrip("#@"))
    while words and words[0] in _MODIFIERS:  # pub mod routes; pub(crate) use ...; public import ...
        words = words[1:]
    return bool(words) and words[0] in _IMPORT_WORDS

docs.title: _without_bindings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:

Description: Strips local alias bindings (as alias, => alias, import x = y) from an import line so that only imported modules and symbols remain.

Parameters:

  • line (str): Import line text.

Returns:

  • str: Sanitized line text with local binding names removed.
def _without_bindings(line: str) -> str:
    line = re.sub(r"\bas\s+[\w$]+", " ", line)
    line = re.sub(r"=>\s*[\w$]+", " ", line)
    return re.sub(r"^(\s*(?:global\s+)?(?:using|import)\s+)[\w$]+\s*=(?!=)", r"\1", line)

docs.title: _bare_path()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:

Description: Strips leading relative path prefixes (./, ../, /, leading dots) from a path string.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Path string.

Returns:

  • str: Cleaned path without leading directory navigations.
def _bare_path(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"^(?:\.{1,2}/|/|\.+)+", "", text)

docs.title: _imports_target()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether evidence actively imports target via an import statement, Go block specifier, or inline qualified code reference, excluding comments and string literals.

Parameters:

  • evidence (str): Evidence line text.
  • target (str): Import target string.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the target is imported.
def _imports_target(evidence: str, target: str) -> bool:
    lines = split_lines(evidence)
    quoted = re.escape(target.strip().strip("\"'`<>"))
    if any(import_statement_like(line) or _GO_BLOCK_LINE_RE.match(line) for line in lines) or re.search(rf"[\"'`<]{quoted}[\"'`>]", evidence):
        return True
    for line in lines:
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith(("//", "#", "/*", "*", "--", ";")):
            continue
        code = re.sub(r"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|`[^`]*`", " ", line)
        if re.search(rf"(?<![\w-]){quoted}(?:::|\.)\w", code):
            return True
    return False

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements a non-crashing, audit-style error handling architecture. Claims that fail verification are recorded in rejected lists with explicit reasons rather than raising fatal exceptions:

# Example of non-fatal claim rejection inside verify_file_claims()
if not matches:
    rejected.append({"kind": "dependency", "target": target, "evidence": evidence, "reason": "evidence not in source"})
    continue

Notable error and fallback patterns across the module include:

  • File System and Deserialization Trapping: load_facts() wraps file loading in a try...except (OSError, ValueError): block, returning an empty dictionary on missing files, permission errors, or invalid JSON.
  • Subprocess Isolation: source_commit() handles subprocess invocations within a try...except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError): guard with a 10-second timeout, gracefully returning None if git is unavailable or the directory is not a git repository.
  • Atomic File Updates: save_facts() writes serialized JSON to a temporary file (.tmp) before calling os.replace(), preventing corrupt or partial writes if the process is terminated mid-execution.
  • Progressive Search Fallbacks: SourceIndex.locate() uses a three-tier fallback (exact single-line match, squashed multiline match, rare token-order search) to tolerate variations in LLM formatting without throwing search errors.
  • Ambiguous Resolution Handling: When an import target matches multiple internal files without corroborating context, ModuleTable.resolve() returns ([], "ambiguous"), allowing judge_dependency() to record a rejection reason ("target matches several modules") rather than picking an arbitrary file.

docs.title: files.py
docs.text: Source: utils/files.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/files.py module provides foundational, in-memory filesystem aggregation and extraction utilities for the Codebase Knowledge Builder pipeline. During the repository ingestion phase, source code extractors such as crawl_local_files.py and crawl_github_files.py scan target repositories and normalize codebase files into ordered lists of (path, content) tuples. This module acts as the formatting and selective retrieval layer that translates these raw tuple collections into token-efficient structural representations and contextual prompt payloads for large language model (LLM) processing nodes.

The module provides two deterministic operations: build_directory_tree and get_content_for_indices. The build_directory_tree function reorganizes linear file records into a two-level lexicographically sorted directory hierarchy where each file is tagged with its array index. This compact tree allows reasoning nodes (such as context routing and abstraction mapping) to inspect the complete directory topology without exhausting prompt context windows on full file contents. The get_content_for_indices function provides surgical extraction of source contents for specific index subsets identified by downstream analysis, generating contextual composite keys that combine positional indices with relative file paths.

Both functions are deterministic, side-effect-free, and stateless. Directory grouping leverages standard library associative containers (collections.defaultdict) and explicit sorting to guarantee identical output regardless of the underlying operating system or crawl order. Defensive indexing prevents out-of-bounds exceptions when processing LLM-selected file indices, ensuring that transient model hallucinations or empty index sets do not crash pipeline nodes.

docs.title: build_directory_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_directory_tree(files_data):

Description: Constructs a compact, human- and machine-readable directory tree string from an enumerated list of (path, content) tuples. The function groups files under their parent directory, appends each file's positional index in the format (idx:{i}), and sorts both directory paths and file entries lexicographically to guarantee deterministic output.

Parameters:

  • files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): Ordered list of 2-tuples where each element consists of a relative file path (str) and the corresponding file content (str).

Returns:

  • str: A multi-line string representing the directory structure, with directory headers terminated by / and nested files indented by two spaces.

Raises:

  • TypeError: Raised if files_data is not iterable or contains elements that cannot be unpacked into a 2-tuple.

Example:

def build_directory_tree(files_data):
    """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples.

    Groups files by directory and formats as a hierarchical tree with file indices.
    Used by ContextRouter, IdentifyAbstractions, MapAbstractions, and CombineTutorial
    to give LLMs structural context about the project layout.
    """
    dir_files = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
        basename = os.path.basename(path)
        dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

    lines = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
        lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
        lines.extend(f"  {fname}" for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]))
    return "\n".join(lines)

The function iterates over files_data using enumerate to track each item's integer index. For each file path, it splits the string into its directory path and base filename using os.path.dirname and os.path.basename. When a file resides in the root scanning directory, os.path.dirname evaluates to an empty string; the expression dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "." ensures such files are grouped under the . directory. Filenames are formatted with their index suffix (f"{basename} (idx:{i})") and collected in a defaultdict(list). Finally, directory keys are sorted alphabetically, each directory is printed with a trailing slash (f"{dirname}/"), and its associated file entries are sorted and indented by two spaces before being joined by newline characters.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):

Description: Retrieves file contents for a specific sequence of integer indices from the files_data list. For each valid index, it constructs a dictionary key that pairs the index with the file path (f"{i} # {path}"), mapping directly to the file's raw content string.

Parameters:

  • files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): Ordered list of (path, content) tuples representing the codebase.
  • indices (iterable[int]): Collection of integer indices indicating which files should be extracted.

Returns:

  • dict[str, str]: Mapping where keys are formatted as "{index} # {relative_path}" and values are file text contents.

Raises:

  • TypeError: Raised if indices is not iterable or if files_data does not support indexed sequence access.

Example:

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    """Get file content for specific indices from files_data list."""
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

The function initializes an empty content_map dictionary and iterates through the provided indices sequence. Before accessing files_data, it verifies bounds using 0 <= i < len(files_data). If the index is negative or greater than or equal to the length of files_data, the entry is bypassed without throwing an IndexError. For each valid index, the corresponding (path, content) tuple is unpacked, and a composite key formatted as f"{i} # {path}" is populated with content. This composite key structure embeds index tracking and file provenance directly into downstream prompt templates without requiring secondary dictionary lookups.

docs.text:
The primary input contract accepted by both functions in utils/files.py. It is an ordered sequence representing all ingested repository files.

docs.text:
The formatted string output produced by build_directory_tree(). It structures repository paths into a two-space indented hierarchy.

Component Format Description Directory Header {dirname}/ Directory path terminated by a trailing slash, sorted alphabetically. Root files use ./. File Line {basename} (idx:{i}) File name indented by two spaces, followed by (idx:{i}) where {i} is the integer index in files_data.

utils/

docs.title: Index boundary protection
docs.text:
In get_content_for_indices(), index lookups are guarded against IndexError using an explicit boundary check:

if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
    path, content = files_data[i]
    content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content

When an LLM hallucination or an upstream routing step supplies an out-of-bounds index (e.g., negative indices or values exceeding len(files_data) - 1), the module discards the invalid index silently rather than raising an exception. This guarantees non-crashing behavior during prompt preparation loops.

docs.title: Root path resolution fallback
docs.text:
In build_directory_tree(), root-level files whose paths contain no directory delimiters cause os.path.dirname(path) to return an empty string (""):

dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."

By using the logical or "." fallback, empty strings are normalized to ".", preventing orphan files from rendering with a leading / or causing malformed tree lines.

docs.title: Empty payload handling
docs.text: Both functions handle empty inputs gracefully: * If files_data is empty ([]), build_directory_tree returns an empty string (""), and get_content_for_indices returns an empty dictionary ({}). * If indices is empty ([]), get_content_for_indices immediately returns an empty dictionary ({}).

docs.title: i18n.py
docs.text: Source: utils/i18n.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/i18n.py module provides an automated runtime internationalization (i18n) and translation synchronization engine for the application's user interface strings. It inspects the localization catalog (strings.csv), identifies missing or untranslated UI messages for a specified target language, compiles an inference payload, and dispatches a translation request via a configured Large Language Model (LLM). Once translated, the module dynamically extends the schema of strings.csv (adding language columns as needed) and persists the updated string catalog to disk using UTF-8 with Byte Order Mark (utf-8-sig) encoding.

Architecturally, this module was decoupled from utils/output.py to resolve a critical circular dependency chain: output.py $\rightarrow$ call_llm.py $\rightarrow$ token_utils.py $\rightarrow$ output.py. Under this decoupled architecture, utils.output delegates missing string resolution to utils.i18n, isolating all direct interactions with utils.call_llm and utils.token_utils inside this single module.

The translation pipeline operates non-destructively: if the target language is already English, if the localization datastore does not exist, or if an inference error occurs, the module logs diagnostic telemetry and safely falls back to English without halting downstream application execution.

docs.title: auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def auto_translate(lang_col, language, csv_path, use_cache, thinking_level):

Description: Orchestrates the automated translation of missing localized strings. It checks whether translations are required, prepares and formats a translation prompt with missing English key-value pairs, logs token estimations, invokes the LLM through call_llm(), parses the JSON response via regular expressions, and updates strings.csv.

Because this function coordinates several discrete logical sub-tasks—file inspection, prompt compilation, LLM querying, and disk serialization—its implementation is analyzed across four logical phases below.

docs.title: Phase 1: Pre-condition Validation and String Scanning
docs.text:
from utils.output import emit_raw

    if lang_col == "english":
        return False

    if not csv_path or not os.path.exists(csv_path):
        return False

    # Collect strings that have no translation in the target language column
    missing = {}
    is_new_column = False
    with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        is_new_column = lang_col not in fieldnames
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue
            # Check if the language column exists and has a value
            lang_text = row.get(lang_col, "").strip() if lang_col in fieldnames else ""
            if lang_text:
                continue  # Already translated

            english_text = row.get("english", "").strip()
            if english_text:
                missing[key] = english_text

    if not missing:
        return False

Phase 1 evaluates fast-return conditions: if the requested language is already English or if csv_path does not exist on disk, execution terminates immediately with False. Otherwise, it opens the localization CSV file with utf-8-sig encoding using csv.DictReader. It determines whether lang_col represents a new column in the CSV schema and iterates across each row, discarding empty keys and comment rows prefixed with #. If the cell corresponding to lang_col is blank or nonexistent, the corresponding English string is extracted into the missing dictionary. If no strings require translation, the function exits early.

docs.title: Phase 2: Prompt Compilation and Token Estimation
docs.text:
# Report what we found
    if is_new_column:
        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] New language '{language}' — adding column to strings.csv")
    emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] {len(missing)} strings need translation to {language}")

    # Batch translate via LLM
    try:
        from utils.call_llm import call_llm

        entries_json = json.dumps(missing, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

        # Load prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md
        prompt_path = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
            "prompts",
            "common",
            "translate_strings.md",
        )
        with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8") as pf:
            prompt_template = pf.read()
        prompt = prompt_template.format(language=language, entries=entries_json)

        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] Calling LLM to translate {len(missing)} strings...")
        from utils.token_utils import log_token_estimation, resolve_max_tokens

        try:
            context_tokens = resolve_max_tokens({})
        except Exception:
            context_tokens = 0
        log_token_estimation("TranslateStrings", prompt, context_tokens)

In Phase 2, telemetry notifications are broadcast to the user interface via emit_raw(), informing consumers of column additions and the count of pending strings. The missing string dictionary is serialized into a formatted JSON string (entries_json) with Unicode preservation (ensure_ascii=False). The function then dynamically resolves the absolute path to prompts/common/translate_strings.md, reads the template, and interpolates the target language name and entries JSON. Token budgeting is performed by resolving maximum available context tokens via resolve_max_tokens({}) and recording metrics through log_token_estimation().

docs.title: Phase 3: Model Invocation and JSON Extraction
docs.text:
response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=use_cache, thinking_level=thinking_level, step="translate_strings")

        # Extract JSON from response
        json_match = re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL)
        if json_match:
            translations = json.loads(json_match.group())
            translated_count = len(translations)

            # Write translations back into strings.csv
            _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations)
            emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] Translated {translated_count}/{len(missing)} strings — saved to strings.csv")
            return True
        emit_raw("WARNING", "[i18n] LLM response did not contain valid JSON — falling back to English")

Phase 3 executes the model inference request using call_llm(), tagging the execution step as "translate_strings" and forwarding caller-specified caching and reasoning levels. Because language models may wrap responses in explanatory conversational text or code block markers, an extraction regex (r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}") scans the raw text with re.DOTALL to isolate the root JSON object. If a matching JSON payload is found, it is deserialized into a Python dictionary. The helper _write_translations_to_csv() is invoked to persist results to disk, an informational success message is emitted, and True is returned. If parsing fails, a warning is broadcast.

docs.title: Phase 4: Exception Handling and Fallback
docs.text:
except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"[i18n] Translation failed: {e} — falling back to English")

    return False

Phase 4 serves as the fallback boundary. The entire inference, estimation, and deserialization block is encapsulated in an untyped try...except Exception clause. If any step fails—such as prompt file I/O errors, network disconnections during LLM execution, token calculation issues, or malformed JSON payloads—the exception is trapped, a descriptive warning is emitted using emit_raw(), and the function returns False. This guarantees that localization failures never crash the host application.

Parameters:

  • lang_col (str): Lowercase column name representing the language in strings.csv (e.g., "vietnamese", "japanese").
  • language (str): Capitalized human-readable language display name passed to the prompt template (e.g., "Vietnamese").
  • csv_path (str): Absolute filesystem path to the target strings.csv datastore.
  • use_cache (bool): Flag determining whether LLM response caching is enabled in call_llm().
  • thinking_level (str | None): Model reasoning effort parameter passed to call_llm().

Returns:

  • bool: True if new translations were received and persisted to the CSV file (indicating that the caller should invalidate and reload in-memory string caches); False if no changes occurred or if translation failed.

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; all internal runtime exceptions are caught and logged as warnings.

Example:

# Invocation pattern within localization setup routines
updated = auto_translate(
    lang_col="vietnamese",
    language="Vietnamese",
    csv_path="/path/to/project/utils/strings.csv",
    use_cache=True,
    thinking_level="low",
)

if updated:
    # Caller reloads localization cache
    pass

docs.title: _write_translations_to_csv()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations):

Description: Persists newly generated translation mappings into strings.csv. It reads the entire file into memory using csv.DictReader to preserve existing translations, appends lang_col to fieldnames if it does not already exist, maps new translated values against row keys, and writes the updated dataset back to disk via csv.DictWriter. The destination file is opened with utf-8-sig encoding and empty newline termination (newline="") to ensure compatibility with spreadsheet editors like Microsoft Excel without character corruption.

def _write_translations_to_csv(csv_path, lang_col, fieldnames, translations):
    """Write LLM translations back into strings.csv, persisting them for future runs.

    If the target language column doesn't exist, it is added to the CSV.
    """
    rows = []

    with open(csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        # Add language column if it doesn't exist
        if lang_col not in fieldnames:
            fieldnames.append(lang_col)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if key in translations:
                row[lang_col] = translations[key]
            rows.append(row)

    # Write with BOM so Excel opens as UTF-8 without extra import steps
    with open(csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)

The function executes a complete in-memory read-modify-write cycle. When appending a new column, the updated fieldnames list is captured dynamically from the active file rather than relying exclusively on caller arguments, mitigating race conditions where columns may have shifted. As it loops through each record, keys present in the translations dictionary update the corresponding row's lang_col entry in-place. Finally, csv.DictWriter.writeheader() and writerows() serialize the mutated state back to csv_path with BOM encoding.

Parameters:

  • csv_path (str): Absolute filesystem path to the strings.csv file.
  • lang_col (str): Lowercase target language column identifier to update or append.
  • fieldnames (list[str]): List of current header field names extracted from strings.csv.
  • translations (dict[str, str]): Mapping of string keys to their translated values returned by the LLM.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates the file system artifact in-place.

Raises:

  • OSError: If the target CSV file cannot be opened for reading or writing due to filesystem permissions.
  • csv.Error: If CSV formatting or field mismatch anomalies occur during writing.

Example:

# Direct implementation usage from auto_translate()
_write_translations_to_csv(
    csv_path="/workspace/utils/strings.csv",
    lang_col="vietnamese",
    fieldnames=["STRING_KEY", "english"],
    translations={
        "PROGRESS_ANALYZING": "Đang phân tích mã nguồn...",
        "ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND": "Không tìm thấy tệp tin.",
    },
)

docs.title: Data Structures
docs.text: The module does not declare custom object classes; instead, it manipulates structured dictionaries and CSV datastores.

docs.title: strings.csv Schema
docs.text:
Represents the physical schema of the persistent tabular localization datastore:

Field Type Description STRING_KEY str Unique uppercase identifier for the UI string. Lines beginning with # are treated as comments and ignored. english str Canonical source text in English, used as the fallback and translation baseline. [lang_col] str Dynamic target language columns (e.g., vietnamese, japanese, spanish) containing translated string values.

docs.title: Missing Strings Payload
docs.text:
The internal dictionary constructed in Phase 1 and serialized as entries_json for prompt injection:

Key Type Description [STRING_KEY] str Mapping key representing the untranslated identifier (e.g., "PROMPT_RUNNING"). value str The corresponding baseline English string to be translated.

Example structure: 

{
  "STAGE_EXTRACT_FACTS": "Extracting architectural facts from codebase...",
  "WARN_FILE_BINARY": "Skipping binary file {path}"
}

docs.title: LLM Translations Response Payload
docs.text:
The parsed dictionary extracted from the LLM's raw text response:

Key Type Description [STRING_KEY] str String key corresponding to a requested key from the missing dictionary. value str Translated localized string ready to be inserted into the target column.

Example structure: 

{
  "STAGE_EXTRACT_FACTS": "Trích xuất các dữ kiện kiến trúc từ mã nguồn...",
  "WARN_FILE_BINARY": "Bỏ qua tệp nhị phân {path}"
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements a robust, non-terminating error-handling strategy to ensure that localization failures do not disrupt the broader execution pipeline:

  • Short-Circuit Bypass: Calls targeting "english" or pointing to a non-existent CSV path exit immediately returning False, bypassing all network and disk overhead.
  • Comment and Blank Filtering: When processing rows from strings.csv, empty string keys or rows where STRING_KEY begins with # are skipped.
  • Broad Exception Shield: The entire translation sequence—encompassing prompt formatting, token estimation, network inference, and response parsing—is guarded by a top-level except Exception block. Errors are caught, surfaced to the UI via emit_raw("WARNING", ...), and resolved by falling back to English strings.
  • Regex-Based JSON Recovery: Model outputs often contain markdown formatting fences or conversational framing. The module uses re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL) to locate and isolate the core JSON object before invoking json.loads().
  • Safe Encoding Practices: All file reads and writes explicitly designate encoding="utf-8-sig". This ensures byte-order marks are properly recognized across POSIX and Windows environments and prevents text corruption in external editors.

docs.title: llm_anthropic.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_anthropic.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/llm_anthropic.py module serves as the native Anthropic Claude client integration layer for the Codebase Knowledge Builder pipeline. It encapsulates all Claude-specific request framing, configuration negotiation, response parsing, and error-recovery behaviors, allowing the higher-level dispatch layer in call_llm.py to remain provider-agnostic. By isolating the anthropic SDK dependency within this module, downstream execution environments that run alternative providers (such as Gemini or OpenRouter) can operate without installing the proprietary Anthropic client library.

Architecturally, the module adapts to modern Claude capabilities across model families (including Claude 5, Claude 4.6, and Haiku 4.5). It natively implements adaptive thinking protocols, mapping user reasoning levels (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) to engine-compatible output configurations or token-budgeted thinking structures. To prevent HTTP connection timeouts under massive output budgets (up to 128,000 tokens), all network invocations are dispatched over streaming connections. Furthermore, the module handles safety refusal mitigations using Anthropic server-side fallback betas and executes automated single-step token budget expansion when responses are truncated by context ceilings.

The module also acts as a precise cost accounting and token telemetry engine. It calculates financial expenditures using longest-prefix pricing rules that factor in prompt caching reads, five-minute cache writes, thinking token overheads, and per-iteration server-side fallback attempts. It feeds observed prompt token deviations back into the pipeline's runtime calibration engine, ensuring that token estimation multipliers remain synchronized with real API token counts throughout long documentation runs.
