docs.title: get_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Resolves the active Anthropic model identifier. It inspects the ANTHROPIC_MODEL environment variable and falls back to the system default defined in DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL (claude-sonnet-5).

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • str: The target model name to be used for API requests.

Raises:

None.

Example:

model = get_model()
effort = normalize_effort(model, thinking_level)

The function queries os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_MODEL") to allow runtime overrides from the environment. If the variable is unset or empty, it defaults cleanly to DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL. This decoupling allows pipeline configurations to specify alternative Claude variants (such as claude-opus-5-5 or claude-haiku-4-5) without altering downstream code.

docs.title: uses_adaptive_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def uses_adaptive_thinking(model: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether a specified model supports adaptive thinking configurations or requires explicit token budget specifications.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier string to evaluate.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the model matches prefixes defined in ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES, False otherwise.

Raises:

None.

Example:

if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
    if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
        thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
        if is_debug():
            thinking["display"] = "summarized"
        params["thinking"] = thinking

The function matches the provided model string against _ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES via _matches. Models supporting adaptive thinking handle internal reasoning tokens without an explicit numeric budget_tokens threshold, instead expecting an output_config.effort parameter. Older architectures or specific models like Haiku 4.5 evaluate to False, signaling to request builders that budget allocations must be statically declared.

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Retrieves the context window and maximum output token capacity for a designated Claude model. It inspects an in-memory session cache, queries the Anthropic Models API via the SDK client if uncached, and falls back to offline default constants if the API endpoint cannot be reached or returns an error.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier string.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A 2-tuple containing (context_window, max_output_tokens).

Raises:

None. API exceptions are trapped internally, logged as warnings, and converted to offline fallback defaults.

Example:

# From _resolve_max_tokens implementation:
context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
cap = anthropic_output_cap()
wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)

The function first consults _model_limits_cache to eliminate redundant network operations during sequential processing. If absent, it queries _get_client().models.retrieve(model). If the Models API returns successfully, it extracts max_input_tokens and max_tokens. In the event of an anthropic.APIError, it emits a WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP event and extracts predefined bounds from _MODEL_LIMITS or _DEFAULT_LIMITS (1_000_000 context window, 128_000 max output tokens).

docs.title: normalize_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Validates and maps a generic pipeline thinking level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) to an effort configuration accepted by the target model.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The target model identifier.
  • level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort string, or None to adopt model defaults.

Returns:

  • str | None: The normalized effort string accepted by the Anthropic API, or None if the model or level adopts defaults.

Raises:

None. Invalid configurations surface a warning diagnostic and return None.

Example:

model = get_model()
effort = normalize_effort(model, thinking_level)
raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)

The function delegates to anthropic_effort(model, level) imported from utils.llm_config. This normalizes user-provided configurations (for example, downscaling xhigh to high on the Claude 4.6 family or mapping minimal to low). If a non-empty level fails normalization, the function emits a WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_INVALID event through utils.output before returning None.

docs.title: call_anthropic()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_anthropic(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches a single-turn prompt to the Anthropic API and returns the generated textual response. It handles token budget estimation, output clamping, streaming execution, server-side fallback detection, automatic truncation retries, cost accounting, and refusal error propagation.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The prompt payload to send to Claude.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): The reasoning effort level requested by the caller ("low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", or None). Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The generated text response. If the response was truncated by output token limits even after retry, an instance of TruncatedResponse (a subclass of str) is returned.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: Raised when the Anthropic safety classifiers decline the request (stop_reason == "refusal").

docs.title: Phase 1: Parameter Configuration and Token Budgeting
docs.text:
model = get_model()
    effort = normalize_effort(model, thinking_level)
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt
    max_tokens, ceiling = _resolve_max_tokens(int(raw_tokens * token_ratio()), model, effort)
    params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, max_tokens)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"Anthropic request | model={model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | max_tokens={max_tokens:,} | "
        f"fallbacks={'on' if betas else 'off'} | prompt_cache={'on' if 'cache_control' in params else 'off'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

Phase 1 resolves the target model and normalizes the thinking effort level. It measures the input prompt tokens using count_tokens_raw and scales them by the runtime token ratio from token_utils. Using _resolve_max_tokens, it computes both the initial planned budget (max_tokens) and the upper hard limit (ceiling). Finally, _build_request frames the parameters dictionary and beta header list.

docs.title: Phase 2: Initial Streaming Request Dispatch
docs.text:
start = time.time()
    message = _send(params, betas)

Phase 2 initiates execution through _send. The invocation utilizes a streaming connection to prevent HTTP connection timeouts on massive context payloads. Network-level socket and transport errors are handled within the Anthropic client SDK, while beta-level 400 Bad Request rejections trigger internal fallback disabling and retries within _send.

docs.title: Phase 3: Dynamic Truncation Recovery
docs.text:
if message.stop_reason == "max_tokens" and max_tokens < ceiling:
        # Thinking + reply outgrew the budget: retry once at the largest budget that fits.
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED_RETRY", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}", cap=f"{ceiling:,}")
        _record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model, observe=False)  # same prompt: observe once
        params, betas = _build_request(prompt, model, effort, ceiling)
        start = time.time()
        message = _send(params, betas)

Phase 3 evaluates whether the generation halted prematurely due to stop_reason == "max_tokens". If the planned max_tokens was clamped below the maximum possible ceiling, the system logs usage for the initial truncated attempt with observe=False and immediately retries the request with max_tokens expanded directly to ceiling.

docs.title: Phase 4: Usage Accounting and Telemetry Recording
docs.text:
_record_usage(message, raw_tokens, effort, time.time() - start, model=model)
    if is_debug():
        _log_thinking(message)

    if _served_by_fallback(message) and message.stop_reason != "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "fallbacks")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_SERVED", model=model, served_by=getattr(message, "model", "unknown"))

Phase 4 records comprehensive accounting metrics for the finalized message via _record_usage. It captures input, output, cache-read, cache-creation, and thinking tokens across all attempt iterations. If debug mode is active, it logs the summarized reasoning chain. If the request was fulfilled by a fallback model, telemetry counters increment and an advisory warning emits.

docs.title: Phase 5: Refusal Verification and Text Extraction
docs.text:
if message.stop_reason == "refusal":
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals")
        details = getattr(message, "stop_details", None)
        category = getattr(details, "category", None) if details else None
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL", model=model, category=category or "unknown")
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC")

    text = _extract_text(message)
    if message.stop_reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS:
        count_event("ANTHROPIC", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED", max_tokens=f"{params['max_tokens']:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(text)
    if not text:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Anthropic response contained no text blocks (stop_reason={message.stop_reason})", dest="LOG")
    return text

Phase 5 examines the terminal status of the message. If safety classifiers triggered a refusal, it increments the refusal metrics, logs the refusal category, and raises an unretryable LLMRefusalError. If the response halted due to context exhaustion or token limits (_TRUNCATION_STOPS), it wraps the accumulated text in TruncatedResponse to prevent upstream caching. Otherwise, it extracts and returns the clean text response.

Example:

# Invocation pattern from utils/call_llm.py:
reply = call_anthropic(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Lazily initializes and returns the module-level singleton instance of anthropic.Anthropic.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • anthropic.Anthropic: The authenticated Anthropic client instance configured with max_retries=3.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        # SDK resolves credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / AUTH_TOKEN / ant profile) and
        # ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL itself. SDK retries 408/409/429/5xx with backoff;
        # PocketFlow node retries sit on top of this.
        _client = anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=3)
    return _client

This helper ensures that the Anthropic SDK client is instantiated only when an Anthropic model call is actually requested. The client automatically resolves credentials from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or local authentication profiles, while configuring a default retry policy for transient 408, 409, 429, and 5xx network errors.

docs.title: _matches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _matches(model: str, prefixes) -> bool:

Description: Tests whether a model identifier begins with any prefix present in a provided iterable of strings.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier string.
  • prefixes (Iterable[str]): A sequence of string prefixes to match against.

Returns:

  • bool: True if any prefix matches the start of the model string; otherwise False.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _matches(model: str, prefixes) -> bool:
    return any(model.startswith(p) for p in prefixes)

This utility provides prefix-based pattern matching across model family identifiers. It is used throughout the module to identify adaptive models, models that think by default, and models subject to server-side fallbacks.

docs.title: _fallback_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:

Description: Determines the server-side fallback configuration, including required beta headers and extra body payloads, based on model capabilities and environment settings.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The primary model identifier string.

Returns:

  • tuple[list[str], dict]: A 2-tuple containing a list of required beta headers and a dictionary containing the extra_body payload for the API request.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _fallback_config(model: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
    """Return (betas, extra_body) for server-side refusal fallbacks, or empty when disabled."""
    setting = (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS") or "default").strip()
    if _fallbacks_disabled or setting.lower() == "off":
        return [], {}
    if setting.lower() == "default":
        if not _matches(model, _FALLBACK_PREFIXES):
            return [], {}
        return [_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA], {"fallbacks": "default"}
    targets = [m.strip() for m in setting.split(",") if m.strip()]
    return [_FALLBACK_LIST_BETA], {"fallbacks": [{"model": m} for m in targets]}

The function reads the ANTHROPIC_FALLBACKS environment setting. If fallbacks are globally disabled (due to prior 400 errors) or set to "off", it returns empty structures. If set to "default", it activates _FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA exclusively for models in _FALLBACK_PREFIXES (Opus 5.x and Fable 5.x). If configured with an explicit comma-separated model list, it binds _FALLBACK_LIST_BETA and constructs an explicit fallback target array.

docs.title: _build_request()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:

Description: Assembles the parameter dictionary and beta header list required for the Anthropic messages API.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The user prompt text.
  • model (str): The model name.
  • effort (str | None): The normalized reasoning effort level.
  • max_tokens (int): The maximum output token allocation.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, list[str]]: A 2-tuple of (params, betas) ready for request dispatch.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _build_request(prompt: str, model: str, effort: str | None, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    params = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    }
    if uses_adaptive_thinking(model):
        if effort or _matches(model, _THINKING_BY_DEFAULT_PREFIXES):
            thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}
            if is_debug():
                # Readable reasoning summaries go to the log file (never to stdout).
                thinking["display"] = "summarized"
            params["thinking"] = thinking
        if effort:
            params["output_config"] = {"effort": effort}
    elif effort:
        budget = min(_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL[effort], max_tokens - 1_024)
        if budget >= 1_024:
            params["thinking"] = {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": budget}

    if (os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE") or "off").strip().lower() == "on":
        params["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}

    betas, extra_body = _fallback_config(model)
    if extra_body:
        params["extra_body"] = extra_body
    return params, betas

The function compiles the basic message payload and then injects reasoning configurations. For models using adaptive thinking, it injects {"type": "adaptive"} along with output_config.effort. For older models, it computes a fixed budget_tokens value using _BUDGET_BY_LEVEL. Furthermore, it appends ephemeral prompt caching headers if ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE is enabled and integrates fallback payloads generated by _fallback_config.

docs.title: _resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Calculates the optimal planned max_tokens and the absolute available token ceiling given the context window, prompt length, and environment restrictions.

Parameters:

  • prompt_tokens (int): The estimated input prompt token count.
  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • effort (str | None): The normalized effort level.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A 2-tuple (wanted, ceiling) representing the requested token allocation and the maximum permissible token limit.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _resolve_max_tokens(prompt_tokens: int, model: str, effort: str | None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (max_tokens, ceiling): the planned budget and the largest budget allowed.

    `prompt_tokens` is the raw tiktoken count scaled by token_utils.token_ratio() (calibrated).
    The ceiling respects the model output cap, the context window (prompt + output +
    ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN — the same margin input_token_budget reserves), and
    ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS when set.
    """
    context_window, output_cap = get_model_limits(model)
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    wanted = anthropic_planned_output(model, effort)  # same value input_token_budget reserved

    room = max(context_window - prompt_tokens - ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096)
    ceiling = min(output_cap, room, cap) if cap else min(output_cap, room)
    if ceiling < wanted:
        # Small shortfalls (template overhead on a budget-packed prompt) are expected; only report real cuts.
        if ceiling < wanted * 0.9:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED", wanted=f"{wanted:,}", available=f"{ceiling:,}")
        wanted = ceiling
    return wanted, ceiling

The function queries model limits and environment output caps (ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS). It determines available headroom by subtracting the prompt tokens and safety buffer (ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_MARGIN) from the context window, enforcing a 4,096 token minimum. If the available ceiling truncates the desired budget by more than 10%, it emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_OUTPUT_CLAMPED to alert the user before clamping wanted to ceiling.

docs.title: _stream_message()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Dispatches a streaming request through the Anthropic SDK and waits for stream completion to assemble the final message object.

Parameters:

  • params (dict): The parameters payload for the messages API.
  • betas (list[str]): List of beta header strings required for experimental features.

Returns:

  • anthropic.types.Message: The fully accumulated message object returned by stream.get_final_message().

Raises:

  • anthropic.APIError: If the streaming request encounters network or API validation failures.

Example:

def _stream_message(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    client = _get_client()
    if betas:
        with client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params) as stream:
            return stream.get_final_message()
    with client.messages.stream(**params) as stream:
        return stream.get_final_message()

The function checks whether beta headers are present. If betas are supplied, it invokes client.beta.messages.stream(betas=betas, **params); otherwise, it executes client.messages.stream(**params). By using context manager streaming blocks and collecting the final message with get_final_message(), the pipeline prevents socket read timeouts even during protracted 128K generation cycles.

docs.title: _fallback_rejected()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:

Description: Analyzes an API 400 error string to verify if the failure was caused by server-side fallback incompatibility rather than malformed client parameters.

Parameters:

  • error_text (str): The error message string returned by the API.
  • params (dict): The request parameters dictionary.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the error reflects an unsupported or unpermitted fallback beta; otherwise False.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _fallback_rejected(error_text: str, params: dict) -> bool:
    """True when a 400 rejects the fallback feature itself (beta header not enabled, or
    `fallbacks: "default"` unsupported for this model/account) — not a user config error."""
    text = error_text.lower()
    if "anthropic-beta" in text and "server-side-fallback" in text:
        return True
    return params.get("extra_body", {}).get("fallbacks") == "default" and "fallbacks" in text

This helper inspects error details for specific phrases indicative of fallback beta permission or compatibility issues. If the error explicitly mentions server-side-fallback under anthropic-beta or references unsupported default fallbacks, the caller treats the failure as a provider capability mismatch rather than an application-level defect.

docs.title: _send()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):

Description: Wraps message streaming with automatic fallback rejection recovery, disabling server-side fallbacks for the remainder of the execution run if rejected by the API.

Parameters:

  • params (dict): The API parameters dictionary.
  • betas (list[str]): List of beta header strings.

Returns:

  • anthropic.types.Message: The assembled response message object.

Raises:

  • anthropic.BadRequestError: Re-raised if the 400 error is not related to fallback rejection.
  • anthropic.APIError: Any other network or API exception.

Example:

def _send(params: dict, betas: list[str]):
    """Send one streamed request; disable fallbacks for the run if the feature is unavailable."""
    global _fallbacks_disabled
    try:
        return _stream_message(params, betas)
    except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
        if "extra_body" in params and _fallback_rejected(str(e), params):
            _fallbacks_disabled = True
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED", error=str(e))
            retry_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k != "extra_body"}
            return _stream_message(retry_params, [])
        raise

The function executes _stream_message within a defensive try-except block. If an anthropic.BadRequestError occurs and _fallback_rejected evaluates to True, the function mutates the module-level _fallbacks_disabled flag to True, emits a WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED warning, strips extra_body from the parameter map, and retries the streaming request without beta headers.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the monetary cost (in USD) for a given token usage breakdown based on model pricing tables.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model name or prefix.
  • tokens_in (int): Uncached input token count.
  • tokens_out (int): Output token count (including thinking tokens).
  • cache_read (int): Prompt cache read token count.
  • cache_write (int): Prompt cache creation token count.

Returns:

  • float | None: The calculated cost in USD, or None if the model has no entry in _PRICING.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _price(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cache_read: int, cache_write: int) -> float | None:
    price = next((_PRICING[k] for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if (model or "").startswith(k)), None)
    if price is None:
        return None
    p_in, p_out, p_read = price
    return (tokens_in * p_in + tokens_out * p_out + cache_read * p_read + cache_write * p_in * 1.25) / 1_000_000

The function matches the provided model name against _PRICING using longest-prefix matching. If matched, it extracts rates for input, output, and cache reads per million tokens. Cache creation writes are billed at 1.25x the standard input token rate. The components are summed and divided by 1,000,000 to produce the final USD cost figure.

docs.title: _tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:

Description: Safely extracts token metrics from an API usage object, providing zero fallbacks for missing or None attributes.

Parameters:

  • usage (Any): The usage object from an Anthropic message or iteration entry.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int, int, int]: A 4-tuple containing (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens).

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _tokens(usage) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    return (
        getattr(usage, "input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
        getattr(usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0,
    )

This helper isolates attribute extraction from diverse SDK response formats and iteration structures. By wrapping access in getattr with boolean or 0 guards, it guarantees integer arithmetic compatibility even if specific cache telemetry fields are returned as None or omitted entirely.

docs.title: _thinking_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _thinking_tokens(usage) -> int:

Description: Extracts the number of internal reasoning/thinking tokens consumed by an operation from the usage details.

Parameters:

  • usage (Any): The usage object from a message or iteration entry.

Returns:

  • int: The count of thinking tokens, or 0 if reasoning was disabled or omitted.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _thinking_tokens(usage) -> int:
    details = getattr(usage, "output_tokens_details", None)
    return getattr(details, "thinking_tokens", 0) or 0

The helper inspects the nested output_tokens_details attribute on the usage object. If present, it retrieves thinking_tokens. These tokens count toward the overall output tokens budget for rate limits and billing, but are logged separately in usage summaries to provide visibility into reasoning depth.

docs.title: _declined_before_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:

Description: Identifies whether a request was rejected by safety classifiers before generating any output tokens.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The response message object.

Returns:

  • bool: True if stop_reason == "refusal" and output_tokens == 0; otherwise False.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _declined_before_output(message) -> bool:
    """A refusal with no output tokens at all is not billed (the same rule as for fallback iterations)."""
    return getattr(message, "stop_reason", None) == "refusal" and not (getattr(message.usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0)

The function checks if the request halted due to safety refusals without generating tokens. Under Anthropic's billing model, requests refused prior to output generation incur no billing charges. This check ensures that ledger entries and cost accounting correctly record $0.00 for refused operations.

docs.title: _billed_entries()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _billed_entries(message) -> list:

Description: Filters and extracts all usage entries subject to financial billing, spanning multi-attempt server-side fallbacks or the top-level usage object.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The completed message object.

Returns:

  • list: A list of usage objects representing billable inference attempts.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _billed_entries(message) -> list:
    """Usage entries of the billed attempts: every usage.iterations entry with output (server-side
    fallbacks), else the top-level usage unless the request was declined before any output."""
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        return [entry for entry in iterations if (getattr(entry, "output_tokens", 0) or 0) > 0]
    return [] if _declined_before_output(message) else [message.usage]

When server-side fallbacks engage, message.usage.iterations records usage across each sequential attempt. This helper extracts each iteration that produced at least one output token. If no iterations exist, it returns [message.usage] unless the request was declined before output generation, in which case it returns an empty list.

docs.title: _billed_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:

Description: Aggregates token statistics across all billable attempts belonging to a message.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The response message object.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int, int, int, int]: A 5-tuple representing (total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking) summed across all billable entries.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _billed_tokens(message) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
    """(total input incl. cache read/write, output, cache_read, cache_write, thinking) summed over the
    billed attempts (_billed_entries), so token totals match _message_cost."""
    total_in = out = cache_read = cache_write = thinking = 0
    for entry in _billed_entries(message):
        tokens_in, tokens_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        total_in += tokens_in + read + write
        out += tokens_out
        cache_read += read
        cache_write += write
        thinking += _thinking_tokens(entry)
    return total_in, out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking

The function iterates over _billed_entries(message) and sums uncached inputs, cache reads, cache writes, output tokens, and thinking tokens. Total input tokens include the sum of direct input, cache reads, and cache creations to reflect the true context volume evaluated across fallback attempts.

docs.title: _message_cost()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:

Description: Estimates the total cost in USD for a response message, accounting for per-attempt fallback iterations at their respective model rates.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The response message object.
  • served_model (str): The default model identifier that fulfilled the request.

Returns:

  • float | None: Total cost in USD, or None if any participating model lacked pricing information.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _message_cost(message, served_model: str) -> float | None:
    """Estimated USD cost of one response. With server-side fallbacks, usage.iterations holds the
    per-attempt usage (each billed at its own model's rate; an attempt declined before any output is
    unbilled); top-level usage covers only the attempt that produced the returned message."""
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    if iterations:
        total, known = 0.0, True
        for entry in iterations:
            tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write = _tokens(entry)
            if tokens_out == 0:
                continue  # declined before any output (primary or fallback attempt): not billed
            cost = _price(getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write)
            known = known and cost is not None
            total += cost or 0.0
        return total if known else None
    if _declined_before_output(message):
        return 0.0  # declined before any output: not billed
    return _price(served_model, *_tokens(message.usage))

The function handles fallback billing dynamics where an initial attempt might run on Opus before cascading to Sonnet. It inspects message.usage.iterations, evaluating each non-zero output entry against the specific model that executed it. If any model price is unlisted in _PRICING, known switches to False and the function returns None. For single-attempt responses, it prices message.usage directly.

docs.title: _record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float, model: str = "", observe: bool = True) -> None:

Description: Dispatches call usage metrics to the shared pipeline ledger and recalibrates the prompt token estimation multiplier.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The response message object.
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): Uncalibrated token count calculated prior to transmission.
  • effort (str | None): The reasoning effort level configured for the request.
  • elapsed (float): Latency in seconds.
  • model (str, optional): The requested model identifier. Defaults to "".
  • observe (bool, optional): Whether to report observed token counts to token_utils.observe_prompt_tokens. Defaults to True.

Returns:

None.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _record_usage(message, raw_prompt_tokens: int, effort: str | None, elapsed: float, model: str = "", observe: bool = True) -> None:
    from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

    served_model = getattr(message, "model", "") or ""
    has_iterations = bool(getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None))
    entries = _billed_entries(message)
    if not entries:
        record_usage("ANTHROPIC", served_model, cost=0.0, measured=False)  # declined before any output: not billed
    # One ledger request per billed attempt (primary + fallback each billed at its own model's rate), so
    # request counts, per-request estimate deviation and the model list stay correct.
    for entry in entries:
        t_in, t_out, read, write = _tokens(entry)
        entry_model = (getattr(entry, "model", None) or served_model) if has_iterations else served_model
        record_usage(
            "ANTHROPIC",
            entry_model,
            input_tokens=t_in + read + write,
            output_tokens=t_out,
            thinking_tokens=_thinking_tokens(entry),
            cache_read=read,
            cache_write=write,
            cost=_price(entry_model, t_in, t_out, read, write) if has_iterations else _message_cost(message, served_model),
        )
    total_in, tokens_out, cache_read, cache_write, thinking = _billed_tokens(message)  # totals for the debug line
    cost = _message_cost(message, served_model)

    # Observed Claude/tiktoken ratio of the attempt that produced this message (top-level usage),
    # fed to the calibration unless another model (server-side fallback) served it.
    tokens_in, _, read, write = _tokens(message.usage)
    attempt_in = tokens_in + read + write
    ratio = attempt_in / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    if observe and model and not _served_by_fallback(message):
        observe_prompt_tokens("ANTHROPIC", model, raw_prompt_tokens, attempt_in, served_model=served_model)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"ANTHROPIC USAGE | model={served_model} | effort={effort or 'default'} | stop={message.stop_reason} | "
        f"in={total_in:,} | out={tokens_out:,} | thinking={thinking:,} | cache_read={cache_read:,} | cache_write={cache_write:,} | "
        f"est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="BOTH",
    )

The function records granular usage into the shared system ledger via record_usage(). For server-side fallbacks, it records separate entries for each attempt so cost attribution and request metrics remain exact. Unless bypassed or served by a fallback model, it passes the observed token ratio to observe_prompt_tokens() to calibrate the dynamic multiplier against Claude's native BPE tokenizer. Finally, it outputs a formatted usage summary to the log.

docs.title: _log_thinking()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _log_thinking(message) -> None:

Description: Extracts summarized reasoning blocks from the response message and writes them to the diagnostic log file.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The response message containing content blocks.

Returns:

None.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _log_thinking(message) -> None:
    for block in message.content:
        if getattr(block, "type", None) == "thinking" and getattr(block, "thinking", ""):
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{block.thinking}", dest="LOG")

The function inspects message.content for blocks with type == "thinking". When found, it routes the text to emit_raw targeted strictly to "LOG". This ensures internal reasoning traces are preserved for diagnostic analysis without leaking into user-facing console output or generated documentation files.

docs.title: _served_by_fallback()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:

Description: Checks if a message was produced by a server-side fallback model rather than the primary requested model.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The response message object.

Returns:

  • bool: True if any content block or usage iteration indicates fallback fulfillment; otherwise False.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _served_by_fallback(message) -> bool:
    if any(getattr(block, "type", None) == "fallback" for block in message.content):
        return True
    iterations = getattr(message.usage, "iterations", None) or []
    return any(getattr(entry, "type", None) == "fallback_message" for entry in iterations)

This helper detects whether Anthropic server-side fallback mechanisms substituted another model to satisfy the request. It checks for content blocks of type "fallback" or usage iteration records tagged as "fallback_message". The outcome determines whether fallback warning events fire and prevents skewed token calibration data from contaminating primary model ratios.

docs.title: _extract_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _extract_text(message) -> str:

Description: Concatenates all textual content blocks from a response message into a single unified string.

Parameters:

  • message (anthropic.types.Message): The response message object.

Returns:

  • str: The joined textual content.

Raises:

None.

Example:

def _extract_text(message) -> str:
    return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text")

The function traverses message.content, selectively filtering for blocks where type == "text". It concatenates their .text properties and returns the result. Thinking blocks, fallback indicators, and non-textual payload artifacts are excluded from the extracted response.

docs.title: EFFORT_LEVELS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

A tuple defining the supported reasoning effort levels recognized by Anthropic model configurations:

Value Type Description "low" str Minimal reasoning depth for straightforward transformations. "medium" str Balanced reasoning depth (default for Claude Opus 5.5). "high" str Deep reasoning depth (default for Claude Sonnet 5). "xhigh" str Extended reasoning depth for complex multi-layered architectural analysis. "max" str Maximum reasoning depth permitted by model limits.

docs.title: _PRICING
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

A dictionary mapping model prefix identifiers to their pricing structure per million tokens: (input_usd, output_usd, cache_read_usd). 5-minute cache writes are billed at 1.25 * input_usd.

Model Prefix Input ($/M) Output ($/M) Cache Read ($/M) Cache Write ($/M) "claude-opus-5-5" 4.00 20.00 0.20 5.00 "claude-opus-5" 5.00 25.00 0.50 6.25 "claude-fable-5-1" 10.00 50.00 0.25 12.50 "claude-fable-5" 10.00 50.00 1.00 12.50 "claude-mythos-5-1" 10.00 50.00 0.25 12.50 "claude-mythos-5" 10.00 50.00 1.00 12.50 "claude-sonnet-5" 2.00 10.00 0.20 2.50 "claude-opus-4-8" 5.00 25.00 0.50 6.25 "claude-opus-4-7" 5.00 25.00 0.50 6.25 "claude-opus-4-6" 5.00 25.00 0.50 6.25 "claude-sonnet-4-6" 3.00 15.00 0.30 3.75 "claude-haiku-4-5" 1.00 5.00 0.10 1.25

docs.title: Model Limits Tuple
docs.text:
A 2-tuple returned by get_model_limits() and offline defaults (_MODEL_LIMITS, _DEFAULT_LIMITS):

Index Field Type Description Example 0 context_window int Maximum combined input + output tokens supported. 1_000_000 1 max_output_tokens int Maximum output tokens supported in a single generation. 128_000

docs.title: Token Resolution Tuple
docs.text:
A 2-tuple returned by _resolve_max_tokens() representing the planned and maximum token thresholds:

Index Field Type Description 0 wanted int Target output tokens planned based on effort and token reservations. 1 ceiling int Hard output token limit allowed by model capacity and context headroom.

docs.title: Request Parameters Dictionary
docs.text:
The dictionary shape constructed by _build_request() and dispatched to the Anthropic Messages API:

Key Type Mandatory Description "model" str Yes Model identifier (e.g., "claude-sonnet-5"). "max_tokens" int Yes Maximum output token ceiling. "messages" list[dict] Yes Message list containing the prompt role and text content. "thinking" dict No Adaptive config ({"type": "adaptive"}) or budgeted config ({"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": int}). "output_config" dict No Effort specification (e.g., {"effort": "high"}). "cache_control" dict No Ephemeral prompt caching config ({"type": "ephemeral"}). "extra_body" dict No Server-side fallback directives (e.g., {"fallbacks": "default"}).

docs.title: Billed Tokens Tuple
docs.text:
A 5-tuple returned by _billed_tokens() summarizing tokens across all valid execution attempts:

Index Field Type Description 0 total_in int Total input volume including prompt, cache reads, and cache writes. 1 out int Total output tokens generated. 2 cache_read int Number of input tokens read from the prompt cache. 3 cache_write int Number of input tokens written to create new cache entries. 4 thinking int Number of internal reasoning/thinking tokens consumed.

docs.title: Refusal Trapping and Propagation
docs.text:
Anthropic models equipped with safety classifiers (such as Opus 5.x and Fable 5.x) may refuse a prompt rather than fulfill it. The module handles this deterministically:

  1. When server-side fallbacks are active (_FALLBACK_DEFAULT_BETA or _FALLBACK_LIST_BETA), the Anthropic infrastructure attempts to re-route refused prompts to alternative models.
  2. If all fallback models refuse or fallbacks are disabled, message.stop_reason returns "refusal".
  3. call_anthropic() catches this condition, extracts the refusal category from message.stop_details.category, records refusal metrics via count_event("ANTHROPIC", "refusals"), emits WARN_ANTHROPIC_REFUSAL, and raises LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="ANTHROPIC").
  4. Refusals with zero output tokens are marked as unbilled in _declined_before_output(), ensuring accounting ledgers reflect $0.00 cost.

docs.title: Dynamic Truncation Recovery
docs.text:
When generating exhaustive documentation chapters, responses may hit output token limits (stop_reason == "max_tokens"):

  • Single-Step Budget Retry: In call_anthropic(), if message.stop_reason == "max_tokens" and the initial budget max_tokens was smaller than the permissible ceiling, the module immediately logs the truncated attempt, updates parameter budgets to ceiling, and executes a single retry.
  • TruncatedResponse Fallback: If the retry still ends in a truncation condition (stop_reason in _TRUNCATION_STOPS), the module logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_TRUNCATED, records a truncation event via count_event, and returns the accumulated text wrapped inside TruncatedResponse(text). Downstream callers in call_llm.py inspect this type to ensure partial outputs are never committed to persistent caches.

docs.title: Server-Side Fallback Degrade
docs.text:
When experimental server-side fallbacks are enabled via beta headers:

  • If an account or model rejects the fallback configuration with an HTTP 400 (BadRequestError), _send() invokes _fallback_rejected().
  • If verified as a fallback incompatibility, the module sets _fallbacks_disabled = True, logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_FALLBACK_DISABLED, strips the extra_body payload, and immediately re-executes the request as standard non-fallback streaming. All subsequent calls in the process lifetime inherit the disabled state.

docs.title: Models API Failures
docs.text: In get_model_limits(), network errors or permission issues encountered while querying client.models.retrieve() raise anthropic.APIError. The module intercepts this exception, logs WARN_ANTHROPIC_MODEL_LOOKUP, and seamlessly injects predefined limits from _MODEL_LIMITS or _DEFAULT_LIMITS, preventing network glitches during model metadata lookup from failing the pipeline.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/llm_common.py module serves as the foundational, provider-neutral utility library for the LLM abstraction layer in Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. It operates without importing any external model SDKs (such as Anthropic, Google GenAI, or OpenAI), relying solely on standard library primitives (contextlib, contextvars, and hashlib). This design ensures that core error representations, response boundary types, execution step context management, warning de-duplication, and token accounting are universally available to all provider drivers and downstream execution nodes without circular dependencies or vendor lock-in.

The module manages two primary stateful subsystems across the execution lifecycle: request memoization and a multi-dimensional usage ledger. First, to avoid redundant billing and prevent wasted rate-limit quotas during retry loops, it computes SHA-256 cryptographic digests of outgoing requests and memoizes terminal refusals (LLMRefusalError). Second, it provides an in-memory accounting engine that tracks token consumption (input, output, reasoning/thinking, and prompt cache reads/writes), monetary costs, event counters, and estimation discrepancies. By leveraging Python's contextvars.ContextVar, the ledger automatically correlates per-request token usage with active pipeline steps (such as ContextRouter, IdentifyAbstractions, or CombineTutorial), even across nested calling contexts.

docs.title: TruncatedResponse
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class TruncatedResponse(str):

Description: A specialized string subclass used to wrap model response texts that were cut off prematurely due to token budget caps or context window boundaries. Downstream caching systems check the truncated attribute to strictly bypass serialization to the persistent response cache, while YAML/JSON response parsers reject it to trigger retry strategies.

Example:

class TruncatedResponse(str):
    """Response text from a reply that was cut off; call_llm returns it but never caches it."""

    truncated = True

The TruncatedResponse class subclasses Python's built-in str, enabling downstream functions to process its contents as ordinary text if needed while carrying the boolean attribute truncated = True. This explicit boundary flag allows orchestrators such as call_llm to distinguish complete generations from cut-off outputs without parsing stop reason metadata. Caching subsystems inspect this attribute prior to persisting payloads, ensuring partial or syntactically broken responses never pollute the response cache. Furthermore, downstream structured output validators immediately fail on encountering a TruncatedResponse, triggering retry and context recovery routines.

docs.title: LLMRefusalError
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):

Description: Custom exception raised when an upstream model provider (and any configured fallback models) declines to service an inference request due to safety restrictions, content moderation, recitation blocks, or policy constraints.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Identifier of the model that issued the refusal.
  • category (str | None): Policy or safety category reported by the provider (e.g., "recitation", "safety", "content_filter").
  • provider (str): Model provider identifier, defaulting to "ANTHROPIC".
  • retryable (bool): Flag indicating whether re-sampling the prompt might succeed (True) or if the decline is deterministic (False).

Example:

class LLMRefusalError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the provider (and any configured fallback) declines a request.

    retryable=False: the same request is declined again (Claude refusal, blocked prompt,
    prohibited content) — call_llm remembers it and does not re-send it on node retries.
    retryable=True: an output-side block that a new sample can pass (Gemini RECITATION / OTHER /
    SAFETY on the candidate, OpenRouter content_filter) — node retries re-sample normally.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: str, category: str | None, provider: str = "ANTHROPIC", retryable: bool = False):
        self.model = model
        self.category = category
        self.provider = provider
        self.retryable = retryable
        super().__init__(f"{provider} model {model} declined the request (category={category or 'unknown'})")

The constructor binds structural metadata (model, category, provider, and retryable) to the exception instance before formatting a descriptive diagnostic message for the standard RuntimeError base class. When retryable is set to False, the decline is considered deterministic (such as an outright prompt safety block), signaling to the calling orchestrator that the request should be permanently memoized in the module's refusal registry to prevent retries. Conversely, when retryable is set to True, the block occurred during output sampling (e.g., Gemini candidate recitation filters or transient moderation flags), signaling that re-submitting the prompt with another sampling attempt may succeed.

docs.title: request_key()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:

Description: Generates an isolated, deterministic SHA-256 hex digest representing a unique LLM invocation scope. Combines provider, model, thinking effort level, and prompt text.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): The model provider identifier (e.g., "anthropic", "gemini", "openrouter").
  • model (str): The specific model name or identifier string.
  • thinking_level (str | None): The reasoning or thinking budget configuration string (e.g., "low", "high"), falling back to "default" if None.
  • prompt (str): The complete raw prompt string passed to the LLM.

Returns:

  • str: A 64-character lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal hash string uniquely identifying the call.

Example:

def request_key(provider: str, model: str, thinking_level: str | None, prompt: str) -> str:
    scope = f"{provider}|{model}|{(thinking_level or 'default').lower()}\n"
    return hashlib.sha256((scope + prompt).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

The function constructs a composite scope prefix consisting of the provider, model, and normalized lowercase thinking level separated by pipe characters and terminated with a newline character. This prefix is concatenated with the complete prompt body and encoded into UTF-8 byte streams before passing into hashlib.sha256(). By incorporating the thinking level and provider alongside the raw prompt, the function guarantees cryptographic isolation across differing model configurations, preventing collision when the same prompt is evaluated under different reasoning budgets.

docs.title: remember_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:

Description: Stores a non-retryable refusal exception in the module's internal refusal memoization table using the call's unique request key.

Parameters:

  • key (str): Cryptographic request key generated by request_key().
  • error (LLMRefusalError): The terminal refusal exception instance to memoize.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def remember_refusal(key: str, error: LLMRefusalError) -> None:
    _refused[key] = error

This function performs a direct assignment of the LLMRefusalError instance into the private module-level _refused dictionary keyed by the calculated hash. It serves as an in-memory write barrier during workflow retry loops, ensuring that deterministic provider rejections are cataloged once and recalled immediately on subsequent invocation attempts without repeating remote HTTP requests.

docs.title: previous_refusal()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:

Description: Inspects the internal refusal table for a previously recorded refusal matching the specified request key.

Parameters:

  • key (str): Cryptographic request key generated by request_key().

Returns:

  • LLMRefusalError | None: The previously stored exception instance if found; otherwise None.

Example:

def previous_refusal(key: str) -> LLMRefusalError | None:
    return _refused.get(key)

The function queries the private _refused map using dictionary lookup semantics via .get(key). If an entry exists for the hash key, the stored LLMRefusalError instance is returned immediately to the caller, allowing the orchestrator to raise or handle the error without dispatching network requests; if no entry exists, it returns None.

docs.title: usage_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_step(step: str | None):

Description: Context manager that binds the current execution context to a designated pipeline step identifier, attributing all token usage and counters within the block to that step.

Parameters:

  • step (str | None): Pipeline step name (e.g., "extract_facts", "draft_chapters"). If None or empty, defaults to "other".

Returns:

  • Generator yielding control within the context manager block.

Example:

@contextlib.contextmanager
def usage_step(step: str | None):
    """Attribute every record_usage / count_event inside the block to `step`."""
    token = _current_step.set(step or "other")
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _current_step.reset(token)

The function employs @contextlib.contextmanager to govern the lifecycle of a contextvars.ContextVar token. Upon entering the context, it sets _current_step to the provided step string (defaulting to "other") and retains the returned state token. Inside a finally block, it guarantees that _current_step.reset(token) is executed upon block exit, restoring the previous step identifier even if exceptions occur within the nested code block.

docs.title: current_step()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def current_step() -> str:

Description: Retrieves the currently active pipeline step identifier bound to the local context variable.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • str: The active pipeline step name, defaulting to "other" if unset.

Example:

def current_step() -> str:
    return _current_step.get()

The helper reads the active value stored in the thread/coroutine-local _current_step context variable by executing _current_step.get(). This enables any downstream utility to introspect the calling step without requiring explicit parameter threading through deep call stacks.

docs.title: record_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature:

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
    measured: bool = True,
) -> None:

Description: Records metrics from a completed LLM request into both the provider-level and step-level usage ledgers, aggregating tokens, pricing, and measurement metadata.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Provider identifier (e.g., "anthropic", "gemini").
  • model (str): Name of the model executing the call.
  • input_tokens (int): Total prompt tokens counted by the provider, including cached tokens. Defaults to 0.
  • output_tokens (int): Total output tokens returned, including reasoning/thinking tokens. Defaults to 0.
  • thinking_tokens (int): Subset of output tokens dedicated to model reasoning. Defaults to 0.
  • cache_read (int): Tokens read from an existing prompt cache. Defaults to 0.
  • cache_write (int): Tokens written into the prompt cache during this request. Defaults to 0.
  • cost (float | None): Monetary cost in USD for the call. If None, marked as unpriced.
  • measured (bool): Flag indicating if the provider reported valid token metrics. Defaults to True.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def record_usage(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    thinking_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_read: int = 0,
    cache_write: int = 0,
    cost: float | None = None,
    measured: bool = True,
) -> None:
    for entry in (_usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry()), _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())):
        if model:
            entry["models"].add(model)
        entry["calls"] += 1
        if not measured:
            entry["unmeasured_calls"] += 1
        entry["input"] += input_tokens or 0
        entry["output"] += output_tokens or 0
        entry["thinking"] += thinking_tokens or 0
        entry["cache_read"] += cache_read or 0
        entry["cache_write"] += cache_write or 0
        if cost is None:
            entry["unpriced_calls"] += 1
        else:
            entry["cost"] += cost

This function performs dual accumulation: it resolves the ledger entry for the given provider in _usage and the entry for the active step via current_step() in _steps, initializing each via _new_entry() if absent. It updates the unique set of model names, increments the total call count, and defensively accumulates token counts using or 0 fallbacks. If measured is False, it increments unmeasured_calls, allowing subsequent telemetry audits to exclude unbilled or uninstrumented requests from token estimation comparisons. If cost is None, it tracks the occurrence under unpriced_calls; otherwise, it adds the float amount directly to cost.

docs.title: count_event()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:

Description: Increments a named operational event counter (e.g., "refusals", "fallbacks", "truncations") simultaneously for a given provider and the active execution step.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Provider identifier against which the event occurred.
  • event (str): The counter dictionary key to increment (must match an integer key in _new_entry()).

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def count_event(provider: str, event: str) -> None:
    """Increment 'refusals' | 'fallbacks' | 'truncations' for a provider (and the current step)."""
    _usage.setdefault(provider, _new_entry())[event] += 1
    _steps.setdefault(current_step(), _new_entry())[event] += 1

The function accesses the corresponding entry dictionaries in both _usage and _steps using .setdefault(), initializing them with _new_entry() if they do not yet exist. It then directly increments the value mapped to the string passed via the event argument. This ensures that non-fatal exceptions, provider fallback switches, and token truncation events are tracked synchronously across provider and workflow step aggregations.

docs.title: record_estimate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:

Description: Records prompt token estimations and cache hit indicators for a specific pipeline step.

Parameters:

  • step (str): The pipeline step name receiving the estimate. Defaults to "other" if empty.
  • estimated_input (int): The calculated input token count estimated prior to provider execution.
  • cache_hit (bool): Flag indicating if the request was resolved directly from the local cache. Defaults to False.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def record_estimate(step: str, estimated_input: int, *, cache_hit: bool = False) -> None:
    """Add call_llm's input estimate for a call (billed or served from the LLM cache) to a step."""
    entry = _steps.setdefault(step or "other", _new_entry())
    if cache_hit:
        entry["cache_hits"] += 1
    else:
        entry["estimated_input"] += estimated_input or 0

The function fetches or initializes the dictionary entry for the designated step within the _steps ledger. When cache_hit is True, it increments the entry's cache_hits counter, tracking requests satisfied from the local disk cache without network transport. When cache_hit is False, it accumulates estimated_input tokens into the entry, enabling downstream reporting tools to compare upfront tokenizer estimations against actual billed tokens.

docs.title: usage_snapshot()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:

Description: Creates a point-in-time copy of a provider's numeric usage counters, excluding non-numeric objects like sets.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Provider identifier to inspect.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing copies of all metric counters for the provider, excluding the "models" key.

Example:

def usage_snapshot(provider: str) -> dict:
    """Copy of a provider's running totals (diff two snapshots to get one call's usage)."""
    entry = _usage.get(provider)
    return {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k != "models"} if entry else {k: v for k, v in _new_entry().items() if k != "models"}

The function inspects _usage for the target provider. If an entry is present, it constructs a new dictionary filtering out the "models" set; if the provider has not yet been registered, it constructs an equivalent blank template from _new_entry() with "models" omitted. This snapshot serves as an isolated baseline that can be subtracted from a subsequent snapshot to compute the exact usage delta of a single request.

docs.title: usage_delta()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:

Description: Computes the arithmetic difference between two usage snapshot dictionaries.

Parameters:

  • before (dict): Baseline usage dictionary captured prior to an operation.
  • after (dict): Terminal usage dictionary captured after an operation.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing the arithmetic difference (after[k] - before[k]) for every counter key.

Example:

def usage_delta(before: dict, after: dict) -> dict:
    return {k: after[k] - before.get(k, 0) for k in after}

The function executes a dictionary comprehension iterating over all keys present in the after dictionary, subtracting the corresponding key's value from before (defaulting missing baseline keys to 0). This calculates the incremental token usage, cost, and event counts incurred specifically between the capture of before and after.

docs.title: get_usage_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_usage_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles a comprehensive usage report mapping each active provider to its normalized metrics dictionary.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • dict: Dictionary mapping provider strings to public ledger summaries for providers that recorded at least one call (calls > 0).

Example:

def get_usage_summary() -> dict:
    """{provider: totals} for every provider that made at least one call this run."""
    return {provider: _public(entry) for provider, entry in _usage.items() if entry["calls"]}

The function filters the _usage registry to include only providers that executed one or more calls (entry["calls"] > 0). For each qualifying provider, it passes the internal mutable entry through _public() to sanitize internal data structures (sorting model names and computing cost validity) before returning the resulting mapping to the caller.

docs.title: get_step_summary()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_step_summary() -> dict:

Description: Compiles an ordered dictionary mapping pipeline step identifiers to their normalized usage metrics.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • dict: Dictionary mapping step strings to public ledger summaries for steps that recorded either remote calls or cache hits.

Example:

def get_step_summary() -> dict:
    """{step: totals} in first-use order, including steps answered only from the LLM cache."""
    return {step: _public(entry) for step, entry in _steps.items() if entry["calls"] or entry["cache_hits"]}

The function iterates over _steps in insertion order, retaining any step that recorded at least one network request (calls > 0) or was fulfilled via the local cache (cache_hits > 0). Each qualifying step dictionary is sanitized via _public(), ensuring that pipeline steps served entirely from cache remain visible in end-of-run summaries.

docs.title: reset_usage()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def reset_usage() -> None:

Description: Clears all in-memory usage ledgers, step tracking entries, and memoized refusal states across the process.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • None

Example:

def reset_usage() -> None:
    _usage.clear()
    _steps.clear()
    _refused.clear()

The function invokes .clear() across all three stateful global dictionaries: _usage, _steps, and _refused. This completely resets token statistics and refusal memoization, preparing the process for an isolated test case or a clean pipeline re-run without restarting the Python interpreter.

docs.title: warn_once()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:

Description: Thread-safe de-duplication mechanism ensuring a warning identified by a key and arbitrary message parts is emitted only once per process execution.

Parameters:

  • key (str): Primary identifier categorizing the warning.
  • *parts (Any): Variable positional components comprising the warning identifier tuple.

Returns:

  • bool: True if this specific warning marker is encountered for the first time during the run; False if it has already been observed.

Example:

def warn_once(key: str, *parts) -> bool:
    """True the first time a (key, parts) combination is seen this run."""
    marker = (key, *parts)
    if marker in _warned:
        return False
    _warned.add(marker)
    return True

The function packs key and any trailing arguments *parts into a single immutable tuple marker. It checks whether marker exists within the module-level set _warned. If present, it immediately returns False; otherwise, it adds marker to _warned and returns True. Callers wrap logging statements in conditional checks on warn_once() to prevent repetitive warnings from flooding console logs across iterative loops.

docs.title: _refused
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _refused = {}

Description: A module-level dictionary singleton mapping 64-character SHA-256 request keys (generated by request_key()) directly to their corresponding LLMRefusalError instances.

Example:

# Refused-request memo: a declined prompt is declined again, so PocketFlow retries
# must not re-send it (wasted rate limit, and billed partial output on mid-stream declines).
_refused = {}

This private dictionary operates as a memoization cache for non-retryable provider declines. Because deterministic refusals will repeat if re-sent, storing the exception object allows orchestrators to bypass network dispatch on workflow retries and re-raise the original refusal immediately.

docs.title: _usage
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _usage = {}

Description: A module-level dictionary singleton mapping provider identifier strings (e.g., "anthropic", "gemini") to their respective mutable accounting entries created by _new_entry().

Example:

# Usage ledger (one per process; a run is sequential)
_usage = {}

This private dictionary aggregates running token totals, financial costs, call volumes, and error metrics partitioned by model provider. It is updated incrementally by record_usage() and count_event(), and read during snapshot creation or summary generation.

docs.title: _steps
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _steps = {}

Description: A module-level dictionary singleton mapping workflow step names (e.g., "extract_manifest", "draft_chapters") to their mutable accounting entries created by _new_entry().

Example:

_steps = {}

Maintained in insertion order, this dictionary records token metrics, cost amounts, and cache statistics broken down by pipeline node execution steps. It mirrors the structure of _usage, allowing callers to inspect resource consumption either by model vendor or by workflow phase.

docs.title: _current_step
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _current_step = contextvars.ContextVar("llm_usage_step", default="other")

Description: Context variable used to track the currently executing pipeline step identifier across synchronous and asynchronous execution boundaries.

Example:

_current_step = contextvars.ContextVar("llm_usage_step", default="other")

By utilizing contextvars.ContextVar, the module ensures thread-safe and task-isolated step tracking. When nested functions or providers record usage, current_step() reads from this variable to attribute consumption to the enclosing workflow step without requiring parameter passing.

docs.title: _warned
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: _warned = set()

Description: A module-level set storing composite marker tuples of previously observed warnings.

Example:

# De-duplicated warnings
_warned = set()

This set accumulates (key, *parts) tuples recorded by warn_once(). Because items are never removed during a process run (except via process termination), it maintains state for deduplicating warnings across the lifetime of the application.

docs.title: _new_entry()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _new_entry() -> dict:

Description: Factory function initializing a standardized ledger entry dictionary with zeroed metric counters and an empty model set.

Returns:

  • dict: A newly allocated ledger dictionary conforming to the internal accounting schema.

Example:

def _new_entry() -> dict:
    return {
        "models": set(),
        "calls": 0,
        "input": 0,
        "output": 0,
        "thinking": 0,
        "cache_read": 0,
        "cache_write": 0,
        "cost": 0.0,
        "unpriced_calls": 0,
        "unmeasured_calls": 0,
        "refusals": 0,
        "fallbacks": 0,
        "truncations": 0,
        "estimated_input": 0,
        "cache_hits": 0,
    }

The function constructs and returns a uniform dictionary tracking fifteen individual metrics. The "models" field is initialized as a mutable Python set to collect distinct model strings encountered during execution. Numeric counters for calls, token breakdowns, cost, operational events, and estimates are initialized to 0 or 0.0.

docs.title: _public()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _public(entry: dict) -> dict:

Description: Transforms an internal mutable ledger entry dictionary into an externally consumable dictionary representation.

Parameters:

  • entry (dict): An internal accounting dictionary created via _new_entry().

Returns:

  • dict: A shallow copy of entry where "models" is converted into a sorted list of strings and a "cost_known" boolean flag is appended.

Example:

def _public(entry: dict) -> dict:
    return dict(entry, models=sorted(entry["models"]), cost_known=entry["unpriced_calls"] == 0)

This helper transforms internal data structures prior to exposing summaries outside the module. Specifically, it converts the mutable "models" set into a deterministic, lexicographically sorted list of strings suitable for serialization. Additionally, it computes the boolean property cost_known (evaluated as entry["unpriced_calls"] == 0), signaling to reporting tools whether the accumulated cost accurately reflects the entire call volume or if unpriced calls were present.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module defines and relies on LLMRefusalError to manage provider declines systematically:

  • Non-Retryable Declines (retryable=False): When an upstream provider rejects a prompt deterministically (e.g., Anthropic Claude safety policy rejections, content moderation violations, or blocked system instructions), the exception is initialized with retryable=False. The orchestrator passes the call's unique hash key to remember_refusal(), which caches the exception instance in _refused. On future retries within PocketFlow or orchestrator workflows, previous_refusal() short-circuits execution before network dispatch, preventing rate-limit depletion and redundant billing for unserviceable requests.
  • Retryable Declines (retryable=True): When a decline occurs due to candidate-level or stochastic output sampling restrictions (such as Google Gemini RECITATION, OTHER, or candidate safety thresholds, and OpenRouter mid-stream content_filter responses), the exception is initialized with retryable=True. These errors are omitted from remember_refusal(), allowing retry handlers to re-sample the request with different seeds or adjusted parameters.
  • Defensive Arithmetic and Missing Keys: Functions that perform counter updates or differential calculations (record_usage(), record_estimate(), and usage_delta()) employ fallback defaulting (or 0, .get(k, 0)). This prevents KeyError or TypeError exceptions if uninitialized entries or partial dictionaries are evaluated.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
This module is a self-contained foundational utility with zero dependencies on other codebase modules. It imports exclusively from the Python standard library (contextlib, contextvars, hashlib).

Used by: main.py, nodes.py, utils/call_llm.py, utils/llm_anthropic.py, utils/llm_config.py, utils/llm_gemini.py, utils/llm_openrouter.py

docs.title: llm_config.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_config.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the foundational accounting and error primitives established in utils.llm_common (doc: utils/llm_common.py.md), llm_config.py serves as the centralized configuration authority and provider resolution layer for the entire Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. The module was extracted from call_llm.py to eliminate circular dependency chains between inference execution and token budget estimation (utils.token_utils). It operates as the single source of truth for runtime provider detection, model endpoint construction, credential validation, context window boundaries, and tokenizer multiplication ratios.

The module provides deterministic resolution of target LLM environments, supporting Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini (via AI Studio and Google Cloud Vertex AI), OpenRouter gateways, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints. It implements proactive authentication and configuration preflight checks (check_llm_auth()) before any file extraction or code graph analysis begins, preventing wasted execution cycles caused by misconfigured environment variables or missing software development kits (SDKs). Additionally, it manages model reasoning parameters, mapping symbolic effort levels (minimal to max) to provider-specific controls such as Claude adaptive thinking, Gemini thinking levels or token budgets, and OpenRouter reasoning configurations.

To support prompt assembly and token budget calculation, llm_config.py manages static prior token ratios against tiktoken (cl100k), detects models that reject classical sampling parameters (such as temperature, top_p, and top_k), and caches remote model metadata from OpenRouter's /v1/models endpoint with failure cooldowns.
