docs.title: anthropic_output_cap()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:

Description: Retrieves the maximum allowed Anthropic completion tokens configured via environment variables. It parses the ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable into an integer using _env_int(). If the variable is unset, empty, non-numeric, or less than or equal to zero, the function returns None.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • int | None: The parsed positive token limit or None if invalid or unset.

Example:

def anthropic_output_cap() -> int | None:
    """ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS as an int, or None when unset/invalid."""
    return _env_int("ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")

The function provides an operational override mechanism for pipeline runs targeting Claude models. Downstream components consult this value to prevent requests from exceeding cost constraints or custom reverse-proxy output boundaries.

docs.title: anthropic_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Calculates the output token budget for adaptive Anthropic models under a specified reasoning effort level. It queries the ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT table using the lowercased effort level (defaulting to the None effort tier if unspecified) and clamps the result against anthropic_output_cap() if an environment cap is defined.

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): The target reasoning effort (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or None).

Returns:

  • int: Planned output token allocation for the request.

Example:

def anthropic_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-effort table value capped by ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (adaptive models)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

The function coordinates output token headroom between request creation in utils.llm_anthropic and prompt sizing calculations in utils.token_utils. By using matching numbers, prompts can be sized aggressively against context windows while guaranteeing that reasoning output tokens are preserved.

docs.title: anthropic_effort()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:

Description: Translates a normalized pipeline thinking level into an effort string accepted by Anthropic's Messages API. It maps minimal to low, validates membership against ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS, downgrades xhigh to high for Claude 4.6 family models (which predate the xhigh setting), and falls back to None for invalid or missing levels to allow the model's default reasoning behavior.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target model identifier (used for prefix family matching).
  • level (str | None): Desired pipeline reasoning level.

Returns:

  • str | None: Validated Anthropic effort parameter (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) or None.

Example:

def anthropic_effort(model: str, level: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Thinking level → effort the model accepts: minimal → low, xhigh → high on the 4.6 family,
    unknown values → None (model default)."""
    if not level:
        return None
    level = level.lower()
    if level == "minimal":
        level = "low"
    if level not in ANTHROPIC_EFFORT_LEVELS:
        return None
    if level == "xhigh" and (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES):
        return "high"
    return level

This normalization handles discrepancies across Claude model generations. Newer adaptive models (Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.7+) support distinct effort levels, while older intermediate architectures like Opus 4.6 or Sonnet 4.6 reject unsupported configurations with API-level 400 validation errors.

docs.title: anthropic_planned_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Computes the total max tokens allocation that the Anthropic request will request. For modern adaptive models (matching ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES), it returns the value calculated by anthropic_output_budget(). For pre-adaptive models (such as Claude Haiku 4.5), it computes the sum of the level-specific reasoning budget (ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL) and the base reply allocation (ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS, 16,000 tokens), capping the total at anthropic_output_cap().

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target Claude model identifier.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Configured pipeline reasoning effort.

Returns:

  • int: Total output token ceiling planned for the inference cycle.

Example:

def anthropic_planned_output(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int:
    """Claude max_tokens the request will plan for (before the model/context ceiling): the per-effort
    table on adaptive models, budget_tokens + 16K on pre-adaptive ones (Haiku 4.5), capped by
    ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Shared by llm_anthropic and token_utils.input_token_budget."""
    effort = anthropic_effort(model, thinking_level)
    if (model or "").lower().startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
        return anthropic_output_budget(effort)
    planned = ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_BY_LEVEL.get(effort, 0) + ANTHROPIC_BUDGET_REPLY_TOKENS
    cap = anthropic_output_cap()
    return min(planned, cap) if cap else planned

This dual-branch planning ensures backward compatibility with older thinking paradigms where thinking tokens were configured as an explicit sub-budget rather than an overall effort setting. Token budgeting components rely on this function to establish identical reservation values across inference calls and context packing.

docs.title: gemini_thinking_mode()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:

Description: Determines the thinking configuration schema supported by a specific Google Gemini model. It evaluates stripped model identifiers against legacy budget ranges (GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES), legacy architectural prefixes (gemini-1, gemini-2), and modern Gemini 3.x series configurations (GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS).

Parameters:

  • model (str): Raw or qualified Gemini model name.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, object]: A two-element tuple consisting of:
    1. Mode tag: "budget", "level", or "none".
    2. Specification: For "budget", a tuple (low, high, can_disable); for "level", a tuple of valid strings; for "none", None.

Example:

def gemini_thinking_mode(model: str) -> tuple[str, object]:
    """('level', allowed_levels) for Gemini 3.x, ('budget', (min, max, can_disable)) for 2.5,
    ('none', None) for models without a thinking control the project maps."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, low, high, can_disable in GEMINI_BUDGET_RANGES:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "budget", (low, high, can_disable)
    if not name.startswith("gemini-") or name.startswith(("gemini-1", "gemini-2")):
        return "none", None  # 1.x / 2.0, other 2.5 variants (image, live, TTS) and non-Gemini ids
    for prefix, levels in GEMINI_THINKING_LEVELS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return "level", levels
    # Other 3.x ids, '-latest' aliases (gemini-flash-latest, gemini-pro-latest) and newer families:
    # the level set every documented 3.x model accepts (a model that rejects it is handled at runtime).
    return "level", GEMINI_3_DEFAULT_LEVELS

Sending thinking_level to a Gemini 2.5 endpoint or thinking_budget to a Gemini 3.x endpoint triggers an HTTP 400 validation error in the Google GenAI SDK. This function enforces strict separation between numerical budget parameters and enumerated level parameters.

docs.title: gemini_model_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes resource-qualified model strings into bare model IDs. It strips whitespace, lowercases the string, and removes preceding URI namespace segments such as models/ or publishers/google/models/.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Raw model string.

Returns:

  • str: Normalized, unqualified Gemini model identifier.

Example:

def gemini_model_id(model: str) -> str:
    """'models/gemini-3.8-flash' / 'publishers/google/models/gemini-3.8-flash' → 'gemini-3.8-flash'."""
    return (model or "").strip().lower().rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

Vertex AI and AI Studio APIs format model references differently in API responses and configuration variables. This utility standardizes all model IDs into a consistent format used for dictionary lookups, location rules, and prefix matching.

docs.title: gemini_vertex_locations()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:

Description: Resolves allowed Vertex AI deployment regions for a given Gemini model family. It checks the normalized model ID against GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS using longest-prefix matching.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The Gemini model identifier.

Returns:

  • tuple | None: A tuple of valid region strings (e.g., ("global", "us")), GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS for unspecified Gemini 3.x variants, or None if regional endpoints are supported.

Example:

def gemini_vertex_locations(model: str) -> tuple | None:
    """Vertex AI locations that serve a Gemini 3.x model (None = any, including regional endpoints)."""
    name = gemini_model_id(model)
    for prefix, locations in GEMINI_VERTEX_LOCATIONS:
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            return locations
    return GEMINI_3_VERTEX_LOCATIONS if name.startswith("gemini-3") else None

Google Cloud Vertex AI serves Gemini 3.x models primarily from multi-region or global endpoints rather than single-region zones (like us-central1). Preflight checks consume this mapping to warn operators before execution if their configured location is unsupported.

docs.title: gemini_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum generation token limit (max_output_tokens) for Gemini requests. It looks up the per-level allowance in GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT, limits the result to the model's reported limit (or GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1]), and applies the GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment override if set.

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired pipeline reasoning level.
  • output_limit (int | None, optional): Known upper output limit for the specific model. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • int: Planned output token limit.

Example:

def gemini_output_budget(thinking_level: str | None, output_limit: int | None = None) -> int:
    """Planned Gemini max_output_tokens: per-level table, capped by the model output limit and
    GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Shared by llm_gemini (request) and token_utils (prompt budget)."""
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, GEMINI_OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    budget = min(budget, output_limit or GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[1])
    cap = _env_int("GEMINI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

Gemini models allocate thinking and response text from the same output ceiling (typically 65,536 tokens). This function enforces that requests allocate sufficient tokens to prevent reasoning traces from cutting off the final response.

docs.title: openrouter_output_budget()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Resolves the completion token ceiling for models accessed via OpenRouter. It fetches metadata via openrouter_model_info(). If the model is not found in the catalog, it falls back to OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS or returns None. When catalog metadata is available, it retrieves the base budget from OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT, caps it against the provider's max_completion_tokens (or 32,000), and applies OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS if defined.

Parameters:

  • model (str): Target OpenRouter model identifier or alias.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Desired reasoning level.

Returns:

  • int | None: Resolved token budget or None if the model's limits are unverified.

Example:

def openrouter_output_budget(model: str, thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Planned OpenRouter max_tokens: shared per-effort table, capped by the catalog's
    top_provider.max_completion_tokens and OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. None when the model is not
    in the catalog (unknown limits, e.g. a non-OpenRouter proxy): max_tokens is then omitted."""
    info = openrouter_model_info(model)
    if info is None:
        return _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    level = thinking_level.lower() if thinking_level else None
    budget = OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT.get(level, OUTPUT_TOKENS_BY_EFFORT[None])
    model_cap = (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("max_completion_tokens")
    budget = min(budget, model_cap) if model_cap else min(budget, 32_000)
    cap = _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS")
    return min(budget, cap) if cap else budget

This dynamic catalog-driven logic avoids hardcoding limits for thousands of upstream models hosted on OpenRouter. If an upstream model is unverified or running behind a proxy, returning None allows the provider to apply its own defaults.

docs.title: context_output_reserve()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:

Description: Calculates how many output tokens share the context window with the input prompt, tailored to the active provider. For Anthropic and OpenRouter, output tokens share the window and require reserving the planned maximum output. For Gemini, input and output limits are managed independently, so the reserve is 0. For unmanaged providers, it returns None.

Parameters:

  • thinking_level (str | None): Configured pipeline reasoning level.

Returns:

  • int | None: Number of tokens to reserve from the context window, or None if unmanaged.

Example:

def context_output_reserve(thinking_level: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Output tokens that share the context window with the prompt, for the active provider.
    ANTHROPIC / OPENROUTER: the planned max_tokens (thinking included). GEMINI: 0 — Gemini's input and
    output limits are separate. None: the provider does not size output (5% reserve in token_utils)."""
    provider, model, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        return anthropic_planned_output(model, thinking_level)
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        return 0
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return openrouter_output_budget(model, thinking_level)
    return None

Prompt budgeting logic in utils.token_utils uses this value to determine the maximum available prompt context. Subtracting this reserve prevents generation errors caused by prompts leaving insufficient room for output tokens.

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Resolves the active provider name from the process environment. An explicit LLM_PROVIDER environment variable takes precedence. If omitted, the presence of GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY falls back to GEMINI. Anthropic is intentionally never auto-selected without an explicit LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC configuration.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • str | None: The uppercase provider name ("GEMINI", "ANTHROPIC", "OPENROUTER", etc.) or None if unconfigured.

Example:

def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:
    """Determine the LLM provider from environment variables.

    Explicit LLM_PROVIDER wins; otherwise Gemini credentials select GEMINI (legacy default).
    ANTHROPIC is never auto-selected: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is often exported globally for other
    tools (e.g. Claude Code), and a silent switch to a paid Claude run would be surprising.
    """
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        return provider.strip().upper()
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        return "GEMINI"
    return None

The selective fallback behavior prevents accidental billable usage. Since developers frequently set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY globally for local developer tooling, requiring LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC ensures that Claude calls are explicitly opt-in.

docs.title: gemini_location()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def gemini_location() -> str:

Description: Reads and normalizes the GEMINI_LOCATION environment variable, falling back to DEFAULT_GEMINI_LOCATION ("global").

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • str: Cleaned, lowercased location string.

Example:

def gemini_location() -> str:
    """GEMINI_LOCATION lower-cased: google-genai matches 'global' / 'us' / 'eu' case-sensitively."""
    return (os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_LOCATION).strip().lower()

The Google GenAI SDK expects case-sensitive region identifiers (global, us, eu). Lowercasing here guarantees consistent matching during Vertex AI endpoint construction.

docs.title: openrouter_base_url()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_base_url() -> str:

Description: Returns the base URL for OpenRouter API requests, defaulting to DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL (https://openrouter.ai/api). It strips trailing slashes and removes any trailing /v1 segment so callers can append paths consistently.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • str: Cleaned base URL without trailing / or /v1.

Example:

def openrouter_base_url() -> str:
    """OPENROUTER_BASE_URL without a trailing '/' or '/v1' (OpenAI SDK style); paths add '/v1/...'."""
    base = (os.getenv("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL).strip().rstrip("/")
    return base.removesuffix("/v1")

This normalization prevents malformed URLs (such as double /v1/v1 prefixes) when integrating with libraries or building path segments for manual HTTP requests.

docs.title: is_openrouter_host()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def is_openrouter_host() -> bool:

Description: Checks whether the resolved OpenRouter base URL points to the official OpenRouter service (openrouter.ai).

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if openrouter.ai appears in the configured base URL; otherwise False.

Example:

def is_openrouter_host() -> bool:
    return "openrouter.ai" in openrouter_base_url().lower()

This check allows the engine to distinguish between official OpenRouter endpoints and third-party or local reverse proxies running an OpenAI-compatible API.

docs.title: resolve_llm_settings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def resolve_llm_settings() -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:

Description: Serves as the central resolver for active LLM configurations. It extracts the provider, model name, endpoint URL, and API key from environment variables and built-in defaults.

docs.title: Phase 1: Gemini Endpoint Resolution
docs.text:
provider = get_llm_provider()
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
        if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            location = gemini_location().lower()
            if location == "global":
                host = "aiplatform.googleapis.com"
            elif location in ("us", "eu"):
                host = f"aiplatform.{location}.rep.googleapis.com"  # multi-region endpoints
            else:
                host = f"{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"
            return provider, model, host, ""
        return provider, model, "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
For GEMINI, the function differentiates between Vertex AI and Google AI Studio based on the presence of GEMINI_PROJECT_ID. For Vertex AI, it builds the appropriate regional Google Cloud endpoint and leaves the API key field empty to prompt ADC authentication. For AI Studio, it configures generativelanguage.googleapis.com alongside GEMINI_API_KEY.

docs.title: Phase 2: Anthropic, OpenRouter, and Generic Resolution
docs.text:
if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        endpoint = os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_ENDPOINT
        return provider, os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_MODEL") or DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL, endpoint, os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "")
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return provider, os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "unknown"), openrouter_base_url(), os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "")
    if provider:
        return (
            provider,
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_MODEL", "unknown"),
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "unknown"),
            os.getenv(f"{provider}_API_KEY", ""),
        )
    return "UNKNOWN", "unknown", "unknown", ""
For ANTHROPIC, the function selects defaults (DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL, DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_ENDPOINT) or pulls from environment overrides. For OPENROUTER, it formats the base URL and returns OPENROUTER_MODEL. Any custom provider falls back to environment variable templates ({PROVIDER}_MODEL, {PROVIDER}_BASE_URL, {PROVIDER}_API_KEY), defaulting to "UNKNOWN" tuples when unconfigured.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, str, str, str]: A 4-tuple containing (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key).

docs.title: is_claude_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def is_claude_model(provider: str | None, model_name: str) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether the specified provider and model combination resolves to an Anthropic Claude model, whether called via the native Anthropic API or routed through an intermediary gateway like OpenRouter or AWS Bedrock.

Parameters:

  • provider (str | None): Active provider identifier.
  • model_name (str): Configured model name or routing slug.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the configuration targets a Claude model; otherwise False.

Example:

def is_claude_model(provider: str | None, model_name: str) -> bool:
    """True for native Anthropic calls and Claude models reached through a gateway (e.g. OpenRouter)."""
    return provider == "ANTHROPIC" or _normalize_claude_id(model_name).startswith("claude-")

Downstream components use this check to apply Claude-specific logic, such as using Claude token multipliers and enforcing adaptive reasoning rules, even when accessing Claude via OpenRouter.

Description: Evaluates whether a given model rejects standard sampling parameters (such as temperature, top_p, or top_k). It checks for Claude models with thinking enabled (Claude Opus 4.7+, Opus/Sonnet 5, Fable, Mythos) and Gemini 3.x series models.

def rejects_sampling_params(model_name: str) -> bool:
    """True for models that reject or ignore temperature/top_p/top_k: Claude Opus 4.7+, Opus/Sonnet 5,
    Fable, Mythos (400), and Gemini 3.x (deprecated; ignored or erroring on some endpoints)."""
    name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)
    return _normalize_claude_id(name).startswith(_NO_SAMPLING_PREFIXES) or "gemini-3" in name.lower()

This helper prevents request failures by identifying modern reasoning models that strictly enforce deterministic sampling when reasoning is enabled. Callers like utils.call_llm use it to strip sampling parameters before dispatching requests.

docs.title: get_token_ratio()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_token_ratio() -> float:

Description: Determines the initial static conversion multiplier from tiktoken (cl100k_base) counts to the active model's native tokenizer. It inspects the provider and normalized model identifier to select the baseline prior, checking environment overrides (ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO, GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO, or LLM_TOKEN_RATIO) within bounds defined by TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • float: Conversion multiplier applied to raw tiktoken prompt estimates.

Example:

def get_token_ratio() -> float:
    """Multiplier from tiktoken (cl100k) counts to the active model's tokenizer.

    tiktoken undercounts Claude tokens (more so on code), so budgets computed with raw counts can
    overflow the real context window. Claude: ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO, default 1.55 for the tokenizer
    introduced with Opus 4.7 and 1.2 for 4.6 and older. Gemini: GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO (default 1.0).
    Others: LLM_TOKEN_RATIO (default 1.0). This is the static prior: token_utils.token_ratio() corrects it
    with the ratio observed in provider-reported usage.
    """
    provider, model_name, _, _ = resolve_llm_settings()
    model_name = _catalog_model_id(model_name)
    if is_claude_model(provider, model_name):
        claude_id = _normalize_claude_id(model_name)  # also handles gateway ids on the native provider
        default = CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_NEW_TOKENIZER if claude_id.startswith(_NEW_TOKENIZER_PREFIXES) else CLAUDE_TOKEN_RATIO_OLD_TOKENIZER
        return max(_ratio_from_env("ANTHROPIC_TOKEN_RATIO", default), 1.0)
    if is_gemini_model(provider, model_name):
        return _ratio_from_env("GEMINI_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)
    return _ratio_from_env("LLM_TOKEN_RATIO", 1.0)

Because tiktoken undercounts tokens on code-heavy prompts when applied to Anthropic models (and particularly with the tokenizer introduced in Opus 4.7), using unadjusted estimates risks context window overflows. This baseline prior protects prompt packaging until utils.token_utils can calibrate ratios against live API responses.

docs.title: openrouter_catalog()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_catalog() -> list | None:

Description: Retrieves the full model catalog from OpenRouter's /v1/models endpoint. Results are cached in the module-level variable _openrouter_models_cache. If a request fails, the failure timestamp is recorded in _openrouter_last_failure and further attempts are suppressed for 60 seconds (_OPENROUTER_RETRY_COOLDOWN). Failed responses are never cached, and errors are reported via utils.output.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • list | None: A list of model specification dictionaries, or None if the request fails or is in a cooldown period.

Example:

def openrouter_catalog() -> list | None:
    """The model catalog, or None when it could not be fetched (yet)."""
    global _openrouter_models_cache, _openrouter_last_failure
    if _openrouter_models_cache is not None:
        return _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_last_failure and time.time() - _openrouter_last_failure < _OPENROUTER_RETRY_COOLDOWN:
        return None
    url = f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/models"
    try:
        resp = requests.get(url, timeout=20)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.json().get("data")
        if not isinstance(data, list):
            raise ValueError("OpenRouter model catalog response has no 'data' list")
        _openrouter_models_cache = data
        return data
    except Exception as e:
        from utils.llm_common import warn_once
        from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

        _openrouter_last_failure = time.time()
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Failed to fetch OpenRouter model info from {url}: {e}", dest="LOG")
        if warn_once("openrouter_catalog_unavailable"):
            emit("WARN_OPENROUTER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE", url=url, error=str(e)[:200])
        return None

The cooldown protects startup workflows from hanging during transient outages. Using warn_once ensures operators receive a clean diagnostic warning rather than repeated errors across multiple nodes.

docs.title: openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Searches the OpenRouter catalog for a model entry matching a given ID. The lookup handles routing suffixes (such as :nitro, :floor, :thinking), canonical slugs, dated slugs (e.g., matching anthropic/claude-4.6-opus to anthropic/claude-4.6-opus-20260205), and resolves alias_target references to underlying target models.

Parameters:

  • model_id (str): Requested model name, slug, or aliased string.

Returns:

  • dict | None: The matching catalog dictionary from OpenRouter, or None if not found or the catalog is unavailable.

Example:

def openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:
    """Catalog entry for a model id: exact id, canonical_slug, routing-suffix variant
    (':nitro', ':floor', ...), dated canonical slug (e.g. 'anthropic/claude-4.6-opus' →
    'anthropic/claude-4.6-opus-20260205'), or a '~...-latest' alias's target."""
    catalog = openrouter_catalog()
    if not catalog or not model_id:
        return None
    wanted = model_id.strip()
    candidates = [wanted, *(wanted[: -len(suffix)] for suffix in _OPENROUTER_ROUTING_SUFFIXES if wanted.endswith(suffix))]
    for name in candidates:
        entry = next((m for m in catalog if m.get("id") == name or m.get("canonical_slug") == name), None)
        if entry is None:
            # Dated canonical slug only ('anthropic/claude-4.6-opus' → '…-20260205'): a looser prefix
            # match would map typos such as 'google/gemini-3.1-pro' onto a different model.
            dated = re.compile(re.escape(name) + r"-\d{8}")
            entry = next((m for m in catalog if dated.fullmatch(str(m.get("canonical_slug", "")))), None)
        if entry is not None:
            target = (entry.get("alias_target") or {}).get("slug")
            if target and target != entry.get("id"):
                return next((m for m in catalog if m.get("id") == target or m.get("canonical_slug") == target), entry)
            return entry
    return None

This matching logic resolves varied model specifications to concrete catalog metadata, ensuring the pipeline correctly extracts context limits and parameter capabilities regardless of the naming style used.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Resolves the maximum input context length (in tokens) for the active model. For Anthropic, it delegates to utils.llm_anthropic.get_model_limits(). For OpenRouter, it reads top_provider.context_length or context_length from the catalog. For Gemini, it calls utils.llm_gemini.get_model_limits() or falls back to GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0] (1,048,576). Other providers default to 100,000 tokens.

Parameters:

  • endpoint_url (str): Base URL or host domain for the provider.
  • model_name (str): Target model identifier.
  • api_key (str, optional): Active provider API key. Defaults to "".

Returns:

  • int: Maximum allowable input context window size in tokens.

Example:

def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    """
    Maximum context length (input tokens) of the active model.
    ANTHROPIC: Anthropic Models API (max_input_tokens), offline fallback table.
    GEMINI: models.get(input_token_limit) on AI Studio, static 1,048,576 (Vertex, or no SDK).
    OPENROUTER: catalog top_provider.context_length, else context_length.
    Other endpoints: 100,000.
    """
    default_limit = 100000
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    try:
        if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
            from utils.llm_anthropic import get_model_limits

            return get_model_limits(model_name)[0]

        if provider == "OPENROUTER" or "openrouter.ai" in (endpoint_url or ""):
            info = openrouter_model_info(model_name)
            if info:
                return (info.get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or info.get("context_length") or default_limit
            return default_limit

        if provider == "GEMINI":
            try:
                from utils.llm_gemini import get_model_limits as gemini_limits
            except ImportError:
                return GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]
            return gemini_limits(model_name)[0]

        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit
        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            return GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS[0]
    except Exception as e:
        from utils.output import emit

        emit("WARN_CONTEXT_LENGTH_FETCH", model=model_name, endpoint=endpoint_url, error=str(e))

    return default_limit

Downstream prompt planners use this context length to establish hard boundaries for prompt packaging. If an unexpected error occurs during provider lookup, the function logs a warning and falls back to a safe default.

docs.title: describe_thinking_support()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def describe_thinking_support(provider: str, model: str) -> str:

Description: Generates a human-readable, one-line summary of how thinking and reasoning parameters apply to the active provider and model, used for terminal logs during startup.

Parameters:

  • provider (str): Target provider name.
  • model (str): Target model identifier.

Returns:

  • str: Localized string describing supported reasoning controls.

Example:

def describe_thinking_support(provider: str, model: str) -> str:
    """One-line description of how thinking levels are applied for the startup display."""
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        name = (model or "").lower()
        if not name.startswith(ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES):
            return "thinking.budget_tokens (low…max → 2,048…32,000)"
        levels = "low, medium, high, max" if name.startswith(ANTHROPIC_NO_XHIGH_PREFIXES) else "low, medium, high, xhigh, max"
        return f"adaptive thinking + output_config.effort ∈ {{{levels}}}"
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
        if mode == "level":
            return f"thinking_level ∈ {{{', '.join(spec)}}}"
        if mode == "budget":
            low, high, can_disable = spec
            return f"thinking_budget {low:,}-{high:,}" + (f" ({_ui('CFG_THINKING_BUDGET_OFF')})" if can_disable else "")
        return "—"
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        info = openrouter_model_info(model)
        if info is None:
            return f"reasoning.effort ({_ui('CFG_THINKING_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE')})" if not openrouter_catalog() else "—"
        reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
        if not isinstance(reasoning, dict):
            return "reasoning.effort" if "reasoning" in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []) else "—"
        efforts = reasoning.get("supported_efforts")
        if "supported_efforts" not in reasoning and reasoning.get("supports_max_tokens"):
            text = "reasoning.max_tokens (minimal…max → 1,024…32,000)"  # llm_openrouter._REASONING_BUDGETS
        elif efforts:
            text = f"reasoning.effort ∈ {{{', '.join(e for e in efforts if e != 'none')}}}"
        else:
            text = "reasoning.effort"
        extras = [_ui("CFG_THINKING_DEFAULT_EFFORT", effort=reasoning["default_effort"])] if reasoning.get("default_effort") else []
        if reasoning.get("mandatory"):
            extras.append(_ui("CFG_THINKING_MANDATORY"))
        return text + (f" · {' · '.join(extras)}" if extras else "")
    return "—"

This diagnostic utility provides visibility into active reasoning settings at startup, confirming whether the run will use adaptive effort parameters, fixed token budgets, or default parameters.

docs.title: parse_ant_auth_status()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def parse_ant_auth_status(output: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:

Description: Parses the raw stdout and stderr of the ant auth status command to extract active Anthropic credentials and workspace profiles. Because the CLI exit code does not indicate health, this function parses rows marked (active) under the Credentials and Workspace sections, redacting credential strings using _redact().

Parameters:

  • output (str): Combined output from ant auth status.

Returns:

  • tuple[str | None, str | None]: A pair containing (active_credential_description, active_workspace_description).

Example:

def parse_ant_auth_status(output: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Return (active credential, active workspace) from `ant auth status` output.

    The command's exit code is not a health signal, so read its `(active)` rows instead:
        Credentials
          (active) * Profile (user_oauth) [via active_config]       sk-ant-oat01-EXA...
        Workspace
          (active) * Workspace                                      wrkspc_01... (Engineering)
    """
    section, credential, workspace = None, None, None
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if not line[0].isspace():
            header = line.strip().lower()
            section = header if header in ("credentials", "workspace") else None
            continue
        if "(active)" not in line:
            continue
        text = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", _redact(re.sub(r"^\s*\(active\)\s*\*?\s*", "", line))).strip()
        if section == "workspace":
            workspace = workspace or text
        else:
            credential = credential or text
    return credential, workspace

This parser extracts authentication details from human-readable CLI output, allowing the system to verify active profiles while redacting sensitive tokens before logging.

docs.title: check_anthropic_auth()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_anthropic_auth() -> bool:

Description: Validates authentication credentials when LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC. The verification follows this sequence: 1. Verifies that the anthropic Python SDK is installed. 2. Checks for ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN. 3. Checks for Workload Identity Federation configuration. 4. Searches for ant CLI credentials or existing profile files in _anthropic_config_dir(). 5. Invokes ant auth status to confirm an active profile.

If authentication cannot be verified, it outputs diagnostic setup instructions and returns False.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if valid credentials are confirmed or the provider is not Anthropic; False if unauthenticated.

Example:

def check_anthropic_auth() -> bool:
    """Preflight for LLM_PROVIDER=ANTHROPIC. Returns False (after printing instructions) when
    the run cannot authenticate; True otherwise, including for every other provider.

    Order: anthropic package installed → ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN →
    Workload Identity Federation env vars → `ant auth status` (active login profile) →
    stored login files when the `ant` CLI is not installed.
    """
    from utils.output import emit, emit_raw

    if get_llm_provider() != "ANTHROPIC":
        return True
    if not _anthropic_sdk_installed():
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_SDK_MISSING")
        return False

    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") and _env_set("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"):
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_KEY_AND_TOKEN")
    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
        return True
    if _env_set("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN")
        return True
    if all(_env_set(v) for v in _FEDERATION_VARS) and (_env_set("ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE") or _env_set("ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN")):
        emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source="Workload Identity Federation")
        return True

    # No key: the SDK falls back to an `ant auth login` profile. Verify one is active.
    ant = shutil.which("ant")
    if not ant:
        stored = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(_anthropic_config_dir(), "credentials", "*.json")))
        if stored:
            emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_ANT_MISSING_LOGIN_FOUND", path=stored[0])
            return True
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NO_CREDENTIALS")
        _emit_auth_help(ant_installed=False)
        return False

    # Run with the same environment the SDK will see; empty key variables are dropped so the
    # CLI reports the profile the SDK will actually use (the SDK treats empty as unset).
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not (k in ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN") and not v.strip())}
    try:
        result = subprocess.run([ant, "auth", "status"], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=30, env=env)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
        emit("WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED", error=str(e))
        return True

    output = f"{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}"
    credential, workspace = parse_ant_auth_status(output)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ant auth status | exit={result.returncode}\n{_redact(output).strip()}", dest="LOG")
    if not credential:
        emit("ERROR_ANTHROPIC_NOT_LOGGED_IN")
        details = _redact(output).strip()
        if details:
            emit_raw("INFO", "\n".join(f"    {line}" for line in details.splitlines()))
        _emit_auth_help(ant_installed=True)
        return False

    source = _ui("AUTH_SOURCE_ANT_LOGIN", credential=credential)
    if workspace:
        source += f" | {_ui('AUTH_SOURCE_WORKSPACE', workspace=workspace)}"
    emit("ANTHROPIC_AUTH_OK", source=source)
    return True

This preflight check catches authentication failures before pipeline execution starts, avoiding failures midway through repository crawling or multi-step chapter generation.

docs.title: check_gemini_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_gemini_config() -> bool:

Description: Validates configuration for LLM_PROVIDER=GEMINI. It confirms that google-genai is installed at version >= 1.56.0 (GEMINI_MIN_SDK), verifies that the selected model is not retired (via GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS), checks Vertex AI region availability and Application Default Credentials when GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is set, or verifies GEMINI_API_KEY for AI Studio.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if configuration and credentials are valid; False if misconfigured.

Example:

def check_gemini_config() -> bool:
    """Preflight for LLM_PROVIDER=GEMINI (or Gemini credentials without LLM_PROVIDER)."""
    from utils.output import emit

    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
    version = _installed_version("google-genai")
    if version is None:
        emit("ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_MISSING")
        return False
    if version < GEMINI_MIN_SDK:
        emit("ERROR_GEMINI_SDK_OUTDATED", version=".".join(map(str, version)), required=".".join(map(str, GEMINI_MIN_SDK)))
        return False

    retired = GEMINI_RETIRED_MODELS.get(gemini_model_id(model))
    if retired:
        replacement, aliased_on_ai_studio = retired
        if aliased_on_ai_studio and not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED", model=model, replacement=replacement)
        else:
            emit("ERROR_GEMINI_MODEL_RETIRED", model=model, replacement=replacement)
            return False

    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        location = gemini_location()
        allowed = gemini_vertex_locations(model)
        if allowed is not None and location.lower() not in allowed:
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_LOCATION", location=location, model=model, allowed=", ".join(allowed))
        try:
            import google.auth

            google.auth.default()
        except Exception as e:  # DefaultCredentialsError, or google-auth missing
            emit("ERROR_GEMINI_VERTEX_CREDENTIALS", error=str(e).splitlines()[0][:200])
            return False
        emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="Gemini", source=_ui("AUTH_SOURCE_VERTEX", project=os.environ["GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"], location=location))
        return True
    if _env_set("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        emit("LLM_AUTH_OK", provider="Gemini", source=_ui("AUTH_SOURCE_AI_STUDIO"))
        return True
    emit("ERROR_GEMINI_NO_CREDENTIALS")
    return False

Enforcing google-genai >= 1.56.0 prevents runtime Pydantic validation errors that occur when passing minimal or medium thinking levels to earlier SDK versions.

def check_openrouter_config() -> bool:

docs.title: check_llm_auth()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def check_llm_auth() -> bool:

Description: Top-level authentication preflight dispatcher. It determines the active provider via get_llm_provider() and routes execution to check_anthropic_auth(), check_gemini_config(), or check_openrouter_config(). For unknown or custom providers, it defaults to True.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the active provider passes preflight validation; False if authentication or configuration checks fail.

Example:

def check_llm_auth() -> bool:
    """Credential/SDK preflight for the active provider, run before any LLM call by main() and the
    utils/call_llm.py self-test. Prints setup instructions and returns False when the run cannot work."""
    provider = get_llm_provider()
    if provider == "ANTHROPIC":
        return check_anthropic_auth()
    if provider == "GEMINI":
        return check_gemini_config()
    if provider == "OPENROUTER":
        return check_openrouter_config()
    return True

Invoked during CLI startup in main.py and before the self-test routines in utils.call_llm, this dispatcher acts as the primary quality gate for provider configuration across the application.

docs.title: _env_int()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _env_int(name: str) -> int | None:

Description: Safely parses a designated environment variable as a positive integer. If the environment variable is unset, contains non-numeric characters, or parses to a number less than or equal to zero, it returns None.

Parameters:

  • name (str): Name of the environment variable.

Returns:

  • int | None: Positive integer value or None.

Example:

def _env_int(name: str) -> int | None:
    value = os.getenv(name, "").strip()
    return int(value) if value.isdigit() and int(value) > 0 else None

This helper centralizes environment variable parsing for token limits (such as ANTHROPIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), ensuring invalid inputs fail gracefully to defaults rather than raising unhandled exceptions.

docs.title: _normalize_claude_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _normalize_claude_id(model_name: str) -> str:

Description: Normalizes Claude model identifiers across various cloud formats (e.g., Anthropic native, AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter slugs, version-first naming) into a consistent family-first format. It replaces dots with dashes, extracts substrings following claude-, and uses _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST to reorder patterns like claude-4-7-opus into claude-opus-4-7.

Parameters:

  • model_name (str): The raw model name or routing string.

Returns:

  • str: Standardized Claude identifier.

Example:

def _normalize_claude_id(model_name: str) -> str:
    """Gateway/cloud IDs → bare family-first Claude ID: 'anthropic/claude-opus-4.7',
    'bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7-v1:0' and the version-first alias
    'anthropic/claude-4.7-opus-20260416' all → 'claude-opus-4-7...'."""
    name = (model_name or "").lower().replace(".", "-")
    start = name.find("claude-")
    name = name[start:] if start >= 0 else name
    match = _CLAUDE_VERSION_FIRST.match(name)
    if match:
        major, minor, family = match.groups()
        name = f"claude-{family}-{major}" + (f"-{minor}" if minor else "") + name[match.end() :]
    return name

This transformation normalizes varied model naming conventions across cloud providers (e.g., bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7-v1:0 vs claude-4.7-opus) so prefix matching against ANTHROPIC_ADAPTIVE_PREFIXES evaluates consistently.

docs.title: _catalog_model_id()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _catalog_model_id(model_name: str) -> str:

Description: Resolves a model name to its canonical identifier via the OpenRouter catalog when the active provider is OPENROUTER. For other providers, it returns the input model name unchanged.

Parameters:

  • model_name (str): Requested model name or alias.

Returns:

  • str: Canonical catalog model ID, or the original string.

Example:

def _catalog_model_id(model_name: str) -> str:
    """On OPENROUTER, resolve aliases ('~anthropic/claude-opus-latest', canonical slugs) through the
    catalog so family checks see the real model; other providers use the name as given."""
    if get_llm_provider() == "OPENROUTER":
        info = openrouter_model_info(model_name)
        if info and info.get("id"):
            return info["id"]
    return model_name or ""

Resolving aliases (such as ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest) to canonical identifiers ensures that downstream checks—like rejects_sampling_params() and is_claude_model()—evaluate the underlying model correctly.

docs.title: _ratio_from_env()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _ratio_from_env(name: str, default: float) -> float:

Description: Parses a float token ratio from an environment variable and clamps it within TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS ([0.5, 3.0]). If parsing fails with a ValueError or produces a non-finite value (inf, NaN), it falls back to default.

Parameters:

  • name (str): Environment variable name.
  • default (float): Fallback ratio.

Returns:

  • float: Validated and clamped conversion multiplier.

Example:

def _ratio_from_env(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    """Float env ratio clamped to TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS; unparsable / non-finite values use the default."""
    try:
        ratio = float(os.getenv(name, default))
    except ValueError:
        ratio = default
    if not math.isfinite(ratio):
        ratio = default
    low, high = TOKEN_RATIO_BOUNDS
    return min(max(ratio, low), high)

Clamping the ratio within [0.5, 3.0] protects prompt sizing from extreme or malformed configuration values that could otherwise lead to empty prompts or context window overflows.

docs.title: _anthropic_sdk_installed()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _anthropic_sdk_installed() -> bool:

Description: Checks whether the anthropic Python package is installed in the current environment without importing it directly, inspecting package specifications via importlib.util.find_spec() and checking sys.modules.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • bool: True if anthropic is available for import; otherwise False.

Example:

def _anthropic_sdk_installed() -> bool:
    try:
        return importlib.util.find_spec("anthropic") is not None
    except (ImportError, ValueError):  # ValueError: module already imported without a spec

Checking module availability via importlib.util.find_spec() avoids loading SDK dependencies into memory when evaluating configuration for other providers.

docs.title: _anthropic_config_dir()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _anthropic_config_dir() -> str:

Description: Resolves the local filesystem path where the ant CLI tool stores its configuration and credential profiles. It respects ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR, falls back to %APPDATA%\Anthropic on Windows, and uses ~/.config/anthropic on POSIX systems.

Parameters:

None.

Returns:

  • str: Absolute path to the Anthropic configuration directory.

Example:

def _anthropic_config_dir() -> str:
    """Directory where `ant auth login` stores profiles (ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR or the OS default)."""
    if os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR"):
        return os.environ["ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR"]
    if os.name == "nt":
        return os.path.join(os.getenv("APPDATA", os.path.expanduser("~")), "Anthropic")
    return os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".config", "anthropic")

This path resolution lets preflight checks find stored profile credentials on disk even when the ant binary itself is missing from the system PATH.

docs.title: _redact()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _redact(text: str) -> str:

Description: Masks sensitive Anthropic API keys and OAuth tokens from CLI logs and terminal output, replacing strings matching _TOKEN_PATTERN (sk-ant-...) with sk-ant-***.

Parameters:

Returns:

Example:

def _redact(text: str) -> str:
    """Mask token prefixes that `ant auth status` prints (e.g. sk-ant-oat01-EXA...)."""
    return _TOKEN_PATTERN.sub("sk-ant-***", text)

This redaction prevents active credentials from leaking into log files or console output during ant auth status parsing and diagnostic emission.

docs.title: _emit_auth_help()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Description: Emits terminal help messages guiding operators on how to authenticate with Anthropic, covering API keys, ant auth login, and platform-specific ant CLI installation instructions.

def _emit_auth_help(ant_installed: bool) -> None:

The output messages adapt based on whether the CLI is installed, directing users to the appropriate installation command for Windows, macOS, or Linux.

docs.title: _installed_version()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _installed_version(dist: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:

Description: Reads the installed version of a Python package distribution using importlib.metadata, parsing up to the first three numeric segments into an integer tuple. Returns None if the distribution is not installed.

Parameters:

  • dist (str): Package distribution name (e.g., "google-genai").

Returns:

  • tuple[int, ...] | None: Numeric version tuple (e.g., (1, 56, 0)) or None if not found.

Example:

def _installed_version(dist: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
    from importlib import metadata

    try:
        raw = metadata.version(dist)
    except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        return None
    parts = []
    for piece in raw.split(".")[:3]:
        digits = re.match(r"\d+", piece)
        parts.append(int(digits.group()) if digits else 0)
    return tuple(parts)

This helper allows check_gemini_config() to perform clean tuple comparisons against GEMINI_MIN_SDK without incurring runtime overhead from heavier version-parsing dependencies.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive validation patterns to catch configuration problems during preflight checks, avoiding unhandled exceptions during inference:

  • Graceful Environment Coercion: Functions such as _env_int() and _ratio_from_env() catch ValueError internally and check for non-finite values (math.isfinite), falling back to safe defaults when variables contain invalid data.
  • Network Fault Resilience in OpenRouter Catalog: When fetching the OpenRouter catalog in openrouter_catalog(), network or JSON parsing failures trigger a 60-second cooldown (_OPENROUTER_RETRY_COOLDOWN). Failed responses are not cached, and transient errors are logged once via warn_once() rather than raising uncaught exceptions.
  • Subprocess Isolation: In check_anthropic_auth(), running ant auth status via subprocess.run() catches OSError and SubprocessError. If the execution fails or times out (30s), it logs a warning (WARN_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_UNVERIFIED) and allows execution to proceed to SDK-level authentication.
  • Dynamic Import Safety: Package presence checks like _anthropic_sdk_installed() and _installed_version() wrap importlib calls in defensive try/except blocks (ImportError, ValueError, PackageNotFoundError), allowing checks to run safely across diverse virtual environment setups.

docs.title: llm_gemini.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_gemini.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the configuration abstractions and provider capability mappings established in utils/llm_config.py, utils/llm_gemini.py provides the dedicated, low-level execution engine for Google Gemini models within the pipeline. It acts as the sole driver importing the official google-genai SDK, isolating external Google Cloud and AI Studio dependencies from the remainder of the architecture. The module encapsulates authentication resolution, thinking mode negotiation, response streaming, finish reason analysis, token accounting, and financial modeling for both Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3.x architectures.

The module interfaces with Google's inference infrastructure through two distinct deployment topologies: Google AI Studio (authenticated via GEMINI_API_KEY) and Google Cloud Vertex AI (authenticated via environment credentials alongside GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and GEMINI_LOCATION). All generations are executed through chunked streaming (generate_content_stream), ensuring long-form documentation synthesis does not encounter transport-layer HTTP timeouts. Furthermore, the engine manages model-specific reasoning controls—translating abstract thinking tiers into discrete reasoning levels on Gemini 3.x or explicit token budgets on Gemini 2.5—while automatically executing a graceful degradation fallback when encountering unexpected provider-side schema rejections.
