docs.title: get_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Resolves and sanitizes the configured Gemini model name from the runtime environment. It reads the GEMINI_MODEL environment variable, falls back to DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL if unset, and strips any Google Cloud resource prefixes (such as models/ or publishers/google/models/) via gemini_model_id() to ensure compatibility across both Vertex AI and AI Studio endpoints.

Parameters:

This function takes no parameters.

Returns:

  • str: The normalized model identifier string (e.g., "gemini-3.7-flash").

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions internally.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py call_gemini()
model = get_model()
raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
max_output = _max_output_tokens(model, thinking_level)

The function queries os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") and passes the value through the canonical normalization logic in utils.llm_config.gemini_model_id. Downstream callers receive a uniform string identifier that can be used directly in API client routing and pricing lookup tables.

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Retrieves the maximum input and output token boundaries for a given Gemini model. If using AI Studio credentials, it queries the Google GenAI SDK's client.models.get() endpoint dynamically to inspect remote limits and caches the result. When running against Google Cloud Vertex AI (where the SDK does not map token limits) or when network lookups fail, it falls back to the static boundaries defined in GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The normalized model identifier string.

Returns:

  • tuple[int, int]: A 2-tuple structured as (input_token_limit, output_token_limit).

Raises:

This function traps all exceptions internally and logs a warning via emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP"), returning default fallback limits instead of raising.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py get_model_limits() implementation
if model in _model_limits_cache:
    return _model_limits_cache[model]
limits = GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS
if not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
    try:
        info = _get_client().models.get(model=model)
        limits = (
            getattr(info, "input_token_limit", None) or limits[0],
            getattr(info, "output_token_limit", None) or limits[1],
        )
        emit_raw(
            "DEBUG",
            f"Gemini models.get | model={model} | input={limits[0]:,} | output={limits[1]:,}",
            dest="LOG",
        )
    except Exception as e:
        emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
_model_limits_cache[model] = limits
return limits

The function checks an in-memory memoization dictionary (_model_limits_cache) to avoid redundant metadata round-trips. When dynamic lookup succeeds on AI Studio, it preserves any missing remote fields by falling back on the corresponding element in GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS. Vertex AI invocations bypass dynamic lookups entirely because the Vertex API does not publish token boundary attributes on model descriptor objects.

docs.title: call_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary entry point for executing single-turn prompt completions against Google Gemini models. It orchestrates prompt token counting, output budgeting, reasoning configuration, streaming consumption, automated failure recovery, telemetry recording, and termination classification.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The complete, formatted prompt string to send to the model.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): The requested reasoning effort tier (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", or None to adopt model defaults). Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The generated text response. If the response was truncated due to output token exhaustion, an instance of TruncatedResponse (a specialized str subclass) is returned.

Raises:

  • LLMRefusalError: Raised when the prompt is blocked by content policy or when the candidate output triggers safety, blocklist, recitation, or language filters.
  • genai_errors.ClientError: Raised if the Google GenAI SDK encounters unhandled client-side or HTTP protocol errors not covered by the thinking recovery fallback.
  • ValueError: Raised if neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment.

docs.title: Phase 1: Parameter Assembly and Configuration
docs.text:
from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw

model = get_model()
raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
max_output = _max_output_tokens(model, thinking_level)
thinking, level_desc = _thinking_config(model, thinking_level)
# No tools are passed, so automatic function calling is off (google-genai warns on streams otherwise).
no_afc = types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True)
config = types.GenerateContentConfig(
    max_output_tokens=max_output,
    thinking_config=thinking,
    automatic_function_calling=no_afc,
)
emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"Gemini request | model={model} | {level_desc} | max_output_tokens={max_output:,} | location={gemini_location() if os.getenv('GEMINI_PROJECT_ID') else 'ai-studio'}",
    dest="LOG",
)

In the initialization phase, the model identifier is normalized and the raw prompt is tokenized using count_tokens_raw(). The maximum allowable output token ceiling is computed via _max_output_tokens(), which harmonizes caller-requested reasoning allocations with the model's hard output limits. The thinking configuration is resolved into an SDK-compatible types.ThinkingConfig instance. Automatic function calling is explicitly disabled via types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True) to prevent the SDK from emitting runtime warnings when processing chunked streams without tool declarations.

docs.title: Phase 2: Stream Execution and Fallback Recovery
docs.text:
start = time.time()
try:
    result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
except genai_errors.ClientError as e:
    # A model that rejects our thinking control (unknown future model, level set changed):
    # warn once and resend without it for the rest of the run.
    if getattr(e, "code", None) == 400 and thinking is not None and "think" in str(e).lower():
        _thinking_rejected.add(model)
        emit("WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
        config = types.GenerateContentConfig(
            max_output_tokens=max_output,
            thinking_config=None,
            automatic_function_calling=no_afc,
        )
        result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
    else:
        raise
elapsed = time.time() - start

The execution phase dispatches the prompt through _stream(). If the remote endpoint returns an HTTP 400 client error caused by an incompatible or deprecated thinking specification, the exception handler catches the genai_errors.ClientError. It verifies the status code and error message, caches the model in the module-level _thinking_rejected set to prevent future incompatible requests, strips the thinking configuration from types.GenerateContentConfig, and immediately retries the generation. Unrelated errors are re-raised without modification.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry Accounting and Token Ratio Observation
docs.text:
if result["usage"] is not None:
    _record(model, result["usage"], raw_tokens, level_desc, result["finish"], elapsed)
else:
    record_usage("GEMINI", model, cost=None, measured=False)  # stream carried no usage_metadata
if is_debug() and result["thoughts"]:
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{result['thoughts']}", dest="LOG")

Once the stream is completely consumed, the response payload is evaluated for telemetry metadata. If usage_metadata was returned by the SDK, _record() extracts token counts across prompt input, candidate output, reasoning/thought tokens, and cached prompt reads, computes estimated billing, and passes prompt statistics to observe_prompt_tokens(). If usage metadata was absent from the stream chunks, the module records an unmeasured fallback event via record_usage(). When debug mode is active, extracted model thought summaries are directed to the execution log.

docs.title: Phase 4: Safety, Refusal, and Truncation Evaluation
docs.text:
if result["block_reason"] or result["finish"] in _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS:
    category = result["block_reason"] or result["finish"]
    # A blocked prompt repeats for the same input; a stop on the candidate may pass on resampling.
    retryable = not result["block_reason"] and result["finish"] in _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS
    count_event("GEMINI", "refusals")
    emit(
        "WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL",
        provider="Gemini",
        model=model,
        category=category,
    )
    raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="GEMINI", retryable=retryable)
if result["finish"] in _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS:
    count_event("GEMINI", "truncations")
    emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="Gemini", max_tokens=f"{max_output:,}")
    return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
if not result["text"]:
    emit_raw("WARNING", f"Gemini response contained no text (finish_reason={result['finish'] or 'n/a'})", dest="LOG")
return result["text"]

The final phase examines prompt feedback and candidate finish reasons. If a prompt-level block reason exists or the candidate finished with a refusal code, the system differentiates between deterministic policy blocks (non-retryable) and candidate-level safety/recitation/sampling stops (retryable=True), recording telemetry and raising an LLMRefusalError. If the generation was halted due to reaching MAX_TOKENS, it logs a truncation warning and wraps the output string in a TruncatedResponse to prevent downstream nodes from caching partial completions. If completed normally, the text is returned as a standard string.

docs.title: _timeout_ms()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _timeout_ms() -> int:

Description: Calculates the total per-request HTTP timeout in milliseconds. It reads GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS from the environment, enforces a minimum baseline of 30.0 seconds to prevent premature disconnections, and converts the resulting floating-point value to an integer millisecond representation.

Parameters:

This helper takes no parameters.

Returns:

  • int: Total request timeout in milliseconds.

Raises:

This helper does not raise exceptions; invalid numeric formats fall back to 1,800 seconds (1,800,000 ms).

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py _timeout_ms() implementation
try:
    seconds = float(os.getenv("GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "1800"))
except ValueError:
    seconds = 1800.0
return int(max(seconds, 30.0) * 1000)

The function provides an operational guard for streaming invocations. Because the Google GenAI SDK applies this timeout across the lifetime of the entire response stream rather than as an idle read timeout, prolonged generations with extended reasoning budgets require deadlines that span several minutes.

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Lazily constructs and caches the global google.genai.Client singleton (_client). It configures transport-level retry policies and determines whether to initialize the client for Google Cloud Vertex AI or Google AI Studio based on ambient environment variables.

Parameters:

This helper takes no parameters.

Returns:

  • google.genai.Client: An initialized, authenticated Google GenAI client instance.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised if neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is configured in the environment.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py _get_client() implementation
global _client
if _client is None:
    http_options = types.HttpOptions(
        timeout=_timeout_ms(),  # milliseconds; with no timeout a stalled connection hangs forever
        # One SDK retry for transient errors; PocketFlow node retries (5 x 20 s) sit on top.
        retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2, http_status_codes=[408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]),
    )
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        _client = genai.Client(
            vertexai=True,
            project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"),
            location=gemini_location(),
            http_options=http_options,
        )
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        _client = genai.Client(
            vertexai=False,
            api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"),
            http_options=http_options,
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
return _client

The helper sets up types.HttpRetryOptions to automatically retry transient HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 status codes up to two attempts at the network layer. When authenticating via GEMINI_API_KEY, it explicitly passes vertexai=False to prevent the SDK from inadvertently redirecting API key credentials to Vertex AI if GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true is set elsewhere in the environment.

docs.title: _thinking_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None):

Description: Resolves the appropriate google.genai.types.ThinkingConfig object and human-readable diagnostic description based on the target model's architecture. It enforces mutual exclusivity between Gemini 3.x thinking levels and Gemini 2.5 thinking budgets.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The normalized model identifier string.
  • level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort tier, or None.

Returns:

  • tuple[types.ThinkingConfig | None, str]: A 2-tuple containing the configured ThinkingConfig instance (or None) and a diagnostic label string (e.g., "thinking_level=high", "thinking_budget=4096", "default").

Raises:

This helper does not raise exceptions. It emits warnings if thinking levels are clamped or unsupported.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py _thinking_config() implementation
mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
include = True if is_debug() else None  # thought summaries only for the debug log
if model in _thinking_rejected:
    return None, "default (thinking config rejected by model)"
if not level:
    return (types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True) if include and mode != "none" else None), "default"
if mode == "level":
    effective = clamp_level(level.lower(), spec) or spec[-1]
    if effective != level.lower() and warn_once("gemini_level", model, level):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effective, model=model)
    return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=effective, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_level={effective}"
if mode == "budget":
    low, high, _can_disable = spec
    budget = min(max(GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS.get(level.lower(), 4096), low), high)
    return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=budget, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_budget={budget}"
if warn_once("gemini_no_thinking", model):
    emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
return None, "unsupported"

The function calls gemini_thinking_mode(model) from utils.llm_config to identify whether the target architecture expects a categorical reasoning level (mode == "level"), an integer token budget (mode == "budget"), or does not support reasoning (mode == "none"). If the model has previously returned an HTTP 400 error against thinking configurations, it bypasses configuration immediately. When debug mode is active, it sets include_thoughts=True so internal reasoning thoughts can be captured in diagnostics.

docs.title: _max_output_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Computes the output token reservation for a request. It determines the target output budget based on the active reasoning level and caps the calculation by the physical model limit retrieved from get_model_limits().

Parameters:

  • model (str): The normalized model identifier string.
  • level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort tier, or None.

Returns:

  • int: The maximum allowed output token budget.

Raises:

This helper does not raise exceptions internally.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py _max_output_tokens() implementation
_input_limit, output_limit = get_model_limits(model)
return gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit)

Because Google Gemini documents separate, non-shared context windows for input and output, output allocations are not diminished by oversized input prompts. The helper delegates directly to gemini_output_budget() in utils.llm_config to resolve the budget against the model's reported output_limit.

docs.title: _name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _name(value) -> str:

Description: Safely normalizes enum members, string representations, or raw objects into a clean, uppercase string identifier.

Parameters:

  • value (Any): An enum instance, string, or object representing a finish reason or block reason.

Returns:

  • str: The uppercase name or string representation, stripped of object namespaces.

Raises:

This helper does not raise exceptions.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py _name() implementation
return (getattr(value, "name", None) or str(value or "")).split(".")[-1].upper()

The helper prevents integration breakages when new or unlisted enum values arrive dynamically from the Google GenAI SDK. By checking getattr(value, "name", None) and splitting by period boundaries, it converts values like FinishReason.MAX_TOKENS or "FinishReason.MAX_TOKENS" reliably into "MAX_TOKENS".

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated monetary cost (in USD) of an inference request based on Google's published multi-tier pricing schedules, introductory rate periods, regional Vertex AI surcharges, and long-context prompt thresholds.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • prompt_tokens (int): Total prompt token count (including cached tokens).
  • cached (int): Number of prompt tokens served from context cache.
  • output_tokens (int): Total output tokens generated (candidate tokens plus thinking tokens).
  • today (datetime.date | None, optional): Override date used for introductory pricing evaluation. Defaults to None (which uses datetime.date.today()).

Returns:

  • float | None: Estimated cost in USD, or None if the model has no pricing entry in _PRICING.

Raises:

This helper does not raise exceptions.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py _price() implementation
key = next((k for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if model.lower().startswith(k)), None)
if key is None:
    return None
row = _PRICING[key]
if key in _INTRO_PRICING and (today or datetime.date.today()) <= _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL:
    row = _INTRO_PRICING[key]
p_in, p_out, p_cache = row[3:6] if len(row) == 6 and prompt_tokens > _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD else row[:3]
uncached = max(prompt_tokens - cached, 0)
cost = (uncached * p_in + cached * p_cache + output_tokens * p_out) / 1_000_000
if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") and gemini_location().lower() != "global":
    cost *= _REGIONAL_UPLIFT
return cost

Pricing lookups match model names against the keys in _PRICING using longest-prefix matching. If the model qualifies for introductory rates prior to _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL, _INTRO_PRICING overrides standard rates. If the prompt exceeds _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD (200,000 tokens) and the model specifies a 6-tuple rate schedule, tier-two pricing is applied. Finally, if executed on Vertex AI outside the global region, a 10% regional uplift (_REGIONAL_UPLIFT) is applied.

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record(model: str, usage, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:

Description: Parses the SDK usage_metadata object, bills output and reasoning tokens, records usage metrics into the centralized accounting ledger, updates runtime token calibration ratios, and emits execution telemetry.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • usage (Any): The usage_metadata object returned on the generation stream chunk.
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): The tiktoken-derived baseline token count for the prompt.
  • level_desc (str): Diagnostic description of the applied thinking configuration.
  • finish (str): Candidate finish reason string.
  • elapsed (float): Generation elapsed time in seconds.

Returns:

  • None: This helper returns nothing.

Raises:

This helper does not raise exceptions.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py _record() implementation
prompt = getattr(usage, "prompt_token_count", 0) or 0
candidates = getattr(usage, "candidates_token_count", 0) or 0
thoughts = getattr(usage, "thoughts_token_count", 0) or 0
cached = getattr(usage, "cached_content_token_count", 0) or 0
output = candidates + thoughts  # thinking is billed as output
cost = _price(model, prompt, cached, output)
record_usage(
    "GEMINI",
    model,
    input_tokens=prompt,
    output_tokens=output,
    thinking_tokens=thoughts,
    cache_read=cached,
    cost=cost,
)
ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

observe_prompt_tokens("GEMINI", model, raw_prompt_tokens, prompt)  # prompt_token_count includes cached tokens
emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"GEMINI USAGE | model={model} | {level_desc} | finish={finish or 'n/a'} | in={prompt:,} | out={candidates:,} | thinking={thoughts:,} | "
    f"cached={cached:,} | est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
    dest="BOTH",
)

The function treats reasoning thoughts as billable output tokens by calculating output = candidates + thoughts. It logs the measured consumption into utils.llm_common.record_usage and invokes utils.token_utils.observe_prompt_tokens to continuously refine the runtime BPE-to-Gemini token multiplier ratio.

docs.title: _stream()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config) -> dict:

Description: Consumes the chunked response generator produced by client.models.generate_content_stream(). It aggregates output text, isolates thinking thoughts, captures prompt feedback block reasons, records candidate finish reasons, and preserves usage metadata.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • prompt (str): The prompt string.
  • config (types.GenerateContentConfig): The request generation configuration.

Returns:

  • dict: An aggregated stream result dictionary containing text, thoughts, finish, block_reason, and usage.

Raises:

  • genai_errors.ClientError: Raised if the stream encounters Google GenAI client errors.
  • Exception: Raised on connection interruptions or SDK stream failures.

Example:

# Extracted from utils/llm_gemini.py _stream() implementation
text, thoughts = [], []
finish, block_reason, usage = "", "", None
for chunk in _get_client().models.generate_content_stream(model=model, contents=[prompt], config=config):
    feedback = getattr(chunk, "prompt_feedback", None)
    if feedback is not None and getattr(feedback, "block_reason", None):
        block_reason = _name(feedback.block_reason)
    if getattr(chunk, "usage_metadata", None) is not None:
        usage = chunk.usage_metadata
    for candidate in getattr(chunk, "candidates", None) or []:
        if getattr(candidate, "finish_reason", None):
            finish = _name(candidate.finish_reason)
        content = getattr(candidate, "content", None)
        for part in (getattr(content, "parts", None) or []) if content is not None else []:
            if getattr(part, "text", None):
                (thoughts if getattr(part, "thought", False) else text).append(part.text)
        break  # candidate_count is 1
return {
    "text": "".join(text),
    "thoughts": "".join(thoughts),
    "finish": finish,
    "block_reason": block_reason,
    "usage": usage,
}

The helper iterates over stream chunks yielded by the Google GenAI SDK. For each candidate part, it checks the boolean part.thought flag; if true, the text segment is accumulated into the thoughts buffer, otherwise it is appended to the text buffer. The loop breaks after evaluating the primary candidate (candidate_count == 1).

docs.title: Pricing Schedules and Operational Constants
docs.text:
The module declares static pricing lookup tables, context thresholds, and operational sets governing response classifications:

_RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS = {"SAFETY", "RECITATION", "LANGUAGE", "OTHER"}
_BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS = _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS | {
    "PROHIBITED_CONTENT",
    "BLOCKLIST",
    "SPII",
    "IMAGE_SAFETY",
    "IMAGE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT",
    "IMAGE_RECITATION",
    "IMAGE_OTHER",
}
_TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS = {"MAX_TOKENS"}

_PRICING = {
    "gemini-3.8-flash-cyber": (1.50, 7.50, 0.15),
    "gemini-3.8-flash": (1.50, 7.50, 0.15),
    "gemini-3.7-flash": (1.50, 7.50, 0.15),
    "gemini-3.6-flash": (1.50, 7.50, 0.15),
    "gemini-3.5-flash-lite": (0.30, 2.50, 0.03),
    "gemini-3.5-flash": (1.50, 9.00, 0.15),
    "gemini-3.1-flash-lite": (0.25, 1.50, 0.025),
    "gemini-3.1-pro": (2.00, 12.00, 0.20, 4.00, 18.00, 0.40),
    "gemini-3-pro": (2.00, 12.00, 0.20, 4.00, 18.00, 0.40),
    "gemini-3-flash": (0.50, 3.00, 0.05),
    "gemini-2.5-pro": (1.25, 10.00, 0.125, 2.50, 15.00, 0.25),
    "gemini-2.5-flash-lite": (0.10, 0.40, 0.01),
    "gemini-2.5-flash": (0.30, 2.50, 0.03),
}
_INTRO_PRICING = {
    "gemini-3.8-flash": (0.75, 3.75, 0.075),
    "gemini-3.7-flash": (0.75, 3.75, 0.075),
    "gemini-3.6-flash": (0.75, 3.75, 0.075),
}
_INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL = datetime.date(2026, 12, 31)
_REGIONAL_UPLIFT = 1.10
_LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD = 200_000
Identifier Type Description _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS set[str] Candidate finish codes indicating stochastic sampling blocks that may pass upon re-sampling. _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS set[str] Union of retryable stops and deterministic policy violations (PROHIBITED_CONTENT, BLOCKLIST, SPII, IMAGE_*). _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS set[str] Candidate finish codes indicating token budget exhaustion ({"MAX_TOKENS"}). _PRICING dict[str, tuple] Standard pricing table mapping model prefixes to USD rates per million tokens. Stores 3-tuples (input, output, cached) or 6-tuples (in, out, cache, long_in, long_out, long_cache). _INTRO_PRICING dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]] Discounted promotional rates per million tokens for select Gemini Flash models. _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL datetime.date Expiration date boundary (2026-12-31) for promotional pricing. _REGIONAL_UPLIFT float Multiplier (1.10) applied to Vertex AI inference outside the global region. _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD int Token threshold (200,000) triggering tier-two pricing on long-context models.

docs.title: Module State Singletons
docs.text:
The module manages private in-memory singletons tracking client instances, model limits, and rejected capabilities:

_client = None
_model_limits_cache = {}
_thinking_rejected = set()
Field Type Description _client google.genai.Client \| None Cached singleton instance of the official Google GenAI SDK client. _model_limits_cache dict[str, tuple[int, int]] Memoization cache mapping model names to (input_limit, output_limit) tuples. _thinking_rejected set[str] Set of model identifiers that returned HTTP 400 when sent thinking configurations.

docs.title: Stream Result Payload
docs.text:
The internal dictionary returned by the _stream() helper function encapsulates the aggregated results of a chunked generation stream:

Field Type Description text str Complete aggregated candidate response text. thoughts str Complete aggregated reasoning thoughts emitted during generation. finish str Normalized uppercase finish reason (e.g., "STOP", "MAX_TOKENS"). block_reason str Normalized prompt feedback block reason if rejected at the input gate. usage Any \| None The final usage_metadata object yielded by the SDK, or None.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements a tiered error management strategy designed to differentiate transient network faults, non-retryable input policy violations, sampling-dependent candidate stops, and provider-side schema rejections:

  • Authentication Validation: In _get_client(), the absence of both GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and GEMINI_API_KEY immediately raises a ValueError, failing fast before any network requests are dispatched.
  • Transient Network Resilience: _get_client() configures the SDK's internal HttpRetryOptions to automatically retry transient HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 responses up to 2 attempts, complementing upstream pipeline workflow retries.
  • Dynamic Thinking Fallback: In call_gemini(), if a model returns an HTTP 400 genai_errors.ClientError referencing "think", the system identifies that the remote endpoint does not accept the supplied thinking parameters. It registers the model in _thinking_rejected, emits WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED, strips the thinking configuration from types.GenerateContentConfig, and re-dispatches the stream.
  • Refusal Bifurcation: In call_gemini(), candidate and prompt blocks are checked against _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS. Prompt-level blocks and policy list violations raise non-retryable LLMRefusalError(retryable=False), preventing pipeline retry loops from re-sending doomed prompts. Stochastic candidate stops (such as "SAFETY" or "RECITATION") raise LLMRefusalError(retryable=True) to permit upstream workflow nodes to re-attempt inference.
  • Truncation Trapping: In call_gemini(), responses terminating with finish_reason == "MAX_TOKENS" emit WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED and return a TruncatedResponse wrapper. This signals callers (such as utils.call_llm) to discard partial payloads and prevent truncated JSON or Markdown from polluting disk caches.

  • utils/llm_config.py — Supplies model resolution helpers (gemini_model_id), output budget tables (gemini_output_budget), thinking specifications (gemini_thinking_mode), and Vertex AI location discovery (gemini_location).

docs.title: llm_openrouter.py
docs.text: Source: utils/llm_openrouter.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The llm_openrouter.py module implements the OpenRouter provider client for the call_llm execution subsystem. It exposes a streaming, OpenAI-compatible chat completions interface configured dynamically through the OpenRouter remote catalog. By querying live catalog metadata rather than relying on static capability maps, the module dynamically normalizes reasoning effort tiers, output budgets, and sampling controls across diverse upstream model families (such as Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and Qwen).

All generation requests operate over Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming connections to prevent transport-layer read timeouts during protracted reasoning cycles. The network engine handles connection keep-alives (filtering : OPENROUTER PROCESSING SSE comments), executes bounded exponential backoff retries respecting HTTP Retry-After response headers, and detects transient gateway anomalies. Furthermore, it intercepts HTTP 403 moderation rejections and upstream refusal markers, distinguishes between deterministic content policy blocks and retryable output filters, and records multi-dimensional token usage and Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) cost metrics.

docs.title: get_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Resolves and returns the target OpenRouter model identifier from the OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable. The raw string is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace to ensure valid routing in request paths and telemetry logs.

Parameters:

This function accepts no parameters.

Returns:

  • str: The model identifier string specified in the environment, or an empty string if unset.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions directly.

Example:

model = get_model()
if not model:
    raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")

The example above illustrates how call_openrouter() invokes get_model() to confirm that a non-empty model identifier is configured before attempting token estimation or payload generation. If the environment variable evaluates to an empty string, execution terminates immediately.

docs.title: build_payload()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_payload(prompt: str, model: str, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, str]:

Description: Compiles the complete HTTP JSON body for an OpenRouter /v1/chat/completions request. It queries utils.llm_config.openrouter_model_info to retrieve catalog metadata, clamps the maximum output token limit to remaining context capacity, configures reasoning schemas (effort strings versus discrete token budgets), and selectively includes sampling temperature when supported.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The full text of the user prompt to send to the model.
  • model (str): The OpenRouter model identifier (e.g., anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet).
  • level (str | None): The requested thinking effort level (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or None).
  • prompt_tokens (int): The estimated prompt token consumption used to calculate remaining context window headroom.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, str]: A 2-tuple containing the constructed dictionary payload ready for JSON serialization, and a short human-readable description of the applied reasoning configuration (e.g., effort=high or reasoning.max_tokens=8192).

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions directly; fallback defaults are used if environment variables or catalog lookups fail.

Example:

def build_payload(prompt: str, model: str, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    info = openrouter_model_info(model)
    max_tokens = _max_tokens(model, info, level, prompt_tokens)
    reasoning, desc = _reasoning(model, info, level, max_tokens)
    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "stream": True,
    }
    if max_tokens:
        payload["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
    if reasoning is not None:
        payload["reasoning"] = reasoning
    if _sends_temperature(model, info, reasoning):
        try:
            payload["temperature"] = float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE", "0.7"))
        except ValueError:
            payload["temperature"] = 0.7
    return payload, desc

The implementation queries catalog capabilities to establish safe context limits and reasoning schemes. Output budgeting deducts prompt tokens and safety margins via _max_tokens(). Temperature sampling is evaluated through _sends_temperature() and safely defaults to 0.7 only when neither reasoning nor catalog restrictions forbid sampling parameters.

docs.title: call_openrouter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def call_openrouter(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes a complete single-turn inference lifecycle against the OpenRouter completions endpoint. It counts raw prompt tokens, generates headers with optional attribution, dispatches an SSE-streamed POST request over a retry-capable transport layer, aggregates streaming chunks, records usage metrics, and evaluates completion finish reasons against refusal policies and token truncations.

Parameters:

  • prompt (str): The complete prompt text to submit.
  • thinking_level (str | None, optional): The requested reasoning intensity tier. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • str: The decoded completion text returned by the model. Returns a TruncatedResponse instance if the model stopped due to reaching token length limits.

Raises:

  • ValueError: Raised when the OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is missing or empty.
  • RuntimeError: Raised when the HTTP request fails across all retry attempts, if the stream returns an explicit error payload, or if the connection closes prematurely without a finish_reason.
  • LLMRefusalError: Raised when the model rejects the prompt via moderation filters, native refusal codes, or HTTP 403 guardrails.

docs.title: Phase 1: Configuration & Payload Preparation
docs.text:
from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw, token_ratio

    model = get_model()
    if not model:
        raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")
    api_key = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "").strip()
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt
    payload, desc = build_payload(prompt, model, thinking_level, int(raw_tokens * token_ratio()))
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", **_attribution_headers()}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"
    max_tokens = payload.get("max_tokens")
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"OpenRouter request | model={model} | {desc} | max_tokens={f'{max_tokens:,}' if max_tokens else 'omitted'} | "
        f"temperature={payload.get('temperature', 'omitted')} | catalog={'yes' if openrouter_catalog() else 'no'} | "
        f"attribution={'on' if 'HTTP-Referer' in headers else 'off'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )

The function verifies that OPENROUTER_MODEL is populated and determines baseline token counts using token_utils.count_tokens_raw(). It scales estimated prompt tokens with token_ratio() to establish token headroom for build_payload(). Optional attribution headers and bearer authentication are assembled, followed by debug emission detailing the planned request parameters.

docs.title: Phase 2: Network Transmission & Stream Ingestion
docs.text:
start = time.time()
    resp = _post(f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/chat/completions", headers, payload)
    generation_id = resp.headers.get("X-Generation-Id")
    result = _consume(resp)
    _record(model, result, raw_tokens, desc, time.time() - start, generation_id)
    if is_debug() and result["reasoning"]:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"REASONING:\n{result['reasoning']}", dest="LOG")

The client records the invocation start timestamp and sends the payload to {openrouter_base_url()}/v1/chat/completions using _post(). It extracts the X-Generation-Id header returned by OpenRouter for tracing. The SSE response stream is consumed into aggregated buffers via _consume(), usage metrics are logged via _record(), and any extracted internal reasoning trace is conditionally emitted if debug mode is active.

docs.title: Phase 3: Response Evaluation & Error Classification
docs.text:
finish, native = (result["finish"] or ""), (result["native"] or "")
    if finish == "error":
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter generation ended with an error (native_finish_reason={native or 'n/a'})")
    if finish == "content_filter" or result["refusal"] or native.lower() in _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS:
        category = native or finish or "refusal"
        # Filters on sampled output (safety, recitation, content_filter) may pass on another attempt.
        retryable = not result["refusal"] and native.lower() not in _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS
        count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
        emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER", retryable=retryable)
    if not finish:
        # No data at all, or the connection dropped mid-answer: never return a partial reply.
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"OpenRouter stream ended without a finish_reason after {result['events']} events ({len(result['text']):,} characters received)"
        )
    if finish == "length":
        count_event("OPENROUTER", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="OpenRouter", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}" if max_tokens else "default")
        return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
    if not result["text"]:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter response contained no text (finish_reason={finish or 'n/a'})", dest="LOG")
    return result["text"]

The completion inspects both OpenRouter's generic finish reason and upstream native finish markers. Streams ending with error raise a RuntimeError. Refusals and content blocks trigger an LLMRefusalError, marked as non-retryable for deterministic input rejections or retryable for stochastic output safety filters. If a stream terminates without any finish_reason, a RuntimeError is raised to prevent partial data leakage. If the model hit token bounds (finish == "length"), the accumulated text is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse to prevent persistent disk caching.

docs.title: _read_timeout()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _read_timeout() -> float:

Description: Parses the OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable to configure the socket read timeout during streaming response consumption. The returned value is clamped to a minimum duration of 30.0 seconds.

Parameters:

This function accepts no parameters.

Returns:

  • float: The configured timeout in seconds, defaulting to 300.0 if unset or malformed.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions; invalid numeric inputs fall back to 300.0.

Example:

def _read_timeout() -> float:
    try:
        return max(float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "300")), 30.0)
    except ValueError:
        return 300.0

The function reads the environment variable and attempts conversion to a float. If a user sets a value lower than 30.0, max() enforces the 30.0-second lower bound to account for slow multi-token streaming intervals.

docs.title: _reasoning()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _reasoning(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, max_tokens: int | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:

Description: Evaluates catalog capabilities to construct the reasoning sub-dictionary in the completions payload. It determines whether a model natively expects reasoning effort strings or discrete token budgets (supports_max_tokens). If a model specifies an allowed list of efforts, it invokes clamp_level to match supported tiers. Internal reasoning output text is excluded from transmission (exclude: True) unless debug mode is active.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The identifier of the target model.
  • info (dict | None): The catalog dictionary retrieved from openrouter_model_info().
  • level (str | None): The requested reasoning intensity tier.
  • max_tokens (int | None, optional): The total completion budget used to ensure thinking budgets do not exceed generation limits. Defaults to None.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict | None, str]: A tuple containing the reasoning configuration dictionary (or None if reasoning is unsupported or unrequested) and a descriptive log string.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions directly.

Example:

def _reasoning(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, max_tokens: int | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:
    """(reasoning payload | None, description)."""
    if not level:
        return None, "default"
    level = level.lower()
    exclude = not is_debug()
    if info is None:
        # Catalog unavailable or model unknown: send the level; OpenRouter clamps server-side.
        return {"effort": level, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={level} (unverified)"
    reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
    if not isinstance(reasoning, dict) and "reasoning" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
        if warn_once("openrouter_no_reasoning", model):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
        return None, "unsupported"
// ...

The logic falls back to unverified effort passing if catalog data is missing. When metadata is present, it validates parameter support, falling back gracefully and logging a single warning if the model lacks reasoning capabilities. For budget-only models, it looks up values in _REASONING_BUDGETS and ensures the budget stays at least 1,024 tokens below max_tokens.

docs.title: _sends_temperature()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether the temperature parameter may safely be included in the request payload. It verifies that reasoning is not enabled, that the model family does not reject sampling parameters (via rejects_sampling_params()), and that catalog metadata explicitly lists temperature without enforcing mandatory reasoning.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • info (dict | None): The catalog dictionary for the model.
  • reasoning (dict | None): The constructed reasoning payload dictionary, if any.

Returns:

  • bool: True if temperature should be sent; otherwise False.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:
    if reasoning is not None or rejects_sampling_params(model):
        return False
    if info is None:
        return True
    if "temperature" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
        return False
    meta = info.get("reasoning") if isinstance(info.get("reasoning"), dict) else {}
    return not (meta.get("mandatory") or meta.get("default_enabled"))

The helper performs defensive checks against models with mandatory thinking (such as OpenAI o-series or Gemini 2.5/3.x variants) where explicit temperature settings cause HTTP 400 Bad Request errors. If catalog metadata is absent, it defaults to sending temperature unless the model is explicitly known to reject sampling parameters.

docs.title: _max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:

Description: Computes the output token budget allocated for a completion request. It references openrouter_output_budget and clamps the budget against the top provider's advertised context length, subtracting estimated prompt tokens and CONTEXT_MARGIN.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • info (dict | None): The catalog entry for the model.
  • level (str | None): The requested reasoning intensity tier.
  • prompt_tokens (int): The estimated count of input prompt tokens.

Returns:

  • int | None: The clamped maximum completion token budget, or None if the model is unlisted in the catalog.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:
    """Planned max_tokens clamped to the context left after the prompt; None = omit (unknown model)."""
    planned = openrouter_output_budget(model, level)
    context = ((info or {}).get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or (info or {}).get("context_length")
    if planned and context:
        planned = min(planned, max(context - prompt_tokens - CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096))
    return planned

The helper verifies context boundaries by inspecting provider-specific context limits. If planned budgets threaten context exhaustion, the function clamps the allowance while preserving a baseline floor of 4,096 tokens.

docs.title: _attribution_headers()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _attribution_headers() -> dict:

Description: Generates opt-in application attribution HTTP headers for OpenRouter analytics and rankings. Headers are constructed only if the OPENROUTER_APP_URL environment variable is defined.

Parameters:

This function accepts no parameters.

Returns:

  • dict: A dictionary containing HTTP-Referer, X-OpenRouter-Title, and X-Title entries if configured; otherwise an empty dictionary.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _attribution_headers() -> dict:
    """OpenRouter app attribution (rankings / activity page), opt-in: nothing identifying the tool is
    sent unless OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set. OpenRouter attributes by HTTP-Referer; the title needs it."""
    url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_APP_URL", "").strip()
    if not url:
        return {}
    return {"HTTP-Referer": url, "X-OpenRouter-Title": _APP_TITLE, "X-Title": _APP_TITLE}  # X-Title: legacy name

This implementation prevents unnecessary telemetry transmission when no application URL is declared. When enabled, it provides both modern (X-OpenRouter-Title) and legacy (X-Title) headers along with the required HTTP-Referer.

docs.title: _retry_after()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _retry_after(resp) -> float | None:

Description: Inspects an HTTP response object for the standard Retry-After header and parses its value as a floating-point delay in seconds.

Parameters:

  • resp: A requests.Response instance.

Returns:

  • float | None: The retry delay in seconds if present and numeric; otherwise None.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _retry_after(resp) -> float | None:
    value = resp.headers.get("Retry-After")
    try:
        return float(value) if value else None
    except ValueError:
        return None

The helper guards against non-numeric or missing headers by wrapping conversion inside a try-except block, returning None if the header is absent or formatted as an HTTP-date.

docs.title: _error_body()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _error_body(resp) -> dict:

Description: Safely deserializes an HTTP error response body as JSON. It extracts nested error sub-dictionaries if present, returning a standardized dictionary structure.

Parameters:

  • resp: A requests.Response instance.

Returns:

  • dict: The extracted error dictionary, or an empty dictionary if parsing fails.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _error_body(resp) -> dict:
    try:
        body = resp.json()
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    err = body.get("error", body) if isinstance(body, dict) else body
    return err if isinstance(err, dict) else {"message": str(err)}

The function handles multiple upstream error payload conventions. If the parsed JSON body is a dictionary containing an "error" field, that object is extracted directly; otherwise, raw scalar responses are wrapped in a standard {"message": str(err)} shape.

docs.title: _error_detail()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _error_detail(resp) -> str:

Description: Produces a detailed diagnostic string from an HTTP error response, combining error messages with nested metadata providers or raw upstream errors.

Parameters:

  • resp: A requests.Response instance.

Returns:

  • str: A formatted error string suitable for log emission.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _error_detail(resp) -> str:
    err = _error_body(resp)
    if not err:
        return resp.text[:300].strip()
    meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
    raw = meta.get("raw") or meta.get("provider_name") or ""
    return f"{err.get('message', err)}" + (f" ({raw})" if raw else "")

If structured JSON parsing via _error_body() produces an empty result, the helper returns up to the first 300 characters of the raw response text. When metadata is available, upstream provider notes are appended in parentheses.

docs.title: _refusal_category()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _refusal_category(resp) -> str | None:

Description: Classifies HTTP 403 Forbidden responses to determine if they represent upstream content moderation blocks or policy refusals.

Parameters:

  • resp: A requests.Response instance.

Returns:

  • str | None: The identified refusal category string (e.g., content_policy_violation), or None if the error does not indicate a moderation rejection.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _refusal_category(resp) -> str | None:
    """Category when an HTTP 403 is a moderation / guardrail / upstream refusal, else None."""
    if resp.status_code != 403:
        return None
    err = _error_body(resp)
    meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
    kind = str(err.get("type") or err.get("error_type") or meta.get("error_type") or "").lower()
    if kind in _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES:
        return kind
    if meta.get("reasons") or meta.get("flagged_input"):
        reasons = meta.get("reasons") or ["moderation"]
        return ",".join(map(str, reasons)) if isinstance(reasons, list) else str(reasons)
    return None

The function inspects error types and metadata fields against _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES. If explicit reasons or flagged_input markers are present in metadata, it compiles a comma-delimited reason string.

docs.title: _post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _post(url: str, headers: dict, payload: dict):

Description: Dispatches the HTTP POST request to OpenRouter with streaming enabled, executing bounded retries for transient HTTP errors and network timeouts.

Parameters:

  • url (str): The target endpoint URL.
  • headers (dict): The HTTP headers including authorization and content types.
  • payload (dict): The JSON-serializable request payload.

Returns:

  • requests.Response: An active streaming HTTP response object with open sockets.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError: Raised when transient connection errors persist beyond _MAX_ATTEMPTS, or when a non-refusal HTTP status code >= 400 is received.
  • LLMRefusalError: Raised when an HTTP 403 response indicates an upstream moderation or policy rejection.

Example:

def _post(url: str, headers: dict, payload: dict):
    """POST with bounded retries on transient failures; returns an open streaming response."""
    for attempt in range(1, _MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
        try:
            resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, stream=True, timeout=(15, _read_timeout()))
        except (requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout) as e:
            if attempt == _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
                raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter request failed after {attempt} attempts: {e}") from e
            time.sleep(2**attempt)
            continue
        if resp.status_code in _RETRYABLE_STATUS and attempt < _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
            wait = min(_retry_after(resp) or 2**attempt * 2, 60)
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter HTTP {resp.status_code}; retrying in {wait:.0f}s ({_error_detail(resp)})", dest="LOG")
            resp.close()
            time.sleep(wait)
            continue
// ...

The retry loop executes up to _MAX_ATTEMPTS (3) times. It traps connection drops and timeouts, applying exponential backoff (2**attempt). When receiving retryable status codes (such as 429 or 503), it respects Retry-After headers clamped to 60 seconds. Fatal 4xx/5xx errors are evaluated by _refusal_category(); rejections raise LLMRefusalError directly, whereas unexpected HTTP errors raise RuntimeError.

docs.title: _consume()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _consume(resp) -> dict:

Description: Reads and processes the incoming Server-Sent Events (SSE) data stream. It handles line decoding, discards comments and keep-alive heartbeats, terminates upon receiving [DONE], and accumulates message fragments into an aggregated dictionary.

Parameters:

  • resp: The open requests.Response stream returned by _post().

Returns:

  • dict: An aggregated output dictionary containing concatenated text, reasoning, finish states, and usage structures.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError: Re-raised if _apply_chunk encounters an in-stream error event.

Example:

def _consume(resp) -> dict:
    """Parse the SSE stream: text, reasoning, finish / native finish reason, refusal, usage.

    Lines are split as bytes and decoded one by one: str.splitlines() (used by
    iter_lines(decode_unicode=True)) also breaks on U+2028 / U+0085, which JSON strings may contain raw.
    """
    out = {"text": [], "reasoning": [], "finish": None, "native": None, "refusal": None, "usage": None, "events": 0}
    try:
        if "application/json" in (resp.headers.get("Content-Type") or "").lower():
            # An OpenAI-compatible proxy that ignores stream=true answers with one JSON body.
            _apply_chunk(out, resp.json())
        else:
            for raw_line in resp.iter_lines():
                line = raw_line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if isinstance(raw_line, bytes) else raw_line
                if not line or line.startswith(":") or not line.startswith("data:"):
                    continue  # blank separators and ': OPENROUTER PROCESSING' keep-alives
                data = line[5:].strip()
                if data == "[DONE]":
                    break
                try:
                    chunk = json.loads(data)
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                _apply_chunk(out, chunk)
    finally:
        resp.close()
    out["text"] = "".join(out["text"])
    out["reasoning"] = "".join(out["reasoning"])
    return out

The function uses byte-level iteration instead of unicode line splitting to avoid accidental breaks on Unicode line separators like U+2028 or U+0085 embedded in raw JSON. It filters SSE comments such as : OPENROUTER PROCESSING before parsing JSON data payloads. In non-streaming fallback scenarios (where an endpoint returns standard application/json), it ingests the single response payload directly. The response socket is guaranteed to close within a finally block.

docs.title: _apply_chunk()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:

Description: Parses an individual SSE chunk or complete response payload and merges its content deltas, reasoning tokens, finish flags, and usage metadata into the accumulator dictionary.

Parameters:

  • out (dict): The accumulator dictionary populated by _consume().
  • chunk (dict): The parsed JSON object representing a single SSE event or JSON response.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates out in place.

Raises:

  • RuntimeError: Raised if the chunk contains an error dictionary at the root or within the choice array.

Example:

def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:
    """Fold one stream chunk (or a whole non-streamed completion) into the _consume result."""
    out["events"] += 1
    if chunk.get("error"):
        err = chunk["error"]
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter stream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")
    if chunk.get("usage"):
        out["usage"] = chunk["usage"]
    for choice in chunk.get("choices") or []:
        delta = choice.get("delta") or choice.get("message") or {}
        if delta.get("content"):
            out["text"].append(delta["content"])
        if delta.get("reasoning"):
            out["reasoning"].append(delta["reasoning"])
        if delta.get("refusal"):
            out["refusal"] = delta["refusal"]
        if choice.get("finish_reason"):
            out["finish"] = choice["finish_reason"]
        if choice.get("native_finish_reason"):
            out["native"] = choice["native_finish_reason"]
        if choice.get("error"):
            err = choice["error"]
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter upstream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")

The method increments the event counter and immediately inspects for error blocks emitted mid-stream by OpenRouter or upstream providers. It supports both streaming (delta) and non-streaming (message) choice payloads, appending text and reasoning fragments to list buffers for string concatenation upon stream completion.

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _record(model: str, result: dict, raw_prompt_tokens: int, desc: str, elapsed: float, generation_id: str | None) -> None:

Description: Extracts token usage metrics, cache utilization, and billing details from the consumption result, registering them in global accounting via utils.llm_common.record_usage and calibrating runtime tokenizer multipliers via utils.token_utils.observe_prompt_tokens.

Parameters:

  • model (str): The model identifier.
  • result (dict): The aggregated stream result dictionary returned by _consume().
  • raw_prompt_tokens (int): The uncalibrated baseline prompt token count.
  • desc (str): The reasoning configuration description string.
  • elapsed (float): The total elapsed wall-clock time for the request.
  • generation_id (str | None): The OpenRouter generation identifier extracted from response headers.

Returns:

  • None: No value is returned.

Raises:

This function does not raise exceptions.

Example:

def _record(model: str, result: dict, raw_prompt_tokens: int, desc: str, elapsed: float, generation_id: str | None) -> None:
    if not result["usage"]:
        # No usage chunk (dropped stream, or a proxy that omits usage): a request, but unmeasured.
        record_usage("OPENROUTER", model, cost=None, measured=False)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"OPENROUTER USAGE | model={model} | no usage reported | generation_id={generation_id or 'n/a'}", dest="BOTH")
        return
    usage = result["usage"]
    prompt = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
    completion = usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0  # includes reasoning tokens
    reasoning_tokens = (usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0
    details = usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}
    cached = details.get("cached_tokens") or 0
    cache_write = details.get("cache_write_tokens") or 0
    cost = usage.get("cost")
    upstream = (usage.get("cost_details") or {}).get("upstream_inference_cost")
    if usage.get("is_byok") and isinstance(upstream, int | float):
        # BYOK: `cost` is only OpenRouter's fee; the provider bills upstream_inference_cost to your key.
        cost = (cost if isinstance(cost, int | float) else 0.0) + upstream
// ...

If the stream finishes without usage statistics (such as when interfacing with certain OpenAI-compatible proxies), the call records an unmeasured event. When usage data is present, it extracts prompt, completion, reasoning, and cache tokens. If the request was billed under Bring-Your-Own-Key (is_byok), it combines OpenRouter's routing fee with upstream_inference_cost before recording the total cost.

docs.title: Module Constants
docs.text:
The module declares internal constants defining retry behaviors, refusal taxonomy, reasoning budgets, and application metadata:

Constant Type Value / Expression Description _RETRYABLE_STATUS set[int] {408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529} HTTP response status codes eligible for bounded retry attempts. _MAX_ATTEMPTS int 3 Maximum number of dispatch attempts for a single request. _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS set[str] {"refusal", "safety", "prohibited_content", "recitation", "blocklist", "spii", "content_filter"} Upstream completion finish markers classified as refusals or safety interventions. _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS set[str] {"refusal", "prohibited_content", "blocklist", "spii"} Upstream rejection reasons that are deterministic and non-retryable for identical inputs. _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES set[str] {"refusal", "content_policy_violation", "moderation"} Error types in HTTP 403 response payloads identified as policy refusals. _REASONING_BUDGETS dict[str, int] {"minimal": 1024, "low": 2048, "medium": 8192, "high": 16384, "xhigh": 24576, "max": 32000} Token budgets mapped to reasoning intensity tiers for models requiring discrete token counts. _APP_TITLE str "Codebase Knowledge Builder" Application title transmitted in OpenRouter analytics attribution headers.

docs.title: Stream Aggregator Schema
docs.text:
Returned internally by _consume() to represent the accumulated state of an SSE stream:

Field Type Description text str Concatenated completion text fragments from delta.content or message.content. reasoning str Concatenated thinking fragments from delta.reasoning. finish str \| None Standardized completion finish reason (e.g., stop, length, error, content_filter). native str \| None Upstream provider-specific finish reason (e.g., safety, prohibited_content, max_tokens). refusal str \| None Explicit refusal message or code delivered in choice deltas. usage dict \| None Raw usage metadata dictionary received from the stream containing token and cost counts. events int Total count of SSE chunk events received during the stream.

docs.title: Request Payload Schema
docs.text:
Generated by build_payload() for serialization as the JSON body in POST requests:

Field Type Description model str The target model identifier. messages list[dict] Array containing conversation turns, configured with [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]. stream bool Set to True to request Server-Sent Events streaming. max_tokens int (optional) Maximum output tokens allocated, omitted if the model limits are unknown. reasoning dict (optional) Reasoning configuration dictionary containing {"effort": str, "exclude": bool} or {"max_tokens": int, "exclude": bool}. temperature float (optional) Sampling temperature (defaults to 0.7), omitted if reasoning is active or model forbids sampling.

docs.title: Attribution Headers Schema
docs.text:
Constructed by _attribution_headers() when OPENROUTER_APP_URL is configured:

Header Name Type Description HTTP-Referer str Application URL used by OpenRouter to group rankings and analytics. X-OpenRouter-Title str Application identifier (Codebase Knowledge Builder). X-Title str Legacy compatibility header mirrored to X-OpenRouter-Title.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module differentiates between network-level failures, model refusals, and stream interruptions:

  • Transient Network & Gateway Errors: HTTP status codes in _RETRYABLE_STATUS (408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529) and requests.exceptions.ConnectionError or Timeout exceptions are intercepted by _post(). It performs up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (2**attempt), parsing any Retry-After header returned by the host. If errors persist beyond 3 attempts, a RuntimeError is raised.
  • Deterministic vs. Retryable Refusals: HTTP 403 errors bearing moderation error types and stream chunks containing refusal flags or _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS trigger LLMRefusalError. If the reason belongs to _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS (refusal, prohibited_content, blocklist, spii) or has an explicit refusal payload, retryable is set to False to prevent downstream workflow loops from re-sending the prompt. If the stop was triggered by output-side sampling filters (content_filter, safety, recitation), retryable is set to True.
  • Token Budget Truncation: When a model stops due to context or budget exhaustion (finish == "length"), the output is wrapped in a TruncatedResponse(result["text"]) object. This notifies callers that the text is incomplete and prevents persistent caching.
  • Stream Interruptions & In-Stream Errors: If an SSE stream terminates without a finish_reason (indicating a dropped socket or proxy failure), or if an in-stream chunk provides an error dictionary, the module raises a RuntimeError so that the workflow node can catch and retry the generation.

docs.title: mkdocs.py
docs.text: Source: utils/mkdocs.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/mkdocs.py module serves as the primary publishing, site generation, and link-normalization engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. Consolidating logic previously divided between workflow nodes and prompt construction helpers, it orchestrates the transformation of generated documentation chapters into a fully functional, deployable MkDocs Material static site or a standalone Markdown collection. The module builds site configuration files (mkdocs.yml), injects specialized interactive assets (such as panzoom-enabled Mermaid runtime scripts), formats index landing pages with visual architecture and dependency diagrams, and validates the integrity of all emitted pages.

Architecturally, the module bridges LLM-synthesized narrative documentation with deterministic static analysis facts. In the api-reference documentation mode, it queries language models to derive hierarchical module groupings and domain roles, while grounding module-level dependencies directly against source-verified AST facts produced by utils.facts. It synthesizes two distinct Mermaid diagrams on the index page: a high-level subsystem architecture map and an interconnected module graph that flags high-fan-in architectural hubs. Furthermore, the module enforces structural stability across generated documentation through a series of deterministic post-processing routines: resolving cross-chapter link targets to relative POSIX paths, appending verified importer references ("Used by"), and purging obsolete documentation artifacts across compilation runs.

The diagram below illustrates the end-to-end output pipeline orchestrated by write_mkdocs_output:

flowchart TD subgraph prepSub["Preparation and Ingestion"] startNode["Initialize Parameters and Documentation Mode"] summariesNode["Extract and Sanitize Chapter Summaries"] decisionMode{"Mode api-reference and 6+ Modules?"} end subgraph groupSub["Structural Grouping and Dependency Resolution"] groupLLM["Invoke call_llm with group_modules Prompt"] parseGroup["Parse Sections and Extract Grouping Extras"] mergeFacts["Ground Dependencies Against Verified Facts"] orderSections["Sort Sections by Role and Reading Order"] end subgraph assetSub["Configuration and Landing Page Assembly"] genConfig["Compile mkdocs.yml and mermaid-init.js"] buildIndex["Build api/index.md with Section Map and Graphs"] end subgraph postSub["Post-Processing and Verification"] usedBy["Inject Verified Used By Back-References"] normLinks["Normalize Cross-Chapter Relative Links"] writeFiles["Serialize Chapter Pages to docs/api/"] pruneFiles["Prune Stale Pages and Empty Directories"] auditSite["Execute site_renderer chapter_check Audit"] end startNode --> summariesNode summariesNode --> decisionMode decisionMode -->|Yes| groupLLM decisionMode -->|No| genConfig groupLLM --> parseGroup parseGroup --> mergeFacts mergeFacts --> orderSections orderSections --> genConfig genConfig --> buildIndex buildIndex --> usedBy usedBy --> normLinks normLinks --> writeFiles writeFiles --> pruneFiles pruneFiles --> auditSite classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5; class startNode entryNode; class groupLLM entryNode; class genConfig entryNode; class usedBy entryNode; Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

docs.title: yaml_str()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def yaml_str(value) -> str:

Description: Serializes and escapes an arbitrary Python scalar into a valid YAML double-quoted string literal using JSON encoding semantics. Because JSON string literals conform directly to YAML scalar syntax, this helper guarantees that section names, titles, and navigation labels containing special characters (such as colons, brackets, apostrophes, or leading @ symbols) do not break mkdocs.yml structure.

Parameters:

  • value (Any): The scalar value, string, or number to be serialized into hand-built YAML syntax.

Returns:

  • str: A valid, JSON-encoded and double-quoted YAML scalar string with leading and trailing whitespace stripped.

Example:

from utils.mkdocs import yaml_str

label = yaml_str("Core: Internal Services & Auth")
# Evaluates to: '"Core: Internal Services & Auth"'

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:

Description: Compiles a complete mkdocs.yml configuration string optimized for MkDocs Material. The generated configuration enables code-copy buttons, instant navigation indices, Pygments syntax highlighting, and Mermaid diagram integration via a specialized .mermaid-raw CSS class that bypasses default theme color overrides. It integrates the panzoom plugin for interactive diagram exploration and allows localization of search and user interface components via an optional language code.

Parameters:

  • site_name (str): The primary site title displayed in the navigation header.
  • nav_yaml (str): Hand-crafted or generated YAML navigation lines (typically generated by build_grouped_nav).
  • include_home (bool): Whether to prepend a root home entry linking to index.md. Defaults to True.
  • lang_code (str): Optional two-letter ISO language code (e.g., "vi", "zh", "fr") to localize Material UI strings. Defaults to "".

Returns:

  • str: A complete, formatted mkdocs.yml configuration string.

Example:

mkdocs_config = build_mkdocs_config(
    site_name="My Project",
    nav_yaml="nav:\n  - Overview: index.md\n",
    include_home=True,
    lang_code="en",
)

docs.title: MERMAID_INIT_JS

It overrides MkDocs Material's default Mermaid coloring by initializing Mermaid with the "default" theme on <div class="mermaid-raw"> containers. It dynamically appends a stylesheet ensuring diagrams in dark mode ([data-md-color-scheme="slate"]) render on a light background card for edge contrast, and catches diagram rendering anomalies gracefully without halting browser thread execution.

with open(js_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

docs.title: site_renderer()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def site_renderer():

Description: Constructs a Markdown-to-HTML rendering callable matching the runtime configuration of the target MkDocs site. It dynamically parses build_mkdocs_config("", "nav:") via yaml.Loader to discover configured Markdown extensions (such as pymdownx.superfences, pymdownx.highlight, and inlinehilite) alongside core extensions (toc, tables, fenced_code). If the markdown library or any configured extension is missing, it emits an alert and returns None.

renderer = site_renderer()
