docs.title: build_chapter_filenames()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_chapter_filenames(chapter_order: list, abstractions: list, is_mkdocs: bool) -> dict:

Description: Establishes a deterministic mapping from chapter sequence indices to target Markdown filenames. For MkDocs compilation, if an abstraction provides an original_path, it mirrors that relative POSIX path; otherwise, it sanitizes the abstraction name into an alphanumeric slug. For standalone output, it prefixes the slug with a zero-padded index (01_name.md). It maintains an internal collision set (treating readme.md as equivalent to directory index.md) and appends numeric suffixes (_2.md, _3.md) when names collide case-insensitively.

Parameters:

  • chapter_order (list): List of integer abstraction indices representing the desired reading sequence.
  • abstractions (list): Master collection of abstraction metadata dictionaries extracted from the codebase.
  • is_mkdocs (bool): Flag indicating whether output targets an MkDocs directory structure (True) or a flat standalone directory (False).

Returns:

  • dict[int, str]: Mapping of chapter position index to relative Markdown filename.

Example:

filenames = build_chapter_filenames(
    chapter_order=[0, 1],
    abstractions=[
        {"name": "App Core", "original_path": "src/core.py"},
        {"name": "Utils", "original_path": "src/utils.py"},
    ],
    is_mkdocs=True,
)
# Result: {0: 'src/core.py.md', 1: 'src/utils.py.md'}

docs.title: split_frontmatter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def split_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:

Description: Strips leading YAML frontmatter blocks from a Markdown string matching MkDocs' native metadata parser semantics. The block must begin at line zero with ---, terminate with --- or ..., and parse as a valid YAML mapping. If the block fails YAML validation or does not parse as a mapping, the text is preserved untouched to avoid truncating Markdown files that open with a horizontal rule.

Parameters:

  • text (str): The raw Markdown text to evaluate.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool]: A 2-tuple containing (body_text, found_flag), where found_flag indicates whether a valid frontmatter mapping was extracted and removed.

Example:

content, has_fm = split_frontmatter("---
title: Home
---
# Content")
# content == "# Content", has_fm is True

docs.title: strip_summary_header()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def strip_summary_header(summary: str) -> str:

Description: Detects and strips initial chapter identification headers prepended by generation prompts (such as <Chapter> N — name:). If the first line matches the summary header regex, it returns the remaining text trimmed of leading whitespace.

Parameters:

  • summary (str): The raw chapter summary text.

Returns:

  • str: The summary text with the chapter identification header removed.

Example:

clean = strip_summary_header("Chapter 1 — Core Architecture:\nThis module handles...")
# Evaluates to: "This module handles..."

docs.title: clip_sentences()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def clip_sentences(text: str, limit: int) -> str:

Description: Truncates prose to whole sentences without exceeding a maximum character limit. Handles both Latin punctuation boundaries and CJK sentence terminators without spacing. If even the first sentence exceeds the character limit, the text is cut at a word boundary (or exact character index for languages without spaces), trailing punctuation is trimmed, open backtick code spans are defensively closed, and an ellipsis (…) is appended.

Parameters:

  • text (str): Prose content to truncate.
  • limit (int): Maximum allowed character length.

Returns:

  • str: Formatted, sentence-bounded string guaranteed not to exceed limit (unless truncated with an ellipsis suffix).

Example:

clipped = clip_sentences("First sentence. Second sentence.", limit=20)
# clipped == "First sentence."

docs.title: table_cell_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def table_cell_text(text: str) -> str:

Description: Prepares raw text for safe inclusion within a Markdown table cell by escaping vertical bar characters (| to \|). The helper parses inline code spans (...) using regular expressions and preserves literal pipes located inside code spans, allowing types such as str | None to render unescaped.

Parameters:

  • text (str): The raw text to escape.

Returns:

  • str: The sanitized text with table cell delimiters escaped outside of inline code spans.

Example:

cell = table_cell_text("Returns str | None | union")
# Returns: "Returns str \\| None \\| union"
cell_code = table_cell_text("Returns `str | None` | union")
# Returns: "Returns `str | None` \\| union"

docs.title: summary_description()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def summary_description(summary: str, limit: int = 300) -> str:

Description: Extracts a concise module description from a multi-point structured chapter summary for use in index tables. It isolates the primary "Component Scope & Responsibility" section (point 1), discards preamble chatter (such as "Here is a structured technical brief..."), strips numeric and bold heading markers, truncates the text to whole sentences within limit characters via clip_sentences, and escapes pipe delimiters via table_cell_text.

Parameters:

  • summary (str): The raw multi-point chapter summary text.
  • limit (int): Maximum character ceiling for the description. Defaults to 300.

Returns:

  • str: A sanitized, single-paragraph description suitable for Markdown table cells.

Example:

desc = summary_description("### (1) Component Scope & Responsibility\nHandles auth.", limit=100)
# desc == "Handles auth."

docs.title: md_link_text()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def md_link_text(text: str) -> str:

Description: Escapes Markdown metacharacters (\, `, *, _, [, ], |) within module names and identifiers. This ensures that filenames with special characters (such as __init__.py) render as literal text rather than triggering Markdown italic or bold styling inside link anchors.

Parameters:

Returns:

escaped = md_link_text("__init__.py")
# escaped == "\_\_init\_\_.py"

docs.title: module_name_lookup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def module_name_lookup(chapter_files: list) -> dict:

Description: Generates a flexible dictionary mapping various aliases of a module to its canonical module_name. Keys include the exact module_name, the relative original_path, and the bare filename basename (provided that the basename is globally unique across all chapters).

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter descriptor dictionaries containing module_name and optional original_path keys.

Returns:

Example:

lookup = module_name_lookup([
    {"module_name": "utils.call_llm", "original_path": "utils/call_llm.py"},
    {"module_name": "nodes", "original_path": "nodes.py"}
])
# lookup["call_llm.py"] == "utils.call_llm"

docs.title: grouping_extras()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def grouping_extras(parsed, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[dict, dict]:

Description: Validates and normalizes supplemental metadata extracted from the group_modules.md LLM response. Resolves module names via module_name_lookup, drops invalid or self-referential dependencies, removes duplicates, and sanitizes descriptions for Markdown table cells (enforcing a 400-character sentence ceiling and escaping pipes).

Parameters:

  • parsed (dict | Any): The parsed JSON or YAML payload from the LLM grouping prompt.
  • chapter_files (list): List of active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • tuple[dict, dict]: A 2-tuple containing:
    1. descriptions: dict[str, str] mapping canonical module names to sanitized descriptions.
    2. dependencies: dict[str, list[str]] mapping source module names to lists of target module names.

Example:

desc, deps = grouping_extras({
    "descriptions": {"call_llm.py": "LLM facade utility."},
    "dependencies": {"call_llm.py": ["token_utils.py"]}
}, chapter_files)

Description: Identifies all modules in chapter_files that successfully completed the ExtractFacts verification pipeline and produced ground-truth AST claims. Modules whose fact extraction failed or returned None are omitted from the returned set.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def verified_dependencies(module_facts: dict, chapter_files: list) -> dict:

Description: Extracts verified cross-module dependency edges directly from module_facts. Only edges whose target modules map directly to a known chapter file are retained, filtering out external third-party dependencies and self-references.

Parameters:

  • module_facts (dict): Mapping of file paths to fact extraction objects containing depends_on lists.
  • chapter_files (list): List of active chapter descriptors.

deps = verified_dependencies(module_facts, chapter_files)
# Result: {"utils.call_llm": ["utils.llm_config", "utils.token_utils"]}

docs.title: build_section_map()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_section_map(sections: list, dependencies: dict, max_listed: int = 8) -> tuple[str, bool, bool]:

Description: Generates Mermaid flowchart syntax representing the high-level architecture overview for api/index.md. Each top-level section is rendered as a single node enumerating up to max_listed member modules (appending localized "+N more" labels when exceeded). Inter-section dependency edges are derived from module dependencies. Sections with 2 or more incoming dependency edges are classified as architectural hubs and styled with the entryNode highlight class.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Hierarchical section tree defining documentation navigation.
  • dependencies (dict): Cross-module dependency graph ({source: [targets]}).
  • max_listed (int): Maximum number of module names printed inside a section node. Defaults to 8.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, bool, bool]: A 3-tuple containing:
    1. mermaid_source (str): Fenced diagram source code, or "" if fewer than two sections exist.
    2. has_arrows (bool): True if any inter-section edges were drawn.
    3. has_hubs (bool): True if any section received the entryNode highlight class.

Example:

source, has_arrows, has_hubs = build_section_map(sections, dependencies)

docs.title: build_module_graph()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_module_graph(sections: list, dependencies: dict, chapter_files: list) -> tuple[str, int]:

Description: Constructs a detailed Mermaid module dependency graph (flowchart LR) for api/index.md. Modules are partitioned into subgraphs corresponding to their top-level navigation sections. High-fan-in hub modules—modules depended upon by at least max(5, total_modules // 4) other files—are highlighted with the entryNode styling class, labeled with an incoming dependency count (used by N modules), and have incoming arrows pruned to avoid diagram sprawl. Returns an empty diagram if total modules exceed _MODULE_GRAPH_MAX_MODULES (80) or if dependencies are empty.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Navigation section tree defining module grouping.
  • dependencies (dict): Module dependency dictionary ({source: [targets]}).
  • chapter_files (list): Complete list of chapter descriptors.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, int]: A 2-tuple containing:
    1. mermaid_source (str): Fenced diagram source string, or "" if skipped.
    2. hub_threshold (int): The numerical fan-in threshold required for hub status (0 if no hubs exist).

Example:

graph_src, hub_thresh = build_module_graph(sections, dependencies, chapter_files)

docs.title: build_index_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def build_index_sections(lines, sections, chapter_files, level=3, summaries=None, descriptions=None):

Description: Recursively populates a list of Markdown strings (lines) with ATX headings and Markdown summary tables for each section. For each module row, descriptions are selected preferentially from LLM grouping descriptions, falling back to trimmed chapter summaries via summary_description.

Parameters:

  • lines (list[str]): Accumulator list of Markdown output lines.
  • sections (list): Hierarchical section tree to render.
  • chapter_files (list): Active chapter descriptor list.
  • level (int): Markdown ATX heading depth. Defaults to 3 (###).

docs.title: normalize_chapter_links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files):

Description: Post-processing routine that scans all Markdown content across chapter_files and rewrites cross-chapter Markdown links ([text](target.md)). It constructs a lookup table of canonical paths and bare basenames, determines the relative directory distance between the current chapter and the link target, and updates link URLs to POSIX-compliant relative paths. Pins relative links with ./ if they collide with another chapter's root path, while leaving external HTTP/HTTPS links unmodified.

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter dictionaries whose content strings are updated in place.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates chapter content in place.

Example:

# In utils/mkdocs.py:
def normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files):
    filenames = [cf["filename"] for cf in chapter_files]
    filename_lookup = {fname: fname for fname in filenames}
    basename_counts = Counter(fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for fname in filenames)
    for fname in filenames:
        basename = fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if basename_counts[basename] == 1 and basename not in filename_lookup:
            filename_lookup[basename] = fname

    link_pattern = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)#]+\.md)(#[^)]*)?\)")
    fixed_count = 0

    for cf in chapter_files:
        current_dir = os.path.dirname(cf["filename"])

        def fix_link(match, _dir=current_dir):
            nonlocal fixed_count
            text, target, anchor = match.group(1), match.group(2), match.group(3) or ""
            if target.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
                return match.group(0)
            canonical = filename_lookup.get(target)
            if not canonical:
                resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(_dir, target)).replace("\\", "/")
                canonical = filename_lookup.get(resolved)
            if canonical:
                correct_rel = os.path.relpath(canonical, _dir).replace("\\", "/") if _dir else canonical
                if _dir and filename_lookup.get(correct_rel, canonical) != canonical:
                    correct_rel = f"./{correct_rel}"
                if correct_rel != target:
                    fixed_count += 1
                return f"[{text}]({correct_rel}{anchor})"
            return match.group(0)

        cf["content"] = link_pattern.sub(fix_link, cf["content"])

The function iterates over each chapter file, determining its enclosing directory depth. When a match for a Markdown link pattern is identified, it extracts the destination target and resolves it against the canonical filename registry. If the relative path calculated from the source chapter to the destination differs from the author's original link text, the link is rewritten and a debug telemetry counter is incremented.

docs.title: add_used_by_lines()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def add_used_by_lines(chapter_files: list, module_facts: dict) -> None:

Description: Appends a verified "Used by" back-reference line to the end of each api-reference chapter based on incoming dependency facts recorded in module_facts. Any existing generated line from prior runs is removed to allow safe regeneration. If the chapter ends in an unclosed code block, a matching closing fence is inserted before appending the back-reference line.

Parameters:

  • chapter_files (list): List of chapter dictionaries whose content strings are modified in place.
  • module_facts (dict): Fact extraction records containing used_by collections.

Returns:

  • None: Mutates chapter content in place.

Example:

docs.title: Phase 2: LLM Nav Grouping and Dependency Inference

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NAV GROUPING CHECK | mode={mode} | module_count={len(chapter_files)} | threshold=6", dest="LOG")

                lines.append(f"- {name}{uses}: {summary or cf['description']}")
            module_list = "\n".join(lines)

            prompt_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", "common", "group_modules.md")
            with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                group_template = f.read()

            language = prep_res.get("language", "english")
            language_note = f"Section names and module descriptions MUST be in {language}." if language.lower() != "english" else ""

            group_prompt = group_template.format(
                project_name=project_name,
                module_count=len(chapter_files),
                module_list=module_list,
                directory_tree=prep_res.get("directory_tree", "N/A"),
                language_note=language_note,
            )

            emit("LLM_CALL_GROUPING", count=len(chapter_files))
            log_token_estimation("NavGrouping", group_prompt, prep_res.get("max_tokens", 100000))
            group_response = call_llm(
                group_prompt, use_cache=prep_res.get("use_cache", True), thinking_level=prep_res.get("thinking_level"), step="group_modules"
            )
            parsed = parse_grouping_response(group_response)
            sections = parsed.get("sections", parsed) if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None
            if isinstance(sections, list):
                sections = prune_sections(sections, chapter_files)
            descriptions, dependencies = grouping_extras(parsed, chapter_files)
            if has_facts:
                dependencies = {source: targets for source, targets in dependencies.items() if source not in with_facts} | verified
                inferred_sources = sorted(source for source in dependencies if source not in with_facts)

For api-reference documentation containing 6 or more modules, this phase invokes call_llm with prompts/common/group_modules.md. It provides the model with directory trees and source-verified dependency facts, merges ground-truth facts over model inferences, and prunes invalid sections.

docs.title: Phase 3: Nav Validation and Reading Order Sorting
docs.text:
if sections:
                reply_order = [section["name"] for section in sections]
                sections = order_sections(sections, chapter_files)
                grouped_modules = collect_all_modules(sections)
                ungrouped = [cf["module_name"] for cf in sorted(chapter_files, key=tree_order_key) if cf["module_name"] not in grouped_modules]
                if ungrouped:
                    sections += order_sections([{"name": get("UI_OTHER"), "modules": ungrouped}], chapter_files)

                nav_lines = build_grouped_nav(sections, chapter_files, indent=4)
                nav_lines.insert(0, "    - api/index.md")
                nav_label = mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation")
                nav_snippet = f"nav:\n  - {nav_label}:\n" + "\n".join(nav_lines)
                emit("DONE_GROUPING", count=len(sections))
            else:
                emit("GROUP_EMPTY_FALLBACK")

        except Exception as e:
            emit("GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK", error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"LLM grouping failed: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]
            sections = None
            descriptions, dependencies, has_facts, inferred_sources = {}, {}, False, []
    else:
        nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]

This phase validates that all modules are accounted for in navigation. Any missing modules are gathered under a localized fallback section ("Other"), sections are reordered into canonical reading order via order_sections, and build_grouped_nav generates the navigation YAML snippet.

docs.title: prune_stale_pages()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def prune_stale_pages(api_docs_path, chapter_files):

Description: Traverses the docs/api directory and deletes any .md files that do not correspond to the current documentation run, removing any empty directories left behind. Files are matched using filesystem device and inode numbers (st_dev, st_ino) rather than string path matching. This prevents case-only file renames on case-insensitive filesystems (such as macOS or Windows) from leaving behind orphaned pages that MkDocs would otherwise include in the site search index.

Parameters:

  • api_docs_path (str): Absolute filesystem path to docs/api.
  • chapter_files (list): List of active chapter file dictionaries.

Returns:

  • None

Example:

prune_stale_pages("/workspace/docs/api", chapter_files)

docs.title: Private Constants and Regular Expressions
docs.text:
The module defines internal regular expressions and constants to parse frontmatter, section headers, summaries, and Markdown syntax:

_FRONTMATTER_RE = re.compile(r"^-{3}[ \t]*\n(.*?\n)(?:\.{3}|-{3})[ \t]*\n", re.DOTALL)
_SUMMARY_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^.+ \d+ — .+:$")
_SUMMARY_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"^[\s#>*_]*\(?1[.)]\W{0,3}[^:\uff1a\n]{1,80}[:\uff1a]\**\s*")
_POINT_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"^[\s#>*_]*\(?1[.)][\s*_]*")
_MD_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(r"([\\`*_\[\]|])")
_POINT_PAREN_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^[ \t#>*_]*\(([1-4])\)")
_POINT_PLAIN_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^[ \t#>*_]*([1-4])[.)]\s")
_CJK_STOPS = ("\u3002", "\uff01", "\uff1f")
_SENTENCE_END_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|(?<=[\u3002\uff01\uff1f])\s*")
_ABBREVIATIONS = ("e.g.", "i.e.", "vs.", "etc.", "cf.", "approx.", "incl.", "resp.", "no.", "fig.")
_CODE_SPAN_RE = re.compile(r"(`+)(?!`).+?(?<!`)\1(?!`)")
_ENTRY_NODE_CLASSDEF = "    classDef entryNode stroke:#d33,stroke-width:3px,fill:#fff5f5"
_MODULE_GRAPH_MAX_MODULES = 80
  • _FRONTMATTER_RE: Matches leading YAML frontmatter blocks bounded by triple dashes (---) or trailing dots (...).
  • _SUMMARY_HEADER_RE: Matches leading chapter identification lines (e.g., Chapter 1 — Core:).
  • _SUMMARY_LABEL_RE and _POINT_MARKER_RE: Detect and strip point (1) headings and labels in summary text.
  • _MD_ESCAPE_RE: Targets Markdown formatting characters requiring backslash-escaping.
  • _POINT_PAREN_RE and _POINT_PLAIN_RE: Locate numbered bullet boundaries in chapter summaries.
  • _CJK_STOPS and _SENTENCE_END_RE: Regular expressions handling sentence splitting across Latin punctuation and East Asian full-width punctuation marks.
  • _ABBREVIATIONS: Whitelist of common abbreviations to prevent incorrect sentence splits.
  • _CODE_SPAN_RE: Matches inline backtick code spans to protect pipe characters from being escaped in tables.
  • _ENTRY_NODE_CLASSDEF: Standardized Mermaid styling string applied to architectural hub nodes.
  • _MODULE_GRAPH_MAX_MODULES: Maximum module threshold (80) beyond which full module graphs are skipped to prevent unreadable diagrams.

docs.title: _sentences()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _sentences(text: str):

Description: Generator that segments text into individual sentences using _SENTENCE_END_RE. Checks each boundary against _ends_with_abbreviation to prevent splitting on common abbreviations like e.g. or vs..

Parameters:

  • text (str): The prose string to segment.

Yields:

  • str: Individual sentence strings.

Example:

# In utils/mkdocs.py:
def _sentences(text: str):
    start = 0
    for match in _SENTENCE_END_RE.finditer(text):
        piece = text[start : match.start()]
        if not piece or _ends_with_abbreviation(piece):
            continue
        yield piece
        start = match.end()
    if text[start:]:
        yield text[start:]

The generator iterates through regex matches finding sentence-ending punctuation. If a substring terminates in an abbreviation, the boundary is skipped. Any trailing characters remaining after the last sentence terminator are yielded as the final segment.

docs.title: _ends_with_abbreviation()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _ends_with_abbreviation(piece: str) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a text fragment terminates with a recognized abbreviation from _ABBREVIATIONS. Ensures that word boundaries match (e.g., matching ... e.g. but not a word ending in those letters like piano.).

Parameters:

  • piece (str): Text fragment ending with a period.

Returns:

  • bool: True if the fragment ends with a recognized abbreviation; otherwise False.

Example:

# In utils/mkdocs.py:
def _ends_with_abbreviation(piece: str) -> bool:
    lower = piece.lower()
    for abbreviation in _ABBREVIATIONS:
        if lower.endswith(abbreviation):
            before = lower[: -len(abbreviation)][-1:]
            if not before or not before.isalnum():
                return True
    return False

The function checks piece against each entry in _ABBREVIATIONS. If matched, it verifies the preceding character is non-alphanumeric or empty, confirming a distinct word boundary.

docs.title: _is_prose()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _is_prose(text: str) -> bool:

Description: Heuristic evaluating whether a text snippet represents running prose rather than a bare label or title line. Checks for sentence-terminating punctuation marks or CJK stops followed by spacing or at the end of the trimmed string.

Parameters:

  • text (str): String to evaluate.

Returns:

  • bool: True if sentence punctuation is found; otherwise False.

Example:

# In utils/mkdocs.py:
def _is_prose(text: str) -> bool:
    stripped = text.rstrip("*_ ")
    return any(mark in text for mark in (". ", "! ", "? ", *_CJK_STOPS)) or stripped.endswith((".", "!", "?"))

The function strips markdown emphasis and trailing whitespace, then inspects the text for sentence-ending punctuation marks followed by spaces or located at the end of the line.

docs.title: _section_members()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _section_members(sections: list) -> list[tuple[str, list]]:

Description: Flattens nested subsections by rolling all child modules into their corresponding top-level root section. If a module is declared in multiple sections, it is assigned strictly to the first section where it appears.

Parameters:

  • sections (list): Section trees to flatten.

Returns:

  • list[tuple[str, list[str]]]: List of 2-tuples mapping each top-level section name to its complete list of module names.

Example:

# In utils/mkdocs.py:
def _section_members(sections: list) -> list[tuple[str, list]]:
    owned = set()

    def modules_of(section):
        found = list(section.get("modules", []))
        for child in section.get("children", []):
            found += modules_of(child)
        return found

    groups = []
    for section in sections:
        members = []
        for name in modules_of(section):
            if name not in owned:
                owned.add(name)
                members.append(name)
        groups.append((section["name"], members))
    return groups

A recursive inner function modules_of collects all modules within a section and its descendants. The outer loop deduplicates module ownership using an owned set, ensuring each module belongs to exactly one top-level group.

docs.title: _mermaid_label()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _mermaid_label(text) -> str:

Description: Sanitizes a string for safe inclusion inside a quoted Mermaid node label. Replaces special characters that would break the Mermaid parser (#, ", `, <, >) with their numeric or HTML entity codes (e.g., # becomes #35;, " becomes #quot;).

Parameters:

  • text (Any): The label string or object to sanitize.

Returns:

  • str: The entity-escaped Mermaid label string.

Example:

# In utils/mkdocs.py:
def _mermaid_label(text) -> str:
    text = " ".join(str(text).split())
    for char, code in (("#", "#35;"), ('"', "#quot;"), ("`", "#96;"), ("<", "#lt;"), (">", "#gt;")):
        text = text.replace(char, code)
    return text

Whitespace is normalized, and individual replacement pairs are applied in order. The # character is escaped first to prevent double-escaping entity prefixes introduced by subsequent replacements.

docs.title: _page_link()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _page_link(page: str, target: str, filenames: set) -> str:

Description: Calculates the relative POSIX link target from chapter page to chapter target. Prepends ./ to the path if the relative path matches another chapter's root-relative path (preventing ambiguous lookups), and wraps the URL in angle brackets (<...>) if it contains whitespace or parentheses.

Parameters:

  • page (str): Relative filename of the source chapter.
  • target (str): Relative filename of the destination chapter.
  • filenames (set[str]): Set of all known chapter filenames.

Returns:

  • str: Formatted, relative Markdown link destination URL.

Example:

# In utils/mkdocs.py:
def _page_link(page: str, target: str, filenames: set) -> str:
    directory = posixpath.dirname(page)
    relative = posixpath.relpath(target, directory) if directory else target
    if directory and relative in filenames and relative != target:
        relative = f"./{relative}"
    return f"<{relative}>" if re.search(r"[\s()]", relative) else relative

The function computes the relative path between the source chapter's directory and the target. It checks for potential naming ambiguities against filenames, pinning with ./ when necessary, and wraps the link in angle brackets if it contains spaces or parentheses.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive programming patterns to prevent build failures during site generation:

  • LLM Grouping Resilience: The grouping pipeline in write_mkdocs_output wraps the call_llm invocation and response parsing in a top-level try/except block. If the LLM call times out, returns malformed JSON, or fails validation, an error event is logged and the pipeline falls back gracefully to prep_res["nav_snippet"] and a flat index table.
  • Frontmatter Parsing Safety: In split_frontmatter, YAML parsing errors (YAMLError, ValueError) triggered by invalid syntax or out-of-range dates are caught. The function safely returns the original text intact with a False flag, preventing content loss.
  • Markdown Renderer Availability: In site_renderer, missing markdown libraries or extension configuration errors are intercepted and logged via emit("CHAPTER_CHECK_NO_RENDERER"), returning None so downstream audits can handle the missing renderer without raising unhandled exceptions.
  • Navigation Tree Validation: In prune_sections, unrecognized module names and sections left empty after filtering are pruned. This prevents emitting empty YAML navigation keys (- "Name":), which causes mkdocs build to terminate with a schema error.
  • Unclosed Markdown Blocks: In add_used_by_lines, chapters ending in unclosed code fences are detected using parse_page. A matching closing fence is inserted before appending the "Used by" line, preventing the reference from being swallowed into a code block.
  • Inode-Based File Pruning: In prune_stale_pages, existing files are matched using filesystem device and inode numbers (st_dev, st_ino) rather than string path matching. This prevents case-only file renames on case-insensitive filesystems from leaving behind orphaned pages that MkDocs would otherwise include in the site search index.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/output.py module serves as the centralized emission, console formatting, ANSI color styling, file logging, and localization gateway for the Codebase Knowledge Builder pipeline. It replaces direct print() statements and standard library logging configurations with a deterministic output bus. Every user-facing emission is mediated through string templates loaded from a persistent tabular catalog (strings.csv), decoupling terminal presentation and localized phrasing from execution logic. In addition to console routing, the module provisions per-run timestamped log files, manages buffering for early boot events, handles encoding normalization across diverse host platforms, and routes missing translations to an LLM-assisted localization worker.

The module routes messages through a dual-destination architecture controlled by message metadata (BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, DBOTH, DSTDOUT). Emissions tagged with debug-sensitive prefixes are dynamically gated depending on whether the global --debug flag is active: when debug mode is disabled, debug emissions are suppressed from standard output while continuing to write into the permanent file log. Before persistent file logging is initialized via configure_logging(), all log messages generated during argument validation and credential verification are buffered inside an in-memory queue (_pending_log) bounded by PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES entries, preventing message loss during the preflight execution phase.

To ensure non-destructive runtime localization without circular dependency chains, output.py coordinates with utils.i18n. When init() is invoked with a non-English target language, the module can trigger LLM translation passes to populate missing message keys and serialize them back into the CSV catalog. The runtime environment is safeguarded against platform-specific character encoding failures through automated stream reconfiguration, preventing UnicodeEncodeError exceptions when output streams are redirected to non-interactive pipes or files on Windows hosts.

docs.title: COLORS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: COLORS = { "PROGRESS": "\033[96m", # Cyan — LLM calls, active steps "SUCCESS": "\033[92m", # Green — completions, cache hits

Description: Module-level mapping linking logical message severity levels to ANSI escape sequences for 16-color/256-color compatible terminal emulators. Levels without visual tinting (INFO, FILE_WRITE, and UI) map to empty strings.

Implementation:

COLORS = {
    "PROGRESS": "\033[96m",  # Cyan — LLM calls, active steps
    "SUCCESS": "\033[92m",  # Green — completions, cache hits
    "WARNING": "\033[93m",  # Yellow — warnings, capacity alerts
    "ERROR": "\033[91m",  # Red — errors, failures
    "INFO": "",  # Plain — config, counts, labels
    "DEBUG": "\033[90m",  # Gray — skipped files, debug
    "FILE_WRITE": "",  # Plain — "  - Wrote {path}" messages
    "UI": "",  # N/A — used in generated docs, never printed
}

The dictionary defines color boundaries across eight operational categories. PROGRESS applies high-intensity cyan (\033[96m) to emphasize ongoing asynchronous steps and model generation loops. SUCCESS utilizes high-intensity green (\033[92m) for completed actions and cache hits. WARNING provides high-intensity yellow (\033[93m) for retry attempts and capacity thresholds, while ERROR applies high-intensity red (\033[91m). Diagnostic statements categorized as DEBUG render in muted dark gray (\033[90m). Uncolored levels default to empty strings to avoid injecting unneeded terminal control characters.

docs.title: RESET
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: RESET = "\033[0m"

Description: ANSI terminal escape sequence used to reset graphic rendition attributes, restoring foreground and background terminal colors back to default settings following styled console emissions.

Implementation:

RESET = "\033[0m"

The sequence \033[0m is appended to all styled standard output strings whenever an associated color code is retrieved from COLORS. If the evaluated color code evaluates to an empty string, the reset token is omitted to avoid emitting unnecessary bytes to the stream.

docs.title: PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES = 5_000

Description: Bounded capacity limit defining the maximum number of formatted log lines permitted in the pre-configuration queue _pending_log.

Implementation:

PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES = 5_000

This integer ceiling enforces memory safety during long execution sequences that emit log lines prior to calling configure_logging(). If pre-configuration log emissions exceed this threshold, the queue evicts items in FIFO order, ensuring that unconfigured CLI runs or long verification sequences cannot trigger unbounded memory growth.

docs.title: init()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True):

Description: Initializes the global state of the output subsystem, configuring localization targets, parsing the string catalog, reconfiguring stream encodings, and optionally triggering missing string translations.

Parameters:

  • language (str): Target human language for CLI messages (e.g., "english", "vietnamese"). Defaults to "english".
  • use_cache (bool): Flag indicating whether downstream LLM translation calls should leverage response caching. Defaults to True.
  • thinking_level (str | None): Model reasoning effort parameter passed to translation worker prompts. Defaults to None.
  • debug (bool): Flag specifying whether verbose debug statements should appear in console streams. Defaults to False.
  • auto_translate (bool): Flag determining whether missing translations are populated immediately. If False, translation must be triggered manually via translate_missing_strings(). Defaults to True.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; stream reconfiguration and file parsing errors are handled internally.

Example:

init(language="english")          # Load strings, set language

Implementation Details:

def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False, auto_translate=True):
    """Initialize the output system: load strings.csv, set language, auto-translate missing.

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments but before any emit() calls.

    Args:
        language: Target language name (e.g., "Vietnamese").
        use_cache: Whether LLM caching is enabled (passed to translation calls).
        thinking_level: LLM thinking level (passed to translation calls).
        auto_translate: Translate missing strings now. main() passes False and calls
            translate_missing_strings() after argument validation and the LLM auth preflight,
            because translation is itself an LLM call.
    """
    global _language, _lang_col, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level, _debug
    _language = language.capitalize()
    _lang_col = language.lower()
    _csv_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "strings.csv")
    _use_cache = use_cache
    _thinking_level = thinking_level
    _debug = debug
    _ensure_utf8_streams()
    _load_strings()
    if auto_translate:
        _auto_translate()

The function normalizes the input language name into two representations: a capitalized string (_language) for terminal display messages and a lowercase identifier (_lang_col) matching column headers in strings.csv. It locates the string catalog relative to the physical directory of output.py and stores inference parameters (_use_cache, _thinking_level) for runtime translation requests. Stream safety is verified by calling _ensure_utf8_streams(), which forces UTF-8 encoding on redirected I/O streams. After populating _strings via _load_strings(), it selectively invokes _auto_translate() based on the auto_translate flag.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def translate_missing_strings():

Description: Dispatches an explicit batch translation request for any strings missing in the active language catalog. This separates catalog population from CLI argument initialization, allowing authentication checks to complete before initiating LLM calls.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; translation and serialization failures are trapped in the downstream translation layer.

Example:

# Extracted from main.py lifecycle sequence:
init_output(language=args.language, use_cache=not args.no_cache, thinking_level=args.thinking, debug=args.debug, auto_translate=False)
# ... validate CLI parameters and preflight credentials ...
translate_missing_strings()

Implementation Details:

def translate_missing_strings():
    """Auto-translate strings missing for the configured language (LLM call); see init(auto_translate=False)."""
    _auto_translate()

This method delegates directly to the internal _auto_translate() helper. It enables a two-phase initialization pattern during pipeline startup: init() is called first with auto_translate=False to safely load base English strings before network calls are permitted. Once preflight credential checks and parameter validation verify the environment, callers invoke translate_missing_strings() to populate missing language entries via LLM inference without risking premature network operations.

docs.title: emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):

Description: Resolves a localized template from the catalog by key, formats it with provided variable substitutions, and outputs the result to the console, file log, or both according to configured routing rules.

Parameters:

  • key (str): Catalog key identifier defined in strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER").
  • suffix (str): Optional string appended to the formatted text before output (e.g., token consumption statistics). Defaults to "".
  • **kwargs (Any): Keyword arguments substituted into template placeholders (e.g., chapter_num=1).

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; missing keys output a fallback warning string, while variable formatting errors fall back to raw template text.

Example:

emit("LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", chapter_num=1, name="flow")  # Print + log

Implementation Details:

def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):
    """Emit a translatable string to stdout and/or log file.

    Args:
        key: String key from strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER").
        suffix: Optional extra text appended after the main message (e.g., token breakdown).
        **kwargs: Variables to substitute into the string template.
    """
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        # Fallback for unknown keys — print raw so nothing is silently lost
        print(f"[UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]")
        return

    text = _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
    if suffix:
        text = text + suffix

    level = entry["level"]
    dest = entry["dest"]

    # D-prefixed destinations (DBOTH, DSTDOUT): debug-gated console output.
    # Without --debug, suppress console but always log. Preserves original color from LEVEL.
    if dest.startswith("D"):
        if _debug:
            dest = dest[1:]  # DBOTH → BOTH, DSTDOUT → STDOUT
        else:
            dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)

The function queries _strings for the specified key. If the key does not exist, it prints [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] to standard output to surface missing catalog entries without crashing the application. If found, the template string is safely formatted with kwargs via _format_safe() and concatenated with any optional suffix.

Destination routing evaluates the dest property. Destinations prefixed with "D" (such as DBOTH and DSTDOUT) are treated as debug-gated channels: if _debug is True, the "D" prefix is stripped to allow console printing; otherwise, dest is converted to "LOG" to restrict output to the log file. If the destination includes console output, the text is wrapped with ANSI codes from COLORS and RESET and printed via print(). If the destination includes file output, the message is passed to _write_log().

docs.title: emit_raw()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):

Description: Emits a pre-formatted string directly to console and log streams with explicit severity styling, bypassing string catalog lookups.

Parameters:

  • level (str): Logical severity level corresponding to a key in COLORS (e.g., "PROGRESS", "WARNING", "ERROR", "INFO", "DEBUG").
  • text (str): The pre-formatted text string to be emitted.
  • dest (str): Routing destination target. Must be "BOTH", "STDOUT", or "LOG". Defaults to "BOTH".

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions.

Example:

emit_raw("WARNING", "Custom message")    # Pre-formatted output

Implementation Details:

def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):
    """Emit a pre-formatted string with explicit level styling.

    Use for dynamic/structural output that doesn't come from strings.csv
    (e.g., numbered file lists, batch details, crawl summary tables).
    """
    # DEBUG-level: suppress console unless --debug is active
    if level == "DEBUG" and not _debug:
        dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _write_log(level, text)

emit_raw() handles structural, non-catalog messages such as dynamic file lists, runtime ASCII banners, markdown summaries, and raw diagnostic dumps. If the provided level is "DEBUG" and global debug mode is inactive (not _debug), the destination is downgraded from "BOTH" or "STDOUT" to "LOG". Terminal colors are looked up directly from COLORS using level. When dest contains "STDOUT" or "BOTH", the colored string is printed to the terminal. When dest contains "LOG" or "BOTH", _write_log() records the message to the file log.

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def get(key, **kwargs):

Description: Retrieves a translated string from the catalog and applies variable formatting without emitting it to console or log streams.

Parameters:

  • key (str): Catalog key identifier defined in strings.csv.
  • **kwargs (Any): Keyword arguments substituted into template placeholders.

Returns:

  • str: The translated and formatted text string. If key is missing from the catalog, returns key as a fallback.

Example:

label = get("UI_TUTORIAL")               # Get raw translated string

Implementation Details:

def get(key, **kwargs):
    """Get a translated string without printing or logging.

    Use for UI strings embedded in generated markdown (index.md headings, etc.).
    Returns the raw translated text with variable substitution applied.
    """
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        return key  # Fallback: return the key itself
    return _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)

get() provides programmatic access to translated strings without writing to output streams. It is used to generate documentation artifacts—such as table-of-contents labels, Markdown chapter titles, and static site navigation strings—that require localized phrasing. If the requested key is not present in _strings, the raw key string is returned to prevent rendering blank UI labels.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):

Description: Initializes file-based logging for the active run, creates the log directory, opens a timestamped log file, writes execution metadata, and flushes any buffered pre-configuration log lines.

Parameters:

  • project_name (str): Identifier of the target codebase. Sanitized to alphanumeric and -_. characters. Defaults to "project".
  • mode (str): Pipeline execution mode (e.g., "tutorial", "api-reference"). Hyphens are normalized to underscores. Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns:

  • str: The absolute or relative filesystem path of the initialized .log file.

Raises:

  • OSError: When directory creation fails or log file permissions are insufficient.

Example:

# Extracted from main.py setup:
log_file_path = configure_logging(project_name=repo_name, mode=generation_mode)

Implementation Details:

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    """Configure file-based logging for this run.

    Creates a new log file per invocation:
        logs/{project_name}_{mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments.
    """
    global _log_file

    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_path = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Close any existing log file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()

    _log_file = open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8")  # noqa: SIM115

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    sep = "=" * 80
    emit_raw("INFO", sep, dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}", dest="LOG")
    emit_raw("INFO", f"Log file: {log_path}", dest="LOG")
    if _pending_log:
        _log_file.write("".join(_pending_log))
        _log_file.flush()
        _pending_log.clear()

    return log_path

The function resolves the output directory by reading the LOG_DIR environment variable, falling back to the local "logs" directory if unset, and creates it via os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True). The log filename follows the pattern {safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log, sanitizing project_name to remove invalid filesystem characters and replacing hyphens in mode with underscores.

If a log file is already open, it is closed before opening the new file handle in append mode ("a") with UTF-8 encoding. It then writes a delimiter banner, metadata header, and log file path via emit_raw(..., dest="LOG"). Finally, any log entries buffered in _pending_log during early application boot are written to disk, flushed immediately, and cleared from the buffer.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public

Signature: def shutdown():

Description: Closes the active log file handle and releases filesystem resources.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions.

Example:

# Extracted from main.py teardown:
try:

finally:

Implementation Details:

def shutdown():
    """Close the log file handle and release resources.

    Should be called at the end of main() in a finally block to ensure
    the log file is properly flushed and closed.
    """
    global _log_file
    if _log_file is not None:
        _log_file.close()
        _log_file = None

shutdown() checks whether _log_file holds an open file handle. If present, it closes the file handle and resets _log_file to None. Calling this function inside a finally block ensures that buffered log buffers are flushed to disk and file locks are released upon process termination.

docs.title: _write_log()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _write_log(level, text):

Description: Writes a timestamped log line to the active file handle. If logging has not yet been configured, appends the line to the bounded pre-configuration buffer.

Parameters:

  • level (str): Message severity label written into the log prefix.
  • text (str): Text content to write.

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions.

Implementation:

def _write_log(level, text):
    """Write a timestamped line to the log file (buffered until configure_logging opens it)."""
    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f")[:-3]
    line = f"{ts} - {level} - {text}\n"
    if _log_file is None:
        _pending_log.append(line)
        if len(_pending_log) > PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES:
            del _pending_log[0]
        return
    _log_file.write(line)
    _log_file.flush()

The function builds a log record prefixed with a microsecond-precision timestamp formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm alongside the severity level. If _log_file is uninitialized (None), the record is appended to the _pending_log list. If the list size exceeds PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES (5,000 entries), the oldest record at index 0 is dropped to maintain a bounded memory footprint. Once _log_file is open, records are written immediately and flushed to disk to guarantee log durability.

docs.title: _ensure_utf8_streams()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _ensure_utf8_streams():

Description: Reconfigures standard output and error streams to use UTF-8 encoding when connected to pipes or redirection sinks on operating systems with legacy ANSI code pages.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions.

Implementation:

def _ensure_utf8_streams():
    """Write UTF-8 when stdout/stderr are piped or redirected.

    On Windows a redirected stream uses the ANSI code page (e.g. cp1252) and any
    non-English CLI string (Vietnamese, CJK, ...) raises UnicodeEncodeError. Interactive
    consoles already use UTF-8 (PEP 528), so only non-TTY streams are reconfigured.
    """
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        encoding = (getattr(stream, "encoding", "") or "").lower().replace("-", "")
        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure") and encoding != "utf8" and not stream.isatty():
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

This helper addresses platform-specific console encoding discrepancies, particularly on Windows environments where redirected streams default to non-UTF-8 character sets like cp1252. Under these code pages, non-English translations containing diacritics or CJK characters trigger fatal UnicodeEncodeError exceptions. The function inspects sys.stdout and sys.stderr; if a stream is not an interactive terminal (not stream.isatty()) and its encoding is not UTF-8, it calls stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"). This guarantees safe streaming across pipes and redirection targets while replacing unencodable code points rather than raising errors.

docs.title: _format_safe()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _format_safe(template, kwargs):

Description: Applies variable substitution to a string template using keyword arguments, falling back to the raw template if formatting fails.

Parameters:

  • template (str): Template string containing format placeholders (e.g., "Processing {repo}").
  • kwargs (dict): Dictionary of keyword substitution values.

Returns:

  • str: The formatted string, or the original template string if formatting encounters an exception.

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions.

Implementation:

def _format_safe(template, kwargs):
    """Apply .format(**kwargs) with graceful fallback on missing keys."""
    try:
        return template.format(**kwargs)
    except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
        return template

The function executes Python's built-in str.format(**kwargs). If the substitution references an undefined key (KeyError), uses invalid positional indexes (IndexError), or encounters malformed format specifiers (ValueError), the exception is caught and the unparsed template is returned as-is. This prevents missing metadata arguments from crashing execution.

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _load_strings():

Description: Reads strings.csv, parses localization rows, resolves language fallbacks, and populates the _strings catalog in memory.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; missing catalog paths return early without side effects.

Implementation:

def _load_strings():
    """Load all strings from strings.csv."""
    global _strings
    _strings = {}

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return

    translated_count = 0
    total_count = 0

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue

            level = row.get("LEVEL", "INFO").strip()
            dest = row.get("DEST", "BOTH").strip()

            # Priority: language column → English fallback
            text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip()
            if text:
                translated_count += 1
            else:
                text = row.get("english", "").strip()

            total_count += 1
            _strings[key] = {"text": text, "level": level, "dest": dest}

    if _lang_col != "english" and translated_count == total_count:
        emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] {_language} — loaded {translated_count} strings from CSV")

The function reads the CSV catalog using utf-8-sig encoding to transparently handle byte-order marks. It skips empty rows and comment entries prefixed with #. For each row, it extracts STRING_KEY, LEVEL (defaulting to "INFO"), and DEST (defaulting to "BOTH").

Text selection follows a priority hierarchy: it first checks for text under the active language column (_lang_col); if empty or missing, it falls back to the canonical "english" column. As rows are parsed, the function tracks translated_count against total_count. If a non-English language is fully translated, it emits a confirmation message via emit_raw().

docs.title: _auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private

Signature: def _auto_translate():

Description: Dispatches an automated translation workflow by importing the utils.i18n engine, requesting missing strings from an LLM, and refreshing the in-memory catalog when new translations are added.

Parameters:

  • None

Returns:

  • None

Raises:

  • Does not raise exceptions; internal network or parsing errors during translation are handled inside utils.i18n.

Implementation:

def _auto_translate():
    """Auto-translate missing strings via LLM and write back into strings.csv."""
    from utils.i18n import auto_translate

    if auto_translate(_lang_col, _language, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level):
        # Reload strings from the updated CSV so all translations are active
        _load_strings()

This helper uses a late import of utils.i18n.auto_translate to break circular import dependencies across output.py, call_llm.py, and token_utils.py. It invokes auto_translate with the active language configuration, target file path, and model reasoning options. If auto_translate populates new translations and writes them back to strings.csv, it returns True, prompting _auto_translate() to call _load_strings() to refresh the in-memory _strings catalog.

docs.title: Catalog Entry Mapping
docs.text:
The internal _strings dictionary stores parsed string records using string keys mapped to entry dictionaries with the following structure:

Field Type Description text str Localized string template, optionally including format placeholders like {name}. level str Message severity category used for ANSI color selection. Matches a key in COLORS. dest str Output destination flag controlling stream routing (BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, DBOTH, DSTDOUT). 
# Representative entry structure inside _strings:
{
    "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER": {
        "text": "Writing chapter {chapter_num}: {name}...",
        "level": "PROGRESS",
        "dest": "BOTH"
    }
}

docs.title: CSV Catalog Schema (strings.csv)
docs.text:
strings.csv defines the persistent storage format for application messages. The file uses commas as delimiters and utf-8-sig encoding.

Column Type Description Example STRING_KEY String Unique identifier used in code invocations. Rows starting with # are treated as comments. LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER LEVEL String Severity level controlling console color formatting. PROGRESS DEST String Stream destination selector (BOTH, STDOUT, LOG, DBOTH, DSTDOUT). BOTH english String Canonical English template text. Serves as the fallback for untranslated rows. Writing chapter {chapter_num}: {name}... <lang> String Dynamic language-specific columns (e.g., vietnamese, japanese) appended as new translations are generated. Đang viết chương {chapter_num}: {name}...

docs.title: Output Destination Routing Directives
docs.text:
The dest attribute in catalog entries and emit_raw() calls determines how messages are routed between terminal output and persistent log files:

Routing Identifier Target Streams Debug Behavior Description STDOUT Console only Standard Emits to sys.stdout with ANSI styling; bypassed by the file log. LOG File log only Standard Written directly to _log_file or _pending_log; bypassed by the console. BOTH Console and file log Standard Simultaneous emission to both terminal and file destinations. DSTDOUT Console only Debug-gated Downgraded to LOG when _debug is False; emitted to console when _debug is True. DBOTH Console and file log Debug-gated Downgraded to LOG when _debug is False; emitted to both when _debug is True.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The utils/output.py module implements defensive error handling to prevent logging or formatting errors from interrupting pipeline execution:

  • Format Substitution Fault Tolerance: _format_safe() catches KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError exceptions raised by str.format(). If an emit() or get() call receives incomplete arguments or invalid placeholders, the module returns the unformatted template string instead of raising an unhandled exception.
  • Stream Encoding Fallback: _ensure_utf8_streams() guards non-interactive and redirected streams against character encoding failures on Windows systems. If standard streams are bound to legacy code pages, the module calls stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") to replace unencodable characters instead of throwing UnicodeEncodeError.
  • Missing Catalog Key Handling: When emit() receives an unrecognized catalog key, it avoids dropping the message by printing a fallback warning in the format [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]. Similarly, get() returns the raw key string when a lookup fails.
  • Pre-configuration Log Buffering: Messages logged before configure_logging() completes are stored in the _pending_log queue. If log configuration is delayed or omitted, the queue is capped at PENDING_LOG_MAX_LINES (5,000 entries) using a FIFO eviction policy (del _pending_log[0]) to prevent unbounded memory growth.
  • Missing Catalog Handling: If strings.csv is missing or the path cannot be resolved, _load_strings() returns an empty catalog without raising an error. Subsequent emit() and get() calls gracefully fall back to displaying missing key warnings.

docs.title: prompts.py
docs.text: Source: utils/prompts.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Connecting from the logging and telemetry facilities implemented in utils/output.py, utils/prompts.py utilizes the module's diagnostic emission mechanisms while serving as the central prompt template loader, inline prompt constructor, and fault-tolerant LLM response parser for the documentation pipeline. The module acts as the serialization boundary between pipeline nodes and Large Language Model (LLM) inference endpoints. It supplies parameterized prompts for codebase file classification, chapter summarization, verified fact grounding, and structural module grouping, while also loading disk-based prompt templates across different operational documentation modes such as tutorial, advanced, SDK, and API reference modes.

A primary technical challenge addressed by this module is the inherent syntactic instability of LLM-generated structured text. Foundation models frequently output YAML blocks containing unquoted special characters (such as @, #, and *), unescaped colons in code signatures, missing closing Markdown code fences, or premature cutoffs caused by context window or output token limits. To prevent catastrophic pipeline failures, utils/prompts.py implements a resilient multi-tiered parsing and salvage strategy. Instead of failing outright on syntax errors, it progressively sanitizes indicator tokens, converts unquoted scalar declarations into YAML block scalars, decomposes corrupted blocks into independent section chunks, and parses individual list items in isolation, accurately tracking discarded facts within an explicit metadata tally.
